english_text: Jesus sent these twelve out and commanded them, saying, “Don’t go among the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.
nagamese_text: Aru baroh ta jon chela khan ke Jisu pora pathai dise. Tai bujhai kene koise, “Porjati manu khan laga rasta te najabi, aru Samaria nogor bhitor te naghusi bhi.

english_text: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
nagamese_text: Kintu harai ja-a mer khan jun ase Israel laga ghor, taikhan logot jabi;

english_text: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’
nagamese_text: aru jitia tumikhan jai, prochar kori kene kobi, ‘Sorgo laga rajyo usor ahi ase.’

english_text: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.
nagamese_text: Bemar khan ke bhal koribi, mora khan ke uthai dibi, kusto bemar thaka khan ke sapha kori dibi, aru biya atma khan ke khedai dibi. Eku daam naterai kene paise, eku daam noloikena dibi.

english_text: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.
nagamese_text: Suna, chandi, nohoile pitol khan eku nabukhibi.

english_text: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor sandals, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
nagamese_text: Eku jola nadhuribi jai thaka somoite, nohoile duita kapra, nohoile chapal, nohoile lathi nadhuribi, kele koile kaam kora khan ke hajira pabo lage.

english_text: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go on.
nagamese_text: Kuntu sheher nohoile bhi bosti te tumikhan jai, utu jagate ekjon bhal manu ke bisaribi, aru jitia tak tumi chari kene najai, tai laga ghor te he thakibi.

english_text: As you enter into the household, greet it.
nagamese_text: Jitia tumi tai laga ghor te ghuse, taike salam koribi.

english_text: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.
nagamese_text: Aru etu ghor to thik hoile, tumikhan laga shanti ta te thakibo dibi. Kintu jodi ghor to thik nohoi, tinehoile shanti to wapas tumikhan laga hobo.

english_text: Whoever doesn’t receive you or hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.
nagamese_text: Judi utu ghor te tumikhan ke ghusibole nadiye, aru utu sheher manu khan pora tumikhan laga kotha nahune, tinehoile etu jaga chari bhi aru tumi laga theng te dhula khan jharikena jai jabi.

english_text: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
nagamese_text: Hosa pora Moi koi ase, jitia Isor laga bisar kora din ahibo, etu dinte etu sheher to Sodom aru Gomorrah town khan pora bhi bisi lobole napara laga saja pabo.

english_text: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.
nagamese_text: Sabi, Ami tumikhan ke ekta mer nisena rong kutta janwar khan majote pathai ase, etu nimite saph nisena gyaani thakibi aru kabotar nisena norom thakibi.

english_text: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.
nagamese_text: Eneka manu khan pora hoshiar koi kene thakibi! Kilekoile taikhan tumikhan ke sabhakhan te loijabo, aru taikhan laga mondoli bhitor te tumikhan ke marikena sajai dibo.

english_text: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Ami nimite tumikhan ke Governor aru raja khan laga age te anibo, dusra khan aru Porjati khan ke ekta gawahi nisena dikhai dibole.

english_text: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan tumikhan ke taikhan hathte di dibo, titia tumikhan ki kobo lage etu karone chinta na koribi, kele koile thik somoite ji kobo lage etu sob tumikhan ke koi dibo.

english_text: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile tumikhan pora nakobo, kintu Baba laga Atma pora he tumikhan nimite koi dibo.

english_text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
nagamese_text: Bhai pora he kokai ke phasai dibo, aru baba pora nijor bacha ke. Bacha khan ama baba khan logote jhagara koribo aru taikhan ke morai dibole koribo.

english_text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
nagamese_text: Moi laga naam nimite tumikhan ke sob pora ghin koribo. Kintu jun khan dukh digdar puwa homoi sob khotom nohua tak dhorjo kori kene thakibo pare, taikhan he bachibo.

english_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man has come.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan pora etu sheher te tumikhan ke biya pora digdar dibo, dusra jagate polai jabi, kele koile Ami hosa pora tumikhan ke koi ase, Manu laga Putro naha age te tumikhan Israel laga sob sheher khan te jai kene khotom kori bole na paribo.

english_text: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.
nagamese_text: Ekjon chela tai laga guru pora dangor nohoi, nohoi lebi ekjon nokor malik pora dangor nohoi.

english_text: It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!
nagamese_text: Ekjon chela tai laga guru nisena hoile etu he thik ase, aru ekjon nokor tai laga malik nisena hoile he thik ase. Judi taikhan etu ghor malik ke Beelzebul koi kene mate koile, kiman bhi biya pora tai laga ghor manu khan ke matibo!

english_text: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.
nagamese_text: Etu karone taikhan ke bhoi nakhabi, kele koile lukaikene thaka eku nai juntu ke janai nadibo, aru juntu janai dibole pare, etu ke lukai kene rakhibo na paribo.

english_text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
nagamese_text: Ji kotha Ami pora tumikhan ke andhera te koi ase, tumikhan pora dinte koi dibi, aru ji kotha tumikhan norom pora kan te huni pai ase, ghor laga sobse untcha jagate uthikena jor pora sobke hunai dibi.

english_text: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
nagamese_text: Jun khan manu ke morai diye eitu khan ke bhoi na koribi kele koile taikhan tumikhan laga jibon ke morai dibole napare. Hoilebi, Isor ke bhoi koribi Jun he tumikhan laga gaw aru jibon ke bhi khotom kori dibole pare.

english_text: “Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father’s will.
nagamese_text: Ekta chutu chandi pora duita ghor chiriya ke kini bole napare naki? Titia bhi tumikhan laga Baba pora najanikena ekta chiriya bhi matite giribole nadiye.

english_text: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan laga matha te chuli thaka khan sob ginti kori kene ase.

english_text: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
nagamese_text: Etu karone bhoi na koribi. Tumikhan ke ghor laga chiriya pora bhi bisi morom kore.

english_text: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.
nagamese_text: Etu karone jun manu sob manu khan laga age te Moi laga naam shikar koribo, Ami bhi tai laga naam sorgote thaka Ami laga Baba age te shikar dibo.

english_text: But whoever denies me before men, I will also deny him before my Father who is in heaven.
nagamese_text: Kintu jun manu pora sob manu laga age te Ami laga naam noloi, Ami bhi tai laga naam sorgote thaka Ami laga Baba age te nolobo.

english_text: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.
nagamese_text: Ami etu prithibi te shanti dibole aha nohoi. Ami shanti loi kene aha nai, kintu talwar loi kene ahise.

english_text: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Ami aha to chokra ke tai laga baba pora alag kori dibole, aru ekjon chukri ke tai laga ama pora alag kori dibole, aru ekjon buari ke tai laga sasuma pora alag kori dibole ahise.

english_text: A man’s foes will be those of his own household.
nagamese_text: Ekjon mota laga dushman khan nijor ghor manu khan he hobo.

english_text: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai nijor baba aru ama ke Ami pora bisi morom kore tai Ami laga chela hobo na paribo; aru jun tai njior chokra nohoi lebi chukri ke Ami pora bhi bisi morom kore, tai Ami laga chela hobo na paribo.

english_text: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me isn’t worthy of me.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai laga nijor Cross to uthaikene moi laga piche nahe, tai Ami laga chela hobo na paribo.

english_text: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai nijor jibon to bacha bole itcha kore tai harai jabo. Kintu jun manu Moi nimite tai laga jibon diye, tai to aru wapas pabo.

english_text: “He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tumike grohon kore, tai Moike bhi grohon kore, aru jun tumike grohon kore, Isor, jun pora Amike pathaise, Taike bhi grohon kore.

english_text: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
nagamese_text: Jun manu ekjon bhabobadi khan ke grohon kore, tai bhabobadi laga inam pabo, aru jun manu dhormik manu ke grohon kore, tai dhormik manu laga inam pabo.

english_text: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.”
nagamese_text: Jun khan etu chutu dukhiya ekjon ke Ami laga chela ase koi kene ek kup thanda pani khilai dibo, hosa pora Ami koi ase, tai to hosa pora bhi tai laga inam to naharabo.”

english_text: When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.
nagamese_text: Eneka hoise jitia Jisu tai laga baroh jon chela khan ke niyom khan bujhai diya pichete, tai ta te pora ulaikena taikhan laga sheher te jai kene prochar kori bole aru sikhai dibole jai jaise.

english_text: Now when John heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te John bondhi ghor te thakise, tai Khrista laga kotha huni paise, aru tai tai laga chela khan ke ekta jankari dibole pathaise

english_text: and said to him, “Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?”
nagamese_text: aru Taike hudise, “Apuni ahibole thaka Jon ase naki, na amikhan dusra ke bisaribo?”

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:
nagamese_text: Jisu pora jowab dikene koise, “Jabi aru John ke koi dibi tumikhan ki hunise aru dikhise.

english_text: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
nagamese_text: Andha manu khan dikhibole paise, lengera khan bera bole parise, kusto bemar thaka khan sapha hoi jaise, behera khan huni bole paise, morija khan jinda hoise, aru gorib manu khan susamachar huni loise.

english_text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
nagamese_text: Jun manu Amike dikhikena biya panai tai to asis paise.”

english_text: As these went their way, Jesus began to say to the multitudes concerning John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan jaise, Jisu pora bhir ke John laga kotha kori bole shuru hoise, “Tumikhan balu laga jagate ki sabole jaise- panite ulai thaka ghas ke hawa pora hilai diya to?

english_text: But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan ta te ki sabole jaise- ekjon manu norom kapra lagai kene thaka ke? Hosa bhi, jun khan norom kapra lagai, taikhan to raja khan laga ghor te he thake.

english_text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan ki sabole ta te jaise- ekjon bhabobadi? Hoi, Ami tumikhan ke koi ase, tai ekjon bhabobadi pora bhi bisi ase.

english_text: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
nagamese_text: Etu tai ase, jun karone eneka Isor kotha te likhi kene ase, ‘Sabi, Ami pora tumikhan laga chehera age te Ami laga khobor diya manu pathai ase, jun pora tumikhan nimite rasta taiyar koribo.’

english_text: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.
nagamese_text: Ami hosa pora tumikhan ke koi ase, tumikhan majote Baptizma diya John nisena kun ama pora bhi jonom diya nai. Hoilebi sorgo laga rajyote thaka sob pora kaam nathaka manu bhi tai pora bisi dangor ase.

english_text: From the days of John the Baptizer until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.
nagamese_text: Baptizma diya John laga din pora loi kene etiya tak, sorgo laga rajyo to mara-mari khan pora dukh paise, aru jhagara pora joborjosti kori kene chingi loise.

english_text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile John naha age te sob bhabobadi khan aru niyom khan laga bhabobani hoi thakise;

english_text: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.
nagamese_text: aru jodi tumikhan lobole itcha ase koile, tai to Elijah ase jun ahibole thakise.

english_text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
nagamese_text: Jun laga kan khan ase, taikhan ke huni bole dibi.

english_text: “But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call to their companions
nagamese_text: Ki logote etu yug laga manu khan ke tulona koribo? Bacha khan bajar te bohi kene thaka nisena, jun ekjon pora ekjon ke mati thake

english_text: and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’
nagamese_text: aru koi, ‘Amikhan pora apnikhan karone shadi laga basuri bajaise, aru apnikhan nacha nai. Amikhan mon dukh hoise aru apnikhan mon dukh laga suku pani bhi ula nai.’

english_text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
nagamese_text: Kilekoile John to pani aru kha luwa khaikena aha nohoi, aru taikhan koise, ‘Tai logot te bhoot ase.’

english_text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her children.”
nagamese_text: Manu laga Putro to pani aru kha luwa kori kene ahise aru taikhan koise, ‘Sabi, tai to bisi khai aru ekjon sharabi ase, poisa utha aru paapi manu khan laga sathi ase!’ Kintu gyaan to tai laga bacha pora he dikhai dibo.”

english_text: Then he began to denounce the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they didn’t repent.
nagamese_text: Pichete Jisu jun to jagate tai laga asurit kaam khan dikhai dise, etu sheher khan laga manu khan ke gali dibole shuru korise, kele koile taikhan mon ghuraikena thaka nai.

english_text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
nagamese_text: “Chorazin, tumike hai ase! Bethsaida, tumike hai ase! Juntu kaam tumikhan nimite korise, eneka kaam Tyre aru Sidon nimite korise koile, taikhan poila pora bosta laga kapra aru jui laga koila lagai kene mon ghuri lobole thakise.

english_text: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Isor pora bisar kora dinte tumikhan pora bhi Tyre aru Sidon nimite he bisi aram hobo.

english_text: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades. For if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remained until today.
nagamese_text: Tumi, Capernaum, tumikhan ke sorgo uporte uthibole nadibo, na uthibo dibo? Tumikhan ke Hades te namai dibo. Kilekoile tumikhan ke koi diya nisena jodi Sodom te bhi asurit aru dangor kaam korise koile, taikhan aji bachikena thakibo thakise.

english_text: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment, than for you.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, bisar laga dinte tumikhan pora bhi Sodom nimite he aram hobo.”

english_text: At that time, Jesus answered, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.
nagamese_text: Etu somoite Jisu pora jowab dise aru koise, “Ami Apuni ke mohima di ase, Baba, Sorgo aru prithibi laga Probhu, kele koile Apuni eitu khan gyaani aru buja manu khan pora lukaikene rakhise, aru chutu bacha khan ke dikhai dise.

english_text: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.
nagamese_text: Hoi, Baba, kele koile etu to Apuni laga suku age te thik ase.

english_text: All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.
nagamese_text: Sob kaam khan moi laga bharosa te Baba pora rakhidise; aru kun bhi Putro ke najane khali Baba he nohoile, aru kun bhi Baba ke najane khali Putro he nohoile, aru utu manu junke Putro pora basikena dikhai dibo.

english_text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
nagamese_text: Ami usorte ahibi, jun manu etu prithibi laga dukh chinta bukhi bo napari kene dabi kene ase, aru Moi tumikhan ke aram dibo.

english_text: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
nagamese_text: Ami laga kotha khan lobi aru Ami pora sikhibi, kele koile Ami laga mon to nomro aru shanti ase, aru tumi laga jibon nimite aram pabo.

english_text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Ami laga kotha khan aram ase aru ami laga boja bisi halka ase.”

english_text: At that time, Jesus went on the Sabbath day through the grain fields. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
nagamese_text: Utu somoite, ek Bisram dinte, Jisu dhaan kheti paar hoi kene jai thakise. Tai laga chela khan bhuk lagi thaka pora dhaan laga guti ulaikena khabole shuru korise.

english_text: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said to him, “Behold, your disciples do what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Pharisee khan etu dikhise, taikhan Jisu ke koise, “Sabi, Apuni laga chela khan Bisram nimite niyom te nathaka kaam kori ase.”

english_text: But he said to them, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him:
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan kitia bhi Isor kotha te purah nai David pora ki korise, jitia tai aru tai logot thaka manu khan bhuk lagise?

english_text: how he entered into God’s house and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
nagamese_text: Tai Isor laga ghor te jaise aru Isor nimite rakhikena thaka roti khaise, juntu tai nimite nohoile tai logote thaka manu khan nimite khabole niyom te nai, kele koile khali purohit khan he ta te pora khabo pare.

english_text: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
nagamese_text: Nohoile tumikhan Moses laga niyom te purah nai naki Bisram laga dinte mondoli te thaka purohit khan Bisram din laga niyom bhangai kintu taikhan ke etu golti ase koi kene nadhure?

english_text: But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, mondoli pora bhi dangor jon to yate ase.

english_text: But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.
nagamese_text: Jodi tumikhan etu laga motlob janikena thaki ase, ‘Moi daya kora he itcha ase aru bolidan diya nohoi,’ koile tumikhan golti nathaka khan ke golti ase koi kene namatibo.

english_text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Manu laga Putro he Bisram Din laga Probhu ase.”

english_text: He departed from there and went into their synagogue.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu ta te pora ulaise aru taikhan laga mondoli te ghusi se.

english_text: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” so that they might accuse him.
nagamese_text: Sabi, ta te ekjon manu thakise jun laga hath sukhikena thakise. Pharisee khan pora Jisu ke eneka koi kene hudise, “Bisram dinte bemar bhal kori diya to niyom ase naki?” Taikhan Jisu ke golti dibole nimite hudise.

english_text: He said to them, “What man is there among you who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, won’t he grab on to it and lift it out?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Kun manu tumikhan majote ase, jun logote khali ekta mer he ase, aru jitia utu mer to Bisram dinte ekdom niche chenda te giri jai koile, tai utu mer ke nauthabo naki?

english_text: Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”
nagamese_text: Tinehoile mer pora bhi manu khan kiman bhi kimti ase! Etu nimite Bisram dinte bhal kaam kora thik niyom ase.”

english_text: Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu utu manu ke koise, “Tumi laga hath ke sida koribi.” Jitia tai hath sida korise, aru jineka dusra hath nisena, etu hath bhi bhal hoi jaise.

english_text: But the Pharisees went out and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan ta te pora ulai jaise aru jai kene taikhan kineka kori kene Jisu ke morai dibo etu kotha khan kori thakise.

english_text: Jesus, perceiving that, withdrew from there. Great multitudes followed him; and he healed them all,
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu eitu khan janibole paise, Tai ta te pora ulai jaise. Bisi manu Tai piche korise, aru Tai sobke bhal kori dise.

english_text: and commanded them that they should not make him known,
nagamese_text: Aru manu khan ke Tai janai dibole hoshiar kori dise,

english_text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
nagamese_text: titia Isor pora bhabobadi Isaiah dwara kowa kotha khan pura hobole karone eitu khan sob tineka he hoi jaise,

english_text: “Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit on him. He will proclaim justice to the nations.
nagamese_text: “Sabi, etu Ami laga noukar ase junke Ami basi loise; Ami laga morom thaka ekjon, junke Moi laga jibon pora khushi ase. Moi Tai uporte Moi laga Atma rakhidibo, Aru Tai pora Porjati khan ke ajad kori dibo.

english_text: He will not strive, nor shout, neither will anyone hear his voice in the streets.
nagamese_text: Tai biya napabo nohoile bhi jor pora nakandibo; Nohoile bhi kun bhi rasta khan te Tai laga awaj nahunibo.

english_text: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a smoking flax, until he leads justice to victory.
nagamese_text: Tai ekta tera koi kene thaka pani-ghas bhi bhangai nadibo; Tai khotom hobole thaka jui ke bhi bhutibole nadibo, Jitia tak Tai bisar ke age loi kene jiti noloi,

english_text: In his name, the nations will hope.”
nagamese_text: aru Tai laga naam uporte he Porjati khan asha thakibo.”

english_text: Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and saw.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete kunba ekjon andha aru gunga, bhoot pora bandi kene thaka, Jisu usorte loi anise. Jisu pora taike changai kori dise, aru tai kotha kori bole aru sabole pari jaise.

english_text: All the multitudes were amazed, and said, “Can this be the son of David?”
nagamese_text: Sob manu khan dikhikena asurit hoise aru koise, “Etu manu to David laga Putro ase nohoi?”

english_text: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Pharisee khan asurit kaam to huni bole paise, taikhan koise, “Etu manu to Saitan laga raja, Beelzebul laga takot pora kaam kori ase, nohoile bhoot khan khedai dibo na paribo.”

english_text: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan laga bhabona jani thakise aru taikhan ke koise, “Juntu rajyo taikhan nijor majote apatti thake, etu rajyo to bhangi jai, aru juntu sheher nohoile bhi ghor to nijor majote apatti thake, etu bhangi jai.

english_text: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
nagamese_text: Etu nimite jodi Saitan pora Saitan ke khedai dile, tai nijor bhirodh te bhag koi kene ase. Kineka kori kene tai laga rajyo to khara koribo?

english_text: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi Moi Beelzebul laga hokti loi kene bhoot khan ke khedai, tinehoile ki hokti pora tumikhan laga bacha khan bhoot khan ke khedai? Etu karone, taikhan pora tumikhan ke bisar koribo.

english_text: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi Ami Isor laga Atma pora bhoot khan ke khedai diye, tinehoile Isor laga rajyo tumikhan uporte ahikena ase.

english_text: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
nagamese_text: Nohoile kineka ekta takot thaka manu ke age nabandi kene utu ghor te ghusi kene saman khan chor koribo paribo? Poila takot manu ke bandibo lagibo etu pichete he tai laga saman khan chor koribo paribo.

english_text: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.
nagamese_text: Jun Ami logote nohoi tai Amike apatti kore, aru jun Ami logote joma nakore taikhan sob ephale-uphale hoi jabo.

english_text: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, sob paap aru hinsa kotha kora khan maph kori dibo, kintu jun manu Atma ke hinsa kore taike maph nadibo.

english_text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this age, or in that which is to come.
nagamese_text: Jun manu pora Manu laga Putro ke apatti koribo tai maph pabo. Kintu jun manu Pobitro Atma ke apatti koribo, tai kitia bhi maph napabo, etu yug te bhi, aru ahibole thaka yug te bhi.

english_text: “Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.
nagamese_text: Ekta bhal ghas to bhal phol dhuri bo, nohoile biya ghas pora to biya phol he dhuri bo, kele koile phol pora he ghas ke janibole pare.

english_text: You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.
nagamese_text: Saph laga bacha khan, tumikhan biya hoi kene, kineka bhal kotha koi? Kilekoile mon bhitor te ki ase, mukh pora etu he koi.

english_text: The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
nagamese_text: Bhal manu laga monte bhal saman khan joma kora nimite bhal khan he ulai, aru biya manu laga monte biya saman khan joma kora nimite biya khan he ulai.

english_text: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.
nagamese_text: Moi apnikhan ke koi ase jun manu misa-misi kotha kobo, taikhan bisar dinte etu laga hisab-kitab dibo lagibo.

english_text: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
nagamese_text: Tumikhan laga kotha para he tumi laga bisar hobo, aru tumi laga kotha pora he tumi bodnam hobo.”

english_text: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete kunba Pharisee aru niyom likha khan Jisu ke eneka koise, “Shika manu, Apuni pora ekta chihna amikhan sabole itcha ase.”

english_text: But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise aru koise, “Ekta biya aru biswas nathaka jamana laga manu khan he chihna sabole bisare. Kintu eku bhi chihna dikhai nadibo khali bhabobadi Jonah laga chihna he sabo dibo.”

english_text: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Jonah to tin din aru tin rati ekta dangor maas laga pet bhitor te thakise, etu nisena Manu laga Putro bhi tin din aru tin rati prithibi laga bhitor te thakibo.

english_text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.
nagamese_text: Nineveh sheher te thaka manu khan bisar dinte etu jamana laga manu khan logote khara koribo aru bodnam dibo. Kilekoile taikhan to Jonah laga kotha huni kene mon ghuraise, aru sabi, ekjon Jonah pora bhi bisi dangor yate khara ase.

english_text: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.
nagamese_text: Sheba laga Rani bisar dinte etu jamana laga manu khan logote uthi kene bodnam dibo. Tai prithibi laga sob pora dur jaga pora ahikena Solomon laga gyaani kotha huni bole ahise, aru sabi, ekjon Solomon pora bhi dangor yate khara ase.

english_text: “When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places seeking rest, and doesn’t find it.
nagamese_text: Jitia ekta letera atma manu laga gaw pora bahar ulai jai, tai pani nathaka jaga pora paar kore aru aram kori bole bisare, kintu jaga napai.

english_text: Then he says, ‘I will return into my house from which I came;’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete tai koi, ‘Juntu jaga pora moi ulaikene ahise etu ghor te wapas jabo.’ Jitia tai ghuri ahe, tai ghor to khali aru sob sapha paise aru ghor te sob thik tak rakhi kene thaka dikhise.

english_text: Then he goes and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”
nagamese_text: Titia tai ta te pora ulaikene tai pora bhi bisi biya sat-ta atma khan ke loi kene ahise aru eke logote thaki jaise. Titia etu manu laga halat to poila pora bhi aru bisi biya hoijai. Thik etu nisena etu jamana laga manu khan ke bhi eneka hobo.

english_text: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu bhir khan ke kotha koi thakise, sabi, Tai laga ama aru bhai khan bahar te khara kori Jisu ke lok kori bole bisari thakise.

english_text: One said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.”
nagamese_text: Ekjon Taike koise, “Sabi, Apuni laga ama aru bhai khan bahar te khara ase, Apuni ke kotha kori bole bisari ase.”

english_text: But he answered him who spoke to him, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
nagamese_text: Kintu jun manu taike khobor disele Jisu taike koise, “Kun Moi laga ama ase aru kun Moi laga bhai khan ase?”

english_text: He stretched out his hand toward his disciples, and said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
nagamese_text: Titia chela khan phale Tai laga anguli ishara kori kene Jisu koise, “Sabi, eitu khan Ami laga ama aru bhai khan ase!

english_text: For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun manu Moi laga sorgote thaka Baba laga itcha kore, etu he Moi laga bhai, aru Moi laga bhoini, aru Moi laga ama ase.”

english_text: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seaside.
nagamese_text: Utu dinte Jisu ghor pora ulaikena nodi kinar te bohi thakise.

english_text: Great multitudes gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.
nagamese_text: Dangor bhir joma hoi kene Tai usorte bohi jaise, etu nimite Tai naw uporte uthise, aru sob manu nodi kinar te khara korise.

english_text: He spoke to them many things in parables, saying, “Behold, a farmer went out to sow.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu taikhan ke dristanto khan bisi koise. Tai koise, “Sabi, ekjon kheti kora manu dhaan bijon hali bole jaise.

english_text: As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai kheti te bijon phelai thakise, kunba bijon rasta kinar te girise, aru chiriya khan ahikena sob khai dise.

english_text: Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth.
nagamese_text: Kunba bijon to bisi pathor thaka jagate girise, aru joldi uthijaise, kele koile mati olop thakise.

english_text: When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia gham ulaise, etu ulai thaka ghas ke julai dise, kele koile etu ghas laga shikor thaka nai, etu karone sob sukhi jaise.

english_text: Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.
nagamese_text: Kunba bijon khan kata ghas majot te girise. Aru etu ghas to olop dangor hoise, hoilebi kata ghas pora morai dise.

english_text: Others fell on good soil and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
nagamese_text: Kunba bijon khan bhal matite girise aru bhal ghas hoi kene bhal guti dhurise, kunba eksoh guti, kunba te saathi guti aru kunba te trista guti dhurise.

english_text: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
nagamese_text: Jun manu laga kaan ase, taikhan ke huni bole dibi.”

english_text: The disciples came, and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu laga chela khan Tai usorte ahise aru hudise, “Apuni kele bhir khan ke dristanto pora kotha koi ase?”

english_text: He answered them, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but it is not given to them.
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan ke sorgo rajyo laga bujhi bo napara kotha khan bujhi bole gyaan dikena ase, kintu taikhan ke diya nai.

english_text: For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he has.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun manu logot olop ase, taike aru bhi dibo, aru tai logote bhorta thakibo. Kintu jun manu logote nai, tai logote ki ase etu bhi loi lobo.

english_text: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they don’t see, and hearing, they don’t hear, neither do they understand.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Moi taikhan ke dristanto pora kotha kore: Taikhan dikhi ase, kintu taikhan sabole napare; aru taikhan huni ase, kintu taikhan huni kene bhi bujhi bo napare.

english_text: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, ‘By hearing you will hear, and will in no way understand; Seeing you will see, and will in no way perceive;
nagamese_text: Taikhan nimite to Isaiah laga bhabobani to purah hoise, juntu eneka koi ase, ‘Tumikhan hosa pora bhi hunibo, kintu janibole na paribo; Tumikhan hosa pora bhi dikhibo, kintu bujhi bole na paribo.

english_text: for this people’s heart has grown callous, their ears are dull of hearing, and they have closed their eyes; or else perhaps they might perceive with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, and I would heal them.’
nagamese_text: Kilekoile etu manu khan laga mon to khali hoise, Aru taikhan huni bole tan kori loise, Aru taikhan laga suku bondh kori loise, Eneka korile taikhan suku pora nasabo nimite, Nohoile taikhan kaan pora nahunibo nimite, Nohoile taikhan laga mon pora nabujibo nimite, Kilekoile eneka kori kene taikhan aru bhi mon naghurabo nimite, Aru Moi taikhan ke bhal kori nadibo nimite.’

english_text: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
nagamese_text: Kintu asis te ase tumikhan laga suku, kele koile taikhan dikhi ase; aru tumikhan laga kaan, kele koile taikhan huni ase.

english_text: For most certainly I tell you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.
nagamese_text: Moi hosa pora koi ase tumikhan ke bisi bhabobadi aru pobitro manu khan to tumikhan ki dikhi ase, eitu khan sabole mon thakise, hoilebi taikhan dikhibole panai. Tumikhan ki kotha huni ase, taikhan bhi huni bole mon thakise, kintu taikhan huni bole panai.

english_text: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite kheti kora manu bijon phela laga dristanto etu laga ki motlob ase huni bhi aru bujhibi.

english_text: When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.
nagamese_text: Jitia kunba manu rajyo laga kotha hune kintu bujhi bole napare, tinehoile biya Jon ahe aru ki tai laga monte bijon hali kene ase etu chingi kene loijai. Etu bijon to rasta kinar te phelai diya bijon ase.

english_text: What was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word and immediately with joy receives it;
nagamese_text: Juntu bijon pathor uporte phelaise, etu to eneka manu ase jun kotha huni loi aru loge-loge khushi pora grohon kore,

english_text: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
nagamese_text: kintu kotha khan tai laga mon bhitor te najai, etu nimite khali olop somoi nimite he rakhe. Jitia etu kotha nimite biya aru dukh-digdar pa-a somoi ahe, tai ekbar te he giri jai.

english_text: What was sown among the thorns, this is he who hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
nagamese_text: Juntu bijon kata ghas khan majote phelaise, etu to eneka manu ase jun kotha to hune, hoilebi etu jamana laga kaam aru dhun sompoti ke mon diya nimite kotha ke dabai kene rakhe, aru etu kotha pora bhal guti nadhure.

english_text: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”
nagamese_text: Juntu bijon bhal matite phelaise, etu to eneka manu ase jun kotha to hune aru bujhi loi. Tai dangor koi kene bhal guti dhure, kunba te eksoh guti dhore, kunba te sathi aru kunba te trista.”

english_text: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke dusra dristanto koise. Tai koise, “Sorgo laga rajyo to ekjon manu nisena ase jun tai laga kheti te bhal bijon phelai.

english_text: but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds also among the wheat, and went away.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia manu khan ghumai jai, tai laga dushman khan ahikena gehu laga kheti te biya ghas laga bijon khan phelai aru jai-jai.

english_text: But when the blade sprang up and produced grain, then the darnel weeds appeared also.
nagamese_text: Jitia kheti te gehu khan dangor koi kene guti ulabole shuru hoise, titia biya ghas khan bhi dangor hoijai.

english_text: The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’
nagamese_text: Etu mati malik laga nokorkhan ahi kene taike koi, ‘Sahab, apuni to bhal bijon kheti te lagase nohoi? Nohoile kineka kori kene etu biya ghas khan ulaise?’

english_text: “He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ “The servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them up?’
nagamese_text: Etu pichete tai pora taikhan ke koise, ‘Dushman pora eneka kore.’ Nokorkhan taike koise, ‘To apuni itcha ase koile amikhan jai kene jongol khan sapha kori dibo?’

english_text: “But he said, ‘No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them.
nagamese_text: Mati malik pora taikhan ke koi, ‘Nai. Kilekoile jitia tumikhan biya ghas khan tanibo, tai logote gehu laga ghas bhi tani kene ulai dibo pare.

english_text: Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”
nagamese_text: Etu nimite duijon ke bhi eke logote dangor koribo dibi, kheti kata somoi naha tak. Jitia kheti kata somoi hobo titia moi kata manu khan ke kobo, “Poila biya ghas khan tani kene ulai lobi aru eke logote bandhi kene rakhibi julai dibo nimite, kintu gehu khan ke dhaan ghor te joma kori rakhibi.’”

english_text: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field,
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu aru ekta dristanto taikhan ke koise. Tai koise, “Sorgo laga rajyo to ekta sorso laga bijon nisena ase jineka ekta manu pora loi kene kheti te phelai de.

english_text: which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
nagamese_text: Etu bijon to hosa pora bhi sobse huru ase sob bijon majote. Kintu jitia tai dangor hoi, bagan laga ghas khan pora bhi tai he dangor hoijai. Tai ekta dangor ghas hoijai, aru akas laga chiriya khan ahe aru etu ghas laga daal khan te ghor bonaikena thake.”

english_text: He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke aru alag dristanto koise. “Sorgo laga rajyo to khomir nisena ase, jineka ekta maiki pora etu khomir ke loi kene tin bhag atta te milai diye jitia tak etu atta to phuli najai.”

english_text: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the multitudes; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to them,
nagamese_text: Eitu khan sob kotha Jisu pora manu khan ke dristanto pora he koi dise; aru Tai ekta kotha bhi dristanto nacholai kene kowa nai.

english_text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”
nagamese_text: Eitu khan sob age te bhabobadi pora koi diya kotha khan sob purah hobole nimite, Tai koi dise, “Dristanto khan pora he Moi mukh khuli bo. Ki kotha etu prithibi laga bhetimul te lukaikene ase eitu khan sob Moi koi dibo.”

english_text: Then Jesus sent the multitudes away, and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu manu khan ke chari kene ghor te jaise. Tai laga chela khan Tai logote ahikena, eneka koise, “Amikhan ke kheti te biya ghas laga dristanto to bujhai dibi.”

english_text: He answered them, “He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Jun bhal bijon to phelai, tai to Manu laga Putro ase.

english_text: the field is the world, the good seeds are the children of the Kingdom, and the darnel weeds are the children of the evil one.
nagamese_text: Prithibi to kheti ase; aru bhal bijon khan to rajyo lage bacha khan ase. Biya ghas to biya jon laga bacha khan ase,

english_text: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
nagamese_text: aru jun dushman pora biya hissi se eitu khan saitan ase. Kheti kata somoi to yug khotom huwa somoi ase, aru kheti kata manu khan to sorgodoth khan ase.

english_text: As therefore the darnel weeds are gathered up and burned with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, jineka biya ghas khan ke joma kori kene jui te julai dise, yug ses huwa dinte bhi eneka hobo.

english_text: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling and those who do iniquity,
nagamese_text: Manu laga Putro pora Tai laga sorgodoth khan ke pathabo, aru taikhan pora Tai laga rajyo pora paap aru biya kaam kora khan ke joma kori kene bahar te ulai dibo.

english_text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
nagamese_text: Taikhan pora eitu khan sobke jui laga chulah te phelai dibo, juntu jagate kandi thaka aru daat kamuri thaka he hobo.

english_text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete dharmik manu khan Baba laga rajyote suryo nisena ujala hobo. Jun laga kan ase, tai hunibo dibi.

english_text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
nagamese_text: Sorgo laga rajyo to ekta kheti te khajana lukaikene thaka nisena ase, jitia ekjon manu pora etu pai, tai etu ke aru bhi lukai diye. Kilekoile tai mon khushi hoijai, aru tai laga dhun sompoti sob bikiri kori kene etu kheti kini loi.

english_text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a merchant seeking fine pearls,
nagamese_text: Aru, sorgo laga rajyo to ekjon vyapari manu kimti laga moti khan bisari thaka nisena ase.

english_text: who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai bisi kimti thaka ekta moti pai, tai laga sob dhun sompoti bikiri kori kene etu kini loi.

english_text: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet that was cast into the sea and gathered some fish of every kind,
nagamese_text: Aru bhi, sorgo laga rajyo to samundar te jaal phela nisena ase, aru sob kisim laga maas dhura nisena ase.

english_text: which, when it was filled, fishermen drew up on the beach. They sat down and gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw away.
nagamese_text: Jitia jal to maas pora bhorta hoi jaise, taikhan etu loi kene samundar kinar te rakhe. Etu pichete taikhan bhal maas basi kene boxsa te joma kore, aru kaam nathaka maas khan sob phelai diye.

english_text: So it will be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
nagamese_text: Thik eneka, etu yug ses huwa dinte bhi eneka hobo. Sorgodoth khan ahibo aru biya manu khan ke dhormik khan pora alag kori dibo.

english_text: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke jui laga chulah te julai dibo, juntu jagate khali kandi thaka aru daat kamuri thaka he hobo.

english_text: Jesus said to them, “Have you understood all these things?” They answered him, “Yes, Lord.”
nagamese_text: Apnikhan eitu khan sob bujise na nai?” Jisu laga chela khan Taike koise, “Hoi.”

english_text: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Etu karone sob niyom likha manu khan jun sorgo rajyo laga chela hoi jaise, eitu khan utu manu ase jun ekta ghor laga malik nisena ase.”

english_text: When Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete jitia Jisu etu dristanto khan koi kene khotom hoise, Tai ta te pora ulai jaise.

english_text: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
nagamese_text: Aru Tai nijor town Nazareth te jaise aru mondoli te manu khan ke sikhai thakise. Jisu laga kotha huni kene taikhan asurit hoi jaise aru taikhan majote koi thakise, “Kot pora etu manu iman asurit gyaan aru hokti paise?

english_text: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
nagamese_text: Etu manu to ekjon barhoi laga chokra nohoi? Tai laga ama to Mary nohoi? Tai laga bhai khan James, Joseph, Simon aru Judas khan nohoi?

english_text: Aren’t all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”
nagamese_text: Tai laga bhoini khan to amikhan logote ase nohoi? To kineka kori kene Tai eitu khan jani paise?”

english_text: They were offended by him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu ke biya paise. Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Ekjon bhabobadi ke tai nijor desh aru tai nijor parivar pora bhi sonman nakore.”

english_text: He didn’t do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
nagamese_text: Tai asurit kaam khan bisi kora nai kele koile taikhan laga biswas nathaka nimite.

english_text: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
nagamese_text: Utu din khan te, raja Herod Jisu laga khobor huni bole paise.

english_text: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”
nagamese_text: Tai laga daruga khan ke koise, “Etu Baptizma diya John ase; tai mora pora jinda hoise. Etu karone etu hokti khan tai logote kaam kori ase.”

english_text: For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Herod to John ke dhurikena thakise, taike bandi se aru bondhi ghor te Herodias, tai laga bhai Philip laga maiki pora kowa nimite rakhise.

english_text: For John said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
nagamese_text: Kilekoile John pora taike koise, “Apuni etu maiki ke lobole niyom hisab te nai.”

english_text: When he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
nagamese_text: Herod to John ke morai dibole mon thakise, kintu tai manu khan ke bhoi lagi thakise, kele koile manu khan pora John to ekjon bhabobadi ase koi kene mani thakise.

english_text: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced among them and pleased Herod.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Herod raja laga jonom din ahisele, Herodias laga chukri sob manu majote nach kori kene Herod raja ke khushi kori dise.

english_text: Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
nagamese_text: Etu dikhi kene, Herod raja kosom khaise tai ki mangibo etu sob taike dibo.

english_text: She, being prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”
nagamese_text: Herodias pora tai laga chukri ke age pora ki mangibo etu sob sikhai dise, etu chukri Herod ke koise, “Moike ekta thali te Baptizma diya John laga matha dibi.”

english_text: The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths and of those who sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,
nagamese_text: Herod etu huni kene bisi mon dukh hoise, kintu tai sob manu age te kosom kha nimite, tai ki mangise etu taike di dibole hukum di dise.

english_text: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
nagamese_text: Herod pora manu ke pathaise aru John laga matha kati dise.

english_text: His head was brought on a platter and given to the young lady; and she brought it to her mother.
nagamese_text: Aru John laga matha thali te rakhi kene etu chukri ke dise kun jai kene tai laga ama ke dise.

english_text: His disciples came, took the body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete John laga chela khan ahi kene tai laga gaw loi jaise aru mati bhitor te hali dise. Aru taikhan jai kene ki hoise etu sob Jisu ke koi dise.

english_text: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place apart. When the multitudes heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu etu khobor hunise, tai utu jaga pora ulaikena naw te kunbi nathaka jagate Tai ekla jai jaise. Jitia manu khan etu huni paise, taikhan laga sheher chari kene theng pora Jisu laga piche kori jaise.

english_text: Jesus went out, and he saw a great multitude. He had compassion on them and healed their sick.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu manu laga dangor bhir thaka dikhise. Taikhan ke bisi morom lagise aru bemar khan ke bhal korise.

english_text: When evening had come, his disciples came to him, saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.”
nagamese_text: Jitia saam hobole shuru hoise, Tai laga chela khan Taike koi, “Etu jagate kunbi nathake aru eku bhi napai, aru ene bhi deri hoise. Manu khan ke jabole dibi, titia taikhan nijor bosti te jai kene kha luwa khabole kini lobo.”

english_text: But Jesus said to them, “They don’t need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Taikhan najaile bhi hobo. Taikhan ke kiba khabole dibi.”

english_text: They told him, “We only have here five loaves and two fish.”
nagamese_text: Tai laga chela khan Taike koise, “Amikhan logote eku bhi nai, khali pansta roti aru duita maas he ase.”

english_text: He said, “Bring them here to me.”
nagamese_text: Jisu koise, “Eitu khan loi kene anibi.”

english_text: He commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass; and he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke and gave the loaves to the disciples; and the disciples gave to the multitudes.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu manu khan ke olop ghas thaka jagate bohi bole koise. Tai etu pansta roti aru duita maas loise, aru sorgo phale saikene, asirbad dise aru etu roti bhangai kene Tai laga chela khan ke dise, aru taikhan pora sob manu khan ke bhag kori dise.

english_text: They all ate and were filled. They took up twelve baskets full of that which remained left over from the broken pieces.
nagamese_text: Aru sob pet bhorta khaise. Pichete chela khan jai kene bachi kene thaka roti baroh ta tukri te joma korise.

english_text: Those who ate were about five thousand men, in addition to women and children.
nagamese_text: Ta te 5,000 manu nisena mota manu khan khaise, bacha aru maiki khan ke chari kene.

english_text: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.
nagamese_text: Aru etu huwa loge-loge, Tai laga chela khan ke naw bhitor te bohibo dise aru taikhan ke nodi laga dusra phale pathai dise. Aru Jisu to taikhan logot najai kene manu khan ke nijor ghor te jai jabole koise.

english_text: After he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into the mountain by himself to pray. When evening had come, he was there alone.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai sob manu khan ke pathai dise, Tai ekla pahar uporte jaise aru prathana korise. Tai saam tak etu jagate ekla thakise.

english_text: But the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
nagamese_text: Kintu utu somoite hawa bisi mara nimite naw to nodi laga majote punchi jaise, kele koile etu hawa to ulta phale mari thakise.

english_text: In the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
nagamese_text: Ekdum phojurte Jisu nodi uporte berai kene taikhan logote ahise.

english_text: When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, “It’s a ghost!” and they cried out for fear.
nagamese_text: Kitia Tai laga chela khan Taike pani uporte bera dikhise, taikhan bisi bhoi khai kene koise, “Etu ekjon bhoot ase,” aru bisi bhoi pora hala korise.

english_text: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Mon dangor koribi, etu Moi ase! Bhoi na koribi.”

english_text: Peter answered him and said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”
nagamese_text: Peter pora Jisu ke jowab dise aru koise, “Probhu, jodi etu Apuni ase, titia amike pani upor pora Apuni logot ahibole hukum dibi.”

english_text: He said, “Come!” Peter stepped down from the boat and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.
nagamese_text: Jisu koise, “Ahibi.” Titia Peter naw pora uthise aru Jisu usorte pani uporte berai kene jaise.

english_text: But when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Peter pora dangor hawa mara dikhise, tai bhoi khai jaise. Jitia tai dubi bole shuru hoise, tai hala kori kene koise, “Probhu, amike bacha bhi!”

english_text: Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
nagamese_text: Loge-loge te Jisu Tai laga hath sida korise, aru Peter ke dhuri loise, aru taike koise, “Tumi komti biswas manu, tumi kele chinta korise?”

english_text: When they got up into the boat, the wind ceased.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu aru Peter naw bhitor te jaise, aru hawa mara to rukhi jaise.

english_text: Those who were in the boat came and worshiped him, saying, “You are truly the Son of God!”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete naw bhitor te chela khan Jisu ke aradhana korise, eneka koi kene, “Hosa pora bhi Apuni to Isor laga Putro ase.”

english_text: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan nodi paar kori loise, taikhan Gennesaret town koi kene ekta jagate ahise.

english_text: When the people of that place recognized him, they sent into all that surrounding region and brought to him all who were sick;
nagamese_text: Jitia ta te laga manu khan Jisu ke chini loise, taikhan usorte thaka sob manu khan ke khobor kori dise, aru sob bemar manu khan ke Jisu logot loi anise.

english_text: and they begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched it were made whole.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu laga kapra chubo nimite bhik mangi kene Taike hudise, aru jiman manu Taike chuise, taikhan sob bhal hoi jaise.

english_text: Then Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Pharisee aru niyom likha manu khan Jerusalem pora Jisu usorte ahise. Taikhan koise,

english_text: “Why do your disciples disobey the tradition of the elders? For they don’t wash their hands when they eat bread.”
nagamese_text: “Kile Apuni laga chela khan bura khan banai diya niyom khan bhangai thake? Kile taikhan hath nadholai kene roti khai.”

english_text: He answered them, “Why do you also disobey the commandment of God because of your tradition?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke jowab dikene koise, “Tinehoile kele tumikhan bhi nijor laga niyom nimite Isor laga niyom khan bhangai?

english_text: For God commanded, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Isor pora hukum dise, eneka koise, ‘Nijor laga baba aru ama ke sonman dibi,’ aru ‘Jun tai nijor baba aru ama laga biya kotha koi, tai hosa pora bhi moribo.’

english_text: But you say, ‘Whoever may tell his father or his mother, “Whatever help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan koi, ‘Jun khan nijor baba nohoile bhi ama ke koi, “Ki modot apnikhan moi pora pabole ase eitu khan etiya pora Isor ke daan dibo,’”

english_text: he shall not honor his father or mother.’ You have made the commandment of God void because of your tradition.
nagamese_text: utu manu to tai laga baba ke sonman nadile bhi hobo. Eneka kori kene tumikhan Isor laga kotha ke hisab nathaka kori dise, tumikhan laga niyom manibo nimite.

english_text: You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
nagamese_text: Dhungi khan! Isaiah pora thik koise, jitia tumikhan nimite tai bhabobani korise,

english_text: ‘These people draw near to me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
nagamese_text: ‘Etu manu khan Moike mukh pora he sonman kore, Kintu taikhan laga mon to Moi pora bisi dur te ase.

english_text: And they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrine rules made by men.’”
nagamese_text: Taikhan Moike aradhana kora to misa-misi ase, Kile mane manu pora bana niyom khan taikhan nijor laga niyom nisena sikhai thake.’”

english_text: He summoned the multitude, and said to them, “Hear, and understand.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu pora joma hoi kene thaka manu khan ke mati kene koise, “Huni bhi aru bujhi bhi-

english_text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”
nagamese_text: Ki saman manu laga mukh te ghuse etu pora manu ke letera nakore. Kintu, ki to mukh pora bahar te ulai, etu pora he manu ke letera kori diye.”

english_text: Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this saying?”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete chela khan ahi kene Jisu ke koise, “Apuni jane na nai etu Pharisee khan jitia Apuni laga kotha hunise, taikhan khushi panai koi kene?”

english_text: But he answered, “Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be uprooted.
nagamese_text: Jisu pora taikhan ke koise, “Sob ghas juntu sorgote thaka Ami laga Baba pora rupa nai, eitu khan sobke mati bhitor pora tani kene phelai dibo.”

english_text: Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke ekla chari bhi, taikhan nijor andha koi kene andha manu ke rasta dikhai ase. Jitia ekta andha manu pora dusra andha manu ke rasta dikhai, tai duijon bhi nala te giri bo.”

english_text: Peter answered him, “Explain the parable to us.”
nagamese_text: Peter jowab dikene Jisu ke koise, “Etu dristanto laga motlob to bujhai dibi.”

english_text: So Jesus said, “Do you also still not understand?
nagamese_text: Jisu koise, “Tumi etiya tak nabuji kene ase?

english_text: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the belly and then out of the body?
nagamese_text: Tumi najane, ki jinis mukh bhitor pora ghusi kene pet te jai, etu he pichete latrine kori kene bahar ulai koi kene?

english_text: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and they defile the man.
nagamese_text: Kintu ji kotha khan mukh pora ulai eitu khan mon pora ulai. Eitu khan pora he manu ke letera kore.

english_text: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile mon pora he biya bhabona, manu morai diya, bebichari, chor kora, misa gawahi, aru hinsa kora eitu khan ulai.

english_text: These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands doesn’t defile the man.”
nagamese_text: Eitu khan pora he manu khan ke letera kore. Kintu hath nadholai kene kha pora manu ke letera nakore.”

english_text: Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu ta te pora ulai jaise, aru Tyre aru Sidon sheher phale jaise.

english_text: Behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely possessed by a demon!”
nagamese_text: Sabi, ta te ekjon Canaan laga mahila utu jaga pora ulaikene ahise. Tai hala kori kene koise, “Moi uporte daya koribi, Probhu, David laga Putro! Moi laga chukri gaw bhitor te bisi biya bhoot pora bandhi kene ase.”

english_text: But he answered her not a word. His disciples came and begged him, saying, “Send her away; for she cries after us.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike ekta jowab bhi diya nai. Tai laga chela khan ahi kene Taike anurodh koise, “Etu mahila ke khedai dibi, kele koile tai amikhan phale hala kori ase.”

english_text: But he answered, “I wasn’t sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu jowab dikene koise, “Kunba nimite moike patha nohoi, kintu Israel laga ghor laga harai ja mer khan nimite ase.”

english_text: But she came and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
nagamese_text: Kintu etu mahila ahise aru athukari kene Tai age te matha niche kori kene koise, “Probhu, amike modot koribi.”

english_text: But he answered, “It is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
nagamese_text: Tai jowab dikene koise, “Bacha khan laga roti loi kene kutta khan ke phelai kene diya to thik nohoi.”

english_text: But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”
nagamese_text: Tai koise, “Hoi, Probhu, kintu kutta bacha khan bhi tai malik laga thali pora tukra gira khan khai.”

english_text: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu etu mahila ke koise, “Maiki, tumi laga biswas to bisi dangor ase; tumi laga ki khushi ase thik eneka he hobo dibi.” Aru tai laga chukri utu somoite bhal hoi jaise.

english_text: Jesus departed from there and came near to the sea of Galilee; and he went up on the mountain and sat there.
nagamese_text: Jisu utu jaga ke chari kene Galilee Nodi usorte jaise. Etu pichete Tai pahar uporte jaise aru ta te bohise.

english_text: Great multitudes came to him, having with them the lame, blind, mute, maimed, and many others, and they put them down at his feet. He healed them,
nagamese_text: Bisi manu joma koi kene Tai usorte ahise. Taikhan logote lengra, andha, juthor rugi bemar thaka, aru gunga khan, aru kisim bemar thaka manu khan ke loi kene ahise. Taikhan Jisu laga theng usorte anise aru Jisu pora taikhan ke bhal kori dise.

english_text: so that the multitude wondered when they saw the mute speaking, the injured healed, the lame walking, and the blind seeing—and they glorified the God of Israel.
nagamese_text: Titia manu khan sob asurit hoise jitia taikhan kotha koribo napara khan kotha korise, lengera khan beraise, aru andha khan dikhi bole paise. Taikhan sob Israel laga Isor ke mohima dise.

english_text: Jesus summoned his disciples and said, “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have continued with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away fasting, or they might faint on the way.”
nagamese_text: Tai laga chela khan ke mati kene Jisu koise, “Etu manu khan nimite moi laga monte morom ase, kele koile taikhan tin din pora moi logote thakise aru taikhan ke khila bole eku bhi nai. Moi taikhan ke nakhilai kene pathai dibole mon nai, nohoile matha ghuri kene giri jabo pare.”

english_text: The disciples said to him, “Where could we get so many loaves in a deserted place as to satisfy so great a multitude?”
nagamese_text: Tai laga chela khan Taike koise, “Etu nisena khali jagate kote pora amikhan iman bisi roti bisari kene manu khan ke khila bo?”

english_text: Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan logote kiman roti ase?” Taikhan koise, “Sat-ta, aru chutu maas khan olop ase.”

english_text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground;
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu manu khan ke matite bohibi koise.

english_text: and he took the seven loaves and the fish. He gave thanks and broke them, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.
nagamese_text: Tai sat-ta roti aru maas ke loise, aru dhanyavad diya pichete, roti bhangai kene chela khan ke dise. Aru chela khan pora manu khan ke bhag kori dise.

english_text: They all ate and were filled. They took up seven baskets full of the broken pieces that were left over.
nagamese_text: Sob khaise aru pet bhorta hoise. Aru taikhan bacha roti sob joma korise aru sat-ta tukri bhorta hoise.

english_text: Those who ate were four thousand men, in addition to women and children.
nagamese_text: Sob milaikena char hajar mota khan thakise, maiki aru bacha khan ke chari kene.

english_text: Then he sent away the multitudes, got into the boat, and came into the borders of Magdala.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete sobke nijor ghor te pathai dise aru Jisu ekta naw te uthi kene Magadan te jaise.

english_text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete, kunba Pharisee aru Sadducee khan ahi kene Jisu ke porikha koribo nimite Taike akas pora kiba ekta asurit kaam kori kene taikhan ke dikhai dibi koise.

english_text: But he answered them, “When it is evening, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise, aru koise, “Jitia saam hoi, tumikhan koi, din to bhal hobo, kele koile akas to lal ase.

english_text: In the morning, ‘It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you can’t discern the signs of the times!
nagamese_text: Aru phojurte, aji din biya hobole ase, kele koile akas to lal ase aru niche hoi ase. Tumikhan akas te saikene din kobo pare, kintu tumikhan bhal biya din laga somoi saikene kobo napare?

english_text: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and there will be no sign given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” He left them and departed.
nagamese_text: “Biya aru biswas nathaka yug laga manu khan he chihna khan sabole bisare, kintu chihna khan dikhai nadibo khali Jonah laga chihna he pabo.” Etu pichete Jisu ta te pora ulai jai.

english_text: The disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to take bread.
nagamese_text: Jitia chela khan nodi paar kori kene dusra phale punchi jaise, taikhan roti lobole pahorise.

english_text: Jesus said to them, “Take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Sai thakibi aru Pharisee aru Sadducee khan laga khomir pora hoshiar hoi jabi.”

english_text: They reasoned among themselves, saying, “We brought no bread.”
nagamese_text: Titia chela khan nijor majote kotha kori thakise, eneka koi kene, “Etu eneka hoise kele koile amikhan roti lobole pahorise.”

english_text: Jesus, perceiving it, said, “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have brought no bread?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan laga bhabona jani thakise aru koise, “Tumi biswas komti thaka khan, kele tumikhan nijor majote roti pahora nimite ase koi kene kotha kori ase?

english_text: Don’t you yet perceive or remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up,
nagamese_text: Tumikhan etiya bhi buja nai nohoile bhi yaad nai kineka Moi pansta roti 5,000 manu nimite dise, aru kiman ta tukri bachi kene joma korise?

english_text: or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
nagamese_text: Nohoile bhi sat-ta roti 4,000 manu nimite dise, aru kiman ta tukri bachi kene joma korise?

english_text: How is it that you don’t perceive that I didn’t speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
nagamese_text: Kineka kori kene tumikhan buja nai Moi roti laga kotha kowa nohoi koi kene? Pharisee aru Sadducee laga khomir pora hoshiar thakibi.”

english_text: Then they understood that he didn’t tell them to beware of the yeast of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete taikhan bujhi jaise Jisu to roti te khomir thaka pora hoshiar hoija bhi kowa nohoi, kintu Pharisee aru Sadducee khan laga kotha sikhai diya pora hoshiar thakibi koi thakisele.

english_text: Now when Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete jitia Jisu Caesarea Philippi town usorte ahise, Jisu Tai laga chela khan ke hudise, “Manu khan pora Manu laga Putro ke kun koi kene mate?”

english_text: They said, “Some say John the Baptizer, some, Elijah, and others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan koise, “Kunba koi John Baptizma diya jon, kunba, Elijah, aru kunba Jeremiah, aru ekjon bhabobadi.”

english_text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Kintu tumikhan Moi kun ase koi kene bhabe?”

english_text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
nagamese_text: Simon Peter pora jowab dikene koise, “Apuni to Khrista ase, jinda Isor laga Putro.”

english_text: Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.
nagamese_text: Jisu taike jowab dikene koise, “Tumi asis paise, Simon Bar Jonah, kele koile manu pora tumike dikhai diya nohoi, kintu Moi laga Baba jun sorgote ase Tai pora he dikhai dise.

english_text: I also tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
nagamese_text: Moi etu bhi tumike koi ase, tumi Peter ase, aru etu pathor uporte Moi laga girja bonabo. Aru Hades laga hokti pora etu girja ke eku koribo na paribo.

english_text: I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumike sorgo rajyo laga chabi khan dibo. Tumi junke prithibi te bandhi bo, sorgote bhi etu bandhi bo, aru juntu prithibi te chari bo, sorgote bhi etu chari dibo.”

english_text: Then he commanded the disciples that they should tell no one that he was Jesus the Christ.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Tai chela khan ke hukum dise kunke bhi Tai to Khrista ase nokobi koi kene.

english_text: From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.
nagamese_text: Utu somoi pora loi kene, Jisu Tai laga chela khan ke Tai Jerusalem te jabo lagibo, aru ta te bura manu khan, aru mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom likha khan pora Taike bisi dukh dibo aru morai dibo, aru tin din pichete mora pora jee uthibo laga kotha khan koi diya shuru hoise.

english_text: Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying, “Far be it from you, Lord! This will never be done to you.”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Peter pora Jisu ke kinar te loi jaise aru gali dibole shuru hoise, eneka koi kene, “Eitu khan Apuni pora dur hobo dibi, Probhu; eitu khan Apuni ke hobole nadibi.”

english_text: But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu ghuri kene Peter ke koise, “Moi laga pichete jabi, Saitan! Tumi Ami laga rasta bondh kori ase, kele koile tumi Isor laga kaam nimite hisab nakore, kintu manu khan laga kaam ke hisab kore.”

english_text: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu tai laga chela khan ke koise, “Jun Ami laga piche koribo mon ase, tai nijorke chari bo lagibo, nijor laga Cross lobi, aru Moi laga piche koribi.

english_text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun manu tai nijor jibon to bacha bole kore tai harai dibo, aru jun manu Ami nimite nijor jibon to harai dibo tai pabo.

english_text: For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ekjon manu laga ki labh ase jitia tai sob duniya to pai jai, kintu nijor jibon to harai diye? Ekjon manu jibon pabo nimite tai ki daam dibo paribo?

english_text: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will give to everyone according to his deeds.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Manu laga Putro to Tai laga Baba laga mohima pora sorgodoth khan logote wapas ahibo. Etu pichete Tai sob manu ke taikhan laga kaam hisab te inam dibo.

english_text: Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Moi hosa pora apnikhan ke koise, tumikhan majote kunba yate khara ase jun namora age te Manu laga Putro ke Tai laga rajyo loi kene akas te ahi thaka dikhibo.”

english_text: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.
nagamese_text: Choi din pichete Jisu tai logote Peter, James aru tai laga bhai John ke loise, aru taikhan nijor pora ekta untcha pahar uporte jaise.

english_text: He was changed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu nijorke taikhan age te alag ekjon kori kene dikhaise. Tai laga chehera suryo nisena ujala dikhaise, aru Tai laga kapra khan puhor nisena boga hoi jaise.

english_text: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.
nagamese_text: Sabi, ta te taikhan logote Moses aru Elijah ulaikene Jisu logote kotha kori thakise.

english_text: Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
nagamese_text: Peter jowab dikene Jisu ke koise, “Probhu, amikhan yate thaka to bhal ase naki. Apuni itcha ase koile, Moi etu jagate aram kori bole chaat bonabo- ekta Apuni nimite, aru ekta Moses nimite, aru ekta Elijah nimite.”

english_text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”
