english_text: They braided a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
nagamese_text: Aru kata laga mukut bonaikena Tai laga matha te lagai dise aru dyna hathte ekta lathi dhori bole dise.

english_text: They spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu usorte athukari loise aru taike sorom khilai dise, aru matha te mari dikene eneka koise, “Hey Yehudi laga Raja!”

english_text: When they had mocked him, they took the robe off him, and put his clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Jisu ke sorom khilai dise, taikhan kapra ulai loise aru tai laga nijor kapra aru lagai dise, aru Cross te mari dibole nimite loi jaise.

english_text: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan bahar te ulai ahise, ekjon Cyrene sheher pora Simon koi kene paise, junke taikhan Cross bukhi bole dise.

english_text: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
nagamese_text: Taikhan Golgotha koi kene ekta jagate ahise, etu motlob to “Matha Laga Hardi Jaga.”

english_text: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu ke dawai milai kene thaka draikha ros khabole dise. Kintu jitia Tai etu jiba te chati saise, Tai etu khabo para nai.

english_text: When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Jisu ke Cross te mari dise, taikhan Jisu laga kapra khan chithi khili kene bhag kori loise,

english_text: and they sat and watched him there.
nagamese_text: aru taikhan ta te bohi kene Jisu ke rukhi thakise.

english_text: They set up over his head the accusation against him written, “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu laga matha uporte taikhan eneka likhi dise, “Etu Jisu ase, Yehudi jati laga Raja.”

english_text: Then there were two robbers crucified with him, one on his right hand and one on the left.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete utu duita chor ke Jisu logote Cross te mari dise, ekjon Tai laga dyna phale aru ekjon ke Tai laga baya phale.

english_text: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads
nagamese_text: Jun manu etu paar kori kene jai taikhan Jisu ke dikhi kene sorom khilai diye aru taikhan laga matha hilai kene hath milai,

english_text: and saying, “You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
nagamese_text: aru eneka koi kene, “Tumi jun Isor laga mondoli ke bhangai kene tin din pichete bonai dibo thakise, nijorke bachabi! Jodi Tumi Isor laga Putro ase koile, Cross pora namikene ahibi!”

english_text: Likewise the chief priests also mocking with the scribes, the Pharisees, and the elders, said,
nagamese_text: Etu nisena moha purohit khan bhi Jisu ke sorom khilai dise, aru taikhan logote niyom jana manu aru cholawta khan bhi thakise, aru koise,

english_text: “He saved others, but he can’t save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
nagamese_text: “Tai dusra manu khan ke bachai dise, kintu Nijorke bacha bole para nai. Tai Israel desh laga Raja ase. Taike Cross pora namikene ahibo dibi, aru etu pichete amikhan Taike biswas koribo.

english_text: He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
nagamese_text: Tai Isor ke biswas kore, Isor ke Taike bacha bole dibi etiya, jodi Isor Taike lage koile. Kile mane Tai koise, ‘Moi Isor laga Putro ase.’”

english_text: The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena chor duita jun Jisu logote Cross te mari dise, tai bhi Jisu ke sorom khilai diya laga kotha koise.

english_text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia choi ghanta hoise pura desh te andhera ahi jaise aru pura nou ghanta nohua tak andhera thakise.

english_text: About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
nagamese_text: Jitia tin baji hoise, Jisu ekdom jor pora eneka koi kene kandise, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” Etu mane, “Ami laga Isor, Ami laga Isor, Apuni kele Moike chari dise?”

english_text: Some of them who stood there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
nagamese_text: Jitia ta te khara kori thaka manu khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan koise, “Tai Elijah ke mati ase.”

english_text: Immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
nagamese_text: Titia ekjon manu polai jai kene norom kapra te tenga ros pani pora bhorta hoi kene thaka loi kene anise, aru ekta lamba ghar laga khuri te lagase, aru taike dikene Jisu ke khila bole dise.

english_text: The rest said, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
nagamese_text: Ta te thaka manu khan pora koise, “Taike ekla chari di bhi. Moi khan sabo jodi Elijah ahikena Taike bachai na nai.”

english_text: Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu aru bhi hala kori kene jor pora kandise aru Tai laga atma ke chari dise.

english_text: Behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom. The earth quaked and the rocks were split.
nagamese_text: Etu somoite, mondoli laga purdah upor pora loi kene niche tak dui bhag hoi kene phatise, aru matise, aru pathor khan bhi bhangi kene adha hoi jaise.

english_text: The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised;
nagamese_text: Aru Isor laga manu kunkhan ghumai jaise, taikhan laga kobor khuli jaise aru taikhan uthijaise.

english_text: and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu jinda huwa pichete kobor pora ulaikene ahise, pobitro sheher Jerusalem te ghusi se, aru bisi manu ke dikhai dise.

english_text: Now the centurion and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were done, were terrified, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God!”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia sipahi aru kun tai logote thaki kene Jisu ke sai thakise, mati hila aru ki hoise etu dikhise, taikhan bisi bhoi lagise aru koise, “Hosa pora etu manu to Isor laga Putro thakise.”

english_text: Many women were there watching from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him.
nagamese_text: Aru bisi maiki khan jun Jisu laga pichete Galilee pora berai thakisele taikhan ta te thakise aru dur pora Jisu ke sai thakise.

english_text: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
nagamese_text: Taikhan majote Mary Magdalene, Joseph aru James laga ama Mary, aru Zebedee laga chokra khan laga ama bhi thakise.

english_text: When evening had come, a rich man from Arimathaea named Joseph, who himself was also Jesus’ disciple, came.
nagamese_text: Jitia saam hoise, ekjon dhuni manu Joseph koi kene Arimathea bosti pora ahise, tai bhi Jisu laga chela thakisele.

english_text: This man went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given up.
nagamese_text: Tai Pilate usorte jai kene Jisu laga gaw to mangise. Etu pichete Pilate pora hukum dikene taike dise.

english_text: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
nagamese_text: Aru Joseph pora Jisu laga gaw to loise, aru mihin kapra pora bandhi dise.

english_text: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock. Then he rolled a large stone against the door of the tomb, and departed.
nagamese_text: Aru tai nijor laga notun kobor te rakhidise, juntu tai pathor kati kene rakhi thakisele. Etu pichete tai ekta dangor chaka nisena pathor pora kobor to bondh kori dise aru tai jai jaise.

english_text: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
nagamese_text: Mary Magdalene aru dusra Mary bhi ta te thakise, kobor laga utu phale bohi thakise.

english_text: Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
nagamese_text: Dusra din, juntu din to Taiyar Kora din pichete thakise, maha purohit khan aru Pharisee khan eke logote Pilate usorte joma hoi kene thakise.

english_text: saying, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise again.’
nagamese_text: Taikhan koise, “Sahab, amikhan yaad ase jitia utu thogai diya manu jinda thaka somoite, tai koise, ‘Tin din pichete moi jinda hobo.’

english_text: Command therefore that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest perhaps his disciples come at night and steal him away, and tell the people, ‘He is risen from the dead;’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
nagamese_text: Etu karone hukum dibi, tin din tak etu kobor to bhal kori kene pehera dibole nimite, nohoile Tai laga chela khan ahikena chor kori loijabo, aru manu khan ke kobo, ‘Tai mora pora jinda hoi jaise.’ Aru poila pora bhi etiya laga kotha to bisi hoi jabo.”

english_text: Pilate said to them, “You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you can.”
nagamese_text: Pilate taikhan ke koise, “Ekjon sipahi ke lobi. Jabi aru tumi kineka pora pehera lagabo paribo, etu nisena koribi.”

english_text: So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan jai kene kobor ke bhal pora pehera dise, pathor te mohor marikena sipahi khan ke rukhibo dise.

english_text: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
nagamese_text: Etiya Bisram din khotom hobole hoise, jitia hapta laga poila din ulai thakise, Mary Magdalene aru dusra Mary kobor sabole ahise.

english_text: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky and came and rolled away the stone from the door and sat on it.
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, ta te bisi dangor mati hili se, kele koile Probhu laga ekjon sorgodoth sorgo pora nichete namise, aru pathor ke ghurai kene hatai dise, aru etu uporte bohi jaise.

english_text: His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
nagamese_text: Tai laga chehera to bhijili nisena, aru tai laga kapra to borop nisena boga thakise.

english_text: For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
nagamese_text: Kobor rukhi thaka sipahi khan dikhi kene bhoi pora hili jaise aru taikhan mora manu nisena hoi jaise.

english_text: The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
nagamese_text: Kintu utu sorgodoth kotha kori kene maiki khan ke koise, “Bhoi na koribi, kele koile moi jani ase tumikhan Jisu ke bisari bole ahise, junke Cross te mari disele.

english_text: He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
nagamese_text: Tai yate nai, kintu jinda hoise, jineka Tai pora koise. Ahi kene sabi juntu jagate Taike rakhi sele.

english_text: Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
nagamese_text: Joldi jabi aru chela khan ke kobi, ‘Tai to mora pora jinda hoise. Sabi, Tai Galilee te tumikhan age jai ase. Ta te tumikhan Taike dikhibo.’ Sabi, Moi tumikhan ke koi dise.”

english_text: They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.
nagamese_text: Mahila khan dangor bhoi aru khushi pora kobor ke chari kene joldi jaise, aru chela khan ke kobole nimite polaikene jaise.

english_text: As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Rejoice!” They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
nagamese_text: Sabi, Jisu taikhan ke lok paise, eneka koi kene, “Salam! Apuni logote shanti thakibi!” Utu mahila khan ahikena Tai laga theng dhuri kene Taike aradhana korise.

english_text: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Bhoi nakuribi. Jabi jai kene Moi laga bhai-kokai khan ke Galilee te jabole kobi. Ta te taikhan Moike dikhibo.”

english_text: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
nagamese_text: Jitia mahila khan jai thakise, titia, kunba sipahi khan sheher te jaise aru moha purohitkhan ke ki hoise sob koi dise.

english_text: When they were assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan bura khan ke lok korise aru taikhan ke bhi ki hoise etu koi dise, aru taikhan sipahi khan ke bisi poisa dise,

english_text: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we slept.
nagamese_text: aru koise, “Eneka kobi, ‘Tai laga chela khan rati te ahikena Tai laga gaw chor korise, jitia amikhan ghumai thakise.’

english_text: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
nagamese_text: Jodi etu khobor Governor tak punchi jai, amikhan tai logote kotha koribo aru tumikhan uporte digdar ahibo nadibo.”

english_text: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
nagamese_text: Titia sipahi khan poisa loise aru taikhan pora ki koise etu he koise. Etu laga kotha bisi Yehudi manu khan pora hunise aru aji tak etu kotha koi thake.

english_text: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
nagamese_text: Kintu egaroh jon chela Galilee te jaise, ekta pahar te jun to Jisu pora ahibole koise.

english_text: When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Jisu ke dikhise, taikhan Taike aradhana korise, kintu kunba taikhan majote bhabona korise.

english_text: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan usorte ahise aru kotha korise aru koise, “Sob sorgo aru prithibi laga adhikar Moike dise.

english_text: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
nagamese_text: Etu nimite jabi aru sob desh te Moi laga chela bonabi. Taikhan ke Baba, Putro aru Pobitro Atma laga naam pora baptizma dibi.

english_text: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke Moi ki hukum dise eitu khan sikhai dibi. Etu janibi, Moi tumikhan logote hodai ase, etu jamana laga hekh din tak.”

english_text: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
nagamese_text: Isor laga Putro, Jisu Khrista laga susamachar eneka shuru huwa ase,

english_text: As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you:
nagamese_text: Jineka Isaiah bhabobadi pora likhise, “Sabi, tumikhan laga age te Moi khobor bukha manu ke pathai ase, Etu ekjon kun tumikhan nimite rasta taiyar kori dibo.

english_text: the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’”
nagamese_text: Ekjon jongol te jor awaj pora mati ase, ‘Probhu nimite rasta to bonai lobi; Aru Tai laga rasta ke sidha rakhi bhi.’”

english_text: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
nagamese_text: Jongol te John ulai ahise aru baptizma dikene mon ghurabole aru paap pora khyama pabo nimite prochar korise.

english_text: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
nagamese_text: Judea laga pura desh aru Jerusalem sheher laga manu khan tai logote jaise. Taikhan ke Jordan Nodi te loi jaise aru taikhan paap shikar kora pichete taikhan ke baptizma dise.

english_text: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
nagamese_text: John laga kapra to uth laga chamra pora bona kapra thakise aru chamra laga peti tai laga komor te bandi kene thakise, aru tai phoring aru jongol mou laga pani khai thakise.

english_text: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
nagamese_text: Tai eneka prochar korise, “Ekjon ahibole ase aru Tai moi pora bhi bisi takot ase, aru moi niche jhukikena Tai laga juta khuli dibole bhi layak nai.

english_text: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke pani pora baptizma di ase, kintu Tai tumikhan ke Pobitro Atma pora baptizma dibo.”

english_text: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
nagamese_text: Etiya eneka hoise olop din pichete Jisu Nazareth town pora Galilee laga jagate ahise, aru John pora Taike baptizma dise.

english_text: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
nagamese_text: Aru loge-loge, jitia Jisu pani pora ulai ahise, sorgo khuli kene Isor laga Atma ekta kopu chiriya nisena Tai uporte ahi thaka tai dikhise.

english_text: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
nagamese_text: Titia sorgo pora ekta awaj ahise, “Tumi Moi laga morom laga Putro ase, Moi Tumi uporte bisi khushi ase.”

english_text: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te, Atma pora Taike jongol te jai jabole nimite koise.

english_text: He was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu jongol te chalis din tak thakise, aru Taike Saitan pora porikha korise. Etu somoite Tai jongol laga janwar khan logote thakise, aru sorgodoth khan Taike sewa kori thakise.

english_text: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,
nagamese_text: John ke dhuri loija pichete, Jisu Galilee laga jagate ahi kene Isor laga susamachar prochar korise.

english_text: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
nagamese_text: Jisu prochar, “Etu homoi pura hoise, aru Isor laga rajyo usor hoise. Mon ghura bhi aru susamachar te biswas koribi.

english_text: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai Galilee Nodi laga kinar te berai thakise, Tai Simon aru tai laga bhai Andrew ke nodi te jal phelai thaka dikhise, kelemane taikhan maas dhora manu asele.

english_text: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Ahibi, Moi laga pichete, aru Moi tumikhan ke manu dhori bole bonai dibo.”

english_text: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te taikhan sob chari kene Jisu laga pichete jaise.

english_text: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu olop age te jaise, titia Tai James, aru tai laga bhai John ke dikhise. Tai duijon to Zebedee laga chokra thakise, taikhan maas dhura jal bonai thakise.

english_text: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
nagamese_text: Aru titia, Jisu taikhan ke matise, taikhan nijor baba aru kaam kora noukar khan ke naw te chari kene Tai laga pichete jaise.

english_text: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu aru chela khan Capernaum town te ahise, aru Bisram laga dinte, Jisu mondoli te jai kene sikhaise.

english_text: They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu pora sikhai diya kotha huni kene asurit hoise, kelemane Tai niyom jani kene thaka manu nisena nohoi kene adhikar thaka ekjon nisena sikhai thakise.

english_text: Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te, ekjon dusto atma pora dhori kene thaka mondoli te thakise, aru tai hala kori kene kandise,

english_text: saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
nagamese_text: Aru koise, “Apuni moi khan logote ki kaam ase, Nazareth laga Jisu? Apuni moi khan ke khotom kori bole ahise naki? Moi jane Apuni Isor laga samachar koi dibole aha Pobitro Ekjon ase!”

english_text: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike gali dikene koise, “Chup thakibi, aru tai pora ulai jabi!”

english_text: The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.
nagamese_text: Titia dusto atma taike nichete phelai dise aru jor pora hala kori kene kandise aru gaw pora ulai jaise.

english_text: They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? What can this new doctrine be? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
nagamese_text: Titia sob manu khan etu dikhi kene asurit hoise, aru ekjon-ekjon ke hudise, aru koise, “Etu ki ase? Ekta notun adhikar pora sikhai diya! Tai dusto atma ke bhi hukum diye aru taikhan Tai laga kotha mane!”

english_text: The report of him went out immediately into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.
nagamese_text: Aru etu laga khobor pura Galilee laga jagate joldi punchi jaise.

english_text: Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
nagamese_text: Aru etu pichete, Jisu aru Tai laga chela khan mondoli pora ulaikene ahi juwa pichete, taikhan Simon aru Andrew laga ghor te ahise, aru taikhan logote James aru John bhi thakise.

english_text: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te Simon maiki laga ama bukhar pora ghumai thakise, aru taikhan joldi pora jai kene etu Jisu ke koi dise.

english_text: He came and took her by the hand and raised her up. The fever left her immediately, and she served them.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu ahise, aru tai laga hath dhorise, aru taike uthai dise. Titia bukhar tai pora jai jaise, aru tai uthikena taikhan ke sewa korise.

english_text: At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick and those who were possessed by demons.
nagamese_text: Jitia saam hoise, aru suryo nami jaise, taikhan bemar thaka manu aru bhoot pora dhori kene thaka sob Tai usorte loi anise.

english_text: All the city was gathered together at the door.
nagamese_text: Aru Capernaum sheher te thaka sob manu khan ahikena dorja usorte joma hoise.

english_text: He healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai alag kisim laga bemar thaka manu khan ke bhal korise, aru bhoot khan pora dhori kene thaka atma khan khedai dise, kintu Tai etu bhoot khan ke kotha kobole diya nai kelemane taikhan jani thakise Tai kun ase.

english_text: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
nagamese_text: Aru phojur nohua age te Tai joldi uthise, aru Tai ekla kun bhi nathaka jagate jai kene ta te prathana kori thakise.

english_text: Simon and those who were with him searched for him.
nagamese_text: Titia Simon aru tai logote thaka khan Taike bisari ahise.

english_text: They found him and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Taike lok paise, taikhan koise, “Sob manu Apuni ke bisari ase.”

english_text: He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai taikhan ke koise, “Ahibi amikhan dusra nogor te jai jabo, ta te bhi Moi prochar koribo lagi ase.” Kelemane Moi etu karone ahise.

english_text: He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai Galilee sob jagah te jai kene taikhan laga mondoli te prochar korise aru bhoot khan ke khedai thakise.

english_text: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
nagamese_text: Titia kusto-rugi bemar thaka ekjon Tai logote ahi kene athukari se aru anurodh kori kene Taike koise, “Jodi Apuni itcha hoile, moike sapha koribo pare.”

english_text: Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike bisi morom lagise. Aru Tai laga hath uthaise, aru taike chuikena eneka koise, “Ami itcha ase. Sapha hoi jabi.”

english_text: When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him and he was made clean.
nagamese_text: Aru loge-loge te kusto-rugi bemar taike chari jaise, aru tai sapha hoi jaise.

english_text: He strictly warned him and immediately sent him out,
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu pora taike samjai dikena jabo dise.

english_text: and said to him, “See that you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
nagamese_text: Aru taike koise, “Sabi tumi kunke bhi eku nokobi, kintu jabi, tumi nijor purohit khan ke dikhai dibi, aru tumi sapha huwa laga dikhai kene Moses laga niyom kori taikhan ke sakhi hobole dibi.”

english_text: But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places. People came to him from everywhere.
nagamese_text: Kintu bemar bhal hoija manu pora etu kotha bisi manu ke koi dise, aru Jisu khula-khula nogor te jabole napara hoise. Kintu Tai bahar alag jagah te thakise, aru manu khan ephale-uphale pora Tai logote ahise.

english_text: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was at home.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu Capernaum nogor te olop din pichete wapas ahise, aru Tai Simon Peter laga ghor te ase koi kene manu khan huni loise.

english_text: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.
nagamese_text: Manu bisi ta te joma hoise aru jaga nathaka hoi jaise, dorjate bhi jaga nathaka hoise, aru Jisu pora taikhan ke Isor laga kotha koise.

english_text: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba manu khan Jisu usorte ekjon juthor bemar para bera bole napara manu ke loi anise; taike charjon pora uthai anise.

english_text: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan manu bisi thaka nimite Jisu usorte taike loi jabole para nai, taikhan kun jagate Jisu thakise, ta te laga chat hatai dise, aru chaat khuli diya pichete, taikhan bisna te ghumai thaka manu ke Jisu usorte namai dise.

english_text: Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu taikhan laga biswas dikhise, Tai etu manu ke koise, “Putro, tumi laga paapkhan sob maph kori dise.”

english_text: But there were some of the scribes sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
nagamese_text: Etiya niyom likha khan kunba ta te bohi thakise, aru taikhan nijor laga monte bhabona korise,

english_text: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
nagamese_text: “Kile etu manu eneka kotha koi ase? Tai misa koi ase! Kun he paap to maph kori bole paribo, khali Isor nohoile?”

english_text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu atma pora jani jaise taikhan nijor monte ki bhabona kori ase. Jisu taikhan ke hudise, “Tumikhan kele monte eneka bhabona kori ase?

english_text: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk’?
nagamese_text: Etu bera bole napara manu ke ki koile bhal ase, ‘Tumi laga paap to maph hoise’ na etu kobole ‘Uthibi, tumi laga bisna uthabi, aru berabi’?

english_text: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan etu jani lobi Manu laga Putro ke etu prithibi te paap pora maph dibole nimite adhikar dise,” aru Jisu bera bole napara manu ke koise,

english_text: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
nagamese_text: “Moi tumike koi ase, uthibi, tumi laga chatai lobi, aru nijor laga ghor te jabi.”

english_text: He arose, and immediately took up the mat and went out in front of them all, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”
nagamese_text: Titia tai joldi uthi kene chatai uthaise, aru sob manu laga usor pora bahar te ulai jaise. Etu dikhi kene, taikhan sob asurit hoi jaise aru taikhan Isor ke dhanyavad dise, aru koise, “Moi khan kitia bhi eneka dikha nai.”

english_text: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Tai aru nodi kinar te jaise, aru bisi manu Tai usorte ahise, aru Jisu taikhan ke sikhaise.

english_text: As he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office. He said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu jai thakise, Tai Aalphaeus laga chokra Levi ke poisa utha manu khan laga tambu te bohi thaka dikhise titia Jisu taike koise, “Moi laga pichete ahibi.” Tai uthi kene Jisu laga pichete jaise.

english_text: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise Jisu Levi laga ghor te khana khai thakise, aru bisi poisa utha manu aru paapi manu khan bhi Jisu aru Tai laga chela khan logote bohi kene eke logote khai thakise, kelemane bisi manu thakise aru taikhan Jisu laga pichete jai thakise.

english_text: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
nagamese_text: Jitia kunba niyom likha khan kunkhan Pharisee khan he asele, Jisu ke dusra paapi aru poisa utha manu khan logote bohi kene khai thaka dikhise, taikhan Jisu laga chela khan ke koise, “Kile Tai poisa utha aru paapi manu khan logote bohi kene khai ase?”

english_text: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu etu hunise, Tai koise, “Gaw bhal thaka manu khan ke dawai nalage, kintu kun manu bemar ase, taikhan he lage. Moi dharmik manu ke mati bole aha nai, kintu paapi manu khan nimite ahise.”

english_text: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”
nagamese_text: Etiya John laga chela khan aru Pharisee khan upwas loi thakise, titia taikhan ahi kene Jisu ke koise, “Kile John laga chela aru Pharisee khan laga chela khan upwas loi ase, kintu Apuni laga chela khan upwas noloi?”

english_text: Jesus said to them, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Shadi te aha manu khan to shadi kori thaka mota taikhan logote thaka tak upwas lobole napare, napare? Jitia tak taikhan logote shadi kora mota ase, taikhan upwas lobole na paribo.

english_text: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
nagamese_text: Kintu eneka din ahibo jitia shadi kora mota ke taikhan pora loijabo, titia taikhan upwas lobo.

english_text: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
nagamese_text: Kun bhi notun kapra te biya kapra hali kene nasilai. Eneka korile kapra biya hoi jabo, notun kapra ke purana kapra pora biya kori dibo, aru etu pora pura kapra biya hoi jabo.

english_text: No one puts new wine into old wineskins; or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
nagamese_text: Aru kun bhi notun angur ros to loi kene purana chamra jola te narakhe. Eneka korile angur ros aru purana chamra jola duita bhi biya hoi kene phati jabo. Kintu notun angur ros ke notun chamra jola te he hali kene rakhibo.”

english_text: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise, Tai Bisram dinte dhaan kheti paar hoi kene jai asele, Tai chela khan juwa somoite dhaan bhangai kene khai thakise.

english_text: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”
nagamese_text: Aru Pharisee khan taike koise, “Sabi, kele juntu kaam Bisram dinte koribo nalage etu kori ase?”

english_text: He said to them, “Did you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise, “Jitia David bhuk lagise- tai aru tai sathi khan ki korise,- etu tumikhan porha nai naki,

english_text: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
nagamese_text: jineka tai Isor laga ghor te jaise jitia Abiathar mukhyo purohit thakise, aru ta te daan diya roti khaise, juntu niyom hisab te tai khabole napare, khali purohit khan he nohoile, kintu tai bhi khaise aru tai laga sathi khan ke bhi dise?”

english_text: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Bisram din to manu karone bonai dise, kintu Bisram din karone manu ke bona nohoi.

english_text: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
nagamese_text: Karone Manu laga Putro to Bisram din laga Probhu ase.”

english_text: He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there whose hand was withered.
nagamese_text: Dusra dinte, Jisu aru mondoli te wapas jaise, aru ta te hath biya thaka ekjon thakise.

english_text: They watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
nagamese_text: Kunba khan Taike golti lagabo karone Bisram dinte Tai bemar manu khan ke bhal kori dibo na nai sai thakise.

english_text: He said to the man whose hand was withered, “Stand up.”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai hath biya thaka ke koise, “Uthi kene age ahibi.”

english_text: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke hudise, “Bisram dinte bhal kaam koribo lage na biya kaam koribo lage, jibon bachabo namorabo?” Kintu taikhan chup-chap thakise.

english_text: When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan laga mon tan huwa dikhikene Jisu bisi khong hoise, aru Tai hath biya thaka manu ke koise, “Tumi laga hath uthabi.” Aru etu manu tai hath uthaise, aru hath bhal hoi jaise.

english_text: The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
nagamese_text: Titia Pharisee khan ulaikene joldi Herod laga manu khan logote mili kene Tai bhirodh te, Taike morai dibo karone taikhan bisara shuru korise.

english_text: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples; and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu Tai chela khan ke loi kene nodi phale jaise, aru Galilee nodi aru Judea desh

english_text: from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.
nagamese_text: aru Jerusalem sheher, Idumea, aru Jordan paar pora aru Tyre aru Sidon sheher khan phale pora bisi manu Tai logot ahise. Tai dangor asurit kaam kori diya huni kene Tai logote dangor bhir Tai logot ahi jaise.

english_text: He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai chela khan ke Tai karone ekta chutu naw bisari bole koise, kelemane bhir pora Taike chipai dibo hoija karone.

english_text: For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Tai bisi manu ke bhal kora karone jiman bemar ase, sob Taike chubole kosis korise.

english_text: The unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him and cried, “You are the Son of God!”
nagamese_text: Aru letera thaka atma khan Taike dikhise, aru Tai laga age te giri kene hala kori Taike koise, “Apuni Isor laga Putro ase.”

english_text: He sternly warned them that they should not make him known.
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai taikhan ke jor pora koise, Tai kun ase manu khan ke janibo nadibi koi kene.

english_text: He went up into the mountain and called to himself those whom he wanted, and they went to him.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai pahar uporte jaise, aru jun manu ke Tai lage, eitu khan ke Tai usorte matise, aru taikhan Tai logote ahise.

english_text: He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach
nagamese_text: Titia Tai logote thaki bole baroh jonke basi loise, - taikhan ke prochar kori bole pathai dibo karone-

english_text: and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:
nagamese_text: Aru bemar khan ke bhal kori dibole aru bhoot khan ke khedai dibole hokti aru adhikar dise.

english_text: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);
nagamese_text: Aru Tai baroh jonke basi loise: Simon jun laga naam Tai Peter rakhise.

english_text: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);
nagamese_text: Zebedee laga Putro James aru tai laga bhai John jun khan laga naam Tai Boanergas rakhidise, etu laga motlob ase, bhijili laga chokra khan.

english_text: Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
nagamese_text: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew Matthew, Thomas, aru Alphaeus laga Putro James, Thaddaeus, Simon Zealot.

english_text: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Then he came into a house.
nagamese_text: Aru Iscariot Judas, jun Taike thogai dise.

english_text: The multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
nagamese_text: Ek din Jisu ekta ghor bhitor te bohise, aru bisi manu ahi joma hoi jaise, etu karone Jisu aru chela khan to bhaat bhi khabole para nai.

english_text: When his friends heard it, they went out to seize him; for they said, “He is insane.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Tai nijor ghor manu khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan Taike dhori loi jabole bhabise, kelemane taikhan koise, “Tai laga dimag biya hoi jaise.”

english_text: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jerusalem pora aha niyom likha khan koise, “Tai logote Beelzebul ase” aru “Tai bhoot khan laga adhikar pora bhoot ke khedai ulai ase.”

english_text: He summoned them and said to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?
nagamese_text: Karone Tai taikhan ke usorte mati ani kene dristanto pora koise, “Kineka kori Saitan he Saitan ke khedai dibo paribo?

english_text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
nagamese_text: Jodi ekta rajyo to nijor bhitor te namili kene bhag hoile, etu rajyo khara koribo na paribo.

english_text: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
nagamese_text: Jodi ekta ghor nijor majot namila hoile, etu ghor bhi khara koribo na paribo.

english_text: If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi Saitan bhi nijor majot te namila hoi kene alag hoile, tai thakibo na paribo, kintu tai khotom hobo.

english_text: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.
nagamese_text: Kun bhi takot manu laga ghor te ghusi kene saman chor koribo na paribo, jitia tak takot manu ke bandhi nolobo, etu pichete he tai saman chor koribo paribo.

english_text: “Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, prithibi te thaka sob laga paap ke maph kori dibo, Isor ke hinsa kora kotha bhi maph kori dibo.

english_text: but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jun bhi Pobitro Atma uporte biya kotha ekta bhi kobo, taike maph nadibo, kintu kitia bhi khotom nohua golti kori dibo.”-

english_text: —because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan koi thakise, “Tai logote dusto atma ase.”

english_text: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu laga ama aru bhai khan ahi kene bahar te rukhise, aru Taike mati bole manu pathaise.

english_text: A multitude was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters are outside looking for you.”
nagamese_text: Dangor bhir tai logote thakise, hoilebi taikhan koise, “Sabi! Apuni laga ama aru bhai khan bahar te ahi kene Apuni ke bisari ase.”

english_text: He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai jowab di koise, “Kun Ami laga ama aru bhai ase?”

english_text: Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
nagamese_text: Titia Tai ghuri kene bohi thaka khan ke saikene koise, “Sabi, eitu khan he Ami laga bhai aru ama khan ase.

english_text: For whoever does the will of God is my brother, my sister, and mother.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane jun Isor itcha koribo, eitu khan he Ami laga bhai, bhoini aru ama ase.”

english_text: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai Galilee Nodi kinar te sikhabole shuru korise, aru bisi Tai usorte dangor bhir joma hoi jaise. Titia Tai ekta naw pora samundar te bohi jaise, aru bisi thaka khan samundar kinar sukha jagate khara thakise.

english_text: He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke dristanto pora bisi kotha sikhai dise, aru Tai updesh te taikhan ke eneka koise.

english_text: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow.
nagamese_text: “Huni bhi! Bijon diya manu ekjon bijon hissi bole jaise.

english_text: As he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise, Tai bijon hissi dise, aru kunba bijon rasta kinar te giri jaise, aru chiriya khan ahikena khai dise.

english_text: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
nagamese_text: Kunba olop mati thaka pathor te giri jaise, ta te mati bisi nathaka karone joldi uthijaise.

english_text: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia suryo uporte uthise aru gham dise, taikhan jor nathaka karone phat sukhi jaise.

english_text: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
nagamese_text: Aru kunba bijon to kata thaka jagate giri jaise, aru kata uthi kene bijon ke dabai loise, etu karone guti dhoribo para nai.

english_text: Others fell into the good ground and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
nagamese_text: Kintu baki bijon bhal matite girise, aru taikhan uthijaise, aru bhal hoi kene guti dhurise, aru kunba tis guna, kunba saat aru kunba sou guna dise.

english_text: He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, jun laga huni bole kaan ase, taike hunibo dibi!”

english_text: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Tai ekla hoi jaise, titia Tai laga chela aru Tai logote thaka khan Taike etu dristanto laga motlob hudise.

english_text: He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan ke to Isor rajyo laga lukaikene thaka kotha janibole dise. Kintu bahar manu khan ke to dristanto pora koi ase,

english_text: that ‘seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’”
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan sai thakibo, kintu nadikhibo, Aru taikhan huni thakibo kintu nabujhi bo, Etu nimite taikhan ghuri ahikena taikhan laga paap pora khyama napai.”

english_text: He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu pora taikhan ke hudise, “Kile tumikhan etu dristanto na bujhe? Tinehoile tumikhan sob dristanto kineka bujhi bo paribo?

english_text: The farmer sows the word.
nagamese_text: Kheti kora manu he Isor laga kotha hissi diya jon ase.

english_text: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
nagamese_text: Rasta kinar te kotha hissi dise, aru jitia taikhan kotha hunise, Saitan joldi ahikena taikhan monte thaka kotha loijai.

english_text: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.
nagamese_text: Tineka he pathor jagate hissi diya khan ke bhi hoise, taikhan kotha huni kene khushi pora joldi mani loise.

english_text: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
nagamese_text: Kintu jor nathaka karone olop din he thakibo parise. Etu pichete jitia kotha karone dukh kosto ahise, titia joldi taikhan giri jaise.

english_text: Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,
nagamese_text: Aru kata te hissi diya to jun manu kotha ke huni loise,

english_text: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
nagamese_text: kintu duniya laga chinta, aru dhun laga thoga baji, aru kisim-kisim jinis laga lalos pora taikhan monte jai kene, kotha ke dabai dise aru phol ulabo napara hoijai.

english_text: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
nagamese_text: Kintu bhal matite hali diya khan ase, jun khan kotha huni kene mani loise, aru phol dibo parise, kunba tis guna kunba sat guna aru kunba sou guna.”

english_text: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke arubi eneka koidi thakise, “Kunbi saaki julai kene ekta tukri nohoile bisna nichete narakhe nohoi? Etu ke jolai kene khamba uporte rakhe nohoi?

english_text: For there is nothing hidden except that it should be made known, neither was anything made secret but that it should come to light.
nagamese_text: Kelemane yate lukai rakhibole eku bhi nai, jitia tak dikhai nadiye, aru lukaikene ki kaam korise eitu khan sob puhor te dikhi jabo.

english_text: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba huni bole kaan ase, taike hunibo dibi!”

english_text: He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you; and more will be given to you who hear.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Tumikhan bhal pora huni bhi, ji naap tumi naapi dise, etu pora tumike bhi naapibo, aru etu pora bhi bisi di dibo.

english_text: For whoever has, to him more will be given; and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane jun logote kiba ase, taike aru di dibo, kintu jun logote eku bhi nai, tai pora olop thaka ke bhi loijabo.”

english_text: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai koise, “lsor laga rajyo to kunba matite bijon hali diya nisena ase.

english_text: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.
nagamese_text: Aru tai ghumai kene rati aru dinte uthi thake, aru bijon dangor hoi thake, kintu tai najane kineka pora dangor hoi.

english_text: For the earth bears fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
nagamese_text: Mati nijor pora ghas ulai aru dhaan diye: poila to phul diye aru hawa khai, etu pichete dangor hoi kene dhaan diye.

english_text: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia dhaan pakki jai, titia tai joldi dhaan kata manu khan ke pathai, kelemane katibo somoi huwa karone.”

english_text: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Kineka pora amikhan Isor laga rajyo ke tulona koribo? Nohoile ki dristanto pora etu dikhai dibo?

english_text: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
nagamese_text: Etu to sorso dana nisena ase, jitia etu matite hissi dise, etu somoi matite sob pora chutu guti ase.

english_text: yet when it is sown, grows up and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
nagamese_text: Kintu, jitia etu ke hissi diye, aru uthi jai, kheti te thaka pata sob pora bhi dangor hoijai, aru tai daal dangor hoi kene, akas laga chiriya bhi etu laga chaya te ghor bonai thake.”

english_text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai dristanto pora eneka bisi kotha taikhan ke bujhi bole koi dise.

english_text: Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.
nagamese_text: Kintu dristanto nohoi kene taikhan ke eku bhi kowa nai. Aru jitia Tai ekla hoise, Tai chela khan ke eitu khan laga motlob samjhai dise.

english_text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
nagamese_text: Etu din jitia saam hoise, Jisu pora chela khan ke koise, “Ahibi, amikhan etu jagate jabo.”

english_text: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan bhir ke chari kene, Tai logot naw te uthise. Aru dusra nawkhan bhi thakise.

english_text: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
nagamese_text: Titia dangor hawa ahise, aru tufan pora naw ke mari thaka karone naw to pani bhorta hoi jaise.

english_text: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu to kinar te palis uporte ghumai thakise. Aru taikhan Taike uthaikene koise, “Shika manu, amikhan khotom hobole ase aru Apuni chinta nai?”

english_text: He awoke and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased and there was a great calm.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu uthi kene andhi ke galise aru nodi ke koise, “Chup thakijabi!” Aru hawa rukhi jaise aru sob shanti hoi jaise.

english_text: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai Taikhan ke hudise, “Kile tumikhan bhoi korise? Tumikhan etiya bhi biswas nakore?”

english_text: They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan bisi bhoi hoi kene ekjon majote kotha korise, “Etu kun ase? Hawa aru nodi bhi Tai laga kotha mane!”

english_text: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu aru chela khan Galilee Nodi laga dusra phale, Gerasenes jagate ahise.

english_text: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu naw pora ulai ahise, ekjon junke dusto atma pora dhorise, joldi kobor pora ulai ahi kene Taike lok paise.

english_text: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,
nagamese_text: Tai kobor te he thake, aru kunbi taike rukhabole manu thaka nai, luha rusi pora bhi bandhi rakhibole napara hoise.

english_text: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.
nagamese_text: Kelemane taike bar-bar theng te luha rusi pora bandhi rakhise, kintu tai bhangai di thake. Aru ta te kun bhi taike dhori kene rakhibo paribole takot thaka nai.

english_text: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
nagamese_text: Tai rati din hoile bhi hodai pahar te aru kobor te he thake, aru kandi kene tai dhar pathor pora nijorke jokhom kori thake.

english_text: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,
nagamese_text: Jitia tai dur pora Jisu ke dikhise, tai Jisu phale polaikene jaise aru salam korise.

english_text: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai jor pora kandi kene koise, “Jisu, Porom Prodhan Isor laga Putro? Apuni ami logote ki kaam ase? Ami Isor naam pora Apuni ke anurodh kori ase, amike dukh nadibi.”

english_text: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
nagamese_text: Kelemane poila pora Jisu eneka koidisele, “O dusto atma, etu manu pora ulai jabi.”

english_text: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taike hudise, “Tumi laga ki naam ase?” Aru tai koise, “Ami laga naam Legion ase, kelemane amikhan bisi ase.”

english_text: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
nagamese_text: Aru tai Jisu ke anurodh korise taikhan ke etu jaga pora bahar napothabo nimite.

english_text: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te pahar te gahori khan kiba khai thakisele,

english_text: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”
nagamese_text: aru biya atma khan Tai logote binti korise, “Amikhan ke gahori laga bhitor te ghusi jabo dibi.”

english_text: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.
nagamese_text: Karone Tai taikhan ke jabole koi dise, titia dusto atma to ulaikene gahori te ghusi jaise, etu sob dui-hajar nisena gahori thakise, rang-khang pora polai ahi kene nodi te giri dubi jaise.

english_text: Those who fed the pigs fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.
nagamese_text: Titia jun manu gahori ke khilai thakisele, taikhan polai ahi kene sheher te aru bosti te thaka sobke koi dise, aru ki hoise koi kene manu khan sabole ulai ahise.

english_text: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan Jisu logote ahise, aru jun logote Legion thakisele, bhal hoi kene kapra lagai thaka dikhi kene taikhan bhoi khaise.

english_text: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
nagamese_text: Aru etu dusto atma thaka manu logot ki hoise aru gahori khan ke ki hoise etu laga kotha bhi sob manu ke koi dise.

english_text: They began to beg him to depart from their region.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan Jisu ke etu desh pora jai jabole koise.

english_text: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu naw te uthijaise, jun manu logote biya atma thakisele, tai Jisu logote jabole binti korise.

english_text: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi Jisu taike Tai logote jabo diya nai kintu koise, “Tumi nijor ghor te jabi, aru tumi laga sathi khan ke kineka tumi laga Probhu pora morom korise aru dangor kaam kori dise etu sob koi dibi.”

english_text: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.
nagamese_text: Aru etu manu Decapolis te jai kene ta te Jisu pora tai nimite ki kori dise etu sobke koise, aru jiman manu hunise, taikhan sob asurit hoise.

english_text: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu naw pora etu pahar hoi kene jaise, titia dangor bhir Tai logote joma hoi jaise, aru Tai nodi kinar te thakise.

english_text: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, Jairus naam mondoli laga cholawta ekjon ahi Jisu laga theng te giri jaise.

english_text: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai logote binti kori koise, “Ami laga chutu swali mori bole ase. Tai bhal hoi kene jinda thaki bole Apuni ahibi aru tai uporte Apuni laga hath dibi.”

english_text: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu tai logote jaise, aru bisi joma thaka khan Tai logote ahise, aru dhaka-dhaki kori kene jai thakise.

english_text: A certain woman who had a discharge of blood for twelve years,
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon mahila baroh saal pora khun jai thaka ta te thakise.

english_text: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
nagamese_text: Aru bhal kora manu khan logote bisi dukh kori toka poisa sob kharcha kori saise, hoile bhi bhal nohoi, kintu aru bisi biya hoi thakise.

english_text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai Jisu ki korise etu laga kotha khan hunise, bhir thaka majot pora ahi kene Jisu laga kapra chuise.

english_text: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane tai bhabise, “Jodi moi Tai laga kapra khali chubo parise koile, moi bhal hoi jabo.”

english_text: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
nagamese_text: Titia tai khun jai thaka rukhi jaise, aru tai laga gaw pora janibo parise bemar bhal hoi jaise.

english_text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
nagamese_text: Aru loge-loge te, Jisu bhi Tai pora hokti ulai ja jani loise. Aru Tai ghuri kene ephale-uphale manu khan ke saikene hudise, “Kun pora Ami laga kapra chuise?”

english_text: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai chela khan Taike koise, “Sabi manu bisi Apuni ke dhaka-dhaki kori jai ase etu dikhi kene bhi, Apuni koise, ‘Kun Moike chuise?”

english_text: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.
nagamese_text: Aru kun he Taike chuishe koi kene Tai ghuri kene saise.

english_text: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
nagamese_text: Aru etu mahila jani loise tai laga bemar bhal hoi jaise aru bisi bhoi hoi kene Jisu laga theng te giri kene Tai logote ki-ki hoise sob hosa koi dise.

english_text: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taike koise, “Chukri, tumi laga biswas he tumike bhal korise, shanti pora jabi, aru etu bemari pora bhal hoi jabi.”

english_text: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house, saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai etu kotha koise, kunba manu khan Yehudi cholawta laga ghor pora ahi kene koise, “Tumi laga swali mori jaise. Etiya sikha manu ke kele aru dukh dibo?”

english_text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan ki koi thakise, etu Jisu huni kene Tai mondoli laga cholawta ke koise, “Bhoi nokoribi. Biswas he rakhibi.”

english_text: He allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai Peter aru James aru James laga bhai John eitu khan ke chari kunke bhi Tai logote jabo diya nai.

english_text: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.
nagamese_text: Aru titia Tai mondoli laga cholawta laga ghor te ahise, ta te manu khan jor pora hala kori kandi thaka dikhise.

english_text: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai bhitor te ahise, aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan kele dukh hoi kene kandi ase? Swali to mora nohoi, kintu tai khali ghumai ase.”

english_text: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Taike hasi dise, kintu Tai taikhan ke bahar te ulai dikene swali laga baba aru ama aru jun manu Tai logote thakise, taikhan ke loi kene bhitor te swali thaka jagate jaise.

english_text: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai swali laga hath dhori kene koise, “Talitha Koum!” Etu motlob ase: Chutu swali, Moi tumike koi ase, uthibi.”

english_text: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.
nagamese_text: Aru loge-loge etu swali uthi kene bera bole hoise,- kelemane tai laga umor baroh saal thakise.- Aru taikhan sob bisi asurit hoi jaise.

english_text: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai kun manu ke bhi janibo nadibi koi kene swali laga baba ama khan ke mana korise aru taike kiba khabole dibi koise.

english_text: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai ta te pora ulaikene nijor town, Nazareth te ahise, aru Tai laga chela khan Tai logote ahise.

english_text: When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?
nagamese_text: Aru Bisram dinte Tai mondoli te sikhai thakise, aru bisi manu Tai kotha huni kene asurit hoise, aru ekjon majot te eneka hudi thakise, “Etu manu to kot pora etu kotha sob jani ase, aru Taike diya etu ki laga gyaan ase? Aru kineka hokti laga kaam etu manu laga hath pora asurit kaam hoi ase?”

english_text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” So they were offended at him.
nagamese_text: “Tai barhoi nohoi, jun Mary laga chokra ase, aru James, Joses, Judas, aru Simon laga bhai to? Aru Tai laga bhoini khan yate amikhan logote thaka nohoi?” Karone taikhan Taike bhal puwa nai.

english_text: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu Taikhan ke koise, “Ekjon bhabobadi to tai laga adar nathaka nohoi, kintu tai laga nijor nogor aru nijor ghor manu khan majot tai adar napai.”

english_text: He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai ta te dusra kaam koribo para nai, khali kunba bemar ke hath lagai kene bhal kori diya he hoise.

english_text: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan biswas nakora karone Tai asurit hoise, aru Tai bosti te berai kene sikhai thakise.

english_text: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai baroh jon chela khan ke Tai usorte mati ani kene taikhan ke duijon kori pathai dise, aru taikhan ke dusto atma khan kheda bole adhikar dise.

english_text: He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke sikhai dise safar juwa somoite, eku bhi noloikena khali ekta lathi he lobi, aru jola, bhaat, aru poisa laga peti te poisa nolobo.

english_text: but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
nagamese_text: Kintu juta lagabo,- aru kapra bhi duita napindhibo.

english_text: He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Jitia tumikhan kunba ghor te ghusi bo, tumikhan etu jaga chari kene najuwa tak etu ghor te he thakibi.

english_text: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
nagamese_text: Aru jodi etu jagate manu kun bhi tumikhan ke grohon nakore, aru kotha nahune, eneka hoile ta te pora juwa somoite tumikhan theng te thaka dhuli jhari dibi, taikhan bhirod de etu pora sakhi hobo karone.”

english_text: They went out and preached that people should repent.
nagamese_text: Karone baroh jon chela khan jai kene manu khan ke mon ghura bole prochar kori dise.

english_text: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick and healed them.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan bisi bhoot khan ke khedai dise, aru bemari ke tel malis kori kene taikhan ke bhal kori dise.

english_text: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”
nagamese_text: Aru Herod raja bhi eitu khan hunise, kelemane sob pora Jisu laga naam jani jaise, aru kunba khan eneka koi thakise, “Baptizma diya John to mora pora jee uthijaise, aru etu karone tai pora he eneka dangor kaam kori ase.”

english_text: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
nagamese_text: Dusra koise, “Tai Elijah ase.” Kintu dusra khan koise, “Tai poila te bhabobadi thaka khan nisena he ekta bhabobadi ase.”

english_text: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Herod etu kotha hunise, “John jun laga matha moi kati disele- tai mora pora jee uthijaise.”

english_text: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.
nagamese_text: Kelemane, Herod to tai nijor bhai Philip laga maiki Herodia ke shadi korise, etu nimite tai manu pathai kene John ke bondhi ghor te rakhi disele.

english_text: For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane John pora Herod ke koise, “Tumi nijor bhai laga maiki ke luwa to Isor laga niyom te thik nohoi.”

english_text: Herodias set herself against him and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,
nagamese_text: Karone Herodias bhi John ke biya paikena taike morai dibo bhabisele, kintu tai para nai.

english_text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Herod to John ke bhoi kori thakise; tai jani thakise John to ekjon dhormik aru pobitro manu ase, aru taike bhal pora bachai kene rakhise. Tai kotha hunile bisi bhoi hoijai, kintu khushi pora huni thake.

english_text: Then a convenient day came when Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.
nagamese_text: Aru ekta bhal dinte, Herod pora tai laga jonom dinte, tai laga daruga khan, senapoti khan aru adhikari manu khan, aru Galilee laga cholawta khan ke rati te khana te matise.

english_text: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
nagamese_text: Aru Herodias laga chukri nachi kene Herod aru ta te thaka sobke khushi kori dise, titia Herod pora swali ke koise, “Mangibi moi pora ki lage, moi tumike dibo.”

english_text: He swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai swali usorte kosom khaise, “Tumi ki mangibo, moi laga adha rajyo mangile bhi, moi tumike dibo.”

english_text: She went out and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
nagamese_text: Karone swali jai kene tai laga ama ke hudise, “Moi ki mangibo?” Titia tai ama jowab dise, “Baptizma diya John laga matha mangibi”.

english_text: She came in immediately with haste to the king and requested, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”
nagamese_text: Tai joldi raja logote ahi koise, “Baptizma diya John laga matha ekta thali pora moike di dibi, etu he ami laga itcha ase.”

english_text: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.
nagamese_text: Titia raja laga mon bisi dukh hoise, kintu tai kosom diya karone aru Tai logote boha alohi manu khan karone tai swali ke nohobo kobo napara hoise.

english_text: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard and commanded to bring John’s head; and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
nagamese_text: Aru raja joldi ekjon sipahi ke John laga matha kati kene anibole hukum dise. Aru bondhi ghor te jai kene tai laga matha kati loise.

english_text: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.
nagamese_text: Aru ekta thali te rakhise aru etu swali ke dise, aru swali pora tai ama logot dise.

english_text: When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
nagamese_text: Jitia John laga chela khan etu hunise, taikhan ahi kene tai laga gaw uthai loijai kene ekta kobor te rakhidise.

english_text: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.
nagamese_text: Titia apostle khan Jisu logote ahi joma hoise, aru ki kaam taikhan korise, aru sikhai dise, sob Taike koi dise.

english_text: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan nijor alag sunsan jagah te jai kene olop somoi aram kori lobi.” Kelemane ta te bisi manu aha-juwa kori ase, karone taikhan khabole somoi bhi napa hoi jaise.

english_text: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan naw pora ekta alag sunsan jagah te jai jaise.

english_text: They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.
nagamese_text: Kintu bisi manu taikhan jai thaka dikhi kene sob nogor pora polai ahise aru Tai logote ahise.

english_text: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu jitia bahar te ulaise, dangor bhir dikhikena taikhan ke morom lagise, kelemane taikhan to roikhya nathaka nisena thakise. Aru Tai bisi kotha taikhan ke sikhai dise.

english_text: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.
nagamese_text: Jitia saam hoi jaise, Jisu laga chela khan ahi kene Jisu ke koise, “Etu sunsan jagah ase, aru homoi to deri hoi jaise.

english_text: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke pathai dibi, taikhan ephale-uphale usor bosti te jai kene nijor karone roti kinibo dibi, kelemane taikhan khabole eku nathaka hoise.”

english_text: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai taikhan ke jowab di koise, “Tumikhan he taikhan ke kiba khabole dibi.” Aru taikhan Jisu ke hudise, “Amikhan jai kene dui-sou dinarii laga roti kini ani kene taikhan ke khabole dibo?”

english_text: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan logote kiman roti ase? Jai kene sabi.” Aru jitia taikhan saikene koise, “Pansta roti aru duita maas.”

english_text: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai sob manu ke ghas te joma hoi kene bohi bole koise.

english_text: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan ke eksoh-eksoh aru pachas-pachas kori kene alag-alag jagate bohi bole koi dise.

english_text: He took the five loaves and the two fish; and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai pansta roti aru duita maas ke loi kene sorgo phale saise aru dhanyavad dikena roti bhangai se aru manu khan ke dibole chela khan ke koise. Aru Tai duita maas ke bhi taikhan sob logote bhag kori dise.

english_text: They all ate and were filled.
nagamese_text: Titia Taikhan sob khai loise aru pet bhorta hoise.

english_text: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.
nagamese_text: Aru baroh ta tukri te bachi juwa roti tukra aru maas joma korise.

english_text: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
nagamese_text: Ta te taikhan roti kha pans hajar manu thakise.

english_text: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai manu khan ke pathai dibo karone chela khan ke naw pora joldi Nodi laga dusra phale, Bethsaida te jabi koi dise.

english_text: After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai prathana kori bole pahar te jai jaise.

english_text: When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
nagamese_text: Jitia saam ahise naw to nodi majote thakise, aru Tai ekla he matite asele.

english_text: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea; and he would have passed by them,
nagamese_text: Titia hawa taikhan ke ulta pora mari thaka karone, naw ke age te loi jabole bisi digdar huwa Tai dikhise. Aru choutha paher nisena Tai nodi te khujkari taikhan logote ahise, aru taikhan pora age ulai jabole bhabise.

english_text: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Tai nodi te Tai khujkari aha dikhise, taikhan bhoot dikhise bhabi kene bisi hala korise.

english_text: for they all saw him and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them and said to them, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan sob Taike dikhi kene bisi bhoi hoise, kintu Tai joldi taikhan logote kotha korise aru koise, “Mon dangor koribi, Moi he ase! Bhoi na koribi!”

english_text: He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan logote naw te ahise, aru hawa rukhi jaise, aru taikhan bisi asurit hoise.

english_text: for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan etu roti laga motlob bhi buja nai. Kintu, taikhan laga mon tan hoi thakise.

english_text: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored to the shore.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan paar kori kene matite ahise taikhan Gennesaret jagate ahi kene naw ta te lagai rakhise.

english_text: When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,
