nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan naw pora ulai ahise, manu khan Taike joldi jani loise.

english_text: and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick on their mats to where they heard he was.
nagamese_text: Aru usorte thaka bosti khan sob polai ahise aru bemari khan ke bisna pora loi anise, aru jun jagah te Tai ase koi kene janibo, ta te loi ani thakise.

english_text: Wherever he entered—into villages, or into cities, or into the country—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.
nagamese_text: Aru jun jagah hobi, bosti, nogor aru desh hobi, Tai kote jai, utu sob jagah te bemari khan ke bajar te bhi rakhi kene Tai laga kapra olop chubole binti kori thakise, aru jiman manu Taike chubo parise, taikhan sob bhal hoijai thake.

english_text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Ek din, Jerusalem pora aha Pharisee aru kunba likha manu khan Tai logote joma hoise.

english_text: Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, they found fault.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Jisu laga chela khan kunba ke hath nadhulai kene bhaat khai thaka dikhise.

english_text: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.
nagamese_text: -Kelemane Pharisee aru Yehudi khan purana niyom ke mani thakisele, taikhan hath nadhui kene eku bhi nakhai.

english_text: They don’t eat when they come from the marketplace unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan bajar jaga pora ahe, hath nadhui kene eku bhi nakhai, aru tineka bisi kotha ase: jun to taikhan mani thake, gilas, thali, tamba laga borton, dhua aru sapha kora.-

english_text: The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why don’t your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?”
nagamese_text: Titia Pharisee aru niyom likha manu khan Jisu ke hudise, “Kile Apuni laga chela khan poila laga niyom namani kene choli thake, aru hath nadholai kene roti khai thake?”

english_text: He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise, “Isaiah he tumi kopoti khan laga kotha bhabobani thik koise. Tai eneka likhise, ‘Eitu khan mukh pora to Moike sonman kore, Kintu taikhan mon to Moi pora dur thake.

english_text: They worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan misa-misi te Moike aradhana kori thake, Kelemane manu para bona niyom loi sikhai thake.’

english_text: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane tumikhan Isor diya niyom chari kene manu bona niyom he mani thake.”

english_text: He said to them, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan manu he bona niyom mani kene, Isor diya bhal niyom khan chari dise.

english_text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
nagamese_text: Kelemane Moses koisele, ‘Tumi laga baba aru ama ke Sonman koribi,’ aru, ‘Jun tai nijor baba, ama ke biya kobo, tai ji hoile bhi moribo.’

english_text: But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban,”’” that is to say, given to God,
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan koi, ‘Jodi ekjon tai nijor baba, ama ke koi, “Moi pora tumi ki modot pabole ase, etu sob Isor pora Corban dise’” - motlob, ‘Isor ke di dise’.

english_text: “then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan etu manu ke tai baba aru ama ke eku bhi modot kori bole nadiye.

english_text: making void the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan Isor laga kotha biya kori thake tumikhan niyom pora. Aru bisi mili thaka nisena kaam kori thake.

english_text: He called all the multitude to himself and said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
nagamese_text: Aru titia Jisu pora manu khan ke Tai usorte mati anikena koise, “Ami laga kotha huni bhi, aru bujhi lobi.

english_text: There is nothing from outside of the man that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
nagamese_text: Eneka jinis to nai, bahar pora manu bhithor te jai kene letera kori diya, kintu ji jinis bhitor pora ulai etu he taike letera kori diye.

english_text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba huni bole kan ase, taike hunibo dibi.

english_text: When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai bhir majot pora ulaikene ghor bhitor te ahise, taikhan Taike etu dristanto laga motlob hudise.

english_text: He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Kile tumikhan bhi eneka nabuja ase? Bahar pora manu laga bhitor te ki jai etu pora manu ke letera nakore.

english_text: because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, making all foods clean?”
nagamese_text: Kelemane etu tai mon para nohoi, kintu mukh pora pet te jai kene aru latrine te ulai jai, kele koile sob kha luwa to sapha ase.”

english_text: He said, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu eneka koi thakise, “Ki mon pora ulai, etu he manu ke letera kore.

english_text: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
nagamese_text: Kelemane manu laga mon pora biya bhabona, bebichari, chor kora aru morai diya,

english_text: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
nagamese_text: lalos, biya kaam kora, thogai diya, biya niyom thaka, suku jola, hinsa kora, dimag napuncha kaam kora, aru phutani kora.

english_text: All these evil things come from within and defile the man.”
nagamese_text: Etu sob biya bostu mon pora ahi manu ke letera kori diye.”

english_text: From there he arose and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.
nagamese_text: Ta te pora Tai uthi kene Tyre aru Sidon laga desh phale jaise. Aru ekta ghor te jaise, aru kunke bhi janibo nadibo bhabisele, kintu Tai Iukabole para nai.

english_text: For a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.
nagamese_text: Kintu ta te ekjon mahila jun laga chutu swali ke dusto atma pora dhurikena thakise, etu mahila Jisu laga kotha hunise, aru ahi Tai laga theng te giri jaise.

english_text: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
nagamese_text: Aru etu mahila Yunani aru Syrophoenicia jaga laga asele, aru tai swali pora bhoot ulai dibi koi kene Jisu ke binti korise.

english_text: But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike koise, “Poila, bacha ke khabole dibi. Kelemane bacha laga roti loi kene kutta khan ke diya thik nohoi.”

english_text: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai jowab dikene koise “Hoi, Probhu, kintu kutta bhi bacha khan laga roti tukra mez nichete giri thaka khabole pai.”

english_text: He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taike koise, “Etu kotha karone tumi, jabi, bhoot tumi laga swali pora ulai jaise.”

english_text: She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.
nagamese_text: Aru tai jitia ghor te ahise, tai swali bisna te ghumai thaka aru bhoot ulai jai kene thaka pai loise.

english_text: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai aru bhi Sidon laga desh pora ulai Decapolis laga desh te hoi Galilee nodi phale ahi jaise.

english_text: They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba ekjon kaan benga aru kotha bhal pora kobo napara jon thakise, Tai laga hath tai uporte rakhi dibi koi kene binti korise.

english_text: He took him aside from the multitude privately and put his fingers into his ears; and he spat and touched his tongue.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taike bisi thaka manu pora alag loijai kene tai laga kan te anguli ghusai dise, aru thuk dikene tai jiba te chui dise.

english_text: Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai sorgo phale saise aru jor pora awaj dikene koise, “Ephphatha!” -Motlob ase “Khuli jabi!”

english_text: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.
nagamese_text: Titia joldi tai kan khuli jaise, aru tai jiba bandi thaka bhi khuli jaise, aru tai sapha pora kotha kori bole parise.

english_text: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke etu kunke bhi nokobi koi mana kori dise kintu jiman taikhan ke mana kore, iman taikhan bisi kobole hoi jaise.

english_text: They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan bisi asurit hoi ekjon majot te koi thakise, “Tai jiman bhi korise sob thik korise. Tai kan nahuna ke bhi huni bole dise, aru kobo napara ke bhi kotha kobole takot dise.”

english_text: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself and said to them,
nagamese_text: Dusra dinte arubi bisi manu joma hoi jaise, aru taikhan logote khabole eku thaka nai. Jisu pora Tai laga chela khan ke matise aru koise,

english_text: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days and have nothing to eat.
nagamese_text: “Moi etu sob manu khan ke bisi morom lage, kelemane taikhan tin din pora Ami logote thaki ase, aru etiya taikhan logote khabole eku nai.

english_text: If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”
nagamese_text: Jodi Moi taikhan ke ghor te bhukha pathai dile, taikhan rasta te komjur pora giri jabo pare, kelemane kunba to dur pora ahise.”

english_text: His disciples answered him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”
nagamese_text: Titia chela khan Taike jowab dise, “Kote pora kunba yate jongol pora roti ani kene eitu khan ke khila bo paribo?”

english_text: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke hudise, “Tumikhan logote kiman ta roti ase?” Taikhan koise, “Sat-ta.”

english_text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke matite bohi bole adesh dise, aru Tai sat-ta roti loi Isor ke dhanyavad dise, aru bhangai kene chela khan ke di dise, aru taikhan pora sobke dise.

english_text: They also had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.
nagamese_text: Taikhan logote ekta huru maas thakise, Tai etu bhi loi dhanyavad dikene taikhan ke dibole koise.

english_text: They ate and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan khai kene aram pai loise, aru bachi juwa khana to sat-ta tukri bhorta uthai loise.

english_text: Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.
nagamese_text: Aru jun khaise, taikhan char hajar nisena asele, aru Tai taikhan ke jabo dise.

english_text: Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai joldi nijor chela khan ke naw te uthi kene Dalmanutha laga desh phale jaise.

english_text: The Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven and testing him.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba Pharisee khan ahi Taike hudise aru porikha korise. Taike sorgo pora ekta chihna taikhan ke dikha bole koise.

english_text: He sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai nijor Atma te dukh paa nisena lamba sans loi koise, “Kile etu yug khan chihna bisari thake? Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, etu yug khan ke eku chihna nadibo.”

english_text: He left them, and again entering into the boat, departed to the other side.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke chari kene, naw te uthijaise, aru nodi paar kori kene dusra phale jai jaise.

english_text: They forgot to take bread; and they didn’t have more than one loaf in the boat with them.
nagamese_text: Aru chela khan roti lobole pahorise, aru naw te taikhan logote ekta roti pora bisi thaka nai.

english_text: He warned them, saying, “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Sai rukhi thaki bhi, Herod aru Pharisee laga khomir pora hoshiar thakibi.”

english_text: They reasoned with one another, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan apaste kotha korise, kelemane amikhan logote roti nathaka hoise.

english_text: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet or understand? Is your heart still hardened?
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu etu jani kene taikhan ke hudise, “Tumikhan roti nathaka karone kele kotha kori ase? Kile etiya bhi najane? Tumi laga mon tan hoi thaki ase?

english_text: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
nagamese_text: Suku thakile bhi, kele nadikhe? Kan thakile bhi, kele nahune? Aru tumikhan yaad nai?

english_text: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Twelve.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Moi pans hajar karone pansta roti bhangai dise, aru tumikhan kiman tukri uthaise?” Taikhan jowab dise, “Baroh-ta tukri uthaise.”

english_text: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Seven.”
nagamese_text: “Aru jitia Moi char hajar karone sat-ta roti bhangai sele, titia tumikhan kiman ta tukri bhorta kori uthaise?” Taikhan koise, “Sat-ta tukhri uthaise.”

english_text: He asked them, “Don’t you understand yet?”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai hudise, “Kile, tumikhan etiya bhi nabuje?”

english_text: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu aru chela khan Bethsaida te ahi jaise, aru taikhan suku nadikha manu ekjon Jisu logote loi anise, aru taike chubole binti korise.

english_text: He took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village. When he had spat on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he asked him if he saw anything.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Tai suku nadikha manu laga hath dhorise aru bosti bahar te loi jaise, aru tai laga suku te thuki kene, Tai hath pora taike chuise aru taike hudise, “Tumi kiba dikhi ase?”

english_text: He looked up, and said, “I see men, but I see them like walking trees.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai uporte sai koise, “Moi ghas nisena manu jai thaka dikhi ase.”

english_text: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai arubi ekbar hath tai laga suku te chuise, aru tai bhal pora sabo parise aru sapha pora sob dikhibo parise.

english_text: He sent him away to his house, saying, “Don’t enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike ghor te pathai dise aru koise, “Town te etiya-etiya nimite najabi.”

english_text: Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do men say that I am?”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu aru Tai chela khan Caesarea Philippi laga usorte thaka bosti khan te jai jaise. Tai rasta te ja somoite, chela khan hudise, “Manu khan Moike kun ase koi?”

english_text: They told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others, one of the prophets.”
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan taike koise, “Baptizma diya John,’ aru kunba koi, ‘Elijah,’ aru kunba koi, ‘Ekjon bhabobadi.’”

english_text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke koise, “Kintu tumikhan Moike ki koi ase?” Peter jowab di koise, “Apuni Khrista ase.”

english_text: He commanded them that they should tell no one about him.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai kun ase etu kunke bhi nokobi koise.

english_text: He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke sikhabole shuru korise, Manu laga Putro bisi dukh koribo lagibo, bura khan aru prodhan purohit aru likha manu khan Taike namanibo aru morai dibo, aru Tai tin din pichete jee uthijabo.

english_text: He spoke to them openly. Peter took him and began to rebuke him.
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke etu kotha sapha pora koi dise, aru Peter Taike alag loijai kene Taike hala korise.

english_text: But he, turning around and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu ghurikena chela khan ke saise aru Tai Peter ke galise aru koise, “Saitan! Ami laga usor pora dur hobi, kelemane tumi Isor laga kotha te nohoi, kintu manu laga bhabona te he thake.”

english_text: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai bhir te thaka manu khan aru chela khan ke matise, aru Tai usorte ani kene koise, “Jodi kunba Ami laga piche koribo mon hoile, tai nijorke tyag koribo lage aru nijor Cross uthai loi Ami laga pichete ahibi.

english_text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jun nijor jibon bacha bole mon koribo, tai jibon harabo, kintu jun Moi karone, aru susamachar karone nijor jibon harabo, tai bachibo.

english_text: For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
nagamese_text: Karone kunba manu sob prithibi pai loi kene tai nijor jibon haraile, tai ki labh ase?

english_text: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
nagamese_text: Karone manu to nijor jibon laga bodli te ki dibo paribo?

english_text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
nagamese_text: Judi biswas nathaka aru paapi yug pora Ami laga kotha ke aru Moi nimite sorom kore, Manu laga Putro bhi jitia Tai laga pobitro duth khan aru Baba laga mohima te ahibo, Tai bhi tai nimite kotha kobole sorom koribo.”

english_text: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke koi thakise, “Hosa pora Moi tumikhan ke kobo, yate khara thaka kunba khan namoribo jitia tak Isor rajyo laga takot loi kene aha ke nadikhe bo.”

english_text: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of them.
nagamese_text: Titia choi din pichete Jisu pora Peter, James aru John ke loi kene ekta untcha pahar te jaise. Titia taikhan usorte, Tai laga gaw bodli hoi jaise.

english_text: His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten them.
nagamese_text: Tai kapra borop nisena bisi boga hoi jaise, etu prithibi te kun dhobi bhi tineka boga kori bole na pora nisena.

english_text: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.
nagamese_text: Titia Moses aru Elijah aha dikhai dise, aru taikhan Jisu logote kotha kori thakise.

english_text: Peter answered Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
nagamese_text: Titia Peter pora Jisu ke koise, “Rabbi, amikhan yate thakile bhal hobo, amikhan ke tinta thaki bole jaga bonabo dibi, ekta Apuni nimite, ekta Moses nimite, aru ekta Elijah nimite.”

english_text: For he didn’t know what to say, for they were very afraid.
nagamese_text: Aru tinjon chela khan bisi bhoi laga karone Jisu taikhan ke ki kobo lage etu najana hoise.

english_text: A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
nagamese_text: Titia ekta badal ahikena taikhan ke dhaki loise, aru badal pora ekta awaj pora koise, “Etu Ami laga morom thaka Putro ase. Taike huni bhi.”

english_text: Suddenly looking around, they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only.
nagamese_text: Titia tinjon chela khan achanak ephale-uphale saise aru Jisu he taikhan logote thaka paise, aru kunke bhi dikha nai.

english_text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them that they should tell no one what things they had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan pahar pora niche ahi thakise, Jisu taikhan ke hukum dikene koise jitia tak Manu laga Putro mora pora jee uthi najai, titia tak taikhan ki dikhise etu kunke bhi nakobo.

english_text: They kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the “rising from the dead” meant.
nagamese_text: Taikhan etu kotha lukai rakhidise aru “Mora pora jee uthi naja tak” ki motlob ase koi kene kotha kori thakise.

english_text: They asked him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Taike hudise, “Kile, likha khan Elijah he poila ahibo lage koi?”

english_text: He said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke jowab dikena koise, “Elijah he poila ahibo lage, aru sob thik tak kori dibo, etu hosa ase. Kintu Manu laga Putro laga kotha te Tai bisi dukh koribo aru Taike ghin hobo etu kele Isor kotha te likhi rakhise?

english_text: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they have also done to him whatever they wanted to, even as it is written about him.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan ke koi dibo Elijah ahi jaise, aru taikhan taike ki kori bole mon thakise etu kori dise, jineka Tai nimite bhi kotha likhi rakhi kene ase.”

english_text: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Tai chela khan logote ahise, bisi manu taikhan laga age pichete thakise, aru niyom likha khan taikhan logote kotha te lagi thakise.

english_text: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, greeted him.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia manu khan Taike dikhise, taikhan asurit hoi kene Jisu logot polai ahise aru Taike salam dise.

english_text: He asked the scribes, “What are you asking them?”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai pora chela khan ke hudise, “Tumikhan taikhan logote ki kotha te lagi ase?”

english_text: One of the multitude answered, “Teacher, I brought to you my son, who has a mute spirit;
nagamese_text: Ekjon bisi manu thaka jaga pora Taike jowab di koise, “Shika manu, moi laga chokra ke Apuni logot loi anise, tai logot gunga atma ase.

english_text: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down; and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they weren’t able.”
nagamese_text: Aru kot te taike dhure, ta te taike phelai diye aru tai laga mukh pora phen ulai, aru daat kamuri kene tai laga bodon to tan hoi thake. Aru moi Apuni laga chela ke etu khedai dibole koise, kintu taikhan para nai.”

english_text: He answered him, “Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”
nagamese_text: Jisu taike jowab dise, “Tumi biswas nakora yug khan, Moi kitia tak tumikhan logote thakibo? Kitia tak Moi tumikhan ke sai thakibo? Taike Moi logote loi anibi.”

english_text: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan chokra ke Tai logote anise. Aru jitia etu gunga atma pora Jisu ke dikhise, joldi tai chokra ke dukh dise, aru matite girai dise, aru tai laga mukh pora phen ulaise.

english_text: He asked his father, “How long has it been since this has been happening to him?” He said, “From childhood.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Jisu tai laga baba ke hudise, “Tai kitia pora bemar ase?” Aru tai koise, “Bacha homoi pora ase.

english_text: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
nagamese_text: Aru bar-bar taike khotom kori bole kitia ba jui te aru kitia ba panite girai di thake, kintu Apuni he kiba koribo parile, morom pora amikhan ke modot koribi.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taike koise, “‘Jodi Apuni pare koile koi ase?’ Biswas manu khan karone to sob koribo paribo.”

english_text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
nagamese_text: Joldi chokra laga baba kandi kene koise, “Hey Probhu, moi biswas ase, moi laga biswas laga upai kori dibi!”

english_text: When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!”
nagamese_text: Jitia bhir khan polai ahi thaka Jisu dikhise, titia Tai dusto atma ke galise, aru koise, “Tumi nahuna aru gunga atma, Moi tumike hukum di ase, tai pora ulai jabi, aru kitia bhi tai bhitor te aru najabi.”

english_text: After crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out of him. The boy became like one dead, so much that most of them said, “He is dead.”
nagamese_text: Titia gunga atma taike bisi dukh dise aru jor pora hala kori kene ulai jaise, aru chokra to mora nisena hoise, etu dikhikena bisi manu eneka koise, “Tai mori jaise.”

english_text: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up; and he arose.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu etu chokra laga hath dhori kene taike uthai dise aru tai khara hoi jaise.

english_text: When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we cast it out?”
nagamese_text: Pichete, jitia Jisu ghor bhitor te ahise, Tai laga chela khan alag pora Taike hudise, “Amikhan kele etu ke khedabo para nai?

english_text: He said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing but by prayer and fasting.”
nagamese_text: Etu karone Tai taikhan ke koise, “Etu sob prathana aru upwas pora he koribo paribo.”

english_text: They went out from there and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu aru chela khan ta te pora ulaikene Galilee paar kori jai asele, kintu Tai kun manu ke bhi janibo dibole itcha kora nai.

english_text: for he was teaching his disciples, and said to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane Tai nijor chela khan ke sikhai thakise aru koise, “Manu laga Putro ke manu hathte dhori dibo, aru taikhan Taike morai dibo; aru tin din pichete arubi Tai jee uthijabo.”

english_text: But they didn’t understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan etu kotha laga motlob bujhi bo pora nai, aru Taike hudibole bhi bhoi lagi thakise.

english_text: He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them, “What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai Capernaum te ahise, aru jitia Tai ghor bhitor te ahise, Tai taikhan ke hudise, “Tumikhan rasta te ki kotha loi huda-hudi kori asele?”

english_text: But they were silent, for they had disputed with one another on the way about who was the greatest.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan eku bhi kowa nai. Kelemane taikhan rasta te ekjon-ekjon logote kun he dangor hobo etu kotha kori thakise.

english_text: He sat down and called the twelve; and he said to them, “If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.”
nagamese_text: Aru bohi kene, Tai laga baroh jon chela ke mati kene koise, “Jodi kunba prothom hobole mon korile tai sob pora piche hobi, aru sob laga noukar hobi.”

english_text: He took a little child and set him in the middle of them. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai ekta huru bacha loi taikhan majote rakhise aru bacha ke Tai laga hathte loi kene taikhan ke koise.

english_text: “Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him who sent me.”
nagamese_text: “Jun Ami laga naam te eitu khan nisena bacha ke grohon koribo, tai Moike grohon kori loise, aru jun Moike grohon koribo, tai Moike he nohoi kintu Moike Jun pathaise, Taike bhi grohon kori loise.”

english_text: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone who doesn’t follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow us.”
nagamese_text: John Taike koise “Shika manu, kunba ejkon pora Apuni laga naam te bhoot khedai thaka paisele, aru amikhan taike mana kori dise, kelemane tai amikhan logote nathaka manu huwa karone.”

english_text: But Jesus said, “Don’t forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able quickly to speak evil of me.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu koise, “Taike mana na koribi, kelemane eneka kun bhi nai, jun Ami laga naam te asurit kaam koribo, aru pichete Moike biya nokobo.

english_text: For whoever is not against us is on our side.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jun bhi Amikhan ke hinsa nakore, tai Ami phale ase.

english_text: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name because you are Christ’s, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jun bhi tumikhan ke Khrista laga koi kene Ami naam pora ekta gilas pani bhi khilai le, Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, tai pabo thaka naharabo.

english_text: “Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.
nagamese_text: Kintu jun bhi, Moike biswas kora chutu ekjon ke bhi biya kori dile, tai karone dhan pisi thaka dangor pathor to tai gola te bandi kene samundar te phelai diya he bhal hobo.

english_text: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
nagamese_text: Jodi tumi laga hath pora tumike paap koribo di thake, etu hath kati phelai dibi, duita hath loi norokte kitia bhi khotom nohua jui te juwa pora tumi hath nathakile bhi jibon te juwa he bhal hobo.

english_text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
nagamese_text: Ta te taikhan laga puka namora aru jui bhi kitia bhi nabhutibo.

english_text: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna, into the fire that will never be quenched—
nagamese_text: Aru jodi tumi laga theng pora tumike paap koribo di thake, etu ke kati phelai dibi. Duita theng loi norokte kitia bhi bhuti bo napara jui te juwa pora tumi lengra hoile bhi jibon te juwa he bhal hobo.

english_text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
nagamese_text: Ta te taikhan ke kamura puka namore aru jui kitia bhi nabhute.

english_text: If your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out. It is better for you to enter into God’s Kingdom with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire,
nagamese_text: Aru jodi tumi laga suku karone tumike paap koribo di thake koile, suku ulaikena phelai dibi. Duita suku loi kene norokte juwa pora to ekta suku loi kene Isor laga rajyote juwa he bhal hobo.

english_text: ‘where their worm doesn’t die, and the fire is not quenched.’
nagamese_text: Ta te taikhan ke kamura puka namore aru jui bhi kitia bhi nabhute.

english_text: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.
nagamese_text: Karone sob jui pora nimokia kori dibo.

english_text: Salt is good, but if the salt has lost its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
nagamese_text: Nimok to bhal ase, kintu nimok bhi tai laga swadh harai jaile tumi ki pora etu ke aru swad koribo? Tumi nijorke nimok nisena rakhibi, aru shanti pora ek-dusra logote thakibi.”

english_text: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu Capernaum chari kene Jordan Nodi paar korise aru Judea desh phale ahi jaise, aru bisi manu Tai logote joma hoise, aru hodai nisena Tai taikhan ke sikhai di thakise.

english_text: Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
nagamese_text: Kunba Pharisee khan Taike porikha kori bole kiba hudise, “Ki karone mota tai maiki ke chari dibole niyom ase?”

english_text: He answered, “What did Moses command you?”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke jowab dikene koise, “Moses tumikhan ke ki hukum disele?”

english_text: They said, “Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan koise, “Moses koise chari bole laga kagos likhi kene taike chari dibole pare.”

english_text: But Jesus said to them, “For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke koise, tumikhan laga mon tan huwa karone tai tumikhan ke etu hukum dise.

english_text: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.
nagamese_text: Kintu sristi laga shuru pora ‘Isor he mota aru maiki bonai dise.’

english_text: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,
nagamese_text: ‘Karone mota to nijor ama aru baba chari kene tai nijor maiki logote mili jabo.

english_text: and the two will become one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
nagamese_text: Aru tai duijon eke sharir hoi jabo.’ Karone taikhan duijon nohoi kintu ekta sharir hoi jabo.

english_text: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”
nagamese_text: Karone ki Isor pora milai dise, etu ke manu pora alag nokoribi.”

english_text: In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan ghor te thakise Tai chela khan Taike aru etu kotha hudise.

english_text: He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
nagamese_text: Karone Tai taikhan ke koise, “Jun bhi tai maiki ke chari dikene aru dusra ke shadi korile tai maiki laga bhirodh te bebichar kori ase.

english_text: If a woman herself divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
nagamese_text: Aru jodi maiki bhi nijor mota chari kene dusra logote shadi korile tai bhi bebichar kori ase.”

english_text: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.
nagamese_text: Ek din kunba manu khan pora taikhan laga bacha khan ke Tai usorte loi anise, taikhan laga matha te Tai laga hath rakhi kene asirbad dibole nimite, kintu chela khan pora taikhan ke rukhai dise.

english_text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu etu dikhikena koise, “Bacha khan ke Moi logote ahibo dibi taikhan ke narukha bhi, kelemane Isor laga rajyo to eneka khan laga he ase.

english_text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
nagamese_text: Moi hosa pora tumikhan ke koi ase, jun pora nije ke ekta chutu bacha nisena kori kene Isor laga rajyo ke swekar nakore, tai ji hoile bhi ta te gusibo na paribo.”

english_text: He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai hath taikhan uporte rakhi kene asirbad dise.

english_text: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu rasta te jai asele, ekjon polai ahise, aru Tai samne te athukari kene Taike hudise, “Bhal Shika manu, anonto jibon pabole moi ki koribo lage?”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike koise, “Tumi Moike kele bhal koi ase? Isor he nohoile kun bhi bhal nohoi.

english_text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not give false testimony,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Honor your father and mother.’”
nagamese_text: Tumi niyom khan jani ase: ‘Manu namora bhi, bebichar na koribi! Chor na koribi, misa gawahi nadibo, manu ke nothogabi, tumi baba ama ke sonman koribi.’”

english_text: He said to him, “Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai jowab di Taike koise, “Shika manu, moi etu sob jawan thaka somoi pora mani ahise.”

english_text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike morom pora saikene taike koise, “Tumi ekta kaam he puncha nai, jabi aru tumi laga ki ase, sob bikiri kori kene dukhia khan ke di dibi, aru tumi sorgote dhun pai jabo, aru ahikena Ami laga piche koribi.”

english_text: But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.
nagamese_text: Kintu tai etu kotha huni kene dukh hoise, aru mon biya hoi kene jai jaise, kelemane tai bisi dhuni asele.

english_text: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu Tai age piche saikene chela khan ke koise, “Dhuni manu Isor laga rajyote gushi bole bisi digdar hobo!”

english_text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
nagamese_text: Aru chela khan Tai kotha pora asurit hoise. Kintu Jisu taikhan ke aru koise, “Bacha khan, Isor laga rajyote gushi bole kiman bhi digdar ase!

english_text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Isor laga rajyote dhuni manu gushi bole para to ekta uth pora bhiji laga suku paar ulai juwa he bisi sosta hobo.”

english_text: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan ekdom asurit hoi kene ekjon-ekjon logote kotha korise, “Tinehoile kun poritran pabo?”

english_text: Jesus, looking at them, said, “With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke saikene koise, “Manu pora hoile etu na paribo, kintu Isor he paribo. Kelemane Isor nimite sob para ase.”

english_text: Peter began to tell him, “Behold, we have left all and have followed you.”
nagamese_text: Titia Peter Taike koise, “Sabi amikhan to sob chari kene Apuni laga piche korise.

english_text: Jesus said, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu koise, “Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, kun bhi Moi karone aru susamachar karone Tai ghor nohoile bhai-bhoini, ama-baba, nijor bacha, aru kheti mati bari chari dile;

english_text: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time: houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.
nagamese_text: taikhan sob ek-sou guna pora bhi bisi pabo: ghor, aru bhai, bhoini, ama aru bacha aru kheti baari khan, aru aha yug te anonto jibon pabo.

english_text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”
nagamese_text: Kintu bisi manu jun khan age ase, taikhan piche hoi jabo, aru jun piche ase taikhan age hoi jabo.”

english_text: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.
nagamese_text: Kitia Jisu aru chela khan Jerusalem te jai thakise, Jisu taikhan sob laga age hoi kene jai thakise. Taikhan asurit hoise, aru Tai laga piche kori thaka khan bhoi lagi thakise. Titia Tai ekbar aru baroh jonke kinar te loijai kene Tai uporte ki ahibole ase etu taikhan ke koise.

english_text: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.
nagamese_text: “Sabi, Amikhan Jerusalem te jai ase, aru Manu laga Putro ke dhorikena mukhyo purohit aru niyom likha khan laga hathte di dibo, aru taikhan Taike golti dibo aru Taike morai dibo. Taike biswas nakora khan laga hathte dikena morai dibo.

english_text: They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Taike ninda kori kene maribo, kintu tin din pichete Tai jee uthibo.”

english_text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”
nagamese_text: Titia Zebedee laga Putro James aru John duijon Tai logote ahikena koise, “Shika manu, ami duijon kiba mangibo, etu kori dibi.”

english_text: He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
nagamese_text: Tai duijon ke koise, “Moi tumikhan karone ki kori dibo?”

english_text: They said to him, “Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left hand, in your glory.”
nagamese_text: Tai duijon pora Jisu ke koise, “Kitia Apuni singhason te bohibi, Apuni laga mohima pora bhorta thaka rajyote, titia, duijon nimite, ekjon Apuni laga dyna hath aru dusra Apuni laga baya hathte bohibo dibi.”

english_text: But Jesus said to them, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumi duijon ki mangi ase, etu najani kene mangi ase, duijon Moi khabole thaka kup pora khabo paribo, aru Moi ki baptizma pora baptizma lobole ase etu paribo?

english_text: They said to him, “We are able.” Jesus said to them, “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you shall be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with;
nagamese_text: Duijon Taike koise, “Amikhan paribo.” Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Duijon Ami khabole thaka kup pora khabole to hosa ase, aru Moi ki baptizma pora baptizma kori bole ase, etu bhi hobo.

english_text: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Ami laga dyna aru baya phale bohi bole to Moi dibo napare, kintu etu to kun nimite rakhikena ase, tai he pabo.”

english_text: When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant toward James and John.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia dos jon chela khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan James aru John duijon ke bisi khong hoise.

english_text: Jesus summoned them and said to them, “You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke mati anikena koise, “Tumikhan jani ase na, Porjati khan kun taikhan laga adhikari khan ase koi kene mane, eitu khan pora he taikhan uporte raj kore aru taikhan laga daruga khan pora taikhan uporte adhikar cholai thake.

english_text: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumi majot to eneka nahobi, kintu jun dangor hobole mon kore tai tumi laga nokor hobo dibi.

english_text: Whoever of you wants to become first among you shall be bondservant of all.
nagamese_text: Aru jun age hobole mon kore taike sob laga ses te thakibo dibi.

english_text: For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane Manu laga Putro bhi sewa lobole aha nohoi, kintu sewa kori bole aru bisi manu ke bacha bole nijor jibon dibole ahise.”

english_text: They came to Jericho. As he went out from Jericho with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan Jericho sheher te ahise. Aru ta te pora Tai aru chela khan aru taikhan logot bisi manu Jericho pora ulai jai thakise, titia Timaeus laga chokra Bartimaeus koi kene andha ekjon rasta kinar te bohi kene bhikh mangi thakise.

english_text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai etu Nazareth Jisu ase koi kene janise, tai hala kori kene koise, “Jisu, David laga Putro, moike daya koribi!”

english_text: Many rebuked him, that he should be quiet, but he cried out much more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
nagamese_text: Titia bisi manu taike gali dikena chup thaki bole koise. Kintu tai arubi jor pora hala kori kene koise, “David laga Putro, moike daya koribi!”

english_text: Jesus stood still and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu rukhise aru taike mati bole koise. Etu nimite taikhan pora andha manu ke koise, “Mon dangor koribi! Uthibi! Tai tumike mati ase.”

english_text: He, casting away his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.
nagamese_text: Aru tai uthikena tai bahar te lagai thaka kapra ke ulaikene phelai dise aru Jisu logote ahise.

english_text: Jesus asked him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, that I may see again.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taike koise, “Moi tumi karone ki kori dibo?” Andha manu Taike jowab dise, “Rabbi, moike dikhi pabo dibi.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your faith has made you well.” Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus on the way.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike koise, “Jai jabi. Tumi laga biswas he tumike bhal kori dise.” Aru etu loge-logote tai dikhibow parise, aru Jisu laga piche korise.

english_text: When they came near to Jerusalem, to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu aru chela khan Jerusalem te, aru Oliv Pahar kinar Bethphage aru Bethany nogorkhan te ahise, aru taikhan age jabole Jisu pora duijon chela ke pathaise.

english_text: and said to them, “Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him and bring him.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Jabi usor thaka bosti te, aru tumi ta te puncha loge-loge gadha puwali juntu uporte kun manu bhi boha nai, etu bandhi thaka pabo. Etu ke Khuli Kena loi anibi.

english_text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs him;’ and immediately he will send him back here.”
nagamese_text: Aru jodi kunba tumike kunba eneka hude, ‘Kile eneka kori ase?’ Titia taike kobi, ‘Probhu ke etu lagi ase, titia tai joldi pathai dibo.’”

english_text: They went away, and found a young donkey tied at the door outside in the open street, and they untied him.
nagamese_text: Karone taikhan jaise aru etu gadha puwali ke dorja bahar rasta te bandha paise, aru taikhan khuli loi anise.

english_text: Some of those who stood there asked them, “What are you doing, untying the young donkey?”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba manu ta te khara khan pora hudise, “Etu ki kori ase, gadha puwali ke kele khuli ase?”

english_text: They said to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu pora kowa nisena taikhan etu manu ke koise, etu pichete taikhan ke jabole dise.

english_text: They brought the young donkey to Jesus and threw their garments on it, and Jesus sat on it.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan gadha puwali loi anise, aru taikhan nijor kapra etu uporte bichai dise, aru Tai etu uporte bohi jaise.

english_text: Many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
nagamese_text: Aru bisi manu nijor kapra rasta te bichai dise, aru dusra khan ghas laga daal kati ani rasta te bichai dise.

english_text: Those who went in front and those who followed cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
nagamese_text: Tai laga age ja-a khan aru piche kora khan sob hala kori kene koise, “Hosanna dhoinyo ase jun Probhu laga naam te ahise.

english_text: Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
nagamese_text: Probhu naam pora ami laga baba David laga rajyo loi aha ke dhoinyo! Hosanna Tai laga naam untcha koribi!

english_text: Jesus entered into the temple in Jerusalem. When he had looked around at everything, it being now evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu Jerusalem sheher te ahi kene mondoli te jaise, aru Tai ghuri kene sob saise, aru bisi deri huwa karone, Tai baroh jonke loi kene Bethany te jai jaise.

english_text: The next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra din jitia taikhan Bethany pora ulai ahise, Tai bhuk lagise.

english_text: Seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
nagamese_text: Aru dur pora ekta dimoru ghas te pata thaka dikhi kene ta te kiba pabo bhabi kene Tai etu usor jaise. Kintu Tai khali pata he thaka paise, kelemane etu somoi to dimoru guti dibole somoi nohoi,

english_text: Jesus told it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!” and his disciples heard it.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora etu ghas ke koise, “Etiya pora kun bhi tumi laga phol aru nakhabo.” Aru Tai chela khan etu kotha kowa hunise.

english_text: They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete taikhan Jerusalem sheher te ahise aru Jisu mondoli bhitor te jaise. Ta te bikiri kori thaka aru kini thaka khan ke bahar te ulai dise, aru taikhan laga mezkhan ultai dise aru kabotar bikiri kori thaka khan laga chowki bhi ultai dise.

english_text: He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai kunke bhi eku jinis mondoli bhitor te loi aha-juwa kori bole diya nai.

english_text: He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers!”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai sikhai dikene koise, “Isor kotha te eneka likha ase nohoi, ‘Ami laga ghor to sob jati khan karone prathana ghor hobo?’ Kintu tumikhan etu ke chor dokait laga ghor bonai dise.”

english_text: The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him. For they feared him, because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.
nagamese_text: Aru mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom likha khan etu hunise aru Taike khotom kori bole bisarise. Taikhan bhoi korise, kelemane sob manu Tai laga kotha huni kene asurit hoi thaka karone.

english_text: When evening came, he went out of the city.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia saam ahise, Tai sheher pora bahar te ulai jaise.

english_text: As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra din phojur jitia taikhan jai asele, taikhan etu dimoru ghas to tai laga jor tak sukhi ja dikhise.

english_text: Peter, remembering, said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which you cursed has withered away.”
nagamese_text: Aru Peter laga monte ahise, aru tai Jisu ke hudise, “Rabbi, sabi! Dimoru ghas junke Apuni shrap disele, etu sukhi jaise.”

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.
nagamese_text: Karone Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Isor ke biswas rakhibi.

english_text: For most certainly I tell you, whoever may tell this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is happening, he shall have whatever he says.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, jun bhi etu ‘pahar ke yate pora ulai samundar te dubi jabi,’ eneka chinta nathakikena etu hoi jabo biswas thakile, etu bhi hoi jabo.

english_text: Therefore I tell you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and you shall have them.
nagamese_text: Karone Moi tumikhan ke kobo, tumikhan prathana te ki mangise, etu sob paise koi kene biswas korile etu pabo.

english_text: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tumikhan prathana kori bole hoi, jodi tumi laga monte kunba ke biya pai thakile, taike maph kori dibi, eneka korise koile tumi laga sorgote thaka Baba bhi tumi laga golti maph kori dibo.

english_text: But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your transgressions.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi tumikhan manu ke maph nadile tumi laga sorgo Baba bhi tumikhan laga golti maph nadibo.”

english_text: They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him,
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu aru chela khan aru Jerusalem sheher te ahise, aru Tai mondoli te berai thakise, titia mukhyo purohit khan, niyom likha khan aru bura khan tai logote ahise.

english_text: and they began saying to him, “By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan hudise, “Apuni ki hokti pora etu sob kori ase Aru kun Tumike etu kori bole dise?”

english_text: Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke jowab di koise, “Moi bhi tumikhan ke ekta kotha hudibo. Moike kobi, aru Moi bhi tumikhan ke kobo Moi ki takot pora eitu khan kori ase.

english_text: The baptism of John—was it from heaven, or from men? Answer me.”
nagamese_text: John pora baptizma diya to sorgo pora ahise, na manu pora ahise? Moike jowab dibi.”

english_text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we should say, ‘From heaven;’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan majote kotha patise, “Jodi amikhan sorgo pora ase koile, Tai kobo, ‘Tumikhan kele taike biswas kora nai?’

english_text: If we should say, ‘From men’”—they feared the people, for all held John to really be a prophet.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi amikhan ‘Manu pora’ koile.....” Bisi manu pora John ke bhabobadi mani thake nimite taikhan bhoi kori thakise.

english_text: They answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
nagamese_text: Karone taikhan Jisu ke koise, “Amikhan najane.” Karone Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Moi bhi tumikhan ke Moi ki laga takot pora etu sob kaam kori ase nokobo.”

english_text: He began to speak to them in parables. “A man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it out to a farmer, and went into another country.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu dristanto pora manu khan ke koise, “Ekjon manu draikha baari ekta bonaise, aru char kona phale bera lagai dise, aru ros khunda jaga bonaise, aru machang bonai kene kunba kaam kora manu ke theka di dikena tai to safar te ulai jaise.

english_text: When it was time, he sent a servant to the farmer to get from the farmer his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
nagamese_text: Jitia ros ulabole somoi ahise, malik pora nokor ke angur pabo pare bhabi kene draikha baari te kaam kora manu khan logote pathaise.

english_text: They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan pora nokor ke dhori kene marise, aru taike khali hath pathai dise.

english_text: Again, he sent another servant to them; and they threw stones at him, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
nagamese_text: Titia tai aru dusra ekjon nokor ke pathaise, hoilebi taikhan etu nokor laga matha te pathor pora mari dikena jokhom kori dise aru sorom khilai se.

english_text: Again he sent another, and they killed him, and many others, beating some, and killing some.
nagamese_text: Aru tai dusra ekjon ke pathaise, aru etu bar to nokor ke morai dise. Tai bisi manu ke pathaise: kintu taikhan arubi kunba ke marise, aru dusra khan ke morai dise.

english_text: Therefore still having one, his beloved son, he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
nagamese_text: Tai logot pathabole ekjon he thaki jaise, tai laga ekjon morom thaka chokra. Tai eneka bhabona korise, ‘Taikhan bhi ami laga chokra ke to morom koribo.’

english_text: But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
nagamese_text: Kintu kaam kora manu taikhan bhithor te kotha korise, ‘etu to uttoradhikari ase, ahibi amikhan taike morai dibo, aru tai laga sob to amikhan laga hoi jabo.’

english_text: They took him, killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan taike loijai kene mari dise, aru taike draikha baari bahar te phelai dise.

english_text: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
nagamese_text: Karone etiya draikha baari laga malik ki koribo? Tai ahi kene kaam kora manu khan ke khotom kori dibo, aru draikha baari to dusra ke di dibo.

english_text: Haven’t you even read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan Shastro te porha nai naki? ‘Pathor mistiri khan pora chari diya pathor kona te thakise, Aru etu he ghor khara kora laga asol pathor hoi jaise.

english_text: This was from the Lord. It is marvelous in our eyes’?”
nagamese_text: Etu Probhu pora he hoise, Ami laga suku pora sabole bisi asurit ase.’”

english_text: They tried to seize him, but they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spoke the parable against them. They left him and went away.
nagamese_text: Aru mukhyo purohit khan, niyom hika khan aru bura khan buji jaise Tai taikhan bhirodh te etu dristanto koise, aru taike dhori bole bhabisele, kintu manu ke bhoi pora chari dise aru jai jaise.

english_text: They sent some of the Pharisees and the Herodians to him, that they might trap him with words.
nagamese_text: Titia Yehudi cholauta khan Jisu laga kotha pora Taike dhori bole kunba Pharisee aru Herod laga manu khan ke Tai logote pathaise.

english_text: When they had come, they asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and don’t defer to anyone; for you aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan koise, “Shika manu, amikhan jane Apuni hosa ase, aru kunke bhi bhoi nakore, kelemane Apuni manu laga mukh saikene kotha nakore, kintu Isor laga hosa rasta he sikhai, karone Caesar ke masul diya to thik ase na nai? Moi khan etu dibo lage na nai?”

english_text: Shall we give, or shall we not give?” But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius, that I may see it.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai taikhan laga chalak jani kene koise, “Kile Moike porikha kori ase? Ekta chandi poisa anikena Moike dikhabi.”

english_text: They brought it. He said to them, “Whose is this image and inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
nagamese_text: Karone taikhan ekta anise, aru Tai koise, “Etu kun laga chehera aru naam ase?” Taikhan koise, “Caesar laga ase.”

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.” They marveled greatly at him.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise, “Eneka hoile ki Caesar laga ase, Caesar ke di dibi, aru ki Isor laga ase, etu Isor ke dibi.” Aru taikhan Taike asurit hoise.

english_text: Some Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. They asked him, saying,
nagamese_text: Titia Sadducee jun khan mora pora jee na uthibo koi, Tai logote ahise. Aru Taike hudise,

english_text: “Teacher, Moses wrote to us, ‘If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife behind him, and leaves no children, that his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
nagamese_text: “Shika manu, Moses he amikhan ke etu niyom likhi disele, jodi kunba bhai bacha nathaki kene mori jai, aru tai laga maiki to thake, titia tai bhai he etu maiki ke lobo aru tai bhai laga naam age loi jabole koise.

english_text: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and dying left no offspring.
nagamese_text: Tinehoile age te sat-ta bhai asele, prothom bhai shadi kori kene bacha nathaki kene mori jaise.

english_text: The second took her, and died, leaving no children behind him. The third likewise;
nagamese_text: Aru dusra bhai etu ke loise aru etu bhi bacha nohoi kene mori jaise, aru tisra bhai ke bhi thik eneka he hoise.

english_text: and the seven took her and left no children. Last of all the woman also died.
nagamese_text: Aru sat-ta bhai sob taike loise aru bacha nathaki kene sob mori jaise, pichete etu maiki bhi mori jaise.

english_text: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For the seven had her as a wife.”
nagamese_text: Karone jee utha pichete tai kun laga maiki hobo? Kelemane tai sat jon bhai laga maiki thakisele.”

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t this because you are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan Shastro te likha kotha khan aru Isor laga hokti najana karone golti kori thake nohoi?

english_text: For when they will rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jitia taikhan mora pora jee uthibo taikhan shadi nakoribo, kintu sorgote Isor laga duth nisena thaki jabo.

english_text: But about the dead, that they are raised, haven’t you read in the book of Moses about the Bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
nagamese_text: Kintu mora pora jee utha kotha khan nimite tumikhan Moses laga kitab te porha nai, joli thaka jhari te, kineka Isor he taike eneka koisele, ‘Moi Abraham laga Isor, Isaac laga Isor, aru Jacob laga Isor ase?’

english_text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore badly mistaken.”
nagamese_text: Isor to mora khan laga Isor nohoi, kintu jinda khan laga Isor ase etu karone tumikhan bisi dangor golti kori thake.”

english_text: One of the scribes came and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”
nagamese_text: Titia ekjon niyom likha jon pora taikhan etu kotha kori thaka hunise. Aru Jisu pora etu laga thik jowab diya huni kene, tai Jisu ke hudise, “Sob pora prothom hukum to ki ase?”

english_text: Jesus answered, “The greatest is: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
nagamese_text: Jisu taike koise, “Sobse poila, ‘Huni bhi Israel, sob pora prothom hukum to amikhan laga Probhu he Isor ase, aru ekjon he Probhu ase.

english_text: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
nagamese_text: Aru tumi pura mon, pura atma, pura dimag, aru pura takot pora Probhu Isor ke morom koribi.’

english_text: The second is like this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
nagamese_text: Aru dusra hukum to etu kowa ase, ‘Tumi laga ghor usor manu khan ke nijor nisena morom koribi.’ Etu duita pora dusra dangor hukum aru nai.”

english_text: The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he;
nagamese_text: Karone likha manu Taike koise, “Bhal Shika manu! Apuni hosa pora koi dise, kelemane Isor ekjon he ase, aru Taike chari kene dusra nai.

english_text: and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
nagamese_text: Aru pura mon, pura dimag, pura atma, aru pura takot pora Isor ke morom kora, aru usor manu khan ke nijor nisena morom kora to daan kora aru bolidan diya pora bhi bisi dangor ase.”

english_text: When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from God’s Kingdom.” No one dared ask him any question after that.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu tai bhal jowab diya dikhise, Tai taike koise, “Tumi Isor laga rajyo pora dur nohoi.” Etu pichete, kun bhi Jisu ke aru kiba hudibole mon dangor kora nai.

english_text: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
nagamese_text: Pichete, Jisu mondoli laga bahar jagate sikhai thakise, Tai hudise, “Kanun likha khan to kineka Khrista to David laga chokra ase koi thake?”

english_text: For David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
nagamese_text: Kelemane David to Pobitro Atma te bhorta hoi kene eneka koise, ‘Probhu he ami laga Probhu ke koise, “Ami laga dyna hath phale bohi thakibi, Jitia tak Moi pora tumi laga dushman khan ke tumi laga theng nichete nadibo, titia tak.’”

english_text: Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so how can he be his son?” The common people heard him gladly.
nagamese_text: David tai nijor Taike ‘Probhu’ koise, to David laga chokra tai kineka hobo? Aru bisi manu khan Tai kotha ke shanti pora huni asele.

english_text: In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk in long robes, and to get greetings in the marketplaces,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu sikhai thaka somoite taikhan ke koise, “Likha manu khan pora hoshiar thakibi, jun kapra lamba kori lagai berai thake, aru bajar te salam diya bhal pai,

english_text: and to get the best seats in the synagogues and the best places at feasts,
nagamese_text: mondoli te bhal jaga, aru kha luwa te bhal jaga bisara khan.

english_text: those who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan bidhowa khan laga ghor hajam kori diye, aru bahana pora lamba prathana kori thake, eitu khan bisi dangor saja pabo.”

english_text: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu mondoli te daan diya daba usorte bohi kene sai thakise jun khan ahikena daba te poisa haali thakise. Aru dhuni khan bisi-bisi di thakise.

english_text: A poor widow came and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.
nagamese_text: Titia gorib bidhowa ahikena duita paisa dise.

english_text: He called his disciples to himself and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai chela khan ke mati anikena koise, “Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo. Manu khan daba te daan diya te etu gorib bidhowa he sob pora bisi dise.

english_text: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane sob manu taikhan nijor dhun bisi thaka pora dise. Kintu tai to bisi nathakilebi tai logote ki ase etu sob dise, motlob tai jinda thakibo laga sob di dise.”

english_text: As he went out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings!”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu mondoli pora ulaikene jai thakise, chela ekjon Taike koise, “Sikha manu, sabi, kineka bhal asurit pathor ase etu, aru kiman asurit ghor ase yate?

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here one stone on another, which will not be thrown down.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu jowab di taike koise, “Tumi etu dangor ghor dikhi ase? Yate ekta pathor bhi ekta uporte nathiki jabo, sob pathor ke girai dibo.”

english_text: As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai mondoli samne te Oliv Pahar te bohi asele, titia Peter, James, John aru Andrew taikhan lukaikene Taike hudise.

english_text: “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are all about to be fulfilled?”
nagamese_text: “Etu sob kotha kitia hobo, etu amikhan ke koi dibi, aru kitia etu sob kotha pura hobole hoi, etu laga chihna kineka hobo?”

english_text: Jesus, answering, began to tell them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke jowab di koise, “Hoshiar hobi, kun pora bhi tumikhan ke thogabo nadibi.

english_text: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he!’ and will lead many astray.
nagamese_text: Kelemane bisi manu Ami laga naam loi ahikena kobo, ‘Moi he Tai ase,’ aru bisi manu ke thogai loijabo.

english_text: “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia tumikhan lorai aru mara-mari laga awaj hunibo, titia chinta nokoribi, kelemane eitu khan hobole dorkar ase, kintu etu bhi hekh somoi nohoi.

english_text: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines and troubles. These things are the beginning of birth pains.
nagamese_text: Kelemane ekta desh pora dusra desh ke bhirodh koribo, ekta rajyo pora dusra rajyo ke bhirodh koribo, aru jaga-jagate mati hili bo, aru titia khabole eku napabo. Etu sob to bacha jonom hobole shuru te bikha nisena ase.

english_text: “But watch yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils. You will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan nijor hoshiar thakibi. Ami nimite tumikhan ke dhori kene sabhakhan te aru mondoli khan te di dibo, tumikhan ke maribo, pitibo, aru tumikhan ke sorkar aru raja khan usorte loijabo, taikhan nimite gawahi hobole.

english_text: The Good News must first be preached to all the nations.
nagamese_text: Kintu prothom te susamachar sob jati ke prochar kori dibo lagibo.

english_text: When they lead you away and deliver you up, don’t be anxious beforehand or premeditate what you will say, but say whatever will be given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan pora tumikhan ke dhori kene manu laga hathte di dibo, tumikhan ki kobo lage, etu nimite chinta na koribi, kintu tumikhan utu somoite ki kobo lage, etu he koi dibi, kelemane tumikhan pora nokobo, kintu Pobitro Atma pora he kobo.

english_text: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
nagamese_text: Titia bhai pora bhai ke dhurikena morai dibo, aru baba pora bacha ke morai dibo, bacha khan pora nijor ama-baba laga bhirodh hoi kene taikhan ke morai dibo.

english_text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
nagamese_text: Aru Ami karone sob tumikhan ke ghin koribo, kintu hekh tak jun dhorjo thakibo paribo tai he poritran pabo.

english_text: “But when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not” (let the reader understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia paap laga ghin kaam khotom kora ke kuntu jagah te khara nathakibole lage ta te khara kora tumikhan dikhile- kun porhibo tai he bujhi bole dibi- titia jun Judea te ase, pahar te polai jabi,

english_text: and let him who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house.
nagamese_text: Jun ghor uporte ase, taike niche najabole aru jai kene ghor bhitor pora kiba bahar te ulabole nadibi.

english_text: Let him who is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
nagamese_text: Aru jun kheti te ase, taike nijor kapra lobole ghuri ahibo nadibi.

english_text: But woe to those who are with child and to those who nurse babies in those days!
nagamese_text: Kintu etu dinte jun maiki khan pet te bacha bukhi se, aru jun bacha dudh khilai thakise, taikhan nimite hai ase.

english_text: Pray that your flight won’t be in the winter.
nagamese_text: Etu sob thanda dinte nohobo nimite prathana kori thakibi.

english_text: For in those days there will be oppression, such as there has not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never will be.
nagamese_text: Kelemane etu din eneka dukh din hobo, jitia shuru pora Isor sristi bona homoi pora aji tak eneka dukh aha nai, aru kitia bhi nohobo.

english_text: Unless the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom he picked out, he shortened the days.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi Probhu he etu din to khata kori nadile kunbi bachibole nohoi, kintu basi luwa khan karone Tai etu din khan khata kori dise.

english_text: Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ don’t believe it.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi kunba tumikhan ke kobo, ‘Sabi, Khrista yate ase nohoile, ‘Sabi Tai ta te ase,’ etu biswas na koribi.

english_text: For false christs and false prophets will arise and will show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
nagamese_text: Kelemane misa khrista aru misa bhabobadi ahibo, aru chihna aru asurit dikha bo, aru jodi parile basi luwa khan ke bhi thogai loijabo.

english_text: But you watch. “Behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
nagamese_text: Kintu hoshiar thakibi, sabi Moi age pora tumikhan ke koi ase.

english_text: But in those days, after that oppression, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light,
nagamese_text: Kintu etu dukh din laga pichete Suryo andhera hoi jabo, Aru chand bhi ujala nadibo.

english_text: the stars will be falling from the sky, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
nagamese_text: Titia akas laga tara bhi giri jabo, Aru akas laga hokti hili jabo

english_text: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
nagamese_text: Titia Manu laga Putro dangor hokti aru mohima hoi badal pora aha taikhan dikhibo.

english_text: Then he will send out his angels, and will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai duth khan ke pathai kene prithibi laga kona pora akas laga kona tak, char phale hawa pora Tai basi luwa sobke joma kori lobo.

english_text: “Now from the fig tree, learn this parable. When the branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near;
nagamese_text: Titia dimoru ghas pora dristanto sikhi lobi, jitia ghas laga daal komoliya hoi, aru pata ulabole hoi, gorom din usor hoise koi kene tumikhan jani jai.

english_text: even so you also, when you see these things coming to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
nagamese_text: Etu karone jitia etu sob hoi thaka dikhile jani lobi Jisu dorja usorte ahi jaise.

english_text: Most certainly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo, jitia tak etu sob kotha pura nohobo, titia tak etu yug laga manu khan harai najabo.

english_text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
nagamese_text: Akas aru prithibi harai jabo, kintu Ami laga kotha khan kitia bhi naharabo.

english_text: “But of that day or that hour no one knows—not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu din aru etu somoi kun bhi najane, sorgodoth khan bhi, aru Putro bhi najane, kintu khali Baba he jane.

english_text: Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you don’t know when the time is.
nagamese_text: Hoshiar pora sai thakibi, uthi kene prathana kori thakibi kelemane tumikhan najane etu somoi kitia ahibo.

english_text: “It is like a man traveling to another country, having left his house and given authority to his servants, and to each one his work, and also commanded the doorkeeper to keep watch.
nagamese_text: Etu to ekjon manu pora tai laga nokorkhan ke adhikar dikene, taikhan sobke nijor kaam dikene aru chokidar ke bhal pora sob sai thaki bole hukum dikene dusra jagate jai ja nisena ase.

english_text: Watch therefore, for you don’t know when the lord of the house is coming—whether at evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning;
nagamese_text: Karone hoshiar thakibi, kelemane tumikhan najane, malik kitia ghor te ahibo, saam te hobo na adha rati te hobo, na murga hala kora homoi te hobo, nohoile phojurte hobo.
