nagamese_text: Enos laga chokra, Seth laga chokra, Adam laga chokra, Isor laga chokra.

english_text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu, Pobitro Atma pora bhorta koi kene, Tai Jordan Nodi pora ghuri jaise, aru Pobitro Atma pora taike jongol te loi jaise.

english_text: for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when they were completed, he was hungry.
nagamese_text: Ta te Taike chalis din saitan pora porikha korise. Etu din khan te tai eku bhi khanai, aru porikha homoi khotom huwa pichete Tai bhuk lagise.

english_text: The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
nagamese_text: Saitan pora taike koise, “Tumi jodi Isor laga Putro hoi, titia etu pathor ke roti hobole hukum dibi.”

english_text: Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”
nagamese_text: Jisu taike koise, “Etu Isor kotha te likha ase, manu to khali bhaat pora jinda nathakibo.”

english_text: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
nagamese_text: Titia saitan pora Jisu ke uporte loi jaise aru ekbar te he Jisu ke duniya laga rajyo dikhai dise.

english_text: The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I want.
nagamese_text: Aru saitan pora taike koise, “Moi tumike etu sob adhikar aru mohima dibo, kelemane etu sob moi loi loise aru moi junke itcha kore, moi taike dibo pare.

english_text: If you therefore will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
nagamese_text: Jodi Tumi moike aradhana kore, etu sob Tumi laga hoi jabo.”

english_text: Jesus answered him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike koise, “Isor kotha te likha ase, tumi khali Isor ke aradhana koribi, aru Tai laga kaam he koribi.”

english_text: He led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here,
nagamese_text: Pichete saitan pora aru Jisu ke Jerusalem te loi jaise, aru mondoli uporte taike loi jaise aru koise, “Jodi Tumi Isor laga Putro hoi, yate pora niche giri jabi.

english_text: for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’
nagamese_text: Kile etu likha ase, tai sorgodoth ke hukum dibo, Tumike bachabo karone.’

english_text: and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’”
nagamese_text: Aru, taikhan Tumi laga hath pora uthai lobo, etu pora Tumi laga theng to pathor te nagiribo.’”

english_text: Jesus answering, said to him, “It has been said, ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”
nagamese_text: Jisu taike koise, “Etu Isor kotha te likha ase, ‘Tumi Isor ke porikha na koribi.’”

english_text: When the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until another time.
nagamese_text: Jitia saitan laga sob porikha khan khotom hoise, etu pichete saitan jai jaise, aru Taike gira bole bhal homoi rukhi thakise.

english_text: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through all the surrounding area.
nagamese_text: Pichete, Jisu Galilee te wapas Pobitro Atma laga hokti loi kene ahise, aru sob jagate Tai laga khobor huni loise.

english_text: He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
nagamese_text: Tai mondoli khan te Isor laga kotha sikhabole shuru korise, aru manu khan pora tai sikhai diya kotha khan huni kene bisi bhal paise.

english_text: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
nagamese_text: Aru tai Nazareth te ahise, jun jagate Tai dangor hoise, aru Yehudi niyom te, tai Bisram dinte mondoli te ghumai se, aru awaj uthaikene jor pora poribole khara kori loise.

english_text: The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and found the place where it was written,
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu ke Isaiah bhabobadi laga kagos poribole dise. Tai kagos Khuli Kena ki likha ase etu paise,

english_text: “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed,
nagamese_text: “Probhu laga Atma moi uporte ase, Tai moike tel hali dikene basi loise gorib khan ke susamachar prochar kori bole, Tai moike pathaise bandhi rakha khan ke khulai diya laga prochar kori bole, Aru andha manu khan dikhi bole, Dukh te dabai rakha manu khan ke bacha bole,

english_text: and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
nagamese_text: Aru Probhu laga dinte sob manu khushi pabole.”

english_text: He closed the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai kagos bondh kori kene cholawta ke wapas di dise aru bohise. Aru mondoli te thaka manu khan Taike he sai thakise.

english_text: He began to tell them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai pora taikhan ke koise, “Aji Isor kotha to purah hoise aru tumikhan huni loise.”

english_text: All testified about him and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth; and they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
nagamese_text: Sob manu Tai laga bhal koise aru asurit hoise aru Tai laga mukh pora ula kotha khan huni kene taikhan koise, “Etu Joseph laga chokra nohoi naki?”

english_text: He said to them, “Doubtless you will tell me this proverb, ‘Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in your hometown.’”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Hosa pora tumikhan Moi etu kotha kobo, ‘Bemar bhal kora manu, nijorke bhal koribi. Tumi Capernaum te ki korise amikhan etu sob huni loise, aru eneka kaam khan nijor desh te bhi koribi.’”

english_text: He said, “Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
nagamese_text: Kintu, “Moi hosa kotha kobo, bhabobadi ke nijor desh te kun bhi sonman nakore.

english_text: But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land.
nagamese_text: Moi hosa pora tumikhan ke koi ase bidhowa bisi jon Israel te Elijah laga dinte thakise, jitia akas to tin saal choi mohina bondh thakise, jitia dangor dukh din etu desh te ahise.

english_text: Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
nagamese_text: Kintu Elijah ke taikhan kun logote te bhi pathai diya nai, hoilebi Zarephath, Sidon te ekjon mota nathaka maiki logote he pathaise.

english_text: There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te kusto-rugi laga bemar thaka manu Israel te bisi thakise. Elisha bhabobadi laga dinte, kintu kunbi bhal huwa nai, khali Syria desh laga Naaman ke chari kene.

english_text: They were all filled with wrath in the synagogue as they heard these things.
nagamese_text: Aru mondoli te thaka khan jitia etu kotha hunise, taikhan sob khong hoi jaise.

english_text: They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that their city was built on, that they might throw him off the cliff.
nagamese_text: Taikhan khara hoise, aru Jisu ke tanikena nogor laga untcha pahar pora phelai dibole korise.

english_text: But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.
nagamese_text: Kintu Taike manu khan majot pora loi juwa homoi te, Jisu alag rasta pora ulai jaise.

english_text: He came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Jisu Capernaum te namise, juntu Galilee laga ekta sheher asele aru ta te sob manu khan ke Sabbath dinte Isor kotha hikai se.

english_text: and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
nagamese_text: Tai laga kotha huni kene taikhan bisi asurit hoise, kele koile Tai adhikar thakikena Isor kotha koi thakise.

english_text: In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,
nagamese_text: Etiya mondoli te ekjon manu bhoot atma pora dhora thakise, aru tai jor pora hala korise aru dangor awaj te koise,

english_text: saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
nagamese_text: “Ha! Apuni logote amikhan ki kaam ase, Nazareth laga Jisu? Moi khan ke borbad kori bole ahise? Moi jane Apuni kun ase- Isor laga Pobitro Ekjon Ase!”

english_text: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!” When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no harm.
nagamese_text: Jisu pora bhoot ke hukum dikena koise, “Chup thakibi, aru tai pora bahar ulai jabi!” Aru bhoot pora manu ke taikhan majote girai dise, aru manu ke eku nuksan nakorikena ulai jaise.

english_text: Amazement came on all and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
nagamese_text: Manu khan saikene asurit lagise, aru ekjon-ekjon logote kotha patikena koise, “Etu ki kotha ase, juntu laga adhikar aru hokti pora Tai dusto atma khan ke hukum kore aru taikhan ulai jai?”

english_text: News about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.
nagamese_text: Aru etu khobor sob jagate punchikena bisi manu huni loise.

english_text: He rose up from the synagogue and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they begged him to help her.
nagamese_text: Pichete, Jisu mondoli chari kene Simon laga ghor te jaise. Etu homoi te Simon laga maiki laga ama bisi bemar thakise, etu nimite Taike ahikena anurodh korise.

english_text: He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she rose up and served them.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu ta te jaise aru tai usorte khara hoi kene, bemar ke gali dise, aru bemar taike charise, aru tai uthikena taikhan ke sewa kori bole shuru hoise.

english_text: When the sun was setting, all those who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
nagamese_text: Jitia suryo nami jaise, jiman manu alag-alag bemar thakise, Jisu usorte loi kene ahise, aru Jisu ke taikhan uporte hath rakhi kene bhal kori dise.

english_text: Demons also came out of many, crying out and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking them, he didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
nagamese_text: Bisi jon pora bhoot khan hala kori kene ulaise, aru koise, “Tumi Isor laga Putro ase!” Hoilebi Jisu hukum dikene bhoot khan ke kotha kobo diya nai, kele taikhan jani thakise Tai Khrista ase koi kene.

english_text: When it was day, he departed and went into an uninhabited place and the multitudes looked for him, and came to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from them.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia din hoise, Jisu ulaikene manu nathaka jagate jaise, kintu manu khan dangor bhir hoi kene Taike bisari ahise. Taikhan ke Jisu pora chari kene najabo nimite manu khan kosis korise.

english_text: But he said to them, “I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Moi aru bhi dusra sheher khan te bhi Isor laga rajyo laga susamachar prochar koribo lage, etu karone Moike duniya te pathaise.”

english_text: He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai Judea desh laga jaga sob te mondoli te jai kene prochar korise.

english_text: Now while the multitude pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
nagamese_text: Etiya eneka hoise, bisi manu Jisu pora Isor kotha kowa huni bole Tai usorte ahi thakise, etu homoi te tai Gennesaret laga pukhuri te rukhi thakise.

english_text: He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai duita naw pukhuri kinar te ani thaka dikhise, kintu maas mara manu khan naw pora namikene taikhan laga jal dhulai thakise.

english_text: He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. He sat down and taught the multitudes from the boat.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu ekta naw te uthise, etu Simon laga naw thakise, aru tai laga naw ke olop panite loi jabole koise. Aru Tai naw te bohi kene manu khan ke hikai se.

english_text: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu kotha koi kene khotom korise, Tai Simon ke koise, “Etu naw to pani bisi thaka phale loijabi aru tumi laga jal to ekbar panite phelabi.”

english_text: Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”
nagamese_text: Simon koise, “Probhu, amikhan raat bhor jal marise aru eku bhi puwa nai, hoilebi apuni laga kotha te, moi jal phelabo.”

english_text: When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan jal phelaise, taikhan bisi maas dhurise, aru taikhan laga jal phati jaise.

english_text: They beckoned to their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
nagamese_text: Dusra naw te thaka sathi khan ke modot mangise. Aru taikhan sob mili kene duita naw te maas khan bhorta korise, etu pora naw to panite dubi bole hoise.

english_text: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Simon Peter etu dikhise, tai Jisu laga theng nichete girikena koise, “Ami usor pora jai jabi, kele moi ekjon paapi manu ase, Probhu.”

english_text: For he was amazed, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had caught;
nagamese_text: Etu kaam dikhikena Peter aru tai laga sathi khan,

english_text: and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
nagamese_text: aru etu nisena James aru John, Zebedee laga chokra khan, jun khan Simon laga sathi thakise taikhan sob kineka iman maas dhuri bo parise koi kene asurit hoise. Jisu pora Simon ke koise, “Bhoi nokoribi; tumikhan etiya pora manu khan dhora jal hobo.”

english_text: When they had brought their boats to land, they left everything, and followed him.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan laga naw mati kinar te anise, taikhan sob chari kene Jisu laga piche korise.

english_text: While he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
nagamese_text: Tai jitia ekta sheher te jaise, ekjon manu kusto-rugi bemar pora bhorta koi kene thaka dikhise. Aru jitia Jisu ke dikhise, tai Jisu laga theng te giri kene mangise aru koise, “Probhu, jodi Apuni itcha kore, Apuni moike sapha koribo pare.”

english_text: He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
nagamese_text: Jisu taike chuikena koise, “Moi itcha ase, sapha hobi.” Etu homoi te kusto-rugi bemar taike charise.

english_text: He commanded him to tell no one, “But go your way and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing according to what Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu pora taike koise kunke bhi nokobi, kintu “Purohit logote jai kene dikha bhi. Aru ekta sapha huwa laga boli koribi, Moses pora niyom diya nisena, etu pora he manu khan nimite ekta gawahi hobo.”

english_text: But the report concerning him spread much more, and great multitudes came together to hear and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu asurit kaam laga khobor to sob jagate punchise, aru bisi manu tai laga kotha huni bole aru bemar pora changai pabole ahise.

english_text: But he withdrew himself into the desert and prayed.
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai manu nathaka jagate jai kene prathana kori thakise.

english_text: On one of those days, he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by who had come out of every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was with him to heal them.
nagamese_text: Eneka he, ek dinte, jitia Tai hikai thakise, Pharisee khan aru niyom hikai diya khan Galilee jaga, Judea desh aru Jerusalem sheher laga usorte thaka alag-alag bosti pora ahise aru taikhan bohi thakise. Changai kori bole Isor laga hokti Jisu logote thakise.

english_text: Behold, men brought a paralyzed man on a cot, and they sought to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
nagamese_text: Titia manu khan he ekjon jothor bemar manu ke chetai te bukhi kene anise, Jisu jun jagate bohi thakise etu jagate anibole kosis korise.

english_text: Not finding a way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop and let him down through the tiles with his cot into the middle before Jesus.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan manu bisi thaka karone taike anibo para nai, taikhan ghor uporte uthise, aru ghor laga chaat khuli kene Jisu usorte namai dise.

english_text: Seeing their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan laga biswas dikhi kene, Jisu koise, “Manu, tumi laga paapkhan maph hoise.”

english_text: The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
nagamese_text: Titia niyom likha khan aru Pharisee khan hudibole shuru hoise, “Tai kun ase eneka misa kobole? Kun he paap maph kori bole pare, khali Isor he nohoile?”

english_text: But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered them, “Why are you reasoning so in your hearts?
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan mon eneka kele bhabi ase?

english_text: Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk’?
nagamese_text: Kuntu kobole asan ase, ‘Tumi paap to maph hoise’ na ‘Uthikena berabi?’

english_text: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,” he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, arise, take up your cot, and go to your house.”
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan janibole koi ase, Manu laga Putro logote prithibi laga paap ke maph dibole hokti ase” - aru Tai jothor thaka manu ke koise- “Moi koi ase, uthibi, tumi laga chatai uthabi, aru ghor te jabi.”

english_text: Immediately he rose up before them, and took up that which he was laying on, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
nagamese_text: Aru etu loge-loge, etu manu khara hoi jaise, aru tai ghumai thaka chatai uthaise, aru Isor ke mohima dikena nijor ghor te jai jaise.

english_text: Amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
nagamese_text: Sob manu khan asurit hoise, aru Isor ke mohima dise, aru manu khan bhoi hoise, aru koise, “Amikhan kitia bhi nadikha asurit kaam khan aji dikhise.”

english_text: After these things he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
nagamese_text: Etu pichete, Jisu bahar te jaise. Aru Tai ekjon poisa utha manu, Levi koi kene naam thaka ke masul dikri laga tombu ghor te bohi thaka dikhise. Tai jai kene koise, “Moi laga pichete ahibi.”

english_text: He left everything, and rose up and followed him.
nagamese_text: Aru tai uthise aru sob chari kene, Jisu laga pichete jaise.

english_text: Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
nagamese_text: Aru Levi pora tai laga ghor te jai kene, ekta dangor ekta khana rakhise, Jisu nimite, aru ta te poisa utha manu khan aru dusra khan bhi eke logote mez usorte bohi thakise.

english_text: Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan aru niyom likha khan chela khan logote hala kori kene koise, “Tumikhan kele poisa utha manu aru dusra paapi khan logote khai ase?”

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
nagamese_text: Jisu pora taikhan ke jowab dise, “Jun manu bhal ase taike bemar bhal kora manu nalage, kintu bemar manu ke he lage.”

english_text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
nagamese_text: Moi dharmik manu ke mati bole aha nai, kintu paapi khan mon ghura bole nimite ahise.”

english_text: They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan pora Taike koise, “John laga chela khan upwas aru prathana kore aru Pharisee khan laga chela bhi eneka he kore. Kintu Apuni chela khan, kha-luwa kore.”

english_text: He said to them, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Shadi te aha manu ke bhukha rakhibo pare naki, jitia tak taikhan logote shadi kori bole mota thaki ase?”

english_text: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.”
nagamese_text: Kintu eneka din ahi ase, jitia shadi kora manu taikhan pora jai jabo, etu din pora taikhan upwas koribo.”

english_text: He also told a parable to them. “No one puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new will not match the old.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise. “Kun bhi phata kapra logote notun kapra nasilai, jodi etu kore, notun kapra bhi phati jabo, aru notun kapra to purana kapra logote namilibo.

english_text: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled and the skins will be destroyed.
nagamese_text: Kun bhi angur ros purana chamra jola te nadhale. Eneka korile, notun ros pora jola to biya kori dibo, aru etu borbad hoi jabo.

english_text: But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.
nagamese_text: Kintu notun ros to notun chamra jola te halibo lage.

english_text: No man having drunk old wine immediately desires new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
nagamese_text: Jun manu bhi purana ros kha pichete notun ros khabole namange, kele tai koi, ‘Purana to he bhal ase.’”

english_text: Now on the second Sabbath after the first, he was going through the grain fields. His disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra Bisram dinte eneka hoise Jisu kheti majote jai thakise, aru chela khan dhaan guti ulaikene hath pora sapha kori kene khai thakise.

english_text: But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan hudise, “Tumikhan eneka kele kori ase, Bisram dinte eneka kori bole niyom nai nohoi?”

english_text: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan Isor laga kotha te pura nai naki David aru tai logote thaka manu khan bhuk laga homoi te taikhan ki korise?

english_text: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
nagamese_text: Tai kineka Isor ghor bhitore jaise aru pobitro jagate bhaat rakha to loi kene khaise, aru tai logote thaka khan ke bhi dise, juntu niyom pora chubo aru khabo napare, khali purohitkhan he khabo pare.”

english_text: He said to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
nagamese_text: Tai taikhan ke koise, “Manu laga Putro to Bisram Din laga bhi Probhu ase.”

english_text: It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
nagamese_text: Aru ekta Bisram dinte eneka hoise, Tai mondoli bhitor te jai kene sikhai thakise. Ta te ekjon manu tai laga dyna hath to murjha asele.

english_text: The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find an accusation against him.
nagamese_text: Aru Bisram dinte, Jisu pora kunba ke bhal kore na nai, etu pora golti dhori bole nimite, niyom likha manu kunba aru Pharisee khan Jisu ke sai thakise.

english_text: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan laga bhabona jani jaise, aru jun laga hath murjha asele etu ke koise, “Uthibi, amikhan majote khara hoi jabi.” Etu manu uthi kene taikhan majote khara hoi jaise.

english_text: Then Jesus said to them, “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
nagamese_text: Pichete Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Moi tumikhan ke hudibo, Bisram dinte bhal kaam koribo lage na manu ke nuksan koribo lage, atma ke bachabo lage na, biya koribo lage?

english_text: He looked around at them all, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu sob phale saikene etu manu ke koise, “Tumi laga hath to sidha koribi.” Tai korise, aru tai laga hath to bhal hoise.

english_text: But they were filled with rage, and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.
nagamese_text: Kintu cholawta khan khong pora bhorta hoise aru Jisu ke kineka phasabo etu kotha korise.

english_text: In these days, he went out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise dusra dinte Tai ulaikene tilla uporte prathana kori bole jaise, aru Tai pura rati Isor logote prathana kori thakise.

english_text: When it was day, he called his disciples, and from them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:
nagamese_text: Aru jitia din hoise Jisu pora chela khan ke matise, aru baroh jonke basi loise, aru taikhan ke apostle naam dise.

english_text: Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
nagamese_text: Simon (junke Peter naam dise) aru tai laga bhai Andrew; James aru John; Philip aru Bartholomew;

english_text: Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Simon who was called the Zealot;
nagamese_text: Matthew aru Thomas; aru James Alphaeus laga chokra; aru Simon junke Zealot bhi mate;

english_text: Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.
nagamese_text: Aru James laga chokra Judas; aru Judas Iscariot, jun he Jisu ke pichete dhoka dise.

english_text: He came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases,
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai tilla pora namikene taikhan logote ahise, aru bisi dangor bhir manu joma hoi thakise. Aru Judea desh, Jerusalem sheher, aru samundar kinar Tyre aru Sidon sheher khan pora ahise bhi bisi manu ahise.

english_text: as well as those who were troubled by unclean spirits; and they were being healed.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Isor kotha huni bole aru bemar pora bhal hobole nimite ahise. Kunkhan dusto atma pora dhori thakise taikhan bhi bhal hoise.

english_text: All the multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all.
nagamese_text: Aru manu khan Jisu ke chubole kosis korise kelemane Tai pora changai laga hokti ulai thakise.

english_text: He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for God’s Kingdom is yours.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai chela khan ke saise, aru koise, “Dhonyo ase dukhia manu khan, kelemane Isor laga rajyo to tumikhan nimite ase.

english_text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
nagamese_text: Dhonyo ase jun bhuk lagi ase, kele koile tumikhan bhorta hobo. Dhonyo ase kun etiya kandi ase, kele koile tumikhan hasibo.

english_text: Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
nagamese_text: Dhonyo ase jitia manu pora tumikhan ke ghin koribo, tumikhan ke chari dibo aru bodnam kori kene naam biya kori dibo, Manu laga Putro karone.

english_text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
nagamese_text: Etu din aha somoite khushi anondo pora nachibi, sabi, tumi laga inam to sorgote dangor ase. Kelemane taikhan baba laga baba khan bhi bhabobadi khan ke eneka he dukh dise.

english_text: “But woe to you who are rich! For you have received your consolation.
nagamese_text: Kintu dhun thaka manu khan, hai ase, kele koile tumikhan aram pai loise.

english_text: Woe to you, you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
nagamese_text: Hai ase kun manu etiya pet bhorta ase, kele koile tumi bhuk lagibo. Hai ase tumi kun etiya hasi ase, kele koile tumi dukh koribo aru kandibo.

english_text: Woe, when men speak well of you, for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
nagamese_text: Hai ase jitia manu pora tumikhan ke bhal ase koi, kele koile taikhan baba laga baba khan bhi misa bhabobadi khan ke bhi eneka koi thakise.

english_text: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
nagamese_text: Kintu kun huni ase, tumikhan ke Moi koi ase, tumi laga dushman khan ke morom koribi aru jun khan pora tumikhan ke ghin kore, taikhan ke bhal kaam dikhai dibi.

english_text: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tumikhan ke shrap diye aru tumike digdar kore, tai nimite prathana koribi.

english_text: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tumike ekta thapor mare, taike aru alag gaal phale bhi mari bole dibi, jun manu tumi laga kapra ekta loijai, dusra ula bhi taike lobole dibi.

english_text: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
nagamese_text: Tumike ki mange, etu di thaki bhi, aru jun manu tumi laga saman loijai, itu aru wapas namangibi.

english_text: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
nagamese_text: Manu ki korile tumi khushi pai, tumi bhi eneka taikhan logot koribi.

english_text: “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
nagamese_text: Jodi apuni pora jun manu tumike morom kore, tumi bhi etu manu ke he morom korile, apuni nimite ki labh ase? Paapi manu bhi eitu khan ke he morom kore jun manu taikhan ke morom diye.

english_text: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tumi karone bhal kaam kore, aru tumi bhi etu manu nimite he bhal kaam kore, eneka hoile tumi nimite ki labh ase? Kile mane dusra paapi manu bhi eneka he kore.

english_text: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
nagamese_text: Jun manu pora wapas pabole asha ase, taike he dile, tumi nimite ki labh ase? Dusra paapi manu pora bhi paapi manu ke dhar diye, taikhan bi etu sob pabole nimite.

english_text: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
nagamese_text: Kintu dushman ke morom koribi aru bhal kaam to dikhai dibi, aru bodli te kiba pabo nimite bhabona nokoribi, eneka korile, tumi laga inam to dangor thakibo, aru tumi Sobse Mohan laga bacha khan hobo, kele koile paapi khan kun Isor ke dhanyavad nadiya, Tai pora eitu khan sobke morom kore.

english_text: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
nagamese_text: Dayalu thakibi, jineka tumi laga Baba bhi dayalu ase.

english_text: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
nagamese_text: Bisar nokoribi, tumike bhi bisar nokorile. Bodnam na koribi, aru tumike bhi bodnam nakoribo, maph dibi, tumi bhi maph pabo.

english_text: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”
nagamese_text: Di thaki bhi, tumi bhi pai thakibo: bhal pora dabai kene aru bhorta hoi kene dibi, aru bisi hoi kene tumi laga theng uporte giri bo. Ki hisab pora tumikhan dibo etu hisab te tumikhan bhi pabo.”

english_text: He spoke a parable to them. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise. “Ekjon andha manu pora aru ekjon andha manu ke rasta dikha bo pare naki? Taikhan jai kene nalah te nagiribo naki?

english_text: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.
nagamese_text: Ekjon chela to guru pora dangor nohoi, kintu jun manu bhal kori kene sikhi loi tai guru nisena hoijai.

english_text: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
nagamese_text: Tumi bhai laga suku letera ke kele sai thake, kintu tumi nijor suku laga dangor letera to nadikhe?

english_text: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
nagamese_text: Tumi laga bhai ke etu kineka kobo, ‘Bhai, tumi laga suku te ki letera ase etu ami sapha kori dibo’; aru tumi laga suku te dangor letera thaka to tumi dikha nai? Kopoti khan! Poila tumi suku te letera thaka to ulabi, titia he tumi sapha pora tumi bhai laga suku te letera thaka to ulabole paribo.

english_text: “For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
nagamese_text: Kelemane bhal ghas te biya phol naulai aru etu nisena biya ghas te bhi bhal phol naulai.

english_text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
nagamese_text: Sob ghas to tai laga phol pora he jani jai. Manu khan kata ghas pora dimoru nakate, aru jongol ghas pora angur phol nakate.

english_text: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
nagamese_text: Bhal manu laga mon pora bhal bostu ulai diye, aru paapi manu bhitor pora biya he ulai diye. Kelemane mon bhitor te ki ase, tai mukh pora koi.

english_text: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
nagamese_text: Tumikhan kele Moike ‘Probhu, Probhu,’ mate aru Moi ki koi etu nakore?

english_text: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show you who he is like.
nagamese_text: Aru jun manu Moi logote ahe aru Moi laga kotha to huni kene kore, Moi tumikhan ke dikhai dibo tai kineka ase.

english_text: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
nagamese_text: Tai ghor bonai thaka ekjon manu nisena ase aru bhal kori kene pathor uporte ghor bonaise aru jitia ban-pani ahise, ghor to pani pora bhorta hoi jaise, kintu ghor ke hila bo para nai, kele koile etu ghor to bhal kori kene bonaise.

english_text: But he who hears and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.”
nagamese_text: Kintu kun manu huni kene kaam nakore, etu manu eneka ase, jun ghor bonaise hoilebi bhetimul to bhal diya nai. Aru jitia etu ghor te dangor hawa pani lagise, achanak pora etu ghor to purah bhangikena pura barbad hoi jaise.”

english_text: After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu sob kotha to koi dise aru manu khan ke hunai dise, Tai Capernaum town te jaise.

english_text: A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
nagamese_text: Aru Rome laga ekjon henapoti laga noukar, junke tai bisi morom kore, tai bemar pora mori bole hoi thakise.

english_text: When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia henapoti pora Jisu laga kotha hunise, tai Yehudi laga bura manu khan ke Jisu logote pathaise, Jisu pora jai kene tai laga noukar ke changai kori bole.

english_text: When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan Jisu usorte ahise, taikhan Jisu ke eneka anurodh korise, “Tai ekjon bhal manu ase aru apuni eneka koridile bhal ase,

english_text: for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
nagamese_text: kelemane tai moi khan laga desh ke morom kore, aru tai moi khan nimite synagogue bhi bonai dise.”

english_text: Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.
nagamese_text: Etu pora Jisu taikhan logote jaise. Kintu Tai jitia ghor te punchibole usor hoise, etu henapoti pora manu ke pathaise, aru Taike koise, “Probhu, Apuni dukh nauthabi, kelemane Moi laga ghor bhitor te Apuni ahibole moi layak nohoi.

english_text: Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite moi nijor bhi Apuni laga usorte ahibole layak nohoi, kintu Apuni ekta kotha koi dibi aru moi laga noukar changai pai jabo.

english_text: For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
nagamese_text: Moi nijor bhi ekta hukum chola manu ase, moi nichete sipahi khan ase. Moi ekjon ke kobo ‘Jabi’ aru tai jai; aru dusra ke kobo, ‘Ahibi’ aru tai ahe; aru moi laga noukar ke, ‘etu koribi,’ aru tai kore.”

english_text: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu etu kotha hunise, Tai bisi asurit hoise aru jun manu khan tai laga piche kori thakise, taikhan ke saikene koise, “Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Israel te Moi eneka biswas thaka manu dikha nai.”

english_text: Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia etu manu khan ke ghor te pathai dise, taikhan noukar to bhal hoi kene thaka dikhise.

english_text: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra dinte eneka hoise jitia Jisu Nain sheher te jaise, aru Tai laga chela aru dangor manu laga bhir bhi tai logote jai thakise.

english_text: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only born son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai sheher laga dorjate ponchise, ekjon mora manu ke uthai loijai thaka Tai dikhise. Mora manu to tai laga bidhowa ama laga ekjon he thaka bacha asele-, aru sheher laga manu khan tai logote thakise.

english_text: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Probhu taike dikhise, Tai etu ama ke bisi morom lagise aru taike koise, “Nakandibi.”

english_text: He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu uthikena mora manu bukhi thaka chatai te chuise, aru mora manu ke bukhi thaka khan bhi ta te sidha khara hoi jaise. Titia Jisu koise, “Jawan manu, Moi tumike koi ase, uthi bhi.”

english_text: He who was dead sat up and began to speak. Then he gave him to his mother.
nagamese_text: Aru titia mora manu to bohi kene kotha kobole shuru hoise, aru Jisu pora etu chokra ke tai laga ama logot di dise.

english_text: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
nagamese_text: Aru etu dikhikene sob manu bhoi lagi jaise, aru Isor ke dhanyavad dibole shuru hoise, aru koise, “Ekjon dangor bhabobadi moi khan majote ahise” aru “Isor he manu uporte morom korise.”

english_text: This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea and in all the surrounding region.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu laga etu khobor to Judea desh aru usorte thaka bosti, nogor sob te bhi khobor to punchise.

english_text: The disciples of John told him about all these things.
nagamese_text: Aru John laga chela khan etu sob khobor to jai kene John ke koise. Titia John pora tai laga diuta chela khan ke matise,

english_text: John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”
nagamese_text: aru taikhan ke Probhu ke hudibole pathaise, “Ahibole thaka Masiha to apuni ase naki, na amikhan to aru dusra ekjon ke rukhibo?”

english_text: When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan Jisu usorte ahise, manu khan koise, “Baptizma Diya John pora amikhan ke etu hudibole nimite pathaise, ‘Ahibole thaka Masiha to apuni ase naki, na amikhan to aru dusra ekjon ke rukhibo?’”

english_text: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te Tai bisi manu ke bemar pora changai korise, biya atma pora dhora manu aru suku andha manu khan ke bhi changai korise.

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan yate pora ja pichete, John ke jai kene tumikhan ki dikhise aru hunise etu kobi. Andha manu khan dikhi pai ase, lengra khan bera bole pari ase, korhi bemar thaka khan sapha hoi ase aru kaan benga khan huni ase, mora manu jinda hoi ase, aru gorib manu khan susamachar laga kotha huni bole pai ase.

english_text: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
nagamese_text: Dhonyo ase jun manu moi uporte biya napai.”

english_text: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
nagamese_text: Aru jitia John laga khobor bukha manu khan jai jaise, Jisu pora manu khan ke John laga kotha kobole shuru hoise, “Tumikhan balu jagate ki sabole jaise? Ekta hawa pora hilai diya jongol ghas to?

english_text: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed and live delicately are in kings’ courts.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan bahar te ki sabole jaise? Ekjon manu norom aru daam kapra lagai kene thaka to? Sabi, jun manu daam kapra lagai ase, aru aram pora thaki ase taikhan sob raja laga ghorkhan te pabo.

english_text: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan bahar te ki sabole nimite jaise? Ekjon bhabobadi? Hoi, moi tumikhan ke koise, tai to bhabobadi pora bhi dangor ase.

english_text: This is he of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
nagamese_text: Etu tai ase jun nimite etu Shastro te likha ase, ‘Sabi, Moi ekjon manu ke pathai ase, tumi laga chehera usorte te, Jun he rasta to taiyar koribo.’

english_text: “For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, jun manu ama pora jonom loise, kun bhi John nisena dangor nai, kintu jun Isor laga rajyote sobse chutu ase, tai pora bhi dangor ase.”

english_text: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
nagamese_text: Aru jiman manu etu kotha hunise, poisa utha manu khan, aru John logote baptizma luwa khan sob Isor pora dharmik ase koi dise.

english_text: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan aru niyom jana Yehudi khan Isor laga itcha namani kene baptizma luwa nai.

english_text: “To what then should I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
nagamese_text: “Tinehoile, Moi, etiya laga jamana khan ke ki logote tulona koribo, taikhan ki nisena ase?

english_text: They are like children who sit in the marketplace and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
nagamese_text: Taikhan bajar te thaka bacha khan nisena ase, bohi kene ekjon-ekjon ke mati kene koi, ‘Ami tumikhan usorte shadi laga basuri bojaise, tumikhan nach kora nai; moi khan mon dukh laga gana korise, hoilebi tumikhan kandia nai.’

english_text: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
nagamese_text: Baptizma Diya John to ahikena bhaat aru angur ros bhi khanai, aru tumikhan koi ase, ‘Tai logote bhoot ase.’

english_text: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
nagamese_text: Kintu Manu laga Putro ahikena kha luwa korise, aru tumikhan koi, ‘Sabi, taike, ekjon khakuwa aru nisa-pani kora, poisa utha khan aru dusra paapi manu laga sathi!’

english_text: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
nagamese_text: Gyaan pora sob bhal aru biya to jani loi.”

english_text: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house and sat at the table.
nagamese_text: Ekjon Pharisee pora Jisu ke tai logote khabole matise. Tai Pharisee laga ghor te punchise, aru Tai khabole bohise.

english_text: Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
nagamese_text: Etiya sabi, etu sheher te ekjon paapi mahila thakise. Jitia tai Jisu to Pharisee laga ghor te khabole bohi thaka dikhise, tai bhal gundh thaka bisi daam laga tel anise,

english_text: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
nagamese_text: aru khara hoi kene Jisu laga theng usorte kandi kene tai laga suku pani pora Jisu laga theng bhi jai dise aru chuli pora mussi kene tai laga theng ke chumai dise, aru bhal gundh tel lagai dise.

english_text: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
nagamese_text: Etu dikhikene, Jisu ke mata Pharisee tai nije ke koise, “Jodi etu manu hosa bhi bhabobadi ase koile, Tai janibo thakise etu jun taike choi ase, etu kineka mahila ase.”

english_text: Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taike koise, “Simon, Moi tumike kiba kobole itcha ase.” Aru tai koise, “Koi dibi, Probhu!”

english_text: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
nagamese_text: “Duita manu poisa dhar loise. Ekjon pansho denari aru dusra to pachas denari loi kene thakise.

english_text: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan logote wapas dibole poisa thaka nai, malik pora duijon ke maph kori dise. Etu nimite kun manu pora taike bisi morom koribo?

english_text: Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
nagamese_text: Simon koise, “Moi hisab te junke tai bisi dhar to maph korise.” Titia Tai taike koise, “Tumi thik bhabona korise.”

english_text: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
nagamese_text: Aru titia Jisu etu mahila phale saikene Simon ke koise, “Tumi etu mahila ke dikhi ase. Moi tumi laga ghor te ahise. Tumi Moike theng dhula bole pani bhi diya nai, kintu tai laga suku pani pora moi laga theng bhi jai dise, aru tai laga chuli pora mussi dise.

english_text: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
nagamese_text: Tumi Moike ekta chuma bhi diya nai, kintu Moi jitia pora yate ahise tai moi laga theng to chuma dibole chara nai.

english_text: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
nagamese_text: Tumi Moi laga matha te tel dhala nai, kintu tai Moi laga theng te bhal gundh thaka tel pora mussi se.

english_text: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”
nagamese_text: Etu nimite Moi tumike koi ase, tai laga paap bisi thakise, etu sob maph kori dise- kelemane tai bisi morom korise, kintu jun manu olop he maph kore, tai olop he morom kore.”

english_text: He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora mahila ke koise, “Tumi laga paap sob khyama koridi ase.”

english_text: Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
nagamese_text: Jun manu khan ta te bohi thakise taikhan majote kobole shuru hoise, “Etu kun ase, jun paap bhi maph kori bole pare?”

english_text: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu mahila ke koise, “Tumi laga biswas he tumike bachai loise. Shanti pora jabi.”

english_text: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise, Jisu alag-alag sheher aru bosti te Isor laga rajyo laga kotha prochar kori kene jai thakise, aru Tai logote baroh jon chela khan bhi thakise,

english_text: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
nagamese_text: aru kunba mahila khan bhi thakise jun khan dusto atma pora changai paise aru bemar pora bhal hoise. Mary, kunke Magdalene mate, jun laga gaw pora sat-ta bhoot khedaise;

english_text: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others who served them from their possessions.
nagamese_text: aru Joanna, Chuza laga maiki, Herod raja laga imandar, aru Susanna; aru dusra manu khan kun Isor laga kaam nimite taikhan logote ki ase etu di thakise.

english_text: When a great multitude came together and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable:
nagamese_text: Aru jitia bisi dangor manu laga bhir joma hoi thakise aru manu khan alag-alag nogor pora ahise, Jisu dristanto pora taikhan ke koise:

english_text: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
nagamese_text: “Ekjon kheti kora manu bijon hissi bole jaise. Aru jitia tai bijon halise, kunba rasta te girise, aru theng pora chipai dise, aru akas te chiriya thaka khan pora khai dise.

english_text: Some seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
nagamese_text: Aru kunba bijon pathor uporte girise, aru jitia dangor hoise, etu sukhi jaise, kelemane pathor uporte bisi patla mati thakise.

english_text: Some fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it and choked it.
nagamese_text: Aru kunba bijon to kata majote girise, aru dangor bhi hoise, hoilebi kata pora dabai dise.

english_text: Some fell into the good ground and grew and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba bijon to bhal matite girise, aru jitia etu dangor hoise, bisi dhan dhurise. “Etu kowa pichete, Tai awaj uthaikene koise, “Kun manu logot huni bole khan ase, tai huni lobi.”

english_text: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
nagamese_text: Titia chela khan Taike hudise, “Etu dristanto laga ki motlob ase?”

english_text: He said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest it is given in parables, that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
nagamese_text: Tai koise, “Tumikhan ke Isor he sorgo laga rajyo janibole dise, kintu dusra manu ke Moi dristanto pora koi, utu karone taikhan sai thakile bhi nadikha aru hunile bhi bujhi bole napare.’

english_text: “Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
nagamese_text: Etiya dristanto laga motlob eneka ase: bijon to Isor laga kotha ase.

english_text: Those along the road are those who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
nagamese_text: Rasta te gira bijon laga motlob kunba khan kotha hunise, kintu bhoot ahi kene mon pora bijon ke chingi loijai, etu pora taikhan biswas nokorile aru roikhya napabo.

english_text: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root. They believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
nagamese_text: Aru pathor uporte bijon gira to kunba Isor laga kotha khushi pora hunise. Kintu tai laga jor to bhitor te jabo napare, aru olop homoi nimite biswas kore, aru porikha aha homoi te giri jai.

english_text: What fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life; and they bring no fruit to maturity.
nagamese_text: Aru kata bhitor te gira bijon ase jun khan kotha hune, kintu duniya pora tani loi, dhun sampoti, rong tamash aru lalaj pora bandhi jai aru uthibole napare.

english_text: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
nagamese_text: Kintu bhal matite gira bijon khan taikhan ase kunkhan mon dikena Isor kotha ke hunise aru monte rakhise, aru thik pora dhuri rakhise aru pichete bhal guti dhore.

english_text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
nagamese_text: Kun manu bhi saaki jolai kene bisna nichete narakhe. Kintu etu ke uporte rakhe, aru sob manu etu laga puhor dikhi bole pai.

english_text: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.
nagamese_text: Eku bostu lukai kene rakhibo na paribo, kele koile puhor pora sob bostu dikhai dibo.

english_text: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
nagamese_text: Etu karone ki hune ase, jun manu logot bisi ase, tai arubi bisi pabo, aru kun manu logot komti ase, tai logote ki ase etu bhi loijabo.”

english_text: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.
nagamese_text: Pichete Jisu laga ama aru bhai khan Jisu usorte ahise, kintu taikhan Jisu thaka usorte jabo para nai kelemane manu laga bhir dangor thakise.

english_text: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
nagamese_text: Jisu ke manu khan khobor dise, “Apuni laga ama aru bhai khan bahar te rukhi ase, Apnike lok kori bole rukhi ase.”

english_text: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu Khrista taikhan ke jowab dise, “Ami laga ama aru bhai eitu khan ase jun manu Isor kotha hune aru kore.”

english_text: Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.
nagamese_text: Etu ek din eneka hoise, Tai chela khan logote ekta naw te uthise, aru taikhan ke koise, “Ahibi amikhan nodi laga dusra phale jabo.” Aru taikhan bohi kene jaise.

english_text: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.
nagamese_text: Naw te jai thaka homoi te Tai ghumai jaise. Etu homoi te dangor andhi ahise. Taikhan laga naw panite gushi bole shuru hoise aru taikhan moribo bhabi thakise.

english_text: They came to him and awoke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are dying!” He awoke and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water; then they ceased, and it was calm.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu ke uthaise aru koise, “Probhu! Probhu! Moi khan sob mori bole ase!” Kintu Tai uthikena hawa pani ke hukum korise, aru bisi shanti hoi jaise.

english_text: He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Being afraid, they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan laga biswas to kot te ase?” Aru taikhan bhoi pora asurit hoi kene majote ke koise, “Etu kun ase, Tai hawa aru pani ke hukum dise, aru taikhan manise?”

english_text: Then they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
nagamese_text: Pichete taikhan nodi paar kori kene Gerasenes, Galilee nodi usorte jaise.

english_text: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu matite namise, ekjon manu bisi bhoot pora dhora sheher pora ahi kene Jisu ke lok paise. Bisi din pora tai gaw te kapra nalagai kene, ghor te bhi thakibo napari kene, koboristan te he thaki asele.

english_text: When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai Jisu ke dikhise, tai jor pora kandise, aru Tai age te girise aru jor pora hala kori kene koise, “Apuni moi logot ki kaam ase, Jisu, jinda Isor laga Putro? Moi anurodh kori ase, moike dukh nadibi.”

english_text: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.
nagamese_text: Jisu he dusto atma ke etu manu pora ulai jabole hukum dise. Bisi bar itu manu ke morai dibo nisena korise, loha laga rusi pora bandhi kene thakile bhi, manu khan pora bandhi rakhile bhi, sob rusi khan bhangai kene taike bhoot pora jongol te loijai thake.

english_text: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora taike hudise, “Tumi laga naam ki ase?” Tai jowab dise, “Legion,” kelemane bisi bhoot khan tai bhitor te thakise.

english_text: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan ke mora manu thaka jagate jabole hukum nadibi koi kene Taike anurodh korise.

english_text: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. Then he allowed them.
nagamese_text: Aru etu usorte gahori khan tilla kinar te dana khai thakise, etu pora biya atma khan gahori bhitor te jabole nimite anurodh korise. Jisu pora eneka hobole dise.

english_text: The demons came out of the man and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.
nagamese_text: Aru bhoot khan manu pora ulaikene gahori bhitor te ghumai jaise, aru gahori sob pahar nichete giri kene mori jaise.

english_text: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled and told it in the city and in the country.
nagamese_text: Gahori pala manu khan etu dikhi kene sheher te polaikene khobor dise.

english_text: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
nagamese_text: Aru manu khan ki hoise etu sabole ahise, aru jun laga gaw pora biya atma ulai jaise, taike Jisu laga theng usorte bohi thaka dikhise, sapha kapra lagase aru bhal hoise aru etu saikene manu khan bhoi lagise.

english_text: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan dikhise kineka bisi bhoot pora dhora manu to bhal hoise, taikhan pora jai kene itu laga khobor sobke dise.

english_text: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. Then he entered into the boat and returned.
nagamese_text: Aru Gerasenes laga sob manu khan bhoi lagi kene Jisu ke etu jaga pora jai jabole koise. Etu pichete, Tai naw te bohi kene wapas jai jaise.

english_text: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
nagamese_text: Jun manu pora biya atma khan ulaikene jaise, tai Jisu logote jabole anurodh korise, kintu Jisu pora taike wapas pathai kene koise,

english_text: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
nagamese_text: “Tumi nijor ghor te jabi aru Isor ki kori dise etu jai kene koi dibi.” Tai pichete tai ghor te jaise, sob sheher te Jisu pora tai nimite ki kori dise etu prochar kori dise.

english_text: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu ahise, sob manu khan taike salam korise, kelemane taikhan Taike rukhi thakise.

english_text: Behold, a man named Jairus came. He was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house,
nagamese_text: Aru ta te ekjon manu thakise tai laga naam Jairus asele, tai mondoli laga cholawta thakise. Tai Jisu laga theng te giri jaise, aru Jisu ke tai laga ghor te ahibole anurodh korise.

english_text: for he had an only born daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.
nagamese_text: Tai laga ekjon baroh saal chukri mori bole asele aru jitia tai rasta te jai thakise, bisi manu khan tai logote joma hoi jaise.

english_text: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians and could not be healed by any,
nagamese_text: Ekjon mahila baroh saal pora khun jai thakise, tai dawai diya manu logote sob taka poisa kharcha korise, kintu kun bhi taike bhal kori bole pora nai.

english_text: came behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak. Immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
nagamese_text: Tai piche pora jai kene manu majot pora Jisu laga kapra chuise, aru etu loge-loge te tai laga khun jai thaka rukhi jaise.

english_text: Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu koise, “Kun pora Moike chuise?” Jitia sob manu chup thakise, Peter koise, “Probhu, bisi manu khan ahi kene Apuni ke chui ase.”

english_text: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu he koise, “Kunba Moike chuise, Moi jani ase, Moi pora hokti ulai jaise.”

english_text: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling; and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
nagamese_text: Jitia mahila to luka bole napara hoise, tai bhoi pora kapi kene Jisu usorte girise. Sob manu usorte tai koi dise ki nimite tai Jisu ke choise, aru kineka tai ekbar pora bhal hoise.

english_text: He said to her, “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
nagamese_text: Jisu pora taike koise, “Swali, tumi laga biswas pora tumi bhal hoise. Shanti pora jabi.”

english_text: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”
nagamese_text: Aru Tai kotha koi thaka homoi te, synagogue laga kunba cholawta ghor pora ahise, aru koise, “Tumi laga swali to mori jaise. Sikhai diya manu ke aru dukh nadibi.”

english_text: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, “Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Jisu etu hunise, Tai eneka taike koise, “Bhoi na koribi; khali biswas koribi, aru tai changai hoi jabo.”

english_text: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai ghor te ahise, Tai kunke bhi bhitor te ahibole diya nai, khali Peter, John aru James, aru bacha laga ama aru baba ke he ahibole dise.

english_text: All were weeping and mourning her, but he said, “Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
nagamese_text: Aru sob manu monte dukh kori kene tai nimite kandi thakise, “Nakandibi, tai mora nai, kintu ghumai ase.”

english_text: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan Taike hasi dise, swali to morise bhabikena.

english_text: But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu, tai laga hath to dhorise aru matikena koise, “Bacha, uthibi!”

english_text: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.
nagamese_text: Titia tai laga atma wapas ahise aru tai uthikena kiba khabole mangise.

english_text: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.
nagamese_text: Tai laga ama aru baba asurit lagise, kintu Jisu pora taikhan ke ki hoise etu kunke bhi nakobi eneka koise.

english_text: He called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu baroh jon chela khan ke matise, Tai pora chela khan ke bhoot khan ke kheda bole aru bemar ke bhal kori bole laga hokti aru adhikar dise,

english_text: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
nagamese_text: aru Tai taikhan ke pathaise, bemar manu ke changai kori bole aru Isor rajyo laga kotha kobole nimite.

english_text: He said to them, “Take nothing for your journey—no staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money. Don’t have two tunics each.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Eku loi najabi- tumi laga jola, lathi, poisa aru bhaat, duita kapra bhi loi najabi.

english_text: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
nagamese_text: Juntu ghor te ghusi bo, ta te he thakibi, jitia tak etu jaga to nachare.

english_text: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”
nagamese_text: Jun jagate tumikhan ke namate, etu sheher pora ula homoi te, tumi laga theng pora dhuli to hatai dibi, etu he taikhan bhirodh te ekta sakhi hobo.”

english_text: They departed and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News and healing everywhere.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan alag hoi kene bosti khan phale jai jaise, Isor laga kotha prochar kori kene, sob jagate changai kori kene jaise.

english_text: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
nagamese_text: Jitia Herod raja pora etukhan sob hunise, tai bhoi hoi kene bhabona korise, kelemane kunba pora koise John to mora pora jinda hoise,

english_text: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
nagamese_text: aru kunba koise Elijah he ahise, aru kunba pora koise, poila laga bhabobadi ekjon jinda hoise.

english_text: Herod said, “I beheaded John, but who is this about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
nagamese_text: Kintu Herod koise, “Moi John laga matha alag kori dise, kintu etu kun ase jun laga moi iman kotha huni ase?” Aru tai Jisu ke sabole kosis kori thakise.

english_text: The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done. He took them and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia apostle khan wapas ahise, taikhan ki korise etu sob Jisu ke koi dise. Titia Jisu pora taikhan ke loi jaise, aru ekdom chup-chap pora Bethsaida sheher te taikhan sob jai jaise.

english_text: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia manu laga bhir khan etu hunise, taikhan bhi Jisu piche korise. Titia Tai sobke matise aru Isor laga rajyo kotha taikhan logote koise, aru jun manu changai lage, taikhan ke changai korise.

english_text: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms and lodge and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
nagamese_text: Etiya saam hobole homoi hoise, baroh jon chela khan Tai usorte ahikena koise, “Manu laga bhir khan ke pathai dibi, taikhan usor bosti te jai kene ghuma bole aru khabole bisaribo, kelemane moi khan eku napai-a jagate ase.”

english_text: But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan manu khan ke kiba khabole dibi.” Kintu taikhan koise, “Moi khan logote pasta roti aru duita maas he ase- jodi moi khan jai kene sob manu nimite khana kina nai koile.”

english_text: For they were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
nagamese_text: -Ta te panch hajar manu thakise.- Titia Tai pora chela khan ke koise, “Taikhan ke ekta bhag te pachas manu kori kene bohibo dibi.”

english_text: They did so, and made them all sit down.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan eneka korise aru sobke bohi bole dise.

english_text: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
nagamese_text: Pasta roti aru duita maas to hathte loi kene, Tai sorgo phale saise, dhonyabad dise aru bhangaikena chela khan ke dibole dise.

english_text: They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
nagamese_text: Taikhan sob khai kene bhorta hoise, aru bachi juwa sob uthaise- aru baroh ta tukri te uthaise.

english_text: As he was praying alone, the disciples were near him, and he asked them, “Who do the multitudes say that I am?”
nagamese_text: Aru ek din eneka hoise jitia Jisu Tai ekla pora prathana kori thakise, aru chela khan bhi Tai logote thakise, aru Tai taikhan ke hudise, “Manu khan pora Moi kun ase koi?”

english_text: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets has risen again.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan koise, “Baptizma Diya John Aru kunba koi Elijah, aru dusra khan pora koi purana homoi pora jinda huwa bhabobadi ekjon.”

english_text: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke koise, “Kintu tumikhan Moi kun ase koi?” Titia Peter he koise, “Isor laga Khrista.”

english_text: But he warned them and commanded them to tell this to no one,
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai pora taikhan ke etu kotha kunke bhi nokobole koise.

english_text: saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
nagamese_text: Tai koise, “Manu laga Putro bisi dukh pabo aru cholawta khan Taike swekar nakoribo, mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom likha khan pora bhi golti dhoribo aru Taike morai dibo, kintu Tai tin dinte arubi jinda hobo.”

english_text: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai sobke koise, “Kunba manu Moi pichete ahibole itcha thakile, tai nijorke pahoribo lage aru hodai cross uthaikene moi pichete ahibo lage.

english_text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake will save it.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai laga jibon to bacha bole kaam koribo tai harai dibo; kintu jun manu moi nimite jibon dibo, tai jibon pabo.

english_text: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
nagamese_text: Jibon te ki labh ase, sob duniya to paile bhi, nijor jibon to nuksan korile?

english_text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
nagamese_text: Kun manu moi laga kotha aru moi nimite sorom kore, jitia Manu laga Putro Tai nijor laga mohima aru Baba laga mohima aru pobitro sorgodoth khan laga mohima pora wapas ahibo, etu homoi te etu manu nimite moi bhi sorom hobo.

english_text: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here who will in no way taste of death until they see God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Kintu moi hosa kotha koi ase, kunba manu khan yate rukhi ase, taikhan Isor laga rajyo nadikha tak namoribo.”

english_text: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
nagamese_text: Etu kotha khan kowa ath din pichete, Tai tilla uporte prathana kori bole jaise, Peter, John aru James khan ke loi kene.

english_text: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai prathana kori thakise, Tai laga chehera bodli hoise, aru Tai laga kapra to asurit laga boga hoise.

english_text: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, duijon manu Tai logote kotha koi thakise, Moses aru Elijah thakise,

english_text: who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Mohima pora taikhan ahise, tai jabo laga kotha to patise, juntu Jerusalem te pura hoi jabo.

english_text: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.
nagamese_text: Jitia Peter aru sathi khan ghumai thakise, aru uthise, taikhan Tai laga mohima dikhise, aru duijon manu Tai logote khara hoi thaka dikhise.

english_text: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.
nagamese_text: Pichete eneka hoise, jitia duijon manu Jisu usor pora jai thakise, Peter Taike koise, “Probhu, amikhan yate tinta khamba bonabo, ekta apuni nimite, ekta Moses karone, aru ekta Elijah karone.” -Tai ki koi thakise tai najane.-

english_text: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia tai etu koise, ekta badal ahikena taikhan ke lukai dise, aru taikhan bhoi lagise.

english_text: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
nagamese_text: Aru akas pora ekta awaj ahise, “Etu Ami laga Putro ase, junke Moi basi loise; Tai laga kotha huni bhi.”

english_text: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.
nagamese_text: Jitia etu kotha khotom hoise, taikhan Jisu ekla thaka dikhise. Taikhan chup thakise aru ki dikhise kunke bhi kowa nai.

english_text: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.
nagamese_text: Aru ek dinte eneka hoise, jitia taikhan pahar upor pora nichete ahise, dangor bhir ke lok paise.

english_text: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only born child.
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, ekjon manu majot pora hala kori, koise, “Sikhai diya manu, moi anurodh korise, ami laga bacha ke sabi, tai moi laga ekjon bacha he ase.

english_text: Behold, a spirit takes him, he suddenly cries out, and it convulses him so that he foams; and it hardly departs from him, bruising him severely.
nagamese_text: Sabi, ekjon atma achanak pora dhori kene tai laga mukh pora letera thuk ulaise. Aru taike jokhom kori kene ulai jaise.

english_text: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they couldn’t.”
nagamese_text: Moi Apuni laga chela khan ke atma kheda bole anurodh korise, kintu taikhan kheda bole para nai.”

english_text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke jowab dise, “Biswas nathaka aru biya rasta te jai thaka manu khan, Moi tumikhan logote kiman din thakibo? Tumi laga chokra ke yate anibi.”

english_text: While he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him violently. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
