nagamese_text: Jitia chokra ke ani thakise, atma pora taike matite girai kene bisi hilai dise. Kintu Jisu pora dusto atma ke gali dise, aru chokra ke bhal kori dise, aru tai baba logot di dise.

english_text: They were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marveling at all the things which Jesus did, he said to his disciples,
nagamese_text: Taikhan Isor laga asurit kaam to dikhise. Kintu jitia manu khan ki hoise etu dikhise taikhan asurit lagise, Jisu tai laga chela khan ke koise,

english_text: “Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man will be delivered up into the hands of men.”
nagamese_text: “Etu kotha tumikhan mon bhitor te jabole dibi: kele koile Manu laga Putro ke manu laga hathte thogai pora di dibole ase.”

english_text: But they didn’t understand this saying. It was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan etu kotha bujhi bole para nai. Etu kotha taikhan pora lukai kene thakise, etu karone taikhan bujhi bole para nai, aru taikhan Jisu ke etu kotha hudibole bhoi lagise.

english_text: An argument arose among them about which of them was the greatest.
nagamese_text: Pichete chela khan majote kun he sob pora dangor hobo itu laga kotha ulaise.

english_text: Jesus, perceiving the reasoning of their hearts, took a little child, and set him by his side,
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan laga monte ki bhabona kori ase etu jani loise, aru ekjon chutu bacha ke Tai usorte uthai loise,

english_text: and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For whoever is least among you all, this one will be great.”
nagamese_text: aru taikhan ke koise, “Jun manu etu bacha ke Moi laga naam pora grohon kore, tai Moike grohon kore; aru jun manu Moike grohon kore, jun Moike pathaise Taike bhi grohon kore. Kun manu nijorke chutu koribo, tai he dangor hobo.”

english_text: John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he doesn’t follow with us.”
nagamese_text: John koise, “Probhu, amikhan dikhise kunba manu Apuni laga naam pora bhoot khedai se aru amikhan taike rukhai dise, kele koile tai moi khan logot nohoi.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Don’t forbid him, for he who is not against us is for us.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu pora taikhan ke koise, “Taikhan ke narukhabi, jun manu tumikhan bhirodh te nai, tai tumikhan logote ase.”

english_text: It came to pass, when the days were near that he should be taken up, he intently set his face to go to Jerusalem
nagamese_text: Etiya, Taike sorgote uthai loi jabole laga din to usorte hoise, Tai Jerusalem te jabole bisi mon hoise.

english_text: and sent messengers before his face. They went and entered into a village of the Samaritans, so as to prepare for him.
nagamese_text: Tai poila ekjon chela ke pathaise, aru taikhan Samaria bosti bhitor te punchi kene sob kaam taiyar korise.

english_text: They didn’t receive him, because he was traveling with his face set toward Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Kintu ta te thaka manu khan Taike grohon kora nai, kelemane tai Jerusalem te jabole he mon thakise.

english_text: When his disciples, James and John, saw this, they said, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from the sky and destroy them, just as Elijah did?”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia chela khan James aru John ke dikhise, taikhan koise, “Probhu, amikhan sorgo pora jui ahi kene taikhan ke khotom kori bole kobo naki?”

english_text: But he turned and rebuked them, “You don’t know of what kind of spirit you are.
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai ghuri kene taikhan ke gali dise,

english_text: For the Son of Man didn’t come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.” They went to another village.
nagamese_text: aru taikhan ta te pora alag bosti te jaise.

english_text: As they went on the way, a certain man said to him, “I want to follow you wherever you go, Lord.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan rasta te jai thaka homoi te, kunba ekjon Jisu ke koise, “Apuni kun jagate jabo moi bhi apuni logote jabo.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.”
nagamese_text: Jisu taike koise, “Siyal khan laga bhi gath ase aru akas te chiriya khan laga bhi ghor ase, hoile bhi Manu laga Putro laga matha rakhibole eku bhi jaga nai.”

english_text: He said to another, “Follow me!” But he said, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu aru ekjon ke koise, “Moi laga piche ahibi.” Kintu tai koise, “Probhu, poila moi jai kene moi laga baba ke kobor dikene ahibo.”

english_text: But Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai koise, “Mora khan pora mora khan ke kobor dibo. Kintu tumi, jai kene Isor laga rajyo prochar koribi.”

english_text: Another also said, “I want to follow you, Lord, but first allow me to say good-bye to those who are at my house.”
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon koise, “Moi bhi Apuni laga piche ahibo, Probhu, kintu moi poila jai kene sob ghor manu ke jai ase kobo.”

english_text: But Jesus said to him, “No one, having put his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu koise, “Jun manu kheti te hal dhori kene pichete nasai, tai he Isor laga rajyo nimite thik ase.”

english_text: Now after these things, the Lord also appointed seventy others, and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and place where he was about to come.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia etu sob kaam pura hoise, Probhu pora aru bhi bahatar manu ke mati kene Isor kaam nimite asirbad korise, aru duijon-duijon kori kene taikhan ke pathaise jun jagate Jisu nijor bhi jabo thakise.

english_text: Then he said to them, “The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest.
nagamese_text: Tai koise, “Kheti to bhorta hoise, kintu kaam kora manu olop he ase. Etu nimite kheti laga Probhu ke kobi, kaam kora manu pathai dibole nimite.

english_text: Go your ways. Behold, I send you out as lambs among wolves.
nagamese_text: Nijor rasta te jai thakibi, sabi, Moi tumikhan ke ekta mer khan nisena rong kutta usorte pathai ase.

english_text: Carry no purse, nor wallet, nor sandals. Greet no one on the way.
nagamese_text: Poisa laga jola nolobi, rasta te jabole laga jola bhi nolobi, aru nijor chapal bhi nolobi, aru rasta te jai thaka homoi te kunke bhi salam nadibi.

english_text: Into whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace be to this house.’
nagamese_text: Jun to ghor te poila ghusi bo, poila kobi, ‘Shanti etu ghor te thakibi!’

english_text: If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you.
nagamese_text: Jodi shanti laga chokra ta te ase koile, titia tumi laga shanti tai uporte thakibo; jodi nohoi, etu shanti tumi logote wapas ahijabo.

english_text: Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go from house to house.
nagamese_text: Etiya etu ghor te he thakibi, ki kha luwa di ase etu khai kene thakibi, kelemane ki kaam kori ase, etu laga labh to pabole lage. Aru ekta ghor pora alag ghor te jai nathaki bhi.

english_text: Into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat the things that are set before you.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan juntu sheher te jabo, jodi taikhan tumike grohon kore, titia tumikhan ke ki khabole diye, etu he khabi.

english_text: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
nagamese_text: Aru jun manu bemar ase taike changai koribi, aru taikhan ke kobi, ‘Isor laga rajyo tumikhan usorte ahise.’

english_text: But into whatever city you enter and they don’t receive you, go out into its streets and say,
nagamese_text: Kintu jun sheher te tumikhan ke namate etu laga rasta te ulaikene kobi,

english_text: ‘Even the dust from your city that clings to us, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless know this, that God’s Kingdom has come near to you.’
nagamese_text: ‘Juntu dhuli moi khan laga theng te lage etu bhi sapha kori ase tumikhan bhirodh te! Kintu etu jani lobi, Isor laga rajyo to usorte ahise.’

english_text: I tell you, it will be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase etu dinte tumikhan Sodom aru Gomorrah te dukh pa pora bhi bisi dukh pabo.

english_text: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
nagamese_text: Hai ase tumi, Chorazin sheher! Hai ase tumi, Bethsaida sheher! Jintu dangor kaam tumikhan nimite kori dise, etu kaam Tyre aru Sidon sheher khan nimite korise koile, taikhan poila pora mon ghurai kene thakibo.

english_text: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
nagamese_text: Kintu Tyre aru Sidon pora bhi bisi dukh tumikhan pabo, juntu dinte tumikhan logote Isor laga bisar hobo.

english_text: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.
nagamese_text: Aru tumi Capernaum town, tumike sorgote uthai loi najabo na, na uthai loijabo? Tumikhan ke ekdom niche, Hades te phelai dibo.

english_text: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
nagamese_text: Jun manu tumikhan laga kotha hune, taikhan Moike hune aru jun tumikhan ke ghin kore taikhan Moike ghin kore, aru jun Moike grohon nakore, tai kun pora Moike pathaise, Taike bhi grohon nakore.”

english_text: The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”
nagamese_text: Aru titia bahatar jon khushi pora jai kene koise, “Probhu, bhoot khan bhi Apuni laga naam te amikhan laga kotha mane.”

english_text: He said to them, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Moi sai thakise Saitan sorgo pora bhijili nisena girise.

english_text: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.
nagamese_text: Sabi, Moi tumikhan ke saph aru bhichoo khan ke khotom kori bole nimite takot dise, aru jiman dushman laga takot ase etu sob khan ke khotom kori bole nimite dise, aru eku pora bhi tumikhan ke jokhom kori bole napari bole dise.

english_text: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
nagamese_text: Hoilebi tumikhan etu dusto atma khan pora tumikhan laga kotha mani ase koi kene he khushi na koribi, kintu khushi koribi ki karone tumikhan laga naam sorgote likha ase.”

english_text: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.”
nagamese_text: Aru etu homoi te Jisu ke Pobitro Atma pora bisi khushi korise aru koise, “Moi Apuni ke dhanyavad di ase Baba, sorgo aru prithibi laga Probhu, kelemane Apuni etu sob kotha to gyaani aru bujhi bole pora manu khan logote lukai kene rakhise, aru etu sob kotha to chutu bacha khan ke janibole dise. Hoi Baba, etu sob Apuni usorte sabole bhal dikhe.”

english_text: Turning to the disciples, he said, “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”
nagamese_text: Etu sob kaam aru kotha to Moi laga Baba pora Moike dise, aru kun bhi najane Putro to kun ase, khali Baba he jane, aru kun Baba ase etu khali Putro pora he jane, aru kunke Putro pora mati lobo taike he sob to dikhai dibo.”

english_text: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai chela khan ke ghuri kene saise aru aste pora koise, “Dhonyo ase etu sukukhan, manu nadikha tumikhan ke sabo dise.

english_text: for I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, bisi bhabobadi aru raja khan tumikhan ki dikhise etu sabole nimite bisi itcha korise, kintu taikhan etu dikha nai, aru tumikhan ki hunise taikhan etu huni bole mon korise kintu taikhan huni bole panai.”

english_text: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, ekjon Yehudi laga niyom jana manu Jisu ke porikha kori bole nimite khara hoise aru, koise, “Probhu moi anonto jibon pabole nimite ki kori bole lage?”

english_text: He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu he taike koise, “Niom hisab te ki likha ase? Tumi etu kineka porhe?”

english_text: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
nagamese_text: Titia tai koise, “Tumi Probhu Isor ke pura mon pora morom koribi, aru tumi laga jibon pora, aru takot pora, aru tumi laga bhabona pora, aru tumi usorte thaka manu ke tumi nijorke kineka morom kore etu nisena morom koribi.

english_text: He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike koise, “Tumi thik kotha koise. Eneka koribi, aru tumi jinda thakibo.”

english_text: But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
nagamese_text: Kintu tai nijorke thik dikha bole nimite, Jisu ke koise, “Moi laga usorte thaka manu to kun ase?”

english_text: Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike jowab dikene koise, “Ekjon manu Jerusalem pora Jericho phale jai thakise. Taike chor aru dokait khan pora dhuri kene marise aru tai laga kapra phatai khan phatai dise aru taike adha mora chari kene polai jaise.

english_text: By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
nagamese_text: Titia achanak pora ekjon purohit etu rasta pora jai thakise, aru jitia tai etu manu ke dikhise, tai dusra phale jai jaise.

english_text: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena, ekjon Levi, jitia tai etu jagate ahikena manu ke dikhise, tai bhi dusra phale jai jaise.

english_text: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon Samaria laga manu, tai safar kori thaka homoi te, etu manu usorte ahise aru jitia taike dikhise, tai bisi mon dukh hoise aru morom lagi jaise.

english_text: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia etu manu usorte punchise, tai laga gaw te jokhom khan tel aru angur ros pora sapha kori kene bandi dise. Aru etu pichete, tai laga janwar uporte uthai dise, aru ekta ghor te loi jaise, aru taike bhal pora sai dise.

english_text: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
nagamese_text: Aru dusra dinte tai duita denari ulaikene ta te thaka manu khan ke dise aru koise, “Taike bhal pora sabi, aru ki khorcha korile bhi, jitia moi aru wapas ahibo, etu homoi te moi sob di dibo.’

english_text: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
nagamese_text: Tumi ki bhabe, taikhan tinjon bhitor te kun he tai laga asol usor thaka manu ase junke dokait aru chor khan pora mari kene chari dise?”

english_text: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Then Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
nagamese_text: Titia tai koise, “Taike morom kora jon pora.” Titia Jisu taike koise, “Jabi aru tumi bhi eneka he koribi.”

english_text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan jai thaka homoi te, Tai ekta bosti te ghusi se, aru ta te Martha koi kene ekjon mahila thakise, tai pora Jisu ke tai laga ghor te matise.

english_text: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard his word.
nagamese_text: Tai laga ekjon bhoini Mary koi kene thakise, aru tai Jisu laga theng usorte bohi kene Tai ki kotha koi ase etu huni thakise.

english_text: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Martha olop biya lagise kelemane tai sob kaam to ekla kori thakise, etu karone tai jai kene koise, “Probhu, Apuni eku chinta nakore naki moi laga bhoini moike kaam kori bole ekla chari dise? Etu nimite moike modot kori bole nimite taike kobi.”

english_text: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
nagamese_text: Titia Probhu pora Martha ke jowab dise, “Martha, Martha, tumi bisi alag kaam nimite chinta kori ase,

english_text: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
nagamese_text: kintu khali ekta kaam he bisi dorkar ase. Aru Mary pora etu bhal kaam bisari loise, aru etu tai logot pora kitia bhi loi najabo.”

english_text: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
nagamese_text: Aru ek din eneka hoise, Jisu ekta jagate prathana kori thakise, jitia khotom hoise, ekjon chela Taike hudise, “Probhu, amikhan ke prathana sikhai dibi jineka John tai laga chela khan ke sikhaise.”

english_text: He said to them, “When you pray, say, ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
nagamese_text: Tai chela khan ke koise, “Jitia tumikhan prathana koribo eneka kobi, ‘Sorgote thaka amikhan laga Baba, Apuni laga naam honmanio hobole dibi, Apuni laga rajyo ahibole dibi.

english_text: Give us day by day our daily bread.
nagamese_text: Hodai laga kha luwa amikhan ke dibi.

english_text: Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’”
nagamese_text: Amikhan laga paap pora amikhan ke maph kori dibi, Amikhan bhi dusra laga paap maph diya nisena Jun khan amikhan ke baki ase. Amikhan ke porikha te giribole nadibi.’”

english_text: He said to them, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan logote kun sathi ase, aru tai logote rati te jai kene koi, “Sathi, moike tinta roti dhaar dibi,

english_text: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
nagamese_text: kele koile moi laga ekjon sathi dusra jaga pora berai kene etiya ahise, moi taike dibole eku nai’?

english_text: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?
nagamese_text: Titia tai bhitor pora amike eneka kobo pare, ‘Moike etiya digdar nokoribi. Dorja to bondh hoise, aru moi aru bacha khan etiya ghumai ase. Moi etiya uthi kene tumike eku dibo na paribo.’

english_text: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
nagamese_text: Moi tumike koi ase, jodi bhi tai uthi kene tai laga sathi ke dibole mon nai, hoilebi tai mangi thaka karone, tai ji hoilebi uthi kene taike jiman lage etu di dibo.

english_text: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
nagamese_text: Moi aru bhi tumike koi ase, mangibi, aru tumi pabo; bisaribi, aru tumi pai jabo, dorjate khat-khata bhi, etu khuli jabo.

english_text: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
nagamese_text: Jun manu mange tai pai; jun manu bisare tai pai; aru jun manu khatai, taike khuli diye.

english_text: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
nagamese_text: Tumikhan majote kun baba eneka ase naki, jodi tai laga bacha pora maas mangile, taike saph dibo?

english_text: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?
nagamese_text: Aru jodi anda mangile, taike bhichoo dibo naki?

english_text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
nagamese_text: Etu karone, tumikhan biya manu hoilebi nijor bacha ke bhal saman he dibole jane, tenehoile sorgote thaka Baba Isor ke kun manu pora mange, taike Pobitro Atma nadibo naki?”

english_text: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled.
nagamese_text: Ek din, Jisu ekta gunga kori diya bhoot ke khedai thakise. Aru jitia bhoot to ulai jaise, etu manu kotha kobo parise, aru ta te thaka manu khan asurit hoise.

english_text: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba manu khan koise, “Tai bhoot ke Beelzebul laga naam pora khedai ase jun he bhoot khan laga raja ase.”

english_text: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra manu khan, Jisu ke porikha kori kene koise, sorgo pora ekta asurit kaam dikha bole koise.

english_text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
nagamese_text: Kintu, taikhan laga bhabona jani kene Jisu pora koise, “Juntu rajyo alag-alag bhabona hoi kene ase, etu bhangi jabo, aru ekta ghor alag-alag bhabona hoile, etu ghor bhangi jabo.

english_text: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi Saitan bhi alag-alag hoijai, eneka hoile tai laga rajyo kineka khara hobo? Tumikhan koi ase Moi Beelzebul laga takot pora bhoot khan ke khedai.

english_text: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
nagamese_text: Jodi Moi bhoot khan ke Beelzebul takot pora khedai ase koile, titia hoile tumikhan laga chela khan kun laga atma pora bhoot khan ke khedai? Etu karone, eitu khan he tumikhan ke bisar koribo.

english_text: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
nagamese_text: Jodi Moi bhoot khan ke Isor laga anguli pora khedai, titia hoile Isor laga rajyo to tumikhan usorte ahise.

english_text: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
nagamese_text: Jitia ekta takot thaka manu pora hathiar loi kene ghor to rukhi thake, tai laga ki ase etu naharai.

english_text: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
nagamese_text: Kintu tai pora bhi bisi takot thaka manu taike hamla korile, taike harai dibo, tai laga hathiar bhi loi lobo, jun uporte tai bharosa kore, aru ji dhun sompoti tai laga ase, sob bhag hoi jabo.

english_text: “He who is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
nagamese_text: Kun manu Moi logote nathake, Moi laga bhirodh te ase, aru kun manu Moi logote nathake, tai alag hoijai.

english_text: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’
nagamese_text: Jitia ekta dusto atma ekjon manu pora ulai jai, tai sukha jagate aram pabole karone berai thake, aru koi, ‘Moi poila kot pora ulaise ta te aru bhi wapas jai jabo.’

english_text: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai ahe, tai sob sapha aru bhal kore kene rakhi thaka dikhe.

english_text: Then he goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
nagamese_text: Tai jai kene tai pora bhi aru bisi biya sat-ta dusto atma loi kene etu manu bhitor te ghusi jai. Aru poila pora bhi etu manu laga jibon to bisi biya hoijai.”

english_text: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
nagamese_text: Etiya eneka hoise, jitia Tai etu kotha koi thakise, ekjon mahila awaj uthaikene manu khan usorte Jisu ke koise, “Dhonyo ase etu ama jun Apuni ke jonom dise aru dudh khilai se.”

english_text: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai koise, “Hoilebi, asishit hobo jun manu Isor kotha huni kene mani thake.”

english_text: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
nagamese_text: Manu laga bhir jitia bisi hoise, Tai kobole shuru hoise, “Etu manu khan paap laga khandan ase. Taikhan kiba ekta sabole bisari thake, kintu, asurit kaam to taikhan ke nadikhabo, khali Jonah laga chihna he nohoile.

english_text: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.
nagamese_text: Jineka Jonah to Nineveh sheher laga manu khan nimite ekta chihna hoise, etu nisena Manu laga Putro bhi manu khan nimite eneka hobo.

english_text: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
nagamese_text: Dakshin laga Rani bisar dinte uthi kene etiya laga manu khan ke bisar koribo, kele tai duniya laga kona pora Solomon raja laga gyaan kotha huni bole ahisele aru sabi Solomon pora bhi mohan ekjon yate ase.

english_text: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
nagamese_text: Nineveh sheher laga manu khan uthaikene etiya laga manu khan ke bisar koribo, kelemane taikhan mon ghuraise Jonah prochar kora homoi te aru sabi, Jonah pora bhi mohan ekjon yate ase.

english_text: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
nagamese_text: Kun bhi saaki to jolai kene lukai narakhe kintu saaki rakha jagate rakhe, aru kun manu ghor bhitor te ahe, puhor to dikhi pai.

english_text: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
nagamese_text: Tumi suku to gaw laga diya ase. Jitia tumi laga suku bhal thake, tumi laga pura gaw to pohor pora bhorta hoi. Kintu jitia biya hoi jaise, tumi laga gaw bhi pura andhar hoijai.

english_text: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, bisi hoshiar hoi jabi etu pora tumi laga jibon to andhar nohobo nimite.

english_text: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
nagamese_text: Jodi tumi laga gaw to ujala pora bhorta hoijai, aru kun jagate bhi andhar nai, titia etu puhor pora bhorta hoi jabo, jineka tumi uporte puhor to bhorta hoi thakibo.”

english_text: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in and sat at the table.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai kotha kora khotom hoise ekjon Pharisee pora Taike khana khabole matise. Aru Jisu tai logote khabole bohise.

english_text: When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.
nagamese_text: Aru Pharisee khan etu dikhi kene asurit hoise, kelemane Jisu to bhaat kha age te, Tai laga hath Yehudi niyom hisab de thaka nisina dhula nai.

english_text: The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
nagamese_text: Kintu Probhu taike koise, “Tumi Pharisee khan kup aru borton laga bahar to sapha kore, kintu tumikhan mon bhitor te biya aru lalchi pora bhorta thake.

english_text: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
nagamese_text: Murkho manu khan! Jun he tumi laga bahar to bonaise, tai he tumi laga bhitor bhi bonaise nohoi?

english_text: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumi bhitor laga morom to dikhai dibi, aru sabi, tumi laga jibon te sob to sapha hoi jabo.

english_text: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan, tumikhan ke hai ase. Tumikhan kheti laga sobji aru bagan te thaka pata khan loi kene dos bhag diye, kintu Isor laga morom to namane. Kintu etu kori bole dorkar ase, aru dusra bhal kaam bhi nacharibo lage.

english_text: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
nagamese_text: Pharisee khan, tumikhan ke hai ase. Tumikhan mondoli te sobse bhal jagate bohi bole mon kore aru bajar te manu bhoi pora salam diya to khushi pai.

english_text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
nagamese_text: Tumikhan ke hai ase, tumikhan nadikha laga kobor nisena ase, etu uporte manu khan najanikena berai thake.”

english_text: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
nagamese_text: Titia ekjon niyom jana manu Jisu ke koise, “Probhu, etu koi kene, Apuni amikhan ke sorom khilai ase.”

english_text: He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu jowab dise, “Hai tumikhan, niyom laga hikhok khan! Tumikhan manu khan ke bhari bhar bukhi bole diye juntu taikhan bukhi bole napare, kintu tumikhan laga anguli pora nijor bhi etu bhar to bukhi bole mon nai.

english_text: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan ke hai ase, bhabobadi khan laga kobor to bonaise, hoilebi tumikhan baba laga baba khan pora he taikhan ke moraise.

english_text: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
nagamese_text: Hosa koile, tumikhan baba laga baba khan pora ki korise etu laga tumikhan sakhi ase, taikhan pora morai dise aru tumikhan kobor khan bonaise.

english_text: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
nagamese_text: Etu karone Isor laga gyaan pora sob koi dise, ‘Moi taikhan logot bhabobadi khan aru apostle khan ke pathabo, aru taikhan pora Moi patha khan ke dukh dibo aru kunba ke morai dibo.’

english_text: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
nagamese_text: Etu karone, duniya shuru pora jiman bhabobadi khan laga khun giraise, sob laga bisar etiya laga jamana khan logote koribo.

english_text: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
nagamese_text: Abel laga khun pora shuru kori kene Zechariah laga khun tak, junke pobitro jagate moraise. Hoi, Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etu sob hisab to etiya laga jamana pora dibo lagibo.

english_text: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
nagamese_text: Kanun hikhok khan ke hai ase. Tumikhan Isor ke janibole gyaan laga chabi to loi kene rakhise; tumikhan nijor bhi etu bhitor te najai aru kun manu jabole mon kore, tumikhan pora taikhan ke bhi jabo nadiye.”

english_text: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him,
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu ta te pora ulai jaise, niyom likha khan aru Pharisee khan etu sob kotha to huni kene khong uthise aru Tai logote jhagara korise,

english_text: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.
nagamese_text: taikhan rukhi thakise, Jisu kiba ekta golti kotha koile, Taike phasabo koi kene.

english_text: Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
nagamese_text: Eneka homoi te, hajar-hajar manu eke logote joma hoise, eneka somoite hazar manu joma huwa karone manu khan ekjon-ekjon uporte girise, Tai chela khan ke poila koise, “Pharisee khan laga chalaki pora hoshiar hobi, kelemane taikhan chalak ase.

english_text: But there is nothing covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.
nagamese_text: Eku kotha lukai rakhibole na paribo, kintu bhitor te thaka kotha to sob ulai jabo.

english_text: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
nagamese_text: Etu karone ki kotha andhar te koise, ujala te sob hunibo aru tumi ghor bhitor te ki kotha khan ki koise etu kotha ghor uporte awaj uthaikene kobo.

english_text: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase moi laga sathi khan, bhoi nakori bhi jun manu tumi laga gaw to morai dibo, aru etu pichete taikhan eku koribo na paribo.

english_text: But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan ke koi dibo Isor ke tumikhan bhoi kori bole lage. Morai diya pichete, norokte phela bole jun laga takot ase, taike bhoi koribi. Hosa Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Isor ke he bhoi koribi.

english_text: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.
nagamese_text: Aru pansta ghor laga chiriya khan ke dui poisa pora bikiri nakore naki? Hoilebi eitu khan ke bhi Isor napahore.

english_text: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan matha laga chuli bhi ekta-ekta pora ginti kori kene ase. Bhoi nokoribi. Tumikhan to ghor te thaka chiriya pora bhi bisi daam laga ase.

english_text: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God;
nagamese_text: Moi aru bhi tumikhan ke kobo, jun manu Moike manu khan usorte paap shikar kore, Manu laga Putro bhi sorgodoth usorte taikhan ke shikar koribo,

english_text: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of God’s angels.
nagamese_text: kintu jun pora manu khan usorte Moike namatibo, Moi bhi sorgodoth usorte taike namatibo.

english_text: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
nagamese_text: Jun manu Moi laga bodnam koribo tai maph pabo, kintu kun manu Pobitro Atma ke bodnam koribo tai kitia bhi maph napabo.

english_text: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer or what you will say;
nagamese_text: Etu karone jitia taikhan tumikhan ke mondoli khan te, aru cholawta khan aru adhikari khan usorte loijabo, titia tumikhan laga safai te ki kobo lage etu karone chinta nokoribi,

english_text: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”
nagamese_text: tumikhan ki kobo lage Pobitro Atma pora etu homoi te sob sikhai dibo.”

english_text: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
nagamese_text: Titia kunba ekjon manu majot pora Jisu ke koise, “Probhu, moi laga bhai ke kobi tai laga dhun sompoti bhag kori kene moike dibole.”

english_text: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike koise, “Manu, tumikhan uporte bhag aru bisar kori bole Moi kun koise?”

english_text: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
nagamese_text: Tai manu khan ke koise, “Lalchi aru biya itcha pora nijorke bachai kene rakhibi, sob thakile bhi manu laga jibon dhun sompoti bisi thaka para nohoi.”

english_text: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise, “Ekjon dhuni manu laga mati ke bhal kheti ulaise,

english_text: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
nagamese_text: etu manu monte bhabikena korise, moi ki koribo, kheti bisi bhal hoise aru rakhibole jaga nai?’

english_text: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
nagamese_text: Kintu tai koise, ‘Moi eneka koribo: dhaan ghor to bhangai kene dangor ghor bonabo aru ta te moi laga dhaan aru sob bhal saman rakhibo.

english_text: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
nagamese_text: Aru moi laga mon ke kobo, “Oh mon, bisi saal nimite kha luwa joma kori kene rakhise. Kha luwa kori kene, khushi koribi.’”

english_text: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
nagamese_text: Kintu Isor he taike koise, ‘Murkho manu, aji rati tumi laga atma uthai lobo, aru ki dhun sompoti tumi joma kori kene rakhise, etu kun laga hobo?’

english_text: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
nagamese_text: Eneka he hobo utu manu logote jun nijor nimite dhun sompoti joma kore, kintu Isor phale dhuni nohoi.”

english_text: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu tai laga chela khan ke koise, “Etu nimite Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, nijor laga jibon nimite chinta nokoribi, ki khabo aru ki pindhibo, nijor gaw nimite chinta nokoribi.

english_text: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jibon to kha luwa pora bhi dangor ase, aru tumi laga kapra pora bhi dangor to tumi laga gaw ase.

english_text: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
nagamese_text: Sabi akas te uri thaka chiriya khan ke, taikhan kheti bhi nakate. Aru taikhan laga dhaan rakhibole jaga bhi nai, kintu Isor he taikhan ke khabole diye. Tinehoile tumikhan chiriya pora bhi daam laga ase.

english_text: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan majot te kun he chinta kori kene jibon to lamba kori bole paribo?

english_text: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
nagamese_text: Aru jodi tumikhan etu chutu kaam bhi kori bole napare koile, tenehoile dusra kaam nimite kele chinta kori ase?

english_text: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
nagamese_text: Sabi kheti te lili phul to kineka dangor hoi. Taikhan kheti bhi nakore aru joma bhi nakore. Hoilebi Moi tumike koi ase, Solomon ekta dangor raja hoilebi lili phul nisena sundur hobo para nai.

english_text: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
nagamese_text: Kintu kheti laga ghas khan juntu aji ase aru kali to chulah te phelai dibo, hoilebi sabi, Isor pora eitu khan sundur pora bonaise, O biswas natakha manu khan, eitu khan pora bhi tumikhan ke sundur nabonabo naki!

english_text: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan ki kha luwa koribo etu nimite chinta nokoribi.

english_text: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
nagamese_text: Etu prithibi manu kunkhan Isor najane, taikhan he eitu khan pichete berai thake, kintu etu tumi nimite dorkar ase koi kene Baba Isor he sob jane.

english_text: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
nagamese_text: Poila Isor laga rajyo bisaribi, titia sob tumikhan ke hali dibo.

english_text: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
nagamese_text: Komti manu khan, bhoi nokoribi, kelemane Baba pora tumikhan ke rajyo dibole khushi ase.

english_text: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan logote ki ase sob bikiri kori kene gorib khan ke de dibi. Jun jagate chor nahibo aru puka pora nakhabo, sorgote tumi laga dhun sompoti joma kora to kitia bhi naharabo.

english_text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun jagate tumi laga dhun sompoti thake, etu jagate mon to hodai thake.

english_text: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
nagamese_text: Tumi laga komor to bandhi lobi, aru saaki to jolai rakhibi,

english_text: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
nagamese_text: aru eneka manu khan nisena hobi jun khan malik ke shadi pora wapas ahibole rukhi thake, aru jitia tai ahi kene dorwaja te mare, taikhan phot kori dorwaja to khuli bole pare.

english_text: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
nagamese_text: Asirbad ase etu noukar khan jun malik aha homoi te rukhi kene thake. Hosa pora moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Tai laga pet te kapra bandi kene taikhan ke khabole jagate bohai dibo, aru Tai ahikena nijor pora taikhan ke kha luwa khabole dibo.

english_text: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.
nagamese_text: Aru malik adha rati te, nohoile bisi phojurte ahile bhi, tai noukar khan pora rukhi thaka dikhile, etu noukar to asirbad ase.

english_text: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu jani lobi, jodi malik to tai laga ghor te chor kitia ahibo etu jani loi, titia tai kitia bhi ghor te chor hobole nadibo.

english_text: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
nagamese_text: Tumikhan bhi taiyar kori thakibi, kelemane Manu laga Putro ki homoi te ahibo tumi kobo napare.”

english_text: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
nagamese_text: Titia Peter koise, “Probhu, Apuni etu dristanto moi khan ke koi ase na, sobke bhi koi ase?”

english_text: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
nagamese_text: Probhu koise, “Tinehoile kun taikhan majote gyaani imandar noukar ase junke malik pora basi lobo tai laga dusra nokorkhan ke sabole, taikhan laga kha luwa thik homoi te dibole?

english_text: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
nagamese_text: Asirbad ase etu noukar jitia tai laga malik ahikena taike kaam kora dikhe.

english_text: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
nagamese_text: Moi hosa koi ase tai etu noukar ke tai laga sob dhun sompoti to sabole di dibo.

english_text: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi noukar tai laga monte bhabe, ‘Moi laga malik to ahibole bisi homoi loi ase,’ aru noukar khan ke mari bole shuru hoi, aru kha luwa kori kene, aru nisa te giri thake,

english_text: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
nagamese_text: aru titia tai laga malik achanak pora ahijai, jun to homoi te tai bhabona kori thaka nai, titia malik pora taike kati phelai dibo aru tai laga bodli dusra bhal ke kaam to di dibo.

english_text: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
nagamese_text: Aru jun noukar tai malik laga itcha to jane, kintu malik laga itcha nisena eku kori kene nathake, titia hoile taike marikena bisi dukh dibo.

english_text: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
nagamese_text: Kintu jun manu eku najane, hoilebi mar kha laga kaam to kori thakise taikhan olop he mari khabo. Kintu jun manu ke bisi dikena ase, taikhan logote pora bisi pabo lage, aru jun manu ke kaam bisi dikena ase, tai logote pora etu sob kaam laga hisab mangibo.

english_text: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
nagamese_text: Moi etu duniya te jui phela bole ahise, aru Moi etu he itcha ase etu shuru hoijai kene thakibo nimite.

english_text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
nagamese_text: Moi baptizma pora baptizma kori bole ase, aru Moi chinta te ase jitia tak etu pura nohoi!

english_text: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan bhabise naki Moi etu prithibi te shanti dibole ahise? Nohoi, Moi hosa koi ase, kintu sob bhag hoi jabo.

english_text: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
nagamese_text: Etiya pora ghor te pans jon bhi bhag hoi jabo- tinjon bhitor te te duijon aru duijon bhitor te tinjon dushman hoi jabo.

english_text: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
nagamese_text: Taikhan alag hoi jabo, baba pora bacha khan ke chari bo, aru bacha khan bhi baba ke chari bo; ama pora chukri ke chari bo aru chukri bhi ama laga dushman hobo, saas pora buari ke chari bo aru, buari bhi saas ke chari bo.”

english_text: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
nagamese_text: Etiya Jisu manu khan ke koise, “Tumikhan jitia paschim phale badal utha dikhe, ‘Borkhon ahise, aru etu ahijai.

english_text: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia dakshin laga hawa mare, tumikhan koi, ‘Bisi gorom ahibo, aru etu hoijai.

english_text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
nagamese_text: O Dhungi khan! Akas prithibi te ki dikhe etu kobole jane, kintu kele tumikhan aha dinte ki hobole ase etu kobo napare?

english_text: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan nijor bhi hosa to ki ase etu bisar nakore?

english_text: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
nagamese_text: Tumi dushman logote bisar kori bole ja homoi te, rasta te he etu jhagara to faisla kori bole itcha koribi, nohoile tumike tanikena bisar ghor te loijabo, tumike daruga hathte di dibo, aru daruga pora tumike bondhi ghor te hali dibo.

english_text: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumike koi ase, tumi poisa laga sob hisab kitab pura nakora tak tumi etu koidi ghor pora ulabole na paribo.”

english_text: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba manu khan etu homoi te Jisu ke eneka khobor dise ki Pilate pora bolidan kora homoi te tai Galilee manu khan ke morai dikena taikhan laga khun bhi milai dise.

english_text: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan bhabise naki etu Galilee manu khan dusra Galilee manu khan pora bhi bisi paapi khan ase kelemane taikhan eneka dukh paise?

english_text: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
nagamese_text: Nohoi, Moi tumikhan ke hosa kobo. Jodi tumikhan mon naghurai, tumikhan bhi eneka he khotom hoi jabo.

english_text: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
nagamese_text: Aru atharo jon manu kunkhan uporte Siloam laga minar giri kene mari dise, tumikhan bhabise naki Jerusalem te thaka manu khan pora bhi taikhan he bisi paapi thakise?

english_text: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
nagamese_text: Nohoi, Moi tumikhan ke koi ase. Jodi tumikhan mon naghuraile, taikhan nisena khotom hoi jabo.”

english_text: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu ekta dristanto koise, “Ekjon manu tai laga bagan te dimoru ghas rupaisile, aru tai etu ghas te phol bisarikena jaise, kintu eku pa-a nai.

english_text: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’
nagamese_text: Titia tai bagan sa-a manu ke koise, ‘Sabi, tin saal moi etu ghas te phol bisari kene ahise, kintu eku pa-a nai. Etu ke kati dibi. Etu mati to kele nuksan koribo?’

english_text: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
nagamese_text: Titia noukar pora malik ke eneka jowab dise, ‘Probhu, etu saal nimite chari dibi, moi aru ekbar bhal pora etu ghas to mol dikene sabo.

english_text: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
nagamese_text: Jodi etu ghas pora etu somoi nisena te phol diye, to bhal ase, kintu jodi etu pora bhal phol diya nai koile, apuni etu ghas to kati dibi!’”

english_text: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
nagamese_text: Aru ek Bisram dinte Jisu mondoli khan te hikai thakise,

english_text: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te ekjon mahila atharo saal pora komjur laga atma thakise, tai laga komor to tera thakise aru ekdom sidha koribo napari kene thakise.

english_text: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu taike dikhise, Tai usorte mati kene koise, “Mahila, tumi laga komjur pora tumi mukti paise.”

english_text: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu tai laga hath etu mahila uporte rakhise, aru etu homoi te tai sida hoi jaise aru tai Isor ke dhanyavad dise.

english_text: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
nagamese_text: Kintu mondoli te thaka cholawta khan bhal pa-a nai aru Jisu pora Bisram dinte changai kaam kora nimite manu khan ke koise, “Choi din tak kaam kori bole dorkar ase. Etu homoi te he bhal hobole ahibi, kintu Bisram dinte nahibi.”

english_text: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?
nagamese_text: Kintu Probhu taikhan ke koise, “Dhongi khan! Tumikhan Bisram dinte tumikhan laga guru, saguli khan ke tai laga ghor pora ulaikene pani khabole loi najai naki?

english_text: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
nagamese_text: Etu mahila, Abraham laga khandan pora ahise, junke Saitan para atharo saal tak bandhi kene rakhise, tenehoile taike Bisram dinte khuli nadibo lage naki?”

english_text: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai etu kotha kori kene khotom hoise, jun Jisu ke ghusa kori thakise taikhan sorom lagi jaise, kintu sob manu khan khushi kori kene dhanyavad di thakise juntu kaam Tai kori kene dikhai diya karone.

english_text: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu koise, “Isor laga rajyo to kineka ase, aru Moi etu ke ki logote tulona koribo?

english_text: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
nagamese_text: Etu ekta sorso dana nisena ase jineka ekjon manu pora loi kene tai laga kheti te phelaise, aru etu dangor ghas hoi jaise, aru ta te chiriya khan bhi ahikena ghor bonaise.”

english_text: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
nagamese_text: Aru Tai koise, “Isor laga rajyo to ki logote tulona koribo?

english_text: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”
nagamese_text: Ekjon mahila pora tin kilo atta te khomir hali dise, jitia tak etu phuli najai.”

english_text: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu nogor aru bosti khan te jai kene hikai thakise aru Jerusalem te jabo nimite taiyar kori thakise.

english_text: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?” He said to them,
nagamese_text: Etiya ekjon pora Taike hudise, “Probhu, jun poritran pai ase taikhan olop jon he ase naki?” Titia Tai taikhan ke koise,

english_text: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.
nagamese_text: “Etu chutu rasta te jabole nimite dukh koribi, kelemane Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, bisi manu etu te ghusi bole kosis koribo, kintu ghusi bole na paribo.

english_text: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
nagamese_text: Jitia ghor laga malik pora dorwaja to bondh kori dibo, titia tumi dorja to marikena kobo, ‘Probhu, moi khan nimite khuli bhi.’ Kintu tai tumikhan ke kobo, ‘Moi tumikhan ke najane, aru tumikhan kot pora ase.’

english_text: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
nagamese_text: Titia tumi he kobo, ‘Amikhan Apuni logote bohi kene eke logote khai sele, aru Apuni amikhan laga jagate ahikena sikhai dise.’

english_text: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’
nagamese_text: Titia Tai kobo, ‘Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Moi tumikhan kot pora ahise najane. Moi usor pora dur hoi jabi sob biya kaam kora khan!’

english_text: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
nagamese_text: Etu jagate, kanda he thakibo, aru dath chababo aru jitia Abraham, Isaac aru Jacob aru sob bhabobadi khan ke Isor laga rajyo to dikhibo, kintu etu pora tumikhan ke bahar te phelai dibo.

english_text: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
nagamese_text: Taikhan purab, paschim, uttor aru dakshin pora ahikena Isor laga rajyote bohibo.

english_text: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, kun manu pichete thakise taikhan age te ase, aru kunba jun age te ase, taikhan pichete hoi jabo.”

english_text: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te, kunba Pharisee khan Tai usorte ahikena koise, “Amikhan ke chari bhi aru yate pora jai jabi, kelemane Herod tumike morai dibole bisari ase.”

english_text: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Jai kene utu siyal Herod ke kobi, ‘Sabi, Moi bhoot khan ke khedai dise aru bemar khan ke aji aru kali bhal korise, aru tin din pichete Moi laga lakshya punchi jabo.’

english_text: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
nagamese_text: Jineka hoile bhi Moi kaam kori thakibo, aji, kali aru aha dinte bhi, kele koile Jerusalem te bhabobadi khan harai ja-a to bhal nai.

english_text: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
nagamese_text: Oh Jerusalem, Jerusalem, kun he bhabobadi khan ke morai diye aru tumikhan usorte ahile pathor pora mari kene pathai diye. Moi kiman itcha korise tumikhan laga bacha khan ke eke logote rakhibole nimite jineka ekta murgi tai laga bacha khan ke pakhi nichete rakhe. Kintu tumikhan etu itcha nakore.

english_text: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
nagamese_text: Sabi, tumikhan laga ghor to khali hoi jaise. Kile Moi kobo, tumikhan Moike aru nadikhibo etu homoi naha tak, jitia tumikhan kobo, ‘Asirbad pabo jun Probhu laga naam te ahise.’”

english_text: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise, Jisu ekjon Pharisee khan laga ghor te Bisram dinte bhaat khabole jaise, aru Jisu ki kori ase etu sob bhal pora taikhan sai thakise.

english_text: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te ekjon manu thakise jun gaw phula bemar pora dukh pai thakise.

english_text: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu Pharisee khan aru Yehudi niyom jana manu khan ke hudi kene koise, “Bisram dinte changai kori bole pare na nai?”

english_text: But they were silent. He took him, and healed him, and let him go.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan eku kowa nai, titia Jisu taike dhorise aru changai kori dise, aru taike pathai dise.

english_text: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai pora taikhan ke hudise, “Tumikhan majote kunba tai laga bacha nahoile bhi tai laga janwar Bisram dinte panite giri le jai kene phot uthai nolobo naki?”

english_text: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.
nagamese_text: Taikhan etu kotha te eku jowab dibo para nai.

english_text: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai arubi taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise, jun khan ke khabole mati sele, taikhan kineka kori kene bhal jagate bohi bole pabo, etu kosis kori thakise.

english_text: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
nagamese_text: Jitia tumikhan ke shadi te khabole mate, tumikhan bhal jagate nabohibi, kele koile tumikhan pora bhi kunba bisi sonman thaka manu ke mati kene thakibo pare,

english_text: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
nagamese_text: aru jitia tumi aru dusra manu junke khana te matise, tai tumikhan ke kobo, ‘Tumi laga jaga to taike dibi,’ aru titia sorom pora taike etu jaga to dikene tumi chutu jagate he bohi jai.

english_text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
nagamese_text: Jitia, tumike mate, jabi aru sobse chutu jagate he bohibi, jitia jun pora tumike matise tai ahibo, tai tumike kobo, ‘Sathi, uporte ahibi.’ Titia tumi laga sonman to dusra manu bohi thaka usorte bisi hoijai.

english_text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
nagamese_text: Jun manu nijorke dangor kori bole bisare tai chutu hoi jabo, aru jun manu tai nijorke chutu kore taike uthai dibo.”

english_text: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
nagamese_text: Titia tai etu manu ke kobo jun he taike matise, “Jitia tumi kha luwa koribo, tumi laga bhal sathi khan, bhai khan aru dhuni manu ke namatibi, nohoile taikhan bhi tumike matibo, aru tumi taikhan nimite ki korise etu he apuni pabo.

english_text: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia tumi kha luwa kore, gorib khan, bera bole napara, andha aru bemar manu khan ke mati bhi,

english_text: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
nagamese_text: aru tumikhan asirbad pabo, kelemane taikhan tumike ghurai kene eku dibole na paribo. Kintu tumikhan ke Jisu Khrista wapas lobole aha homoi te biswasi khan logote sob kaam laga inam dibo.”

english_text: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
nagamese_text: Jitia jun ekjon mez te bohi thakise aru eitu khan huni thakise, tai Jisu ke koise, “Dhonyo ase jun Isor laga rajyote roti khabo!”

english_text: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise, “Ekjon manu dangor kha luwa bonai kene manu khan ke matise.

english_text: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
nagamese_text: Aru jitia khabole homoi ahise, tai laga noukar khan ke pathai kene jun manu khan ke matise taikhan ke koise, ‘Ahibi, sob to taiyar hoi jaise.’

english_text: They all as one began to make excuses. “The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’
nagamese_text: Kintu mata khan sob nijor bahana kori bole shuru hoise. Poila ekjon pora koise, ‘Moi ekta kheti kinise, aru moi ta te jai kene sabo lagibo. Morom pora biya napabi.’

english_text: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon pora koise, moi pansta guru kinise, moi taikhan ke kheti te loijai kene ekbar sabo. Morom pora biya napabi.’

english_text: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
nagamese_text: Aru dusra ekjon pora koise, ‘Moi ekjon maiki logote shadi korise, aru etu nimite moi ahibole na paribo.’

english_text: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
nagamese_text: Titia noukar khan sob kotha to tai laga malik ke ahikena koise. Ghor laga malik khong uthi kene, noukar khan ke koise, ‘Bahar te joldi jabi aru bosti rasta pora gorib manu, bera bole napara, suku andha aru bemar manu ke loi anibi.’

english_text: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
nagamese_text: Sewak pora etu kaam kori kene tai koise, ‘Probhu Apuni ki koise eneka kori dise, aru bhi alohi manu bisi karone jaga ase.’

english_text: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
nagamese_text: Titia malik tai laga noukar khan ke koise, ‘Bahar te jabi aru rasta kinar aru jun jaga pora hoile taikhan ke mati kene loi anibi, Moi laga ghor to bhorta hobo lage.

english_text: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, jun manu khan ke Moi poila mati sele taikhan Moi ki kha luwa bonaise etu khabole napabo.’”

english_text: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,
nagamese_text: Aru bisi manu khan Jisu laga pichete jai thakise, aru Tai ghuri kene taikhan ke koise,

english_text: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
nagamese_text: “Jun manu Moi logote ahibole itcha ase kintu tai nijor laga baba, ama, maiki, bacha, bhai, bhoini aru nijor jibon to ghin nakore, tai Moi laga chela hobole na paribo.

english_text: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai nijor laga Cross uthaikene Moi pichete nahe tai Moi laga chela hobole na paribo.

english_text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
nagamese_text: Jun manu ekta ghor bona bole itcha kore, poila tai bohi kene, tai logote thaka poisa pora ghor bona khotom koribo paribona nai koi kene ginti nakore naki?

english_text: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
nagamese_text: Jitia, tai ghor laga bhetimul to uthai dibo, aru ghor to khotom kori bole naparile, sob manu saikene taike hasi dibo,

english_text: saying, ‘This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
nagamese_text: aru kobo, etu manu ghor to bona bole shuru korise kintu khotom kori bole para nai.’

english_text: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon raja, dusra raja logote lorai kori bole ase, tai poila bohi kene nasabo naki, tai laga dos hajar manu pora dusra raja laga bis hajar logote lorai koribo paribona nai?

english_text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.
nagamese_text: Kintu, tai dur te thaka homoi te, ekjon manu ke shanti pora kotha kori kene lorai to rukhai dibo.

english_text: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena, jun manu tai laga sob dhun sompoti chari kene nahile, tai Moi laga chela hobole na paribo.

english_text: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
nagamese_text: Etu nimite nimok to bhal ase, kintu nimok laga swadh harai dile kineka etu ke aru swadisht bonabo?

english_text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
nagamese_text: Etu ke mati nimite bhi aru kheti te mol bona bole bhi kaam nathake. Taikhan etu ke phelai dibo. Jun manu logote huni bole kan ase, taikhan huni bhi.”

english_text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
nagamese_text: Aru ek din poisa utha manu khan aru dusra paapi manu khan Jisu laga kotha huni bole nimite ahise.

english_text: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Pharisee khan aru niyom likha khan ekjon-ekjon logote koi thakise, “Etu manu paapi khan ke mate, aru taikhan logote bohi kene khai.”

english_text: He told them this parable:
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu he etu dristanto taikhan ke koise,

english_text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
nagamese_text: “Yate kun ase, jun logote eksoh mer ase kintu tai ekta haraise koile, tai ninyanve ke jongol te chari kene jun to haraise etu ke bisari bole najabo?

english_text: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai etu mer to pai jai, tai laga pithite uthaikene khushi pora loi ane.

english_text: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
nagamese_text: Jitia tai ghor te ahijai, tai sobke mate, tai laga sathi aru usorte thaka manu khan ke koi, ‘Moi logot khushi koribi, moi laga harai ja-a mer paise.’

english_text: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, sorgote bhi eneka khushi koribo jitia ekjon paapi manu mon ghurai kene ahibo, etu ninyanve thaka pora bhi bisi khushi hobo, kele koile taikhan to mon ghura bole eku nai.

english_text: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
nagamese_text: Aru kun mahila, jun logote dosta chandi poisa thakise, jodi ekta harai diye, titia tai saaki jolai kene ghor jharu marikena sob sapha kori bisaribo nohoi jitia tak etu poisa napai?

english_text: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai pai loi, tai laga sathi aru ghor usorte thaka manu khan ke matikena, koi ‘Moi logote khushi koribi, kelemane moi laga harai juwa poisa to moi paise.’

english_text: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
nagamese_text: Etu nisena he, Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, aru Isor laga sorgodoth majote bhi khushi hoi jitia ekjon paapi manu mon ghurai kene ahe.”

english_text: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu he koise, “Ekjon manu laga duita chokra thakise,

english_text: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
nagamese_text: aru chutu chokra pora baba ke koise, ‘Baba, moi laga dhun sompoti te ki bhag ase etu moike dibi.’ Titia tai laga baba pora dui bhag kori kene duijon ke di dise.

english_text: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
nagamese_text: Aru bisi din nohoi kene, chutu chokra tai laga ki ase etu sob joma kori kene dur jagate jai jaise, aru ta te tai laga sob dhun sompoti cholai kene khotom kori dise.

english_text: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai logote ki thakise etu sob khotom hoi jaise, titia etu pura desh te dangor akaal ahi jaise, aru tai bisi dukh paise.

english_text: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
nagamese_text: Titia tai kaam bisari kene ekta manu laga ghor te jaise, aru etu manu pora taike kheti te gahori ke dana khila bo nimite pathai dise.

english_text: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
nagamese_text: Tai bisi bhuk laga pora gahori dana hoilebi khabo bhabi kene jaise, kintu tai khabole eku pa-a nai.

english_text: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
nagamese_text: Jitia tai nijor laga halat dikhise, tai nijorke kotha korise, ‘Moi laga baba ghor te kiman jon hajira kora manu khan ase taikhan bhi pet bhorta kha-luwa khabo pai, kintu moi yate bhuk pora mori bole ase!

english_text: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
nagamese_text: Moi tayar kene moi laga baba ghor te jabo, aru taike kobo, “Baba, moi sorgo aru apuni age te paap korise.

english_text: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
nagamese_text: Moi apuni laga chokra kobole layak nai; moike bhi apuni laga ekjon hajira manu nisena he bonai kene rakhibi.’”

english_text: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
nagamese_text: Titia tai uthi kene baba laga ghor te jaise. Jitia tai dur te he thakise, tai laga baba pora dikhise aru morom pora bhorta hoi jaise, aru polaikene taike dhurise aru chuma dise.

english_text: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
nagamese_text: Titia chokra pora koise, ‘Baba, moi sorgote thaka Isor aru apuni usorte paap korise. Moi apuni laga chokra kobole layak nai.’

english_text: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
nagamese_text: Kintu baba pora tai laga noukar khan ke koise, ‘Sobse bhal kapra joldi anibi, aru taike lagai dibi, aru tai laga anguli te anguthi lagai dibi, aru notun chapal bhi lagai dibi.

english_text: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
nagamese_text: Aru sobse bhal guru laga bacha to ani kene maribi, aru moi khan sob kha luwa kori kene khushi koribo!

english_text: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi laga chokra to mori jaisele, kintu etiya jinda hoise; tai harai jaise, kintu etiya pai loise.’ Titia taikhan sob khushi korise.

english_text: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te tai laga dangor chokra kheti te thakise. Jitia tai ghor usorte ponchise, tai manu khan gana kori kene nachi thaka awaj hunise.

english_text: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.
nagamese_text: Titia tai ekjon noukar ke matikena ki hoi ase etu hudise.

english_text: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
nagamese_text: Titia noukar pora koise, ‘Tumi laga bhai wapas ahise aru tumi laga baba pora sobse bhal guru laga bacha katise. Kelemane baba pora tumi laga bhai ke bhal kori kene wapas pai loise.’

english_text: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.
nagamese_text: Kintu dangor chokra to khong uthise aru bhitor te jabole mon kora nai, etu karone tai laga baba bahar te ulaikene taike ahibole nimite matise.

english_text: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
nagamese_text: Kintu dangor chokra pora tai laga baba ke koise, ‘Sabi, iman saal moi apuni nimite kaam korise, aru kitia bhi niyom bhanga nai, hoilebi apuni moike ekta chutu saguli bhi diya nai ami laga sathi khan logote jai kene khushi kori bole,

english_text: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
nagamese_text: kintu jitia apuni laga etu chokra ahise, jun he apuni laga dhun sompoti sob to biya kaam kori kene phelai dise, tai nimite apuni sobse bhal guru laga bacha to katise.’

english_text: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
nagamese_text: Titia baba taike koise, ‘Bacha, tumi hodai moi logote ase, aru etu sob to tumi laga he ase.

english_text: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”
nagamese_text: Kintu etu kha luwa kori kene khushi kori bole nimite dorkar thakise, kelemane tumi laga etu bhai jinda ase; tai harai jaisele, hoilebi etiya taike pai loise.’”

english_text: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu chela khan ke koise, “Ekjon dhuni manu thakise aru tai laga ekjon imandar thakise, kintu tai malik laga poisa khorcha kori ase koi kene kunba pora malik ke koi dise.

english_text: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
