nagamese_text: Titia dhuni manu taike mati kene hudise, ‘Eneka kotha khan tumi laga moi kele huni ase? Tumi ki kaam korise etu sob hisab kitab moike dibi, kelemane tumi etiya pora moi nimite kaam kori bole na paribo.’

english_text: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
nagamese_text: Titia etu imandar tai nijorke koise, ‘Moi etiya ki koribo, moi laga malik pora kaam to moi pora loi lobole ase? Moi iman takot nai mati khundikena kaam kori bole aru moi bhik mangi bole sorom lage.

english_text: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
nagamese_text: Moi ki kori bole lage moi jane, jitia moike kaam pora ulai dibo, manu khan taikhan laga ghor te moike matibo.’

english_text: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
nagamese_text: Titia noukar pora jiman manu malik pora dhar loi kene thakise sobke tai matise, aru poila ekjon ke hudise, ‘Tumi moi laga malik ke kiman dibole ase?’

english_text: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
nagamese_text: Tai koise, ‘Moi eksoh botol oliv tel dibole ase.’ Titia tai koise, ‘Tumi laga hisab lobi aru joldi bohi kene yate pachas eneka likhibi.’

english_text: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
nagamese_text: Aru baki luwa dusra ke hudise, ‘Aru tumi kiman dibole ase?’ Tai koise, ‘Eksoh jola chawal.’ Taike koise, ‘etu hisab lobi, aru joldi pora likhibi assi dhan bosta.’

english_text: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
nagamese_text: Titia malik pora etu biya imandar jun chalaki pora kaam korise, taike bhal paise. Kilekoile, etu yug laga chokra khan to taikhan nijor yug laga chokra khan, jun khan jyoti laga ase, taikhan pora bhi bisi chalak ase.

english_text: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, paap laga dhun sompoti pora sathikhan bonai, aru jitia etu pora eku kaam nadiye, taikhan pora tumikhan ke kitia bhi khotom nohua jagate grohon kori lobo.

english_text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
nagamese_text: Jun manu olop te bhi biswas hoi kene thake tai bisi te bhi eneka he thake, aru jun manu olop te bhi thoga baji kore tai bisi te bhi eneka he kore.

english_text: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
nagamese_text: Jodi tumikhan etu sapha nathaka dhun to bhal pora cholai kene rakhibo napare, tenehoile etu hosa dhun to tumikhan ke kun pora dibo?

english_text: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
nagamese_text: Aru tumikhan dusra manu laga dhun to bhal kori kene nacholaile, titia tumi nijor laga dhun to kineka chola bo?

english_text: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
nagamese_text: Ekjon nokor pora duita malik laga kaam koribo na paribo, eneka korile tai ekjon ke ghin koribo aru ekjon ke morom koribo, aru nohoile ekjon ke chari kene dusra ke jai jabo. Tumikhan Isor aru dhun sompoti eke logote sewa kori bole na paribo.

english_text: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia poisa morom kora Pharisee khan etu kotha khan hunise, taikhan Jisu uporte biya paise.

english_text: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan manu usorte nijorke bhal dikhai, kintu Isor he tumikhan laga mon to jane. Jun manu usorte dangor hobole bisare tai Isor usorte komjur hoijai.

english_text: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
nagamese_text: Bhabobadi khan aru niyom khan John laga homoi tak he thakise. Etu homoi para Isor laga rajyo laga susamachar prochar hoise, aru sob manu etu janibo nimite joborjosti jaise.

english_text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
nagamese_text: Sorgo aru prithibi harabo nimite asan ase, kintu niyom te ki likhi kene ase, etu laga ekta chutu bhag bhi naharabo.

english_text: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
nagamese_text: Kun manu tai laga shadi maiki ke chari diye aru dusra maiki ke shadi kore, tai bebichari kaam korise, aru jun manu mota pora chari diya maiki logote shadi kore, tai bhi bebichari kaam kori ase.

english_text: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon dhuni manu thakise, tai daam begoni rong kapra aru bhal mihin kapra lagai kene thakise, aru hodai din khushi aru moja pora thake.

english_text: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon gorib manu Lazarus koi kene tai laga mukhyo diwar te thakise aru tai laga gaw pura te biya ghaw pora bhorta koi kene thake,

english_text: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
nagamese_text: aru etu dhuni manu laga thali pora ki gire eitu khan khabole nimite rukhi thake. Kintu kutta khan bhi ahikena tai laga ghaw to chati thake.

english_text: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
nagamese_text: Etiya etu gorib manu to mori jaise, aru tai laga atma ke sorgodoth pora Abraham laga usorte loi jaise. Aru etu dhuni manu bhi mori jaise aru taike kobor te di dise,

english_text: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
nagamese_text: aru mora manu laga desh pora tai laga suku to uthaikene Abraham ke dikhise aru tai laga usorte Lazarus ke bohi thaka dikhise.

english_text: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
nagamese_text: Titia etu dhuni manu kandi kene koise, ‘Baba Abraham, moi uporte morom koribi aru Lazarus ke yate pathai dibi, tai laga anguli pora hoilebi moike pani dikene jiba ke thanda kori dibole, kelemane moi etu jui te juli kene dukh pai ase.’

english_text: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.
nagamese_text: Kintu Abraham pora koise, ‘Bacha, yaad koribi tumi laga jibon te sob bhal saman he paise, aru Lazarus to sob biya he paise. Kintu etiya tai yate aram pora ase, aru tumi dukh te ase.

english_text: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
nagamese_text: Etu sob to charikena, tumi aru amikhan majote ekta dangor khai ase, etu thaka pora manu yate pora tumi logote jabo na paribo aru taikhan bhi ta te pora yate ahibo na paribo.’

english_text: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—
nagamese_text: Titia dhuni manu koise, ‘Moi apnike anurodh kori ase, baba, apuni kunba ke moi laga baba ghor te pathai dibi-

english_text: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
nagamese_text: kele koile moi laga pans jon bhai ase, taikhan ke hoshiar kori dibi, taikhan bhi etu dukh khotom nohua jagate nahibo nimite.’

english_text: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
nagamese_text: Kintu Abraham koise, ‘Taikhan logote Moses pora likha aru dusra bhabobadi khan pora likha bhi ase; taikhan ke taikhan laga kotha hunibo dibi.’

english_text: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
nagamese_text: Kintu dhuni manu pora koise, ‘Nohoi Baba Abraham, kintu kunba mora pora uthi kene jaile he, taikhan mon ghura bo.’

english_text: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
nagamese_text: Kintu Abraham taike koise, ‘Jodi taikhan Moses pora likha aru dusra bhabobadi khan pora likha kotha mana nai koile, mora manu uthi jaile bhi taikhan mon naghurabo.’”

english_text: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
nagamese_text: Aru ek din Jisu pora chela khan ke koise, “Paap koribi dibole porikha to ahibo, kintu jun manu eitu khan loi kene ahe, taike hai ase!

english_text: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
nagamese_text: Eneka manu dusra ke dukh diya pora nijor gola te pathor bandhi kene pani nichete phelai dile he bhal hobo.

english_text: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
nagamese_text: Nijorke bhal pora sai lobi. Jodi tumi laga bhai paap kori ase, tinehoile taike rukhai dibi; aru jodi tai mon ghurai loile, taike maph dibi.

english_text: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
nagamese_text: Jodi bhi tai tumi logote sath bar paap kaam kore ek dinte, aru sath bar wapas ahi kene koi, ‘Moike maph dibi, titia tumi taike maph koribo lage!”

english_text: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
nagamese_text: Apostle khan pora Probhu ke koise, “Moi khan laga biswas dangor kori dibi.”

english_text: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
nagamese_text: Titia Probhu he koise, “Tumikhan laga biswas ekta sorso dana nisena thakile bhi, tumikhan etu mulberry ghas ke kobo, ‘Nijor laga niche shikor pora ulai jabi, aru jai kene samundar te ulabi,’ aru tumi laga kotha manibo.

english_text: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?
nagamese_text: Aru yate kun manu tai laga noukar kheti te kaam kori thaka homoi te, nohoile bhi saguli rukha homoi te taike kobo, ‘Joldi ahikena kha luwa koribi’?

english_text: Wouldn’t he rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
nagamese_text: Kintu, tai etu manu ke eneka nokobo naki, ‘Moi kiba khabole nimite taiyar koribi, aru tumi laga kapra ke peti bandi lobi jitia moike kha luwa di ase, aru etu pichete tumi kha luwa koribi’?

english_text: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
nagamese_text: Tai laga noukar ke ki hukum dise etu tai kori diya nimite malik pora taike dhanyavad dise naki?

english_text: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
nagamese_text: Etu nisena tumikhan bhi, jitia tumikhan ke ki hukum diya sob kori loise, tumikhan eneka kobo lage, ‘Moi khan layak nathaka noukar ase. Moi khan ke ki koise etu he korise.’”

english_text: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
nagamese_text: Aru etu homoi te jitia Jisu Jerusalem sheher te jaise, Tai Samaria aru Galilee jaga khan phale pora jai thakise.

english_text: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai ekta bosti te ponchise, dos jon kusto-rugi bemar thaka khan ke lok paise. Taikhan durte khara kori thakise.

english_text: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan awaj uthaikene, koise, “Jisu, Probhu, amikhan uporte morom koribi.”

english_text: When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai taikhan ke dikhise, Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Jabi aru nijorke purohit khan ke dikhabi.” Aru jitia taikhan jai thakise, taikhan sob sapha hoi jaise.

english_text: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
nagamese_text: Titia ekjon taikhan majot pora, bhal howa dikhi kene ghuri kene saise aru jor awaj pora Isor ke mohima korise.

english_text: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
nagamese_text: Tai Jisu laga theng nichete giri jaise, aru Taike dhanyavad dise. Tai Samaria laga manu thakise.

english_text: Jesus answered, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike hudise, “Dos jun manu bhal huwa nai naki? Nou jun to kot te ase?

english_text: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”
nagamese_text: Taikhan majote aru Isor ke dhanyavad dibole kun bhi wapas aha nai naki, khali etu manu he nohoile jun alag desh pora ase?”

english_text: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu he taike koise, “Uthibi aru jabi. Tumi laga biswas pora tumike bhal korise.”

english_text: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
nagamese_text: Pharisee khan pora Jisu ke Isor laga rajyo kitia ahibo eneka hudise, Tai jawab dise, “Isor laga rajyo to koi kene nahe.

english_text: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
nagamese_text: Aru eneka nokobo, ‘Sabi, yate ase!’ Nohoile ‘Ta te ase!’ Kintu sabi, Isor laga rajyo to tumikhan majote ase.”

english_text: He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu laga chela khan ke koise, “Eneka din ahibo, jitia tumikhan Manu laga Putro ke sabole itcha koribi, kintu tumikhan dikhi napabo.

english_text: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away or follow after them,
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan pora tumike kobo, ‘Sabi ta te!’ Nohoile ‘Sabi yate!’ Tumi taikhan laga pichete napola bhi,

english_text: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to another part under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
nagamese_text: jitia akas te bhijili mara homoi te ekta jaga pora dusra jagate ujala dikhe etu nisena Manu laga Putro bhi Tai wapas aha homoi te eneka hobo.

english_text: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
nagamese_text: Kintu poila Tai bisi dukh pabo lagibo etu jamana manu khan hath pora.

english_text: As it was in the days of Noah, even so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
nagamese_text: Jineka Noah laga homoi te hoisele, eneka din Manu laga Putro laga homoi te bhi eneka hobo.

english_text: They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
nagamese_text: Taikhan kha luwa kori thakise, shadi kori thakise, aru jibon to duniya laga khushi pora moja kori thakise, utu din tak jitia Noah dangor naw bhitor te ghusi jaise, aru dangor hawa pani ahi kene manu ke khotom kori dise.

english_text: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
nagamese_text: Aru eneka din Lot laga homoi te bhi hoise- taikhan kha luwa nisa-panite moja kori thakise, ekjon-ekjon logote luwa-diya kori thakise, kunba ghor bonai thakise aru kunba kheti kori thakise:

english_text: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky and destroyed them all.
nagamese_text: kintu jitia Lot Sodom pora ulai ahise, akas pora jui ahi kene sob manu ke khotom kori dise.

english_text: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka he din ahibo jitia Manu laga Putro wapas ahibo aru sob manu Taike dikhi pabo.

english_text: In that day, he who will be on the housetop and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
nagamese_text: Aru etu dinte, jun manu ghor uporte ase aru tai laga saman khan ghor te ase, taike etu saman lobole nimite nichete jabo nadibi; aru jun manu kheti te kaam kori ase, etu ke ghuri kene pichete sabole nadibi.

english_text: Remember Lot’s wife!
nagamese_text: Lot laga maiki ke yaad koribi.

english_text: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
nagamese_text: Jun manu tai laga jibon bacha bole bisare tai harai dibo, kintu jun manu nijor jibon to Isor nimite harai diye tai bachibo.

english_text: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. One will be taken and the other will be left.
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etu rati te duijon ghumai thakibo. Ekjon ke uthai lobo, aru ekjon ke chari jabo.

english_text: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other will be left.”
nagamese_text: Aru etu nisena duita mahila eke jagate dhaan khundi thakibo. Ekjon ke uthai loijabo aru ekjon ke chari jabo.

english_text: They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?” He said to them, “Where the body is, there the vultures will also be gathered together.”
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan pora Jisu ke koise, “Kot te Probhu?” Aru Tai pora taikhan ke koise, “Jun jagate manu laga gaw thake, ta te pucha mangso kha chiriya khan bhi joma kori kene thake.”

english_text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
nagamese_text: Ek din Jisu pora chela khan ke dristanto pora hikaise kineka taikhan prathana kori thakibo lage aru kitia bhi mon chutu nokorile lage.

english_text: saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
nagamese_text: Aru koise, “Ekta sheher te ekjon niyom chola manu thakise aru tai Isor ke bhoi nakore aru manu khan ke bhi hisab nakore.

english_text: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
nagamese_text: Aru etu sheher te ekta bidhowa mahila thakise, aru tai, etu manu usorte hodai ahi thake, aru koi, ‘Moi laga dushman khan logot pora moike niyai dibi.’

english_text: He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
nagamese_text: Bisi din pora tai etu mahila laga kaam kori dibo mon thaka nai, kintu etu mahila bisi kowa nimite tai nijorke koise, ‘Moi Isor ke bhoi nakore aru manu ke hisab nakore,

english_text: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
nagamese_text: kintu etu mahila moike hodai digdar diya nimite, moi tai nimite niyai kori dibo, eneka kori dile tai aru hodai ahi kene moike digdar nokorile.’”

english_text: The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
nagamese_text: Titia Probhu pora aru koise, “Huni bhi etu thik nathaka ukil pora ki koise.

english_text: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
nagamese_text: Etiya Isor junke bachai loise taike sajai nadibo naki? Jun tai usorte din aru rati kandi thake? Taikhan laga kotha hunibo nimite deri rukhi thakibo naki?

english_text: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, tai joldi pora niyai to ani dibo. Jitia Manu laga Putro ahibo, Tai etu duniya te biswas pabo na napabo?”

english_text: He also spoke this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others:
nagamese_text: Aru Tai etu dristanto bhi koise jun taikhan nijorke dharmik manu ase koi thake aru dusra ke ghin kori thake,

english_text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
nagamese_text: “Duijon manu prathana kori bole nimite jaise- ekjon Pharisee, aru ekjon poisa utha manu.

english_text: The Pharisee stood and prayed by himself like this: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men: extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
nagamese_text: Aru Pharisee to tai alag phale khara kori kene tai nijor logote eneka prathana kori thakise, ‘Isor, moi Apnike dhanyavad di ase moi dusra manu khan nisena nohoi- chor, biya manu, paap kaam kori kene thaka manu aru poisa utha manu khan nisena bhi nohoi.

english_text: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
nagamese_text: Moi hapta te duibar upwas loi. Moi ki pai etu laga dos bhag bhi diye.’

english_text: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
nagamese_text: Kintu poisa utha manu, durte khara kori kene, tai nijor matha bhi sorgo phale sa nai, kintu tai laga chati to marikena prathana korise, ‘Isor, moi uporte daya koribi, moi paapi manu.’

english_text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etu Pharisee, jun poisa utha manu thakise, tai Isor usorte mohima paikena nijor ghor te jaise. Kelemane jun manu tai nijorke untcha uthabole bisare tai chutu hoi jabo, kintu jun manu nijorke chutu kore taike uthai dibo.”

english_text: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
nagamese_text: Ek din kunba manu khan Jisu usorte bacha khan ke loi kene anise, Jisu laga hath taikhan uporte dikene asirbad dibole nimite. Kintu jitia chela khan pora etu dikhise, taikhan ke ahibo diya nai.

english_text: Jesus summoned them, saying, “Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke matise aru koise, “Chutu bacha khan ke Moi usorte ahibo dibi, aru taikhan ke narukhabi. Kelemane Isor laga rajyo to taikhan nisena nimite ase.

english_text: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
nagamese_text: Moi hosa pora tumikhan ke koi ase, jun pora ekta bacha nisena hoi kene Isor rajyo ke swekar nakore, tai ji hoilebi ta te gusibo na paribo.”

english_text: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon Yehudi cholawta manu Taike hudise, “Bhal hikhok, moi anonto jibon pabo nimite ki koribo lage?”

english_text: Jesus asked him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one: God.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike jowab dise, “Moike kele bhal koi ase? Kun bhi bhal nai, khali Isor he bhal ase.

english_text: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”
nagamese_text: Isor laga niyom tumikhan jane bebichar nokorile, manu ke nomorabi, chor nokoribi, manu laga misa kotha nokobi, baba, ama ke morom koribi.”

english_text: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”
nagamese_text: Kintu cholawta manu he koise, “Moi jawan pora etu sob manikena ahise.”

english_text: When Jesus heard these things, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu tai kowa kotha hunise, Tai koise, “Ekta kotha etiya bhi tumi mana nai: Tumi laga ki ase etu sob bikiri kori dibi aru gorib khan ke bhag kori dibi, titia tumi laga dhun sompoti sorgote thakibo- aru Moi laga pichete ahibi.”

english_text: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
nagamese_text: Jitia cholawta manu Jisu laga kotha hunise, tai bisi mon dukh paise kele koile tai bisi dhuni manu thakise.

english_text: Jesus, seeing that he became very sad, said, “How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into God’s Kingdom!
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike saikene koise, “Dhuni manu sorgote jabole kiman digdar ase!

english_text: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Biji laga chenda pora ekta uth jabole asan ase, hoilebi dhuni manu Isor laga rajyote jabole nimite asani nohoi.

english_text: Those who heard it said, “Then who can be saved?”
nagamese_text: Jun etu kotha hunise taikhan koise, “Tinehoile kun he poritran pabo?”

english_text: But he said, “The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu koise, “Juntu kaam manu napare, Isor he pare.”

english_text: Peter said, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
nagamese_text: Titia Peter he koise, “Sabi amikhan sob chari kene Apuni laga piche ahise.”

english_text: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, for God’s Kingdom’s sake,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Hosa pora Moi tumikhan ke koi ase jun manu tai laga ghor, maiki, bhai, ama, baba, bacha ke Isor laga rajyo nimite charise,

english_text: who will not receive many times more in this time, and in the world to come, eternal life.”
nagamese_text: etu duniya te aru bisi napabo- aru ahibole duniya te, anonto jibon pabo.”

english_text: He took the twelve aside and said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai baroh jonke alag kori kene koise, “Sabi, amikhan Jerusalem te jabo, aru bhabobadi khan pora Manu laga Putro nimite Isor kotha ki likhise, etu sob purah hobole ase.

english_text: For he will be delivered up to the Gentiles, will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit on.
nagamese_text: Karone Taike Porjati khan hathte di dibo, aru Taike bodnam koribo, aru bisi sorom khila bo, aru Tai uporte thuk phelabo.

english_text: They will scourge and kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.”
nagamese_text: Aru Taike chabuk pora maribo, aru morai dibo, aru tisra dinte, Tai aru bhi jee uthijabo.”

english_text: They understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they didn’t understand the things that were said.
nagamese_text: Kintu chela khan etu kotha bujhi panai, aru etu kotha taikhan pora lukai rakhise, aru ki kotha koise etu bujhi bo para nai.

english_text: As he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
nagamese_text: Etiya eneka hoise, jitia Jisu Jericho sheher te ahise, ekjon andha manu rasta kinar te bohi kene bhik mangi thakise.

english_text: Hearing a multitude going by, he asked what this meant.
nagamese_text: Tai manu khan hala kori kene jai thaka to hunise, tai hudise etu ki hoi ase.

english_text: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
nagamese_text: Taikhan andha manu ke koise, “Nazareth laga Jisu etu rasta pora jai ase.”

english_text: He cried out, “Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!”
nagamese_text: Titia tai kandikena jor pora koise, “Jisu, David laga Putro, moi uporte morom koribi.”

english_text: Those who led the way rebuked him, that he should be quiet; but he cried out all the more, “You son of David, have mercy on me!”
nagamese_text: Jun manu Jisu age te jai thakise khong pora taike chup thaki bole koise. Kintu tai bisi hala kori thakise, “David laga Putro, moi uporte morom koribi.”

english_text: Standing still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. When he had come near, he asked him,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu khara kori kene etu manu ke usorte anibole koise. Aru jitia tai usorte ahise, Jisu taike hudise,

english_text: “What do you want me to do?” He said, “Lord, that I may see again.”
nagamese_text: “Moi tumi nimite ki kori bole tumi itcha ase?” Tai koise, “Probhu, moi suku pora sabole itcha ase.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Receive your sight. Your faith has healed you.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu he taike koise, “Tumi laga suku khuli bhi. Tumi laga biswas pora tumi bhal hoise.”

english_text: Immediately he received his sight and followed him, glorifying God. All the people, when they saw it, praised God.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te tai sabo parise aru Jisu pichete jaise, Isor ke mohima dikene, sob manu khan jitia etu dikhise, taikhan Isor ke stuti dise.

english_text: He entered and was passing through Jericho.
nagamese_text: Aru titia Jisu ahise aru Jericho sheher phale jaise.

english_text: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
nagamese_text: Etiya ekjon manu Zacchaeus koi kene thakise, aru tai poisa utha manu khan majote sobse dangor aru dhuni manu thakise.

english_text: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.
nagamese_text: Tai Jisu kun ase koi kene sabole itcha korise, kintu bhir dangor huwa pora sabo para nai, aru tai khata manu thakise.

english_text: He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
nagamese_text: Titia tai Jisu ke sabole nimite polai jai kene ekta sycamore ghas te uthise, kelemane Jisu etu rasta pora he jabo thakise.

english_text: When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu etu jagate ahise, Jisu taike saikene koise, “Zacchaeus, joldi namikene ahibi, aji Moi tumi laga ghor te jai kene thakibo.”

english_text: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.
nagamese_text: Titia tai joldi kori kene nichete nami ahise, aru khushi pora Jisu ke tai laga ghor te ahibole matise.

english_text: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
nagamese_text: Jitia manu khan etu dikhise, taikhan sob biya paise aru apaste koi thakise, “Jisu ekjon paapi manu laga ghor te jaise.”

english_text: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”
nagamese_text: Aru titia Zacchaeus uthikena Probhu ke koise, “Sabi, Probhu moi laga adha saman khan gorib ke di dibo, aru jodi moi kunba ke thogaise, tai laga bhag pora bisi aru char bhag milaikena dibo.”

english_text: Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taike koise, ‘Aji poritran etu ghor te ahise, kelemane tai bhi Abraham laga khandan pora ase.

english_text: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane Manu laga Putro to harai kene thaka manu khan ke bisari bole aru bacha bole ahise.

english_text: As they heard these things, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that God’s Kingdom would be revealed immediately.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan etu kotha huni thakise, Jisu ekta dristanto kobole shuru hoise, kelemane tai Jerusalem te jabole nimite usor hoise, aru taikhan bhabise Isor laga rajyo to ta te joldi ahibole ase.

english_text: He said therefore, “A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, ekta bhal ghor te jonom huwa manu dur ekta desh te tai laga rajyo pabo nimite jaise, aru etu pichete tai wapas ahi jabole thakise.

english_text: He called ten servants of his and gave them ten mina coins, and told them, ‘Conduct business until I come.’
nagamese_text: Etu karone tai laga dosta noukar khan ke matise, aru taikhan ke dosta mina dikene koise, ‘etu mina loi kene tumikhan ki kaam koribo pare etu kori kene thakibi moi wapas naha tak.’

english_text: But his citizens hated him, and sent an envoy after him, saying, ‘We don’t want this man to reign over us.’
nagamese_text: Kintu manu khan taike bhal panai aru tai laga pichete ekjon ke pathai kene taike koise, ‘etu manu moi khan uporte raj kora to moi khan nalage.’

english_text: “When he had come back again, having received the kingdom, he commanded these servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by conducting business.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai rajyo paikena wapas ahi jaise, titia tai koise jun manu ke tai poisa dise taikhan ke mati kene tai usorte loi anibole, ta te tai sabo kun pora bisi kaam kori kene labh paise.

english_text: The first came before him, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made ten more minas.’
nagamese_text: Poila ekjon tai usorte ahi kene koise, ‘Malik, apuni pora diya poisa loi kene moi aru etu laga dos bhag dise kori dise.’

english_text: “He said to him, ‘Well done, you good servant! Because you were found faithful with very little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
nagamese_text: Titia etu bhal manu pora taike koise, ‘Bisi bhal korise, bhal noukar. Kelemane tumi olop diya te bhi bhal kaam kori kene thakise, tumi etu dosta sheher uporte adhikar chola bo.’

english_text: “The second came, saying, ‘Your mina, Lord, has made five minas.’
nagamese_text: Aru dusra jon bhi ahise, aru koise, ‘Malik, apuni pora panch poisa diya to moi pans bhag bisi kori dise.’

english_text: “So he said to him, ‘And you are to be over five cities.’
nagamese_text: Titia etu bhal manu taike koise, ‘Tumi bhi bhal kaam korise etu nimite pansta sheher uporte tumi adhikar chola bo.’

english_text: Another came, saying, ‘Lord, behold, your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief,
nagamese_text: Aru tisra noukar ahise, aru koise, ‘Malik, etu apuni diya laga poisa ase, moi etu loi kene kapra pora bandhi rakhise,

english_text: for I feared you, because you are an exacting man. You take up that which you didn’t lay down, and reap that which you didn’t sow.’
nagamese_text: kele koile, moi apnike bhoi lagi thakise. Kelemane apuni hisab kitab thik rakha manu ase. Apuni ki joma nakore etu uthai aru ki narupai etu he kate.’

english_text: “He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I will judge you, you wicked servant! You knew that I am an exacting man, taking up that which I didn’t lay down and reaping that which I didn’t sow.
nagamese_text: Titia etu manu pora taike koise, ‘Tumi laga mukh pora he moi tumike bisar koribo, tumi biya noukar! Tumi jani thakise naki moi ekjon joborjosti kori thaka manu ase, aru moi ki joma nakore etu loi, aru ki nadhale etu kata manu ase?

english_text: Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
nagamese_text: Titia hoile tumi etu poisa to kele poisa-ghor te joma kora nai, aru jitia moi ahibo, etu homoi te bisi labh hobo thakise?’

english_text: He said to those who stood by, ‘Take the mina away from him and give it to him who has the ten minas.’
nagamese_text: Titia tai jun manu usorte khara kori thakise taikhan ke koise, ‘Tai logot pora poisa to loi lobi, aru jun logote dos bhag ase taike di dibi.’

english_text: “They said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten minas!’
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan koise, ‘Malik, tai logote dos bhag ase.’

english_text: ‘For I tell you that to everyone who has, will more be given; but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.
nagamese_text: ‘Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, jun manu logote bisi ase taike aru bhi bisi dibo, kintu jun manu logote eku nai, ki tai logote ase etu bhi loi lobo.

english_text: But bring those enemies of mine who didn’t want me to reign over them here, and kill them before me.’”
nagamese_text: Kintu etu moi laga dushman khan, jun manu moike taikhan uporte raj kori bole dibo mon thaka nai, yate loi kene anibi aru moi usorte morai dibi.’”

english_text: Having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Etu sob pichete, Jisu aru chela khan sob Jerusalem phale jaise.

english_text: When he came near to Bethsphage and Bethany, at the mountain that is called Olivet, he sent two of his disciples,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Tai Bethphage aru Bethany nogorkhan usorte ahise, Olivet kuwa ekta pahar te, Tai duijon chela ke pathaise,

english_text: saying, “Go your way into the village on the other side, in which, as you enter, you will find a colt tied, which no man has ever sat upon. Untie it and bring it.
nagamese_text: aru koise, “Tumikhan etu age te thaka bosti te jabi. Jitia ta te punchibo, tumikhan ta te kun pora bhi naboha ekta ghora laga bacha ke bandi kene thaka dikhibo. Etu ke Khuli Kena yate loi anibi.

english_text: If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say to him: ‘The Lord needs it.’”
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba tumikhan ke hude, ‘Kile etu ke khuli ase?’ Tumikhan etu kobi, ‘Probhu ke etu dorkar ase.’”

english_text: Those who were sent went away and found things just as he had told them.
nagamese_text: Aru jun khan ke etu karone pathaise, taikhan pora thik eneka he dikhi paise.

english_text: As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan etu ghora bacha ke khuli thakise, malik ahikena taikhan ke koise, “Kile etu ghora bacha ke khuli ase?”

english_text: They said, “The Lord needs it.”
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan pora koise, “Probhu ke etu dorkar ase.”

english_text: Then they brought it to Jesus. They threw their cloaks on the colt and sat Jesus on them.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan Jisu usorte anise, aru taikhan laga kapra gadha uporte phelai dise aru Jisu ke gadha uporte bohi bole dise.

english_text: As he went, they spread their cloaks on the road.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan jai thakise, manu khan kapra ulaikene rasta te rakhidise.

english_text: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu Oliv pahar usorte ahi ponchise, aru chela aru manu khan dhanyavad dibole shuru hoise. Manu khan Jisu laga dangor kaam khan dikhi kene hala kori kene Isor ke mohima dikena

english_text: saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
nagamese_text: koise, “Dhonyo ase etu raja jun manu Probhu laga naam te ahise! Sorgote shanti hobo aru sob untcha jagate mohima dibo!”

english_text: Some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples!”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba Pharisee manu khan majot pora koise, “Shika manu, Apuni laga chela khan ke chup thaki bole kobi.”

english_text: He answered them, “I tell you that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu koise, “Moi tumikhan ke koi ase jodi taikhan chup thake, pathor khan pora he hala kori jabo.”

english_text: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Jisu Jerusalem sheher usorte ponchise, Tai kandise,

english_text: saying, “If you, even you, had known today the things which belong to your peace! But now, they are hidden from your eyes.
nagamese_text: aru koise, “Aji tumikhan pora kineka shanti ahe etu jani thakile! Kintu tumikhan laga suku pora lukaikene ase.

english_text: For the days will come on you when your enemies will throw up a barricade against you, surround you, hem you in on every side,
nagamese_text: Tumikhan uporte eneka din khan ahibo jitia dushman khan pora tumikhan ke sob phale pora dhori rakhibo aru dewar bonai kene tumikhan ke sob kinar pora dabai dibo.

english_text: and will dash you and your children within you to the ground. They will not leave in you one stone on another, because you didn’t know the time of your visitation.”
nagamese_text: Tumi aru tumi laga bacha khan ke matite girai dibo. Taikhan ekta pathor bhi tumikhan uporte nacharibo, kelemane etu laga homoi te ki dikhai dise, etu tumikhan janibole para nai.”

english_text: He entered into the temple and began to drive out those who bought and sold in it,
nagamese_text: Jitia Jisu mondoli bhitor te ghusi se, Tai bhitor te bajar kori thaka manu khan ke khedai se,

english_text: saying to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke koise, “Etu Isor kotha te likha ase, ‘Moi laga ghor to prathana laga ghor hobo,’ kintu tumikhan chor laga ghor bonai dise.”

english_text: He was teaching daily in the temple, but the chief priests, the scribes, and the leading men among the people sought to destroy him.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu mondoli te sikhai thakise. Etu homoi te mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom likha khan aru Pharisee khan Jisu ke mora bole rukhi thakise,

english_text: They couldn’t find what they might do, for all the people hung on to every word that he said.
nagamese_text: kintu kineka pora Taike dhoribo etu taikhan koribo para nai, kelemane sob manu Jisu laga kotha to huni kene bohi thakise.

english_text: On one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the Good News, the priests and scribes came to him with the elders.
nagamese_text: Ek din jitia Jisu ekta jagate manu khan ke mondoli te sikhai thakise aru susamachar prochar kori thakise, mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom jana manu aru cholawta khan Tai logot ahise.

english_text: They asked him, “Tell us: by what authority do you do these things? Or who is giving you this authority?”
nagamese_text: Taikhan pora Taike eneka hudise, “Amikhan ke kobi ki adhikar pora Apuni etu kori ase, aru kun ase jun pora etu kori bole Apuni ke adhikar dise.”

english_text: He answered them, “I also will ask you one question. Tell me:
nagamese_text: Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Moi bhi tumikhan ke ekta kotha hudibo, aru tumikhan Moike kobi.

english_text: the baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?”
nagamese_text: John laga baptizma: Isor pora hoise na manu pora hoise?”

english_text: They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
nagamese_text: Taikhan ekjon-ekjon logote kotha patikena, koise, “Jodi moi khan koi, ‘Isor pora ase,’ Tai kobo, ‘Tenehoile tumikhan taike kele biswas kora nai?’

english_text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”
nagamese_text: Kintu amikhan jodi koi, ‘Manu pora ase’ koile, sob manu amikhan ke pathor maribo, kele koile taikhan John to ekjon bhabobadi ase koi kene biswas kore.”

english_text: They answered that they didn’t know where it was from.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Jisu ke koise etu kot pora ahise taikhan najane koi kene.

english_text: Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Moi bhi tumikhan ke nokobo ki adhikar pora Moi eitu khan kori ase.”

english_text: He began to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard and rented it out to some farmers, and went into another country for a long time.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai manu khan ke etu dristanto koise, “Ekjon manu kheti te angur ghas hali se, aru tai etu kheti kora manu khan ke di dise, aru tai dusra desh te bisi din nimite jai jaise.

english_text: At the proper season, he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia homoi ahise tai ekjon noukar ke kheti kora khan logot pathaise, kheti te angur ulaikene thakile, tai nimite pothabole. Kintu kheti kora manu khan etu noukar ke marise aru khali hath pathai dise.

english_text: He sent yet another servant, and they also beat him and treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra manu ke pathaise, kintu taike bhi marise aru bisi sorom khilai dise, aru taike khali hath pathai dise.

english_text: He sent yet a third, and they also wounded him and threw him out.
nagamese_text: Titia aru ekjon ke pathaise, kintu taike bhi jokhom kori kene bahar te phelai dise.

english_text: The lord of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. It may be that seeing him, they will respect him.’
nagamese_text: Titia kheti laga malik pora nijorke koise, ‘Moi ki koribo? Moi bisi morom kori thaka bacha ke pathai dibo. Eneka korile taikhan taike adar koribo pare.’

english_text: “But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.’
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia kheti kora manu khan pora taike dikhise, taikhan ekjon-ekjon logote kotha patise, aru koise, ‘Etu uttoradhikari ase. Ahibi taike morai dibo, titia etu sob kheti to moi khan laga hoi jabo.’

english_text: Then they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan pora chokra ke kheti pora bahar te phelai dise aru taike morai dise. Titia hoile kheti laga malik pora taikhan ke ki koribo?

english_text: He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.” When they heard that, they said, “May that never be!”
nagamese_text: Kheti malik to ahi kene etu kheti kora manu khan ke khotom kori dibo aru etu kheti to dusra manu khan ke di dibo.” Kintu jitia manu khan etu hunise, taikhan koise, “Eneka kitia bhi hobo nadibo!”

english_text: But he looked at them and said, “Then what is this that is written, ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the chief cornerstone’?
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke saikene koise, “Tinehoile Isor kotha te etu likhi kene rakha to ki ase: ‘Juntu pathor ghor bona manu khan pora phelai dise, etu pathor he ghor ke khara kori kene rakha pathor hoi jaise’?

english_text: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces, but it will crush whomever it falls on to dust.”
nagamese_text: Jun manu etu pathor te giribo, tai bhangi kene tukra hoi jabo. Kintu jun manu uporte etu gire, taike mihin kori dibo.”

english_text: The chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, but they feared the people—for they knew he had spoken this parable against them.
nagamese_text: Titia niyom likha aru mukhyo purohit khan etu homoi te Tai uporte hath laga bole bisarise, kelemane taikhan jani jaise Jisu to etu dristanto taikhan nimite he koise. Kintu taikhan manu khan ke bhoi kori thakise.

english_text: They watched him and sent out spies, who pretended to be righteous, that they might trap him in something he said, so as to deliver him up to the power and authority of the governor.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Taike taikhan bhal kori kene sai thakise, aru Tai pichete manu lagai dise, jun dharmik thaka nisena dikhai thakise kintu Jisu laga kotha khan te golti bisari thakise, aru taikhan laga cholawta khan laga aru governor laga hathte di dibole karone.

english_text: They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you say and teach what is right, and aren’t partial to anyone, but truly teach the way of God.
nagamese_text: Titia, Yehudi cholauta khan pora manu potha khan to ahi kene Jisu ke hudise, “Probhu, moi khan jane Apuni hosa kotha he sikhai, aru kun logote bhi alag pora bebohar nakore, aru Apuni Isor laga kotha to hosa pora sikhai.

english_text: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
nagamese_text: Moi khan ke koi dibi, Caesar ke poisa diya to niyom te thik ase na nai?”

english_text: But he perceived their craftiness, and said to them, “Why do you test me?
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan laga chalaki jani jaise, aru taikhan ke koise,

english_text: Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” They answered, “Caesar’s.”
nagamese_text: “Moike etu denarius dikha bhi. Kun laga chehera aru kotha ta te likha ase?” Titia taikhan koise, “Caesar laga.”

english_text: He said to them, “Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Etu nimite ji to Caesar laga ase etu Caesar ke dibi aru ji to Isor ke dibo lage etu Isor ke dibi.”

english_text: They weren’t able to trap him in his words before the people. They marveled at his answer and were silent.
nagamese_text: Etu kotha pora taikhan Jisu ke manu majot pora dhori bole para nai, kintu Jisu laga jowab te sob asurit hoi thakise, aru taikhan chup-chap hoi jaise.

english_text: Some of the Sadducees came to him, those who deny that there is a resurrection.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba Sadducee khan, kunkhan jun jee utha te biswas nakore, Jisu usorte ahikena hudise,

english_text: They asked him, “Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up children for his brother.
nagamese_text: “Probhu, Moses pora moi khan ke likhise, jodi kunba laga bhai ase aru tai maiki chari kene mori jaise, aru tai bacha nai, tenehoile etu morija laga bhai to maiki ke lobo pare aru tai laga morija bhai naam te bacha jonom kori kene khandan ulabo pare.

english_text: There were therefore seven brothers. The first took a wife, and died childless.
nagamese_text: Ta te sat-ta bhai thakise, aru dangor wala pora maiki ke shadi korise, kintu bacha nathakikena mori jaise;

english_text: The second took her as wife, and he died childless.
nagamese_text: aru dusra pora etu maiki ke loise kintu tai bhi bacha nathaki kene mori jaise.

english_text: The third took her, and likewise the seven all left no children, and died.
nagamese_text: Aru tisra jon pora bhi maiki ke loise, kintu tai bhi eneka he mori jaise, aru etu nisena sath jon bhi maiki ke loise, kintu tai bhi bacha nathaki kene mori jaise.

english_text: Afterward the woman also died.
nagamese_text: Aru hekh te maiki bhi mori jaise.

english_text: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be? For the seven had her as a wife.”
nagamese_text: Etu nimite jee utha dinte, tai kun laga maiki hobo? Kelemane tai sat jon laga bhi maiki thakise.”

english_text: Jesus said to them, “The children of this age marry and are given in marriage.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Etu yug laga manu khan shadi kore aru shadi koribo nimite di diye.

english_text: But those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi jun khan etu yug te thaki bole nimite layak hoise, aru mori kene jee uthibo, taikhan to shadi bhi nakore, aru shadi te bhi nadiye;

english_text: For they can’t die any more, for they are like the angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
nagamese_text: kelemane taikhan kitia bhi namoribo, taikhan sorgodoth hoi jabo; aru taikhan jinda thaka Isor laga bacha khan ase kobo, kelemane taikhan jee utha laga chokra khan ase.

english_text: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he called the Lord ‘The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
nagamese_text: Aru Moses pora bhi juli thaka ghas pora morija uthai diya dikhai dise, jitia tai Probhu ke Abraham laga Isor, Isaac laga Isor aru Jacob laga Isor matise.

english_text: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him.”
nagamese_text: Etiya Tai to mora laga Isor nohoi kintu jinda khan laga ase, kelemane moi khan sob tai logote jinda ase.”

english_text: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, you speak well.”
nagamese_text: Titia kunba niyom likha khan pora Jisu ke koise, “Probhu, Apuni bhal pora koise.”

english_text: They didn’t dare to ask him any more questions.
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan aru Taike hudibole himot kora nai.

english_text: He said to them, “Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora taikhan ke hudise, “Taikhan kineka kobo pare, Khrista to David laga chokra ase?

english_text: David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand,
nagamese_text: David nijor pora Bhajan Geet laga kitab te likhise, Probhu pora moi laga Probhu ke koise, ‘Moi laga dyna hathte bohibi,

english_text: until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.”’
nagamese_text: Jitia tak moi dushman khan ke tumi laga theng nichete giribole nadiye.’

english_text: “David therefore calls him Lord, so how is he his son?”
nagamese_text: David tai nijor pora Khrista ke ‘Probhu’ mate, tinehoile Tai kineka tai laga chokra hobo?”

english_text: In the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,
nagamese_text: Jitia sob manu khan huni thakise, Jisu pora chela khan ke koise,

english_text: “Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the best seats in the synagogues, and the best places at feasts;
nagamese_text: “Etu niyom likha khan pora hoshiar thakibi, jun khan lamba kapra te bera bole bisare, aru bajar te sob pora bhal jaga bisare, aru mondoli te sob pora untcha jagate bohi bole bisare, aru kha luwa jagate bhi bhal he bisare.

english_text: who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation.”
nagamese_text: Bidhowa khan laga ghor khan khotom kori diye aru dikha bole nimite lamba prathana kore. Eitu khan nisena pichete dangor sajai pabo.”

english_text: He looked up and saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury.
nagamese_text: Etiya Jisu uporte saise aru dhuni manu khan pora taikhan laga dhun laga daan khazana te di thaka dikhise.

english_text: He saw a certain poor widow casting in two small brass coins.
nagamese_text: Aru titia Tai ekjon gorib bidhowa aha dikhise aru tai logot duita poisa thaka ke daan te di dise.

english_text: He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow put in more than all of them,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu pora chela khan ke koise, “Hosa pora Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etu gorib bidhowa he sob pora bisi daan dise.

english_text: for all these put in gifts for God from their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all that she had to live on.”
nagamese_text: Jiman manu daan dise taikhan logote bisi thaka hisab te dise. Kintu etu bidhowa, tai logote eku nai, hoilebi tai ki ase etu sob di dise.”

english_text: As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia kunba manu khan mondoli laga kotha koi thakise, kineka sundur pathorkhan aru manu khan laga daan pora mondoli ke bonaise, Tai koise,

english_text: “As for these things which you see, the days will come in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”
nagamese_text: “Etu tumikhan etiya dikhi thaka to, eneka din ahibo, jitia ekta pathor bhi nabachibo aru juntu ekta uporte ekta ase, etu sobke girai dibo.”

english_text: They asked him, “Teacher, so when will these things be? What is the sign that these things are about to happen?”
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan Taike, koise, “Shika manu, etu sob to kitia hobo, aru eneka din ahibole ase koi kene moi khan kineka janibo?”

english_text: He said, “Watch out that you don’t get led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is at hand.’ Therefore don’t follow them.
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu koise, “Hoshiar thakibi aru kun pora bhi tumike thogai dibo nadibi. Bisi manu Moi laga naam loi kene ahibo, aru kobo, ‘Moi Jisu ase,’ aru ‘Homoi to usorte ahise.’ Taikhan laga piche najabi.

english_text: When you hear of wars and disturbances, don’t be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end won’t come immediately.”
nagamese_text: Jitia tumikhan lorai aru jhagara laga kotha khan hunibo, bhoi nokoribi, kelemane eitu khan sob poila hobo lagibo, kintu eneka sob hoilebi hekh homoi to eitu khan huwa loge-loge te nahibo.”

english_text: Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Ekta desh pora dusra desh bhirodh te uthibo, aru ekta rajyo pora dusra rajyo logote lorai koribo.

english_text: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places. There will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
nagamese_text: Aru dangor mati hili bo, khabole napabo aru alag kisim bemar khan ulabo. Ekdom biya ghatna khan hobo aru etu logot te akash te asurit chihna khan dikhibo.

english_text: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and will persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.
nagamese_text: Kintu eitu khan huwa age te, manu khan pora tumikhan laga uporte hath uthabo aru bisi dukh dibo, tumikhan ke mondoli khan aru bondhi ghor khan te bhi hali dibo, raja khan aru Governor khan usorte anibo moi laga naam luwa nimite.

english_text: It will turn out as a testimony for you.
nagamese_text: Eitu khan huwa pora tumikhan gawahi dibole nimite ekta bhal homoi hobo.

english_text: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how to answer,
nagamese_text: Etu nimite nijor mon to shanti rakhibi aru homoi naha age te ki safai dibo lagibo etu nimite chinta nokoribi,

english_text: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand or to contradict.
nagamese_text: kintu Moi tumikhan ke kotha kobole aru gyaan dibo, aru ta te tumikhan usorte kun ahibo taikhan tumi laga kotha mana kori bole na paribo.

english_text: You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan laga nijor ama baba pora tumike chari dibo, aru bhai khan, aru ghor manu khan, sathi khan bhi chari dibo, aru kunba ke to taikhan morai dibo.

english_text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake.
nagamese_text: Moi laga naam nimite tumikhan ke sob manu pora ghin koribo.

english_text: And not a hair of your head will perish.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumi laga matha te thaka ekta chuli bhi naharabo.

english_text: “By your endurance you will win your lives.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan nomro aru biswas te thakile tumikhan laga atma labh lobo.

english_text: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Jerusalem ke sipahi khan pora gherikena thaka dikhibo, titia jani lobo, khotom hobole homoi to ahise.

english_text: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the middle of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.
nagamese_text: Aru Judea te thaka khan pahar te polai jabi, etu jaga majote thakile chari kene jai jabi, aru jun manu etu desh bhitor te nai taikhan ke gushi bole nadibi.

english_text: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
nagamese_text: Etu din to niyai kora laga homoi ase, aru Isor kotha te ki likha ase etu pora hobole nimite.

english_text: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land and wrath to this people.
nagamese_text: Kintu hai ase jun khan bacha bukhi ase, aru jun bacha khan ke sai ase! Etu jagate dangor dukh ahibole ase, aru manu khan uporte Isor laga khong ahibole ase.

english_text: They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
nagamese_text: Kunba to nijor talwar laga dhar pora giri jabo, aru dusra desh te taikhan ke dhori kene loijabo, aru Jerusalem to Porjati khan pora raj chola bo jitia tak Porjati khan laga homoi pura nohoi.

english_text: “There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars; and on the earth anxiety of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the waves;
nagamese_text: Aru chihna khan to suryo, chand aru tara khan ke dikhibo, aru prithibi te thaka desh khan sob samundar laga pani bisi hili thaka nisena dangor chinta hobo.

english_text: men fainting for fear and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
nagamese_text: Etu duniya te ki ahibole ase eitu khan bhabikena bhoi pora manu khan behosh hoi jabo, kelemane sorgo laga takot sobke hilai dibo.

english_text: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
nagamese_text: Titia sob manu khan Manu laga Putro badal te hokti thaka aru dangor mohima pora loi kene ahi thaka dikhibo.

english_text: But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
nagamese_text: Jitia etu sob hoi thakibo, khara koribi aru matha to uporte uthai lobi, kelemane tumike bachai lobole usor hoise.”

english_text: He told them a parable. “See the fig tree and all the trees.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai taikhan ke ekta dristanto koise: “Sabi etu dimoru ghas ke, aru sob ghas khan ke.

english_text: When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near.
nagamese_text: Jitia ghas te phul ulai jai, tumikhan dikhi kene nijor pora jani jai gorom din ahi ase.

english_text: Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that God’s Kingdom is near.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena, jitia tumikhan etu sob hoi thaka dikhibo, titia tumikhan jani lobi Isor laga rajyo usorte ahise.

english_text: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all things are accomplished.
nagamese_text: Hosa pora Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etiya laga manu khan khotom hoi najabo jitia tak etu sob pura nohoi.

english_text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
nagamese_text: Sorgo aru prithibi harai jabo, kintu Moi laga kotha ki koise etu kitia bhi naharabo.

english_text: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
nagamese_text: Nijorke bhal kori kene rakhibi, nisa pani khai kene tumikhan laga mon ke bhari kori bole nadibi, aru jibon laga kiman chinta bhabona ase etu pora mon dukh nokorile, kelemane etu din achanak pora ahibo aru tumike dhuri lobo.

english_text: For it will come like a snare on all those who dwell on the surface of all the earth.
nagamese_text: Ekta jal phela nisena, jiman manu duniya te thaki ase taikhan uporte ahibo.

english_text: Therefore be watchful all the time, praying that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will happen, and to stand before the Son of Man.”
nagamese_text: Kintu sob homoi te hoshiar thakibi, prathana te takot koribi etu sob ki hobole ase eitu khan pora polabole paribo nimite, aru Manu laga Putro usorte khara kori bole paribo nimite.”

english_text: Every day Jesus was teaching in the temple, and every night he would go out and spend the night on the mountain that is called Olivet.
nagamese_text: Aru etu din khan te Tai mondoli te sikhai thakise, aru rati te Tai Olivet pahar uporte jai kene thakise.

english_text: All the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.
nagamese_text: Aru bisi phojurte manu khan Jisu laga kotha huni bole mondoli te punchise.

english_text: Now the feast of unleavened bread, which is called the Passover, was approaching.
nagamese_text: Etiya Khomir Nokhuwa Roti laga Purbb dinte, juntu ke Nistar din eneka mate, etu din usor hoise.

english_text: The chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death, for they feared the people.
nagamese_text: Mukhyo purohit khan aru niyom likha khan Jisu ke kineka morai dibole etu laga upai bisari thakise, kele koile taikhan manu khan ke bhoi lagi thakise.

english_text: Satan entered into Judas, who was also called Iscariot, who was counted with the twelve.
nagamese_text: Titia Saitan pora Judas bhitor te ghusi jaise, jun laga naam Iscariot bhi asele, tai bhi chela bhitor te ekjon thakise.

english_text: He went away and talked with the chief priests and captains about how he might deliver him to them.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Judas jai kene mukhyo purohit khan aru henedhikari khan logote kineka kori kene Jisu ke dhoribo etu upai bisarise.

english_text: They were glad, and agreed to give him money.
nagamese_text: Taikhan khushi paise, aru taike poisa dibole nimite kotha milaise.

english_text: He consented and sought an opportunity to deliver him to them in the absence of the multitude.
nagamese_text: Aru etu kori bole Judas mani loise, aru Jisu ke kineka pora manu nathaka homoi te dhoribo etu upai bisari thakise.

english_text: The day of unleavened bread came, on which the Passover must be sacrificed.
nagamese_text: Aru khomir nadiya roti kha laga din ahise, etu dinte Nistar laga mer ke bolidan kori bole niyom ase.

english_text: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare the Passover for us, that we may eat.”
nagamese_text: Jisu pora Peter aru John duijon ke pathai kene koise, “Jaikena amikhan nimite Nistar naam pora kha luwa rakhibi, amikhan mili kene khabo.”

english_text: They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare?”
nagamese_text: Taikhan pora Taike koise, “Probhu kun jagate jai kene amikhan taiyar koribo?”

english_text: He said to them, “Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him into the house which he enters.
nagamese_text: Tai pora koise, “Sabi, jitia tumikhan sheher te ponchibo, ekjon manu pani laga baltin loi kene thaka lok pabo. Tai laga piche jabi jun to ghor te tai ghuse.

english_text: Tell the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
nagamese_text: Titia ghor laga malik ke jai kene kobi, ‘Shika manu pora apuni ke koi ase, “Bahar manu thaki bole laga kamra to kot ase, jun jagate Moi laga chela khan ke loi kene Nistar naam laga khana koribo?’”

english_text: He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
nagamese_text: Titia tai tumikhan ke uporte loijai kene dangor ekta bhal kamra dikha bo. Jaikena ta te he taiyari koribi.”

english_text: They went, found things as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan jai kene Jisu kineka koise eneka he paise. Titia taikhan Nistar laga kha luwa jai kene taiyar korise.

english_text: When the hour had come, he sat down with the twelve apostles.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Nistar laga khana khabole homoi ahise, Jisu bohi jaise aru Tai laga apostle khan bhi bohi jaise.

english_text: He said to them, “I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer,
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Moi dukh napa age te tumikhan logote bohi kene etu Nistar laga khana khabole mon thakise.

english_text: for I tell you, I will no longer by any means eat of it until it is fulfilled in God’s Kingdom.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, Moi etu nakhabo jitia tak etu sob Isor laga rajyote pura nohoi.”

english_text: He received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said, “Take this and share it among yourselves,
nagamese_text: Titia Jisu kup to loise, aru dhanyavad dikena koise, “Etu lobi, aru ekjon-ekjon logote bhag kori lobi.

english_text: for I tell you, I will not drink at all again from the fruit of the vine, until God’s Kingdom comes.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, etiya pora Isor laga rajyo naha tak, Moi etu angur ros laga pani napibo.”

english_text: He took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai roti to loise aru Isor ke dhanyavad dise, Tai bhag kori kene taikhan ke dise aru koise, “Etu Moi laga gaw ase juntu tumikhan karone dise. Moike yaad kori bole eneka koribi.”

english_text: Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
nagamese_text: Tai kup to loi kene koise, “Etu kup to Moi laga khun te notun niyom bonai ase, juntu tumikhan nimite bohi ulai ase.

english_text: But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me on the table.
nagamese_text: Kintu sabi, kun manu Moike dhoka dibole ase, tai bhi amikhan logote bohi ase.

english_text: The Son of Man indeed goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”
nagamese_text: Manu laga Putro ke ki hobole ase etu sob to Isor pora poila te he likhi kene ase. Kintu O jun manu pora Taike thogabole ase, tai hai paise!”

english_text: They began to question among themselves which of them it was who would do this thing.
nagamese_text: Chela khan majote hudi thakise amikhan majote kun pora eneka kaam koribo.

english_text: A dispute also arose among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
nagamese_text: Pichete chela khan majot jhagara ulaise kun he taikhan majote sob pora dangor hobo laga kotha te.

english_text: He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
nagamese_text: Titia Tai koise, “Porjati laga rajakhan pora taikhan ke raj kore, aru taikhan uporte adhikari chola khan ke ‘bhal kori diya khan’ eneka mate.

english_text: But not so with you. Rather, the one who is greater among you, let him become as the younger, and one who is governing, as one who serves.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan eneka nakoribo lage. Tumikhan majote kun manu dangor bhabi thake tai sob pora chutu hobo lage; aru jun manu age te ase, tai to ekjon sewa kori thaka manu nisena hobo lage.

english_text: For who is greater, one who sits at the table, or one who serves? Isn’t it he who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
nagamese_text: Kintu bhabi sabi kun he dangor ase, khabole boha manu na sewa kora manu? Kun khabole bohi ase tai nohoi? Kintu Moi tumikhan majote ekjon noukar nisena ase.

english_text: “But you are those who have continued with me in my trials.
nagamese_text: Kintu tumikhan Moi laga porikha te Moi logote ase.

english_text: I confer on you a kingdom, even as my Father conferred on me,
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke di ase jineka Ami laga, Baba pora Moike ekta rajyo dise,

english_text: that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom. You will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
nagamese_text: etu nisena tumikhan bhi Moi laga rajyote kha luwa koribo, aru tumikhan singhason te bohi kene Israel laga baroh jati uporte bisar koribo.

english_text: The Lord said, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat,
nagamese_text: Aru Jisu pora koise, “Simon, Simon, sabi Saitan he tumike gehu dana nisena chani loise.

english_text: but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn’t fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumi nimite prathana korise, etu pora tumi laga biswas to naharabo; aru tumi, jitia ghurai ahibo, tumi laga biswasi bhai khan ke mojbut koribi.”

english_text: He said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Peter koise, “Probhu, moi Apuni logot jabole taiyar ase, bondhi ghor te bhi aru mori bole bhi.”

english_text: He said, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will by no means crow today until you deny that you know me three times.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Tai koise, “Moi hosa koise, Peter, murgi hala nakora age te tumi Moike najane koi kene tin bar misa kobo.”

english_text: He said to them, “When I sent you out without purse, bag, and sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “Nothing.”
nagamese_text: Jisu pora chela khan ke koise, “Jitia Moi tumikhan ke poisa laga jola, dorkar laga saman, aru juta noloikena jabole dise, titia kiba napuncha thakise naki?” Taikhan koise, “Eku komti huwa nai.”

english_text: Then he said to them, “But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a bag. Whoever has none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai pora taikhan ke koise, “Kintu etiya, kun manu poisa laga jola ase tai loi lobi, aru etu nisena, ki saman laga jola ase, tai loi lobi, aru kun manu logote talwar nai tai nijor kapra bikiri kori kene kini lobi.

english_text: For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’ For that which concerns me is being fulfilled.”
nagamese_text: Moi tumikhan ke koi ase, ji kotha Moi nimite Isor kotha te likha ase etu pura hobo lagibo, ‘aru Taike niyom nathaka khan logote ginti kori dise.’ Kelemane ji kotha moi nimite koise etu sob pura hoi ase.”

english_text: They said, “Lord, behold, here are two swords.” He said to them, “That is enough.”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan koise, “Probhu, sabi! Yate duita talwar ase.” Etu nimite Tai taikhan ke koise, “Etu kafi ase.”

english_text: He came out and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him.
nagamese_text: Aru bahar te ulaikene, adat pora kori thaka nisena, Tai Oliv Pahar te jaise, aru chela khan bhi tai laga pichete jaise.

english_text: When he was at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan ekta jagate ahise, Tai pora taikhan ke koise, “Prathana koribi tumikhan porikha te nagiribo karone.”

english_text: He was withdrawn from them about a stone’s throw, and he knelt down and prayed,
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan pora olop dur te jai kene, Tai matite athukari kene prathana korise,

english_text: saying, “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
nagamese_text: aru koise, “Baba, jodi Apuni itcha kore, etu dukh laga kup to Moi pora hatai dibi. Kintu Ami laga itcha nohoi, Apuni laga itcha hobole dibi.”

english_text: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
nagamese_text: Titia sorgodoth khan ahikena Jisu ke modot korise.

english_text: Being in agony, he prayed more earnestly. His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down on the ground.
nagamese_text: Tai dukh pora prathana kora homoi te Tai laga posina khun hoi kene matite giri thakise.

english_text: When he rose up from his prayer, he came to the disciples and found them sleeping because of grief,
nagamese_text: Aru Jitia Tai prathana kori kene uthise, Tai laga chela khan usorte jaise, aru taikhan mon dukh pora ghumai thaka dikhise,

english_text: and said to them, “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
nagamese_text: etu nimite Tai pora taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan kele ghumai ase? Uthibi aru prathana koribi, etu pora tumikhan porikha te nagiribo.”

english_text: While he was still speaking, a crowd appeared. He who was called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came near to Jesus to kiss him.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Tai kotha koi thakise, ta te bisi manu ahi jaise, aru jun laga naam Judas thakise, baroh jon chela majot ekjon, tai age kori kene manu khan ke loi anise. Tai Jisu usorte chuma dibole ahise.

english_text: But Jesus said to him, “Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taike koise, “Tumi Manu laga Putro ke chuma dikene thogai ase?”

english_text: When those who were around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
nagamese_text: Aru jiman chela khan Jisu usorte khara asele, taikhan ki hobole ase jani jai kene Jisu ke koise, “Probhu, amikhan talwar ulaikene taikhan logote lorai koribo naki?”

english_text: A certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
nagamese_text: Titia maha purohit laga noukar ke chela ekjon pora dyna kan to kati phelai dise.

english_text: But Jesus answered, “Let me at least do this”—and he touched his ear and healed him.
nagamese_text: Kintu Jisu taikhan ke koise, “Eneka nokoribi!” Aru Jisu he kan wapas lagaikena changai kori dise.

english_text: Jesus said to the chief priests, captains of the temple, and elders, who had come against him, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
nagamese_text: Aru Taike dhori bole aha manu khan, mukhyo purohitkhan, aru mondoli laga henedhikari khan aru cholawta khan ke Tai koise, “Tumikhan talwar aru hathiar khan loi kene ekjon chor manu ke dhura nisena ahise naki?

english_text: When I was with you in the temple daily, you didn’t stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.”
nagamese_text: Moi jitia mondoli te hodai din tumikhan logote thakise, tumikhan moi uporte hath utha nai. Kintu etiya homoi tumikhan laga ase, aru andhar laga hokti ase.”

english_text: They seized him and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Jisu Khrista ke dhurikena maha purohit laga ghor bhirorte loi jaise. Aru Peter bhi taikhan laga pichete jai thakise.

english_text: When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete taikhan ghor bahar te jui jolai kene eke logote bohise, aru Peter bhi taikhan logot bohi thakise.

english_text: A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”
nagamese_text: Aru ekjon mahila noukar, Peter ke jui usorte bohi thaka dikhi kene koise, “Etu manu bhi Jisu logote thakise.”

english_text: He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Peter koise nohoi, “Mahila, moi Taike najane.”

english_text: After a little while someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them!” But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”
nagamese_text: Aru olop pichete ekjon pora taike dikhise, aru koise, “Tumi bhi Jisu logote beraise.” Kintu Peter koise, “Bhai moi nohoi.”

english_text: After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”
nagamese_text: Ek ghanta pichete aru ekjon ahikena koise, “Hosa pora, etu manu bhi Tai logote thakise, tai bhi ekjon Galilee laga manu ase.”

english_text: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
nagamese_text: Kintu Peter koise, “Bhai, moi najane tumi ki kotha koi ase.” Etu kotha koi thaka homoi te, ekta murga hala korise.

english_text: The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”
