english_text: ‘Behold, you scoffers! Wonder and perish, for I work a work in your days, a work which you will in no way believe, if one declares it to you.’”
nagamese_text: ‘Sabi, hinsa kora khan, asurit hoi kene nijor harai jabi; Moi apuni khan laga homoi te kaam kori ase, Etu kaam juntu tumikhan kitia bhi biswas nakore, jodi bhi kunba apuni khan ke ahikena koi dile bhi.’”

english_text: So when the Jews went out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul aru Barnabas jaise, manu khan taikhan ke anurodh korise etu kotha ahi kene aru Bisram dinte koi dibole.

english_text: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia mondoli laga sabha khotom hoise, Yehudi khan aru Yunani bhasa kotha koi thaka Yehudi khan Paul aru Barnabas pichete jaise, aru taikhan pora duijon ke Isor laga morom to koi thaki bole nimite koise,

english_text: The next Sabbath, almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.
nagamese_text: Aru Bisram laga dusra dinte, pura sheher eke logote joma hoise Probhu laga kotha huni bole nimite.

english_text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Yehudi khan pora dangor bhir dikhise, taikhan suku jolise aru Paul laga biya kotha koise aru taike sorom khilai dise.

english_text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from yourselves, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul aru Barnabas mon dangor kori kene koise, “Isor kotha apuni khan logote poila kobole bisi dorkar thakise. Kintu Isor kotha to hatai diya dikhi kene tumikhan Tai laga rajyote jabole layak nai, sabi, amikhan Porjati khan logot jai ase.

english_text: For so has the Lord commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’”
nagamese_text: Etu karone Probhu he moike hukum dise, aru koise, ‘Moi tumikhan ke biswas nathaka khan laga ekta puhor bonai dise, Etu pora tumikhan prithibi laga sob kona te jai kene anonto jibon laga kotha to koi dibo.’”

english_text: As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.
nagamese_text: Jitia Porjati khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan khushi paise aru Probhu laga kotha ke dhanyavad dise. Aru jiman manu anonto jibon pabole ase eitu khan biswas kori loise.

english_text: The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.
nagamese_text: Aru Probhu laga kotha sob usor-usor jagate prochar hoi jaise.

english_text: But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their borders.
nagamese_text: Kintu niyom luwa manu aru dorkar thaka maiki, aru sheher te manu majote naam thaka khan ke Yehudi khan pora Paul aru Barnabas ke digdar dibole korise, aru duijon ke taikhan laga desh pora bahar ulai dise.

english_text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul aru Barnabas taikhan usor pora theng laga dhula sapha korise. Aru ta te pora Iconium laga sheher te jaise.

english_text: The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
nagamese_text: Aru chela khan Pobitro Atma pora bhorta hoi kene khushi pora thakise.

english_text: In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
nagamese_text: Etiya Iconium te eneka hoise, Paul aru Barnabas pora Yehudi khan laga mondoli te jaise aru kineka tai duijon kotha koise, etu huni kene bisi Yehudi aru Porjati manu khan biswas korise.

english_text: But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
nagamese_text: Kintu kotha namana Yehudi khan pora manu khan laga bhabona biya kotha pora bhorta kori kene nijor bhai khan laga dushman kori dise.

english_text: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan ta te olop din thakise, aru Isor laga kotha mon dangor pora koise, aru Isor he Paul aru Barnabas laga hath pora Tai laga asurit kaam manu khan ke dikhai dise.

english_text: But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews and part with the apostles.
nagamese_text: Kintu sheher te thaka manu khan bhag hoi jaise; kunba Yehudi phale jaise, aru kunba apostle khan phale jaise.

english_text: When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia biswas nakora khan aru Yehudi aru taikhan laga cholawta khan mili kene duijon ke hinsa kori kene pathor mari bole bisarise,

english_text: they became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.
nagamese_text: tai duijon etu jani loise aru ta te pora Lycaonia, Lystra aru Derbe aru etu usorte thaka sheher te polai jaise,

english_text: There they preached the Good News.
nagamese_text: aru taikhan Isor laga kotha prochar kori thakise.

english_text: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.
nagamese_text: Aru Lystra town te ekjon lengra manu bohise, tai laga theng te khara hobole olop bhi takot thaka nai, tai ama laga pet pora he lengra jonom hoise, tai kitia bhi bera nai.

english_text: He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
nagamese_text: Etu manu Paul kotha kowa hunise, titia Paul etu manu ke bhal hoi jabole mon kori thaka laga biswas dikhi kene taike bhal pora sai thakise.

english_text: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.
nagamese_text: Aru titia tai untcha awaj pora koise, “Uthi kene tumi laga theng te khara hobi.” Titia etu manu uthi kene bera bole shuru hoise.

english_text: When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
nagamese_text: Jitia manu khan Paul ki korise etu dikhise, taikhan laga awaj uthaise aru Lycaonia laga bhasa te koise, “Isor khan manu laga gaw loi kene amikhan majote ahise.”

english_text: They called Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan Barnabas ke “Zeus,” matise, aru Paul ke “Hermes,” kelemane tai he kotha bisi koi thakise.

english_text: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.
nagamese_text: Titia Zeus mondoli laga purohit jun to sheher usorte thakise, bail guru aru phul laga mala loi kene dorja usorte ahise; tai aru ta te laga manu khan boli dibole mon jaise.

english_text: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes and sprang into the multitude, crying out,
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia apostle Barnabas aru Paul etu hunise, taikhan laga kapra phatai kene manu khan laga majote jai kene jor pora kandise.

english_text: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of the same nature as you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;
nagamese_text: Aru koise, “Manu khan, tumikhan kele eneka kori ase? Amikhan bhi apuni khan nisena bhabona thaka manu he ase. Amikhan apuni khan ke Isor laga kotha prochar kori bole ahise, etu kotha huni kene Isor pora itcha nakora kaam khan chari bole, sorgo, prithibi aru samundar te jiman jinis ase sob Tai pora he bonaise.

english_text: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.
nagamese_text: Poila homoi te, manu khan ke nijor khushi pora berabo disele.

english_text: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”
nagamese_text: Kintu, Tai manu khan ke chari diya nai, Tai sorgo pora pani dise aru phul ulaikene khabole nimite bhal mohina dise aru sob bhal kaam kori dise.”

english_text: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.
nagamese_text: Etu kotha koi kene, Paul aru Barnabas taikhan ke boli dibole rukhaise.

english_text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
nagamese_text: Titia Antioch aru Iconium pora kunba Yehudi khan ta te ahise aru manu khan laga monte biya kotha hali dise. Aru titia Paul ke pathor mari kene sheher laga bahar te tani ulai dise, taikhan bhabise Paul mori jaise.

english_text: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
nagamese_text: Kintu chela khan tai usorte khara kori thakise, titia tai uthi kene sheher te jaise. Aru dusra dinte, Barnabas logote Derbe te jaise.

english_text: When they had preached the Good News to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai duijon Isor laga kotha koi kene bisi chela bonaise, taikhan Lystra te jaise, aru Iconium aru ta te pora Antioch te jaise.

english_text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan chela khan ke biswas te hodai mon dangor hoi kene thaki bole sikhaise, aru koise, “Amikhan Isor laga rajyote jabole bisi dukh kori bole lagibo.”

english_text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord on whom they had believed.
nagamese_text: Aru sob girja te taikhan ke cholai loijabo nimite dangor manu basi dise, aru upwas rakhikena prathana korise, aru taikhan ke Isor hathte dise, junke taikhan biswas korise.

english_text: They passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
nagamese_text: Aru etu pichete duijon Pisidia jaga paar kori kene Pamphylia te ahi jaise.

english_text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Perga te Isor kotha koi dise, ta te pora taikhan Attalia sheher te jaise.

english_text: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
nagamese_text: Ta te pora duijon naw te uthi kene Antioch te jaise, ta te taikhan Isor laga anugrah kaam kori bole pathai sele, aru duijon etu kaam pura kori dise.

english_text: When they had arrived and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Antioch te ahise aru girja manu khan ke joma korise, Isor pora ki korise, aru kineka Porjati khan nimite biswas laga dorja to khuli dise etu sob taikhan ke koi dise.

english_text: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.
nagamese_text: Aru duijon to chela khan logote bisi din tak ta te thakise.

english_text: Some men came down from Judea and taught the brothers, “Unless you are circumcised after the custom of Moses, you can’t be saved.”
nagamese_text: Olop din pichete, kunba manu Judea jaga pora ahi kene Antioch te thaka bhai khan ke sikhai kene koise, “Jitia tak tumikhan Moses laga niyom te diya nisena sunnot nakore, tumikhan nabachibo.”

english_text: Therefore when Paul and Barnabas had no small discord and discussion with them, they appointed Paul, Barnabas, and some others of them to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.
nagamese_text: Etu kotha kowa nimite Paul aru Barnabas logote manu khan mon mila nai aru taikhan uporte khong uthise. Paul aru Barnabas aru ta te kunba khan ke Jerusalem te jabole basi loise aru jai kene apostle aru bura manu khan ke taikhan ki koise etu hudibole nimite pathaise.

english_text: They, being sent on their way by the assembly, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. They caused great joy to all the brothers.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan ke girja pora pathaise, aru Phoenicia aru Samaria laga jaga khan pora juwa homoi te Porjati khan mon ghura laga kotha koidi thakise. Sob bhai khan etu khobor paikena bisi khushi korise.

english_text: When they had come to Jerusalem, they were received by the assembly and the apostles and the elders, and they reported everything that God had done with them.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Jerusalem te ponchise, taikhan ke girja laga apostle aru bura khan pora ahibole dise, aru Isor pora taikhan majot ki kori dise etu sob manu khan ke koi dise.

english_text: But some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba biswas kora manu, kunkhan Pharisee khan logote mili kene thakise, khara kori kene koise, “Taikhan karone to sunnot kori bole dorkar ase aru Moses laga niyom mani kene thaki bole nimite sikhai dibole lage.”

english_text: The apostles and the elders were gathered together to see about this matter.
nagamese_text: Titia apostle aru bura manu khan eke logote joma hoi kene etu kotha patise.

english_text: When there had been much discussion, Peter rose up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that a good while ago God made a choice among you that by my mouth the nations should hear the word of the Good News and believe.
nagamese_text: Jitia etu kotha bisi dangor hoi jaise, Peter khara kori kene taikhan ke koise, “Bhai khan, Isor poila te apuni khan majote te moike basi loise, moi laga mukh pora Porjati khan Isor laga kotha hunibo aru biswas koribo nimite.

english_text: God, who knows the heart, testified about them, giving them the Holy Spirit, just like he did to us.
nagamese_text: Isor, Tai manu laga mon jane, aru sob gawahi diye, Pobitro Atma pora bhorta kori diye, jineka Tai moi khan uporte bhi korise;

english_text: He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
nagamese_text: aru Isor dwara Porjati khan aru amikhan majote eku alag bhabona nai, aru taikhan laga mon biswas pora sapha kori dise.

english_text: Now therefore why do you tempt God, that you should put a yoke on the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
nagamese_text: Etu nimite tumikhan kele Isor ke bisar kori ase, chela khan laga gola uporte amikhan aru amikhan laga baba khan pora kitia bhi uthabole napara bhar to kele hali bole bisari ase?

english_text: But we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are.”
nagamese_text: Kintu amikhan biswas kore Probhu Jisu laga anugrah aru morom pora poritran pabo, kineka taikhan paise amikhan bhi pabo.”

english_text: All the multitude kept silence, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul reporting what signs and wonders God had done among the nations through them.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te thaka sob manu khan chup hoi jaise jitia Paul aru Barnabas pora Porjati khan majote Isor pora ki asurit kaam kori dise etu taikhan ke koise.

english_text: After they were silent, James answered, “Brothers, listen to me.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan kotha kori kene khotom hoise, James pora koise, “Bhai khan, moi laga kotha huni bhi.

english_text: Simeon has reported how God first visited the nations to take out of them a people for his name.
nagamese_text: Simon pora poila koise kineka Isor pora Porjati khan ke modot kori dise aru taikhan majot pora Tai laga naam ulabole nimite.

english_text: This agrees with the words of the prophets. As it is written,
nagamese_text: Aru bhabobadi khan etu kotha to manise, jineka etu Shastro te likha ase,

english_text: ‘After these things I will return. I will again build the tabernacle of David, which has fallen. I will again build its ruins. I will set it up
nagamese_text: ‘Etu pichete moi aru bhi ahibo, Aru moi David laga bhangi juwa tombu uporte ghor bonabo; Aru biya hoija khan sob wapas bhal kori kene khara kori dibo,

english_text: that the rest of men may seek after the Lord: all the Gentiles who are called by my name, says the Lord, who does all these things.’
nagamese_text: Kelemane manu khan Isor ke bisaribo, Aru sob Porjati khan moi laga naam matibo. Etu Probhu pora koi ase, jun he etu sob kaam to kori dise.

english_text: “All of God’s works are known to him from eternity.
nagamese_text: Etu sob kaam shuru pora manu khan ke jonai dise.

english_text: Therefore my judgment is that we don’t trouble those from among the Gentiles who turn to God,
nagamese_text: Etu karone, moi laga bhabona eneka ase, amikhan Porjati khan Isor phale aha to digdar nokorile lage.

english_text: but that we write to them that they abstain from the pollution of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan ke likhi kene taikhan murti puja kora aru mangso laga itcha kaam kora, aru janwar laga gola kati kene khun kha etu sob nakoribole koi dibo.

english_text: For Moses from generations of old has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.”
nagamese_text: Moses laga kotha sob sheher te ase, poila khandan pora loi kene, aru jun manu tai laga naam loi kene mondoli khan te prochar kore, aru tai laga naam hodai Bisram dinte loi thake.”

english_text: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole assembly, to choose men out of their company, and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers.
nagamese_text: Titia sob apostle khan, bura khan aru girja manu khan etu kotha khan bhal paise, aru basi luwa khan ke Paul aru Barnabas logote Antioch te pathai dibole taikhan sai loise. Titia Judas, kunke Barsabbas bhi mate, aru Silas taikhan biswasi bhai khan majote cholawta thakise, taike pathaise.

english_text: They wrote these things by their hand: “The apostles, the elders, and the brothers, to the brothers who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: greetings.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan hath pora chithi likhi dise: “Apostle aru bura khan pora, amikhan jun apuni khan laga bhai khan ase, jun khan Antioch, Syria, aru Cilicia te ase, aru Porjati khan ke salam di ase!

english_text: Because we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying, ‘You must be circumcised and keep the law,’ to whom we gave no commandment;
nagamese_text: Amikhan hunise, kunba manu amikhan majot pora ulai jaise, aru amikhan ke eku huda nai, aru apuni khan ke ulta kotha sikhai kene Atma te dukh pabole dise.

english_text: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose out men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
nagamese_text: Etu nimite, amikhan eke logote lok kori kene apnikhan ke pathabole bhal manu basi bo, jun khan logote amikhan bisi morom kora Barnabas aru Paul duijon bhi pathabole ase.

english_text: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
nagamese_text: Etu manu khan nijor laga jibon dikene Probhu Jisu Khrista laga naam nimite dukh uthai thake.

english_text: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who themselves will also tell you the same things by word of mouth.
nagamese_text: Etu karone Judas aru Silas ke pathai ase, taikhan bhi etu kotha khan nijor mukh pora apnikhan ke koi dibo.

english_text: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit, and to us, to lay no greater burden on you than these necessary things:
nagamese_text: Kelemane Pobitro Atma pora amikhan nimite etu he bhal ase bhabise, apuni khan uporte eku kaam nathaka laga bhar pora dukh nadibo nimite:

english_text: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality, from which if you keep yourselves, it will be well with you. Farewell.”
nagamese_text: murti puja ke boli diya pora apuni khan dur thakibo, aru khun para, aru gola kati kene morai diya pora, aru biya paap pora. Jodi apuni khan pora eitu khan sob pora dur thakise koile, apuni khan nijor nimite bhal ase. Bhal pora thakibi.”

english_text: So, when they were sent off, they came to Antioch. Having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan ke jabole dise, taikhan Antioch te ahi punchise; aru sob manu khan ke joma kora pichete, chithi taikhan ke dise.

english_text: When they had read it, they rejoiced over the encouragement.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia girja pora etu porhise, taikhan bisi mon dangor kori diya kotha dikhi kene taikhan bisi khushi korise.

english_text: Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.
nagamese_text: Judas aru Silas, duijon bhi bhabobadi thakise, aru ta te thaka bhai khan ke nijor kotha pora manu khan laga biswas aru mon dangor kori dise.

english_text: After they had spent some time there, they were dismissed in peace from the brothers to the apostles.
nagamese_text: Aru olop din ta te thaki kene, taikhan ke kun bhai khan pora pathaise, taikhan logot wapas shanti pora pathai dise.

english_text: But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul aru Barnabas to Antioch te thaki jaise, Isor laga kotha manu khan ke sikhai thakise- dusra khan bhi duijon logote thakise.

english_text: After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
nagamese_text: Olop din pichete, Paul pora Barnabas ke koise, “Ahibi amikhan poila jun sheher te jai kene Isor kotha prochar korise ta te laga bhai khan ke jai kene lok koribo, aru taikhan kineka ase etu sabo.”

english_text: Barnabas planned to take John, who was called Mark, with them also.
nagamese_text: Barnabas taikhan logote John kunke Mark bhi mate taike loi jabole mon thakise.

english_text: But Paul didn’t think that it was a good idea to take with them someone who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia, and didn’t go with them to do the work.
nagamese_text: Kintu Mark ke loi juwa to thik nohoi eneka Paul pora bhabise, ta te pora John to Pamphylia te jaise aru taikhan ki kaam nimite jaise etu kaam te tai aru age naja hoise.

english_text: Then the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away to Cyprus,
nagamese_text: Etu nimite tai duijon majot kotha mila nai, aru ta te pora tai duijon alag hoi jaise, aru Barnabas pora Mark ke loi kene naw pora Cyprus te jai jaise.

english_text: but Paul chose Silas and went out, being commended by the brothers to the grace of God.
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul pora Silas ke basi loise aru ta te bhai khan pora duijon ke Isor laga anugraha te rakhi kene sob kaam di dise.

english_text: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.
nagamese_text: Aru tai Syria aru Cilicia te jaise, aru girja khan te jaikena biswasi khan laga mon dangor kori dise.

english_text: He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete tai Derbe aru Lystra sheher te jaise; aru sabi, ta te ekjon chela Timothy koi kene thakise, tai ekjon biswasi aru Yehudi mahila laga chokra asele; kintu tai laga baba to Yunani manu thakise.

english_text: The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.
nagamese_text: Lystra aru Iconium te thaka biswasi bhai khan tai laga bhal kotha he koise.

english_text: Paul wanted to have him go out with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those parts, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
nagamese_text: Paul pora Timothy ke loi jabole mon thakise; aru taike sunnot kori dise kelemane etu jagate Yehudi khan thakise, aru ta te laga manu khan sob jani thakise tai laga baba Yunani manu ase koi kene.

english_text: As they went on their way through the cities, they delivered the decrees to them to keep which had been ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul, Silas aru Timothy khan sheher te ja-a homoi te, taikhan girja khan te manu khan ke Isor kotha mani bole sikhaise, juntu kotha Jerusalem te thaka apostle aru girja laga bura khan pora taikhan ke kobole faisla kori dise.

english_text: So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.
nagamese_text: Etu pora girja khan biswas te takot hoi thakise, aru hodai din manu bhi bisi-bisi hoi jaise.

english_text: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.
nagamese_text: Paul aru tai laga sathi khan Phrygia aru Galatia laga jaga phale pora jaise, kelemane Pobitro Atma pora taikhan ke Asia te prochar kori bole mana korise.

english_text: When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Mysia sheher usorte ahise, taikhan Bithynia te jabole kosis korise, kintu Jisu laga Atma pora ta te jabole mana korise.

english_text: Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
nagamese_text: Etu karone taikhan Mysia paar kori kene Troas sheher te jaise.

english_text: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”
nagamese_text: Etu rati te Paul ekta darshan dikhise: ekjon manu Macedonia jagate khara kori thakise, aru taike mati kene koise, “Ahi kene amikhan ke Macedonia te modot koribi.”

english_text: When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.
nagamese_text: Jitia Paul etu darshan dikhise, etu homoi te amikhan joldi Mecedonia te jaise, kelemane taikhan ke susamachar koi dibole Isor amikhan ke matise.

english_text: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan Troas pora naw te uthi kene sidha Somothrace laga majuli te jaise, aru dusra din Neapolis sheher te ahi jaise.

english_text: and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te pora Mecedonia laga sob pora dangor sheher Philippi te punchise, Rome manu khan laga jaga, aru amikhan ta te olop din thakise.

english_text: On the Sabbath day we went outside of the city by a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and we sat down and spoke to the women who had come together.
nagamese_text: Aru Bisram dinte amikhan sheher bahar te ulaikene nodi kinar phale, prathana kori bole jagah ase bhabi kene ta te jaise. Titia amikhan bohise aru ta te mahila khan joma hoi kene thaka khan logote kotha korise.

english_text: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us. The Lord opened her heart to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.
nagamese_text: Ta te ekjon mahila Lydia koi kene asele, Thyatira te tai begoni rong kapra bikiri kori thake, tai Isor ke mohima kore, aru tai amikhan laga kotha hunise. Probhu he etu mahila laga mon khuli kene Paul laga kotha bhal pora huni bole dise.

english_text: When she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay.” So she persuaded us.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai aru tai laga ghor manu sob baptizma loise, tai amikhan ke hudi kene koise, “Jodi apuni khan moi Isor usorte biswasi ase koi kene bisar kore, ahi kene moi laga ghor te thaki bhi.” Aru amikhan tai laga ghor te rukhibole jaise.

english_text: As we were going to prayer, a certain girl having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune telling.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te, amikhan prathana kori bole ekta jagate jai thakise, titia amikhan ekjon jawan jyotishee kora mahila ke lok paise. Tai etu kaam kori kene tai laga malik khan ke bisi poisa kamaikena di thakise.

english_text: Following Paul and us, she cried out, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!”
nagamese_text: Etu mahila Paul aru amikhan laga pichete ahi kene hala korise, aru koise, “Etu manu khan sobse Mohan Isor laga noukar khan ase. Taikhan pora apnikhan logot prochar kora to poritran pabole rasta ase.”

english_text: She was doing this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” It came out that very hour.
nagamese_text: Tai bisi din eneka koi thakise, kintu tai eneka kowa to Paul ke bhal panai, aru tai ghurai kene dusto atma ke koise, “Moi Jisu Khrista naam pora tumike hukum di ase tai pora ulai jabi,” aru etu homoi te atma ulai jaise.

english_text: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia tai laga malik khan poisa aha rasta to bondh hoija dikhise, taikhan Paul aru Silas ke dhori kene bajar laga adhikari khan usorte loi anise.

english_text: When they had brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, are agitating our city
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan ke bisar kora manu khan usorte anise, taikhan koise, “Etu manu khan amikhan laga sheher ke biya kori ase. Taikhan Yehudi manu ase.

english_text: and advocate customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans.”
nagamese_text: Moi khan ki niyom manibo napare etu sikhai ase aru Rome laga niyom lobole koi ase.”

english_text: The multitude rose up together against them and the magistrates tore their clothes from them, then commanded them to be beaten with rods.
nagamese_text: Titia manu khan Paul aru Silas uporte khong korise, aru bisar kora manu khan pora tai duijon laga kapra phatai kene pitabole hukum dise.

english_text: When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely.
nagamese_text: Aru tai duijon ke bisi marise, aru bondhi ghor te bondh kori dise aru bondhi ghor laga adhikari ke bhal pora duijon ke rukhibole hukum dise.

english_text: Having received such a command, he threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai etu hukum paise, bondhi ghor laga adhikari pora tai duijon laga theng bandhi kene bondh kora bhitor kamra te rakhidise.

english_text: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
nagamese_text: Aru adha rati te Paul aru Silas prathana kori kene Isor laga gana gayi thakise, aru bondhi ghor te thaka dusra koidi khan taikhan ke huni thakise.

english_text: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.
nagamese_text: Achanak pora dangor mati hili se, aru bondhi ghor laga khamba khan hili jaise; aru etu homoi te dorja khan khuli jaise, aru manu khan ke bandhi rakha loha rusi sob khuli jaise.

english_text: The jailer, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
nagamese_text: Titia adhikari ghumai thaka pora uthijaise aru dorja khan sob khula dikhise; aru tai laga talwar ulaikene nijorke morai dibole korise, kelemane tai bhabise bondhi ghor te thaka manu khan sob polai jaise.

english_text: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul jor pora hala kori kene koise, “Nijorke jokhom nadibi, kelemane amikhan sob yate ase.”

english_text: He called for lights, sprang in, fell down trembling before Paul and Silas,
nagamese_text: Titia bondhi ghor laga adhikari pora saaki mangi kene bhitor te polai ahise, aru bhoi pora kapi kene, Paul aru Silas laga theng te giri jaise,

english_text: brought them out, and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
nagamese_text: aru tai duijon ke bahar te loi ani kene koise, “Sahab khan, poritran pabole moi ki koribo lage?”

english_text: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
nagamese_text: Titia duijon Taike jawab dise, “Probhu Jisu ke biswas koribi, titia tumi aru tumi laga ghor manu sob bachi jabo.”

english_text: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his house.
nagamese_text: Titia duijon taike aru tai laga ghor manu sobke Probhu laga kotha hunai dise.

english_text: He took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes, and was immediately baptized, he and all his household.
nagamese_text: Titia bondhi ghor laga sipahi pora etu rati te duijon ke loi jaise, aru taikhan laga jokhom sapha kori dise, tai laga sob ghor manu aru tai etu homoi te baptizma loise.

english_text: He brought them up into his house and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly with all his household, having believed in God.
nagamese_text: Aru duijon ke tai laga ghor te loi anise aru kha luwa dise, aru tai Isor ke biswas korise koi kene tai laga sob ghor manu bisi khushi korise.

english_text: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, “Let those men go.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia din hoise, titia sahab khan pora sipahi khan ke pathaise aru koise, “Taikhan ke jabole dibi.”

english_text: The jailer reported these words to Paul, saying, “The magistrates have sent to let you go; now therefore come out and go in peace.”
nagamese_text: Titia sahab pora jai kene etu kotha Paul ke koise, “Bisar kora manu pora moike apuni khan ke chari dibole koise. Etu nimite bahar te ulabi, aru shanti pora jabi.”

english_text: But Paul said to them, “They have beaten us publicly without a trial, men who are Romans, and have cast us into prison! Do they now release us secretly? No, most certainly, but let them come themselves and bring us out!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul taikhan ke koise, “Amikhan Rome laga manu ase, hoilebi bisar laga niyom nacholai kene ami duijon ke marise, aru bondhi ghor te hali dise. Etiya to moi khan ke lukai kene pathai dibole mon ase? Eneka nohoi! Kintu, taikhan nijor ahi kene amikhan ke bahar te loi jabole dibi.”

english_text: The sergeants reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans,
nagamese_text: Titia sipahi khan bisar kora manu khan ke jai kene etu kotha koise, aru jitia Paul aru Silas Roman manu ase koi kene janise, taikhan bhoi lagi jaise.

english_text: and they came and begged them. When they had brought them out, they asked them to depart from the city.
nagamese_text: Titia bisar kora manu khan ahi kene taikhan ke maph mangise, aru duijon ke bahar te ulaikene anise, aru sheher pora jai jabole koise.

english_text: They went out of the prison and entered into Lydia’s house. When they had seen the brothers, they encouraged them, then departed.
nagamese_text: Titia duijon bondhi ghor pora ulaikene Lydia laga ghor te jaise. Aru jitia Paul aru Silas duijon bhai khan ke dikhise, taikhan laga mon dangor koridi kene sheher pora jai jaise.

english_text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
nagamese_text: Ek din paul aru silas duijon Amphipolis aru Apollonia laga sheher paar kori kene jaise, aru Thessalonica laga sheher te ahi ponchise, ta te Yehudi khan laga ekta mondoli thakise.

english_text: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them; and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
nagamese_text: Aru Paul laga adat ekta thaka nisina, tai taikhan logote jaise, aru tin Bisram din tak taikhan logote Isor laga kotha koi thakise.

english_text: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Christ.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai Shastro khuli kene taikhan ke bujhai thakise ki Khrista dukh pabo aru mora pora jinda hoi jabo, aru etu eneka hobole dorkar thakise. Aru tai koise, “Etu Jisu kun laga kotha koi kene moi prochar kori ase Tai he Khrista ase.”

english_text: Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas: of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and not a few of the chief women.
nagamese_text: Ta te kunba Yehudi khan Paul aru Silas laga kotha huni kene tai duijon logote milai loise, aru taikhan logote kunba Yunani khan aru kunba maiki khan bhi mili jaise.

english_text: But the unpersuaded Jews took along some wicked men from the marketplace and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar. Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.
nagamese_text: Kintu biswas nakora Yehudi khan mon julise, aru bajar pora biya manu ke joma kori loise, aru bisi manu lagai kene sheher te hala korise. Aru jitia Jason laga ghor bhangai dise, aru Paul aru Silas ke manu khan dhori kene loi anibole bisarise.

english_text: When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here also,
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia taikhan duijon ke panai, taikhan Jason aru kunba biswasi bhai khan ke dhori kene sheher laga adhikari khan usorte loi jaise, aru hala kori kene koise, “Etu manu khan jun duniya ke ulta koridi ase, taikhan bhi yate ahikena ase.

english_text: whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”
nagamese_text: Jason pora tai laga ghor te manu kunkhan rakhise kunkhan Caesar laga kotha mana nai, aru taikhan koi ase Jisu koi kene dusra raja ase.”

english_text: The multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled when they heard these things.
nagamese_text: Aru etu kotha huni kene bisi manu khan aru sheher laga adhikari khan sob chinta hoise.

english_text: When they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan Jason aru tai laga saathi khan pora poisa loise, aru dusra biswasi khan ke jabole dise.

english_text: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
nagamese_text: Titia biswasi bhai khan etu rati te Paul aru Silas ke Berea sheher te pathai dise. Aru jitia duijon ta te ponchise, tai duijon Yehudi khan laga mondoli te jaise.

english_text: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.
nagamese_text: Aru Thessalonica te thaka manu khan to dusra jaga laga manu khan pora bhi bhal thakise, kelemane taikhan hodai din Isor laga kotha te ki likha ase etu saikene bhal mon pora grohon kori thakise.

english_text: Many of them therefore believed; also of the prominent Greek women, and not a few men.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite bisi manu Jisu ke biswas kori loise, aru ta te laga Yunani niyom mani thaka mahila khan aru kunba mota manu khan bhi biswas korise.

english_text: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Beroea also, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Thessalonica laga Yehudi khan Paul pora Berea te Isor laga kotha koi ase koi kene janise, taikhan jai kene manu khan laga monte biya kotha hali dise aru mon biya kori bole dise.

english_text: Then the brothers immediately sent out Paul to go as far as to the sea, and Silas and Timothy still stayed there.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te, biswasi bhai khan joldi Paul ke samundar phale pora jabole dise, kintu Silas aru Timothy to Berea te thaki jaise.

english_text: But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.
nagamese_text: Aru jun manu Paul ke loi jaise taikhan Athens sheher pora aru dur te taike loi jaise. Aru jitia taikhan Silas aru Timothy duijon ke Paul pora tai usorte te joldi ahibole dibi koi kene khobor paise, taikhan nijor laga ghor te jai jaise.

english_text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.
nagamese_text: Jitia Paul Athens te Silas aru Timothy ke rukhi thakise, tai etu sheher te murti bhorta thaka dikhi kene tai laga atma pora bisi mon dukh hoise.

english_text: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.
nagamese_text: Titia tai mondoli te jai kene Yehudi aru hosa Isor ke aradhana kora manu khan logote kotha korise, aru hodai tai jitia bajar te jai ta te bhi manu lok paile etu laga kotha kori thakise.

english_text: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.
nagamese_text: Titia Epicurean aru Stoic khan laga pondit kunba ahi kene tai logot kotha lagi thakise, aru kunba koise, etu ke najana manu ki kobole mon kori ase? Dusra koise tai dusra jaga laga dhorom manu ase, kelemane tai Jisu laga kotha aru jee utha laga kotha prochar kori ase.

english_text: They took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which you are speaking about?
nagamese_text: Taikhan Paul ke Aropagus laga usorte loi jaise aru koise, “Tumi ki koi ase aru sikhai ase etu amikhan bhi janibole paribo?

english_text: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane amikhan laga kan pora kitia bhi nahuna kotha huni bole pai ase. Etu nimite, amikhan bhi janibole mon ase etu kotha laga ki motlob ase.”

english_text: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.
nagamese_text: -Etiya sob Athens laga manu aru dusra desh pora ahi kene thaka manu khan dusra eku kaam nakori kene kiba notun kotha hunile etu laga kotha koi kene bohi thake.

english_text: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.
nagamese_text: Titia Paul Areopagus majote khara hoi kene koise, “Tumi Athens laga manu khan, moi dikhi ase tumikhan sob kaam te bhal ase.

english_text: For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.
nagamese_text: Jitia moi tumikhan laga puja kori thaka saman khan saikene paar kori thakise, tumikhan pathor pora bona bedi te eneka likhi kene rakha dikhise, “Ekjon najana Isor nimite.” Etu karone junke apnikhan najani kene puja kori thaki ase, etu laga kotha tumikhan ke moi kobo.

english_text: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.
nagamese_text: Isor jun he prithibi aru ta te thaka sob bonai dise, Tai sorgo aru prithibi laga Isor ase, manu pora bonai diya laga mondoli te nathake.

english_text: He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.
nagamese_text: Aru Tai manu laga hath laga sewa nalage, aru manu pora eku nibisare, kelemane Tai he sobke jibon aru saas diye aru manu ki lage Tai etu sob diye.

english_text: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai ekjon manu pora he ekta desh aru jiman manu etiya thaki ase etu sobke bonai dise, ki homoi te kineka dibole lage aru kun manu laga jat kote thaki bole lage etu sob Tai pora bonai kene rakhidise,

english_text: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.
nagamese_text: Eneka korile manu khan Taike bisaribo aru taikhan Isor phale mon dibo aru Tai usorte ahibo. Kintu Tai amikhan pora kitia bhi dur thaka nai.

english_text: ‘For in him we live, move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’
nagamese_text: Kelemane amikhan Tai logote jinda ase aru amikhan laga ki ase etu sob to Tai laga he ase, jineka apuni khan laga majote kitab likha ekjon pora koise, ‘Amikhan sob Tai laga bacha khan he ase.’

english_text: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, amikhan Isor laga bacha ase, amikhan eneka bhabona kori bole nalage ki tai laga sobhab to suna, chandi, aru pathor nisena ase- eitu khan jinis to manu laga bhabona pora bonai.

english_text: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,
nagamese_text: Etu nimite Isor poila te manu laga paap dhyan nakori kene chari dise, kintu etiya Tai sob manu ke paap pora mon ghura bole hukum dise.

english_text: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane, ek dinte rakhi kene ase, juntu dinte, Tai pora basi luwa ekjon pora etu duniya ke dhormikta pora bisar koribo. Isor he Jisu ke mora pora jinda kori kene Tai hosa Isor ase koi kene dikhai dise.”

english_text: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Athens laga manu khan mori kene jinda huwa kotha hunise, kunba ta te thaka khan Paul ke hinsa korise; kintu kunba koise, “Amikhan etu kotha apuni pora aru hunibo.”

english_text: Thus Paul went out from among them.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Paul taikhan laga majot pora ulai jaise.

english_text: But certain men joined with him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba tai logote mili jaise aru tai ki kotha koise etu biswas korise, etu majote Dionysius jun Areopagus laga ekjon manu, aru Damaris koi kene ekjon mahila, aru dusra manu khan bhi taikhan logote thakise.

english_text: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Paul Athens pora Corinth sheher te jaise.

english_text: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,
nagamese_text: Ta te tai ekjon Yehudi manu Aquila koi kene lok paise, tai Pontus laga manu thakise, aru tai olop din age te Italy pora tai laga maiki Priscilla ke loi kene ahise, kelemane Claudius pora Yehudi manu khan ke Rome pora jai jabole hukum dise. Paul taikhan usorte jaise,

english_text: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.
nagamese_text: aru kelemane taikhan ki kaam kore etu Paul bhi kora nimite, taikhan logote thaki kene kaam korise, kele koile taikhan sob tambu bona manu asele.

english_text: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuaded Jews and Greeks.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul to mondoli te jai kene hodai Bisram dinte taikhan logote kotha kori thakise. Tai Yehudi aru Yunani manu khan ke Isor laga kotha mani kene thaki bole nimite koi thakise.

english_text: When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
nagamese_text: Jitia Silas aru Timothy duijon Macedonia pora ahise, Paul Isor laga kotha te pura mon dikene thakise, aru Yehudi manu khan ke Jisu Khrista laga gawahi koi thakise.

english_text: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”
nagamese_text: Kintu Yehudi manu khan tai laga kotha mana nai aru taike sorom khilai dise, Paul tai laga kapra jharikena taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan laga khun tumikhan nijor matha uporte ahibole dibi; moi eku golti kora nai. Etiya pora moi Isor najana manu usorte he jabo.”

english_text: He departed there and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
nagamese_text: Aru tai ta te pora ulaikene ekjon manu Titus Justus laga ghor te jaise, tai Isor ke mohima kora ekjon thakise. Tai laga ghor mondoli laga usorte thakise.

english_text: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.
nagamese_text: Crispus, mondoli laga ekjon cholawta, Probhu ke biswas kori loise, aru tai laga ghor manu sob bhi biswas korise; aru Corinth te kiman manu Isor laga kotha hunise taikhan bhi biswas kori kene baptizma loise.

english_text: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;
nagamese_text: Aru ek rati, Probhu he Paul ke sapna te koise, “Bhoi na koribi, kintu moi laga kotha koi thakibi aru kitia bhi chup nathakibi.

english_text: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi tumi logote ase, aru kun bhi tumike ahi kene eku kori bole na paribo, aru tumike nuksan nakoribo, kelemane etu sheher te moi laga manu bisi ase.”

english_text: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul ta te ek saal aru choi mohina thakise, Isor laga kotha manu khan ke sikhai thakise.

english_text: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Gallio pora Achaia laga Governor hoise, sob Yehudi manu khan mili kene Paul laga bhirodh te khara hoise aru taike dhori kene bisar kora jagate loi anise;

english_text: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”
nagamese_text: taikhan koise, “Etu manu amikhan laga niyom bhirodh te jai kene Isor laga kotha sikhai ase aru mani bole koi ase.”

english_text: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul pora kotha kobole mukh khuli se, Gallio pora Yehudi khan ke koise, “Tumi Yehudi khan, jodi etu kotha golti aru paap kaam kora laga ase koile, moi tumikhan nimite bisar koribo.

english_text: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”
nagamese_text: Kintu tai koi thaka kotha kunba laga naam nimite aru tumikhan laga niyom laga ase koile, tumikhan nijor hai sai lobi. Moi etu kotha khan nimite bisar kori bole mon nai.”

english_text: So he drove them from the judgment seat.
nagamese_text: Titia Gallio bisar laga jaga pora taikhan ke jabole dise.

english_text: Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan sob Sosthenes usorte jaise, mondoli laga ekjon cholawta, aru taike bisar kora jagate jai kene marise. Kintu Gallio to eitu khan nimite eku chinta kora nai.

english_text: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul, bisi din ta te thaka pichete, ta te laga bhai khan ke chari kene Syria te jaise, Priscilla aru Aquila bhi tai logote thakise. Tai Cenchrea te tai nijor laga chuli kati dise kelemane tai kosom khaise.

english_text: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan Ephesus te ahise, Paul pora Priscilla aru Aquila ke ta te chari dise, kintu tai nijor jai kene Yehudi khan logote kotha kori thakise.

english_text: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Paul ke ta te aru olop din thaki bole koise, tai mana nai.

english_text: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.
nagamese_text: Kintu tai anurodh kori kene taikhan ke koise, “Isor itcha hoile moi aru bhi ahibo.” Ta te pora tai naw te uthi kene Ephesus te jai jaise.

english_text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul Caesarea te namise, tai jai kene Jerusalem girja te manu khan ke salam dise aru ta te pora tai Antioch te jaise.

english_text: Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
nagamese_text: Aru olop din ta te thaka pichete, Paul ta te pora ulai jai kene Galatia aru Phrygia laga desh te kiman biswasi manu khan ase taikhan laga mon dangor kori dise.

english_text: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.
nagamese_text: Ta te Apollos koi kene ekjon manu thakise, tai jonom pora Alexandria laga manu thakise, kintu tai Ephesus te ahise. Tai to Isor laga kotha bhal pora jana aru kobo para ekjon gyaani manu thakise.

english_text: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.
nagamese_text: Apollos ke Probhu laga rasta te thik pora mani kene thaki bole koi dise. Atma te bhal kori kene thaki bole nimite, aru mon dikene Jisu laga kotha manu khan ke sikhai thake, kintu tai John pora diya baptizma he jane.

english_text: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite Apollos mondoli te jai kene mon dangor pora kotha koi thakise. Kintu jitia Priscilla aru Aquila tai laga kotha hunise, taike kinar te loijai kene Isor laga kotha aru bhi bhal pora bujhai dise.

english_text: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him; and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;
nagamese_text: Jitia tai Achaia jaga ke paar kori kene jabole itcha korise, titia biswasi bhai khan pora tai laga mon dangor kori dise aru taike bhal pora grohon koribi koi kene Achaia te thaka chela khan ke ekta chithi likhi dise. Jitia tai ta te punchise, tai Isor laga anugrah pora biswasi khan ke bisi modot dise.

english_text: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
nagamese_text: Aru Apollos pora manu khan usorte mon dangor kori kene Yehudi khan ke kotha pora jitise aru Shastro te likhi kene thaka pora Jisu he Khrista ase koi kene dikhai dise.

english_text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Apollos Corinth te thakise, Paul to upor phale thaka desh paar kori kene Ephesus laga sheher te punchise, aru ta te kunba chela khan ke lok paise.

english_text: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
nagamese_text: Aru Paul taikhan ke koise, “Tumikhan biswas kora homoi te Pobitro Atma paise?” Kintu taikhan taike koise, “Nai, amikhan Pobitro Atma ase koi kene huna bhi nai.”

english_text: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul koise, “Tenehoile tumikhan ki pora baptizma loise?” Taikhan koise, “John laga baptizma pora.”

english_text: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul koise, “John pora mon ghura laga baptizma pora tumikhan ke baptizma dise. Tai manu khan ke koise tumikhan John laga pichete ekjon ahi ase Taike biswas koribi, Tai Jisu ase.”

english_text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
nagamese_text: Jitia manu khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan sob Probhu Jisu laga naam te baptizma loise.

english_text: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul taikhan laga uporte hath rakhidise, Pobitro Atma taikhan laga uporte ahi jaise titia taikhan alag kotha pora bhabobani kobole shuru hoise.

english_text: They were about twelve men in all.
nagamese_text: Ta te taikhan sob milai kene baroh jon manu thakise.

english_text: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul mondoli te jai kene tin mohina tak Isor laga kotha mon dangor kori kene koise, manu khan ke Isor laga rajyo kotha bhujai kene biswas kori bole koi dise.

english_text: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba Yehudi khan mon tan kori kene kotha mana nai, taikhan manu khan usorte biya kotha kobole shuru hoise. Titia Paul taikhan ke chari kene chela khan ke loi jaise, aru hodai din Tyrannus hall te jai kene kotha koi thakise,

english_text: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka dui saal tak hoi thakise, etu karone Asia te kiman manu thakise taikhan sob Probhu laga kotha hunise, Yehudi aru Yunani manu khan bhi.

english_text: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,
nagamese_text: Isor pora Paul laga hath pora kitia bhi nadikha asurit kaam khan korise,

english_text: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
nagamese_text: etu karone manu khan rumal nohoile kapra loi kene tai gaw ke chui dibo, aru bemar bhal hoi thake, aru biya atma khan bhi gaw chari kene bahar ulai jai thakise.

english_text: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”
nagamese_text: Titia kunba Yehudi khan etu jaga phale beraikena jadu-tona, jhara-jhari kori thakise. Taikhan bhi jun manu logot dushto atma thakise utu khan ke Probhu Jisu laga naam lobole kosis kori kene eneka koise, “Moi tumike Paul pora prochar kori thaka Jisu laga naam pora bahar te ulai jabole hukum di ase.”

english_text: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
nagamese_text: Aru Yehudi laga maha purohit kaam kora Sceva laga sat jon chokra khan tineka kaam kori thakise.

english_text: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”
nagamese_text: Aru dushto atma koise, “Moi Jisu ke jane aru Paul ke bhi jane, kintu tumi kun ase?”

english_text: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
nagamese_text: Titia jun logot te dusto atma thakise, utu manu taikhan uporte uthi kene taikhan ke marise aru harai dise, aru manu khan sob utu ghor pora lengta hoi kene, bisi jokhom paikena polai jaise.

english_text: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
nagamese_text: Aru utu kotha Ephesus te thaka Yehudi aru Yunani khan sob jani jaise, aru taikhan sob bhoi lagi jaise, aru Probhu Jisu naam ke prosansa kori thakise.

english_text: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.
nagamese_text: Aru jun biswas kori loise utu khan pora bisi manu ahi kene nijor-nijor he taikhan ki biya kaam korise etu sob laga paap shikar korise.

english_text: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
nagamese_text: Aru jadu-tona kori thaka khan nijor-nijor jadu laga kitab khan joma kori sob manu pora dikhikena jolai dise, aru jitia utu daam hisab kori saise, etu chandi poisa te pachas hajar toka nisena thakise.

english_text: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.
nagamese_text: Karone Probhu laga kotha pora jiti kene biswasi khan bisi hoi jaise.

english_text: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul Ephesus te tai laga sewkai kaam khotom korise, tai Atma te bhabi loise jitia tai Jerusalem te jabo, titia tai Macedonia aru Achaia te bhi jabo; aru koise, “Ami ta te juwa pichete, aru Rome te bhi jai kene sabo lagibo.”

english_text: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
nagamese_text: Etu karone tai sewa te thaka Timothy aru Erastus duijon ke Macedonia te pathai kene tai olop homoi karone Asia te thaki jaise.

english_text: About that time there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way.
nagamese_text: Aru etu homoi te, Ephesus te Isor laga Rasta laga kotha nimite dangor gondugol hoise.

english_text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,
nagamese_text: Demetrius koi kene chandi laga kaam kora ekjon thakise aru tai chandi pora Artemis laga mondoli te murtikhan bisi bonaise, aru etu pora kaam kora khan bisi labh hoi thakise.

english_text: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.
nagamese_text: Aru tai pora tai nisena kaam kori thaka khan sobke mati anikena koise, “Hey sahab khan, apnikhan bhi jani ase, amikhan etu kaam kora pora bisi poisa pai thake.

english_text: You see and hear that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods that are made with hands.
nagamese_text: Aru apnikhan bhi dikhi aru huni ase, khali Ephesus te he nohoi kintu pura Asia te eneka koi kene Paul pora bisi manu ke biswas kori loi ase, tai koi ase juntu hath pora bonaise utu Isor nohoi.

english_text: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”
nagamese_text: Etu karone khali ami laga kaam ke he nohoi, kintu Asia te, aru pura duniya te puja kori thaka maha devi Artemis laga mondoli ke bhi bodnam koridi ase, aru devi laga naam bhi harai jabole bhoi hoise.”

english_text: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
nagamese_text: Jitia manu khan etu kotha hunise, taikhan bisi khong uthise, aru bisi jor pora hala kori koise, “Ephesus laga Artemis mohan ase.”

english_text: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
nagamese_text: Eneka hoi kene pura sheher te hala hoi jaise; titia taikhan mili kene ahise aru Gaius aru Aristarchus jun Paul logote safar kori thaka manu khan asele, tai duijon ke dhori kene moncho ghor te loi anise.

english_text: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul to ta te jabole bisi mon korise, kintu chela khan pora taike jabo diya nai.

english_text: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba Asia te thaka adhikari khan pora taikhan laga sathi khan ke khobor pathai kene Paul ke moncho ghor te najabi koise.

english_text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.
nagamese_text: Aru bhir te thaka kunba pora kiba kobo, aru dusra pora kiba kobo eneka hoi thakise, etu pora bhir te manu khan bisi matha ghurai thakise. Ta te bisi manu etu bhi jani kene thaka nai taikhan kele ta te joma thakise.

english_text: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.
nagamese_text: Aru Yehudi khan pora Alexander ke age te loi rakhidise, aru Alexander tai laga hath uthaikene manu khan ke bujhai dibole korise.

english_text: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia tai Yehudi manu ase koi kene jani loise, sob mili kene dui ghanta tak, “Ephesus laga Artemis mohan ase” eneka hala kori thakise.

english_text: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?
nagamese_text: Aru titia sheher laga cholawta he sob manu ke chup kori kene koise, “Hey Ephesus manu khan, Ephesus laga sheher to maha devi laga mondoli rakhi thaka jaga ase koi kene, aru murti nisena sabole juntu akas pora ahise etu kun manu najane?

english_text: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rash.
nagamese_text: Karone utu jinis khan to nohoi kobo napare, titia hoile chup-chap hoi jabole lage, aru eku kori bole dorkar nai.

english_text: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.
nagamese_text: Kelemane etu duijon mondoli te chor dokaiti kora nohoi aru tumi laga devi laga uporte eku biya kotha kowa nohoi, hoilebi tumikhan pora taikhan ke dhori anise.

english_text: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.
nagamese_text: Karone Demetrius aru tai logote kaam kora khan he kunba logot kotha namila thakile, bisar kora jaga aru sabha to khula ase, taikhan ta te pora bisar koribo dibi.

english_text: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi apnikhan etu te bhi aru kiba ase koile, thik homoi te sabha pora bisar kori lobo lage.

english_text: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane aji gondugol kora nimite ami upor golti dibole bhoi ase, etu eku motlob nathaki kene gondugol kora etu laga jowab dibole na paribo.”

english_text: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
nagamese_text: Aru tai etu kotha koi kene sabha ke chari dise.

english_text: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
nagamese_text: Jitia gondugol to khotom hoise, Paul chela khan ke mati anise aru taikhan ke samjai dise, aru taikhan ke bhidai kori kene tai Macedonia te jai jaise.

english_text: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.
nagamese_text: Titia tai utu desh khan paar kori kene khotom huwa pichete, tai Greece te ahi jaise.

english_text: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
nagamese_text: Aru tai ta te tin mohina thakise aru ta te pora Syria te jabole thakise, kintu Yehudi khan taike morai dibole thaka jani kene, Macedonia phale pora he wapas jabole bhabi loise.

english_text: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
nagamese_text: Aru Berea manu Sopater laga chokra, aru Thessalonica pora Aristarchus aru Secundus aru Derbe pora Gaius aru Timothy aru Asia pora Tychicus aru Trophimus taikhan tai logote jaise.

english_text: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.
nagamese_text: Kintu eitu khan amikhan age te jai kene Troas te rukhi thakise.

english_text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
nagamese_text: Aru khomir nahala roti laga utsov din pichete amikhan Philippi pora naw te uthi kene pans din pichete Troas te taikhan logot ponchise, aru saat din tak ta te thakise.

english_text: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.
nagamese_text: Titia hapta laga prothom din jitia biswasi chela khan eke loge mili kene roti bhangai sele. Paul dusra dinte jabole thakise, etu karone tai taikhan logot adha rati tak kotha kori thakise.

english_text: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.
nagamese_text: Upor kamra kot te amikhan joma thakisele ta te bisi saaki khan jolai rakhise.

english_text: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead.
nagamese_text: Aru Eutychus koi kene jawan ekjon khirki te bohi thakise, aru Paul bisi deri kotha koi thaka pora, tai ghumai kene tin tola upor pora nichete girikena morise.

english_text: Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul niche jai kene tai usorte tai laga gaw ke lamba korise, aru taike dhurise. Aru tai koise, “Bhoi nokoribi, kelemane tai laga jibon etiya bhi tai logot he ase.”

english_text: When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.
nagamese_text: Titia tai aru upor jai kene roti bhangai khaise aru phojur tak kotha kori thakise, aru etu pichete jai jaise.

english_text: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan utu chokra jinda pa karone ekdom shanti paise.

english_text: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
nagamese_text: Titia amikhan naw pora Assos te jaise, aru ta te pora naw te Paul ke uthabole thakise, kelemane tai nije pora he tai berai kene jabo koise, aru tai he eneka kori bole amikhan ke koise.

english_text: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
nagamese_text: Aru tai Assos te ahi amikhan ke lok paise, aru amikhan taike uthaikene Mitylene te ahi jaise.

english_text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te pora naw te uthi kene dusra din Chios usorte ahi jaise, utu din amikhan Samos ponchise, aru Tragyllium te thaki kene dusra din Miletus te ahi Jaise.

english_text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Paul Asia te homoi phelabo mon kora nai, tai naw pora Ephesus paar kori bole mon korise, kelemane parile Pentecost din tai Jerusalem te thakibo mon kori kene tara-tari kori thakisele.

english_text: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
nagamese_text: Tai Miletus pora khobor pathai kene Ephesus girja laga bura khan ke matise.

english_text: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taikhan tai logot ahise, tai koise, “Moi juntu din pora Asia te ahise, utu prothom din pora kineka moi tumi logote thakise, apnikhan jani ase.”

english_text: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
nagamese_text: Moi nomrota korise aru suku pani girikena aru Yehudi khan pora chalak kori kene moike dukh di thakile bhi moi Probhu laga sewa kori thakise.

english_text: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
nagamese_text: Aru moi apnikhan ke sikha khan te, manu usorte nohoile ghor te hoilebi tumi bhal nimite kaam nakori kene chari diya nai.

english_text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
nagamese_text: Yehudi aru Yehudi hobi, moi taikhan ke mon ghurai kene Isor phale ahibole aru Jisu ke biswas kori bole sikhai ahise.

english_text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, etiya moi Atma laga kotha mani kene Jerusalem te jai ase hoilebi ta te moi logote ki hobo moi najane.

english_text: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.
nagamese_text: Juntu sheher te jaile bhi Pobitro Atma pora ami laga gawah koridi thakise, aru khali bandha aru dukh he moike rukhi ase koi kene.

english_text: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
nagamese_text: Kintu moi nijor jibon karone eku chinta nathaki, kintu Probhu Jisu pora ji kaam moike kori bole dise, utu Isor anugrah laga susamachar ke khushi pora manu ke jonai dibole aru etu pura kori bole he bhabi thake.

english_text: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
nagamese_text: Aru sabi, moi jani ase, moi Isor rajyo kotha loi kene sob jagate prochar koribo, aru apnikhan etiya pora ami laga chehera aru nadikhibo.

english_text: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,
nagamese_text: Etu moi aji apnikhan ke sakhi di ase, moi ekjon golti nathaka manu laga khun phale hoile golti nai.

english_text: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Isor laga itcha phale sob kotha moi apuni khan ke koi diya hoise.

english_text: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.
nagamese_text: Etu karone apnikhan nije bhi hoshiar thakibi aru Pobitro Atma pora apnikhan ke sabole mer khan dise. Hoshiar pora Isor laga girja ke roikhya koribi, jintu Isor Tai Nijor laga bacha khun pora kinise.

english_text: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi jani ase moi juwa pichete rong kutta khan tumi laga majote ahibo, aru tumikhan ke nacharibo jun khan etiya bisi ase.

english_text: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
nagamese_text: Aru moi jani ase tumikhan nijor bhitor pora bhi misa kowa ulabo aru biswasi khan ke taikhan phale kori loi lobo.

english_text: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
nagamese_text: Karone hoshiar koi kene thakibi, aru bhabona koribi, moi tin saal tak rati din suku pani girai kene sob manu ke sikhaise.

english_text: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
nagamese_text: Aru bhai khan moi etiya apnikhan ke di ase, Isor aru tai anugrah laga kotha juntu pora tumikhan ke uthidibo pare aru sapha kori diya khan logote milaikena tai laga miras pabo thaka khan ase.

english_text: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.
nagamese_text: Moi kun laga suna, chandi, kapra khan lalos kora nohoi.

english_text: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan jani ase, moi nijor hath pora sewa kori kene nijor aru jun moi logot thakise, taikhan ke ki lage sob kori ahise.

english_text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
nagamese_text: Moi apnikhan ke sob rasta sikhai dise, kineka sewa kori kene dukhia khan ke modot koribo lage, aru Probhu Jisu kotha monte bhabona kori bole, juntu Tai nijor pora koise: “Lu-a pora to diya jon he bisi asishit ase.”

english_text: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai etu kotha koi diya hoise, tai athukari kene taikhan logote prathana kori loise.

english_text: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan sob bisi kandise, aru Paul ke dhori kene taike chuma dise.

english_text: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
nagamese_text: Taikhan bisi mon dukh huwa to Paul laga kotha karone hoise, aru kitia bhi tai laga chehera nadikhibo kowa karone, aru taikhan taike loijai kene jahaaj tak punchai dise.
