english_text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan pora alag koi kene amikhan jahaaj te uthi kene sidha rasta jaise aru Cos te ponchise, aru dusra din Rhodes te, aru ta te pora Patara te ahi jaise.

english_text: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
nagamese_text: Ta te pora ekta jahaaj Phoenicia te jabole thaka paise, etu pora amikhan bhi ta te uthi kene jaise.

english_text: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.
nagamese_text: Cyprus sheher ke dikhikena aru paar korise aru amikhan Syria phale jaise, aru Tyre te nami jaise, kelemane ta te jahaaj laga saman namabole thakise.

english_text: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te kunba biswasi chela khan lok paikene amikhan saat din ta te thakise. Aru taikhan Atma dwara Paul ke Jerusalem te najabole koise.

english_text: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
nagamese_text: Jitia amikhan laga din pura hoi jaise titia taikhan pora alag hoi kene amikhan logote taikhan maiki khan aru bacha khan sob loi kene amikhan ke sheher bahar te loijai dise, amikhan sob ta te pora athukari kene prathana korise,

english_text: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
nagamese_text: titia alag hoi kene amikhan jahaaj te uthijaise, aru taikhan nijor-nijor ghor te jai jaise.

english_text: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia amikhan Tyre pora safar khotom hoise, amikhan Ptolemais te ponchise. Aru bhai khan ke salam jonai kene taikhan logote ek din thakise.

english_text: On the next day, we who were Paul’s companions departed and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
nagamese_text: Dusra din amikhan ta te pora ahi Caesarea te ponchise, aru prochar kora Phillip jun saat jon laga majote ekjon asele, tai ghor te ahi kene tai logot thakise.

english_text: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
nagamese_text: Etu manu laga shadi nakorikena thaka charjon swali thakise, aru utu khan sob bhabobani koi thakise.

english_text: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te bisi din thaki jaise, titia bhabobadi ekjon Agabus koi kene Judea pora ahise.

english_text: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
nagamese_text: Jitia tai amikhan logot ahise tai Paul laga peti loi nijor hath theng ke bandi kene koise, “Jun manu etu komor bandha peti laga malik ase taike ‘Jerusalem te Yehudi khan pora taike eneka bandi kene Isor najana khan laga hathte dibo, eneka Pobitro Atma koi ase.’”

english_text: When we heard these things, both we and the people of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Etu kotha huni kene amikhan aru ta te thaka khan sob pora Paul ke Jerusalem te najabi koi kene rukhaise.

english_text: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul koise, “Apuni khan ki kori ase, kandi-kandi kene ami laga mon dukhai ase? Moi to taiyar ase, khali bandibole nimite nohoi, hoilebi Probhu Jisu naam karone mori bole bhi taiyar ase.”

english_text: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”
nagamese_text: Jitia amikhan janise Paul to namanibo, titia amikhan chup thaki jaise aru titia moi khan koise, “Amikhan Isor laga itcha hobo dibi.”

english_text: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Aru utu din pichete amikhan saman bandhi kene Jerusalem te jai jaise.

english_text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.
nagamese_text: Caesarea te kunba chela khan amikhan logote ahise, aru taikhan Mnason koi kene Cyprus manu ekjon jun purana chela asele, taike amikhan logote thaki bole loi anise.

english_text: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia amikhan Jerusalem te ponchise, biswasi bhai khan bisi khushi pora amikhan ke swekar korise.

english_text: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra dinte Paul amikhan ke James laga ghor te loi jaise, ta te girja bura khan sob joma thakise.

english_text: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.
nagamese_text: Titia tai taikhan ke salam jonai kene Isor pora tai laga sewkai dwara ki kaam Porjati khan logote korise, eitu khan sob ekta-ekta kori kene sob koi dise.

english_text: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.
nagamese_text: Taikhan etu huni kene Isor ke mohima korise, aru tai koise, “Bhai khan etu sabi, Yehudi khan majote hajar manu bhi biswas kori loise, aru taikhan sob bhal pora niyom mani thake.

english_text: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke manu khan pora apuni laga kotha koi dise, apuni Porjati khan laga jagah te thaka Yehudi khan ke Moses laga niyom ke namanibi koi kene hikai ase, aru bacha khan laga sunnot nakorile bhi hobo eneka sikhai ase hunise.

english_text: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.
nagamese_text: Tinehoile amikhan ki koribo? Taikhan apuni yate ahi ponchise koi kene jani thakibo pare.

english_text: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.
nagamese_text: Karone ekta kaam koribi amikhan logote kiba kori bole kosom luwa charjon ase.

english_text: Take them and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
nagamese_text: Taikhan ke loi kene taikhan logote nijorke bhi pobitro kori lobi, aru taikhan matha chuli pura kati bole kharcha dibi. Titia sob manu jani lobo taikhan pora tumikhan laga ki kotha koi ase etu sob misa ase, kintu tumikhan to thik pora thaki ase aru niyom manikena thaki ase koi kene jani lobo.

english_text: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Porjati khan ke jun biswas kori loise utu khan ke amikhan age pora likhi dise, murti ke boli diya laga bostu aru khun, aru gola mussri kene mangso kha-a aru bebichar kora, etu sob pora bachi thakibi koise.”

english_text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
nagamese_text: Titia Paul dusra din manu khan ke loi taikhan logote sapha kori loise, aru girja te jai kene ekjon-ekjon laga kiman din tak sapha koribo lage koi dise aru sob nimite daan korise.

english_text: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia saat-din khotom hobole hoise, kunba Yehudi khan Asia pora ahikena taike mondoli te dikhise, aru manu khan ke chukli mari kene taike dhori loise.

english_text: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”
nagamese_text: Taikhan hala kori kene koise, “Hey Israel khan, amikhan ke modot dibi, etu manu pora sob jagah te manu khan ke manu khan, niyom khan aru etu jaga laga bhirodh kotha koi ase aru sikhai ase, aru tai Yunani manu khan ke bhi girja te anikena pobitro jaga ke letera kori dise.”

english_text: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
nagamese_text: Age te Paul ekbar Trophimus koi kene Ephesus laga manu logote berai thaka dikhise, aru taikhan bhabise Paul he eitu ke loi girja te anise eneka bhabi thakise.

english_text: All the city was moved and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.
nagamese_text: Titia etu sheher te gondugol hoise, sob polai ahi kene Paul ke dhuri loise, aru taike tani bahar te loi jaise, aru joldi mondoli laga dorja khan bondh kori dise.

english_text: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan taike morai dibole thaka homoi te, pura Jerusalem te hungama hoi ase koi kene etu khobor mukhyo henedhikari logote ponchise.

english_text: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.
nagamese_text: Titia tai joldi sipahi khan aru henapoti khan loi kene niche phale polaikena taikhan logot punchise, aru jitia manu khan mukhyo henedhikari aru sipahi khan ke dikhise, taikhan Paul ke mari thaka pora rukhi jaise.

english_text: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.
nagamese_text: Titia mukhyo henedhikari usorte ahi kene taike dhori loise, aru duita luha rusi pora taike bandi lobole koi dise, aru hudise etu manu kun ase aru tai ki korise.

english_text: Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
nagamese_text: Aru bhir te kunba kiba-kibi koise, aru kunba dusra kiba koi thakise, aru bisi hala kora karone tai thik pora eku bujhi bo para nai, etu karone taike bondhi kora jagate loi jabole hukum dise.

english_text: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
nagamese_text: Jitia tai siri te ponchise, manu khan bisi khong kora karone sipahi khan taike uthaikene loi jaise.

english_text: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”
nagamese_text: Kelemane bisi manu tai piche-piche hala kori thakise, “Taike morai dibi!”

english_text: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan Paul ke bondhi rakha jagate loi jabole thakise, tai mukhyo henedhikari ke koise, “Moi apuni ke kiba kotha kobo paribo?” Tai koise, “Tumi Yunani kotha kobo pare?

english_text: Aren’t you then the Egyptian who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
nagamese_text: Olop din age te, ekjon Egypt manu, jun pora chukli mari kene gondugol kori dise, aru char-hajar ‘Hathiara manu khan ke’ jongol te loi jaise, utu manu to tumi nohoi?”

english_text: But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul koise, “Moi to Tarsus laga Yehudi ase Cilicia sheher te jonom huwa manu ase. Aru moi utu khas sheher laga ekjon manu ase. Etu nimite, apuni logote anurodh kori ase, moike manu khan logot kotha kori bole dibi.”

english_text: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
nagamese_text: Jitia tai agya dise, Paul siri te khara hoi kene kotha kobole tai hath uthaise, aru manu khan chup hoi jaise, aru jitia taikhan chup hoise, titia tai Yehudi bhasa te kotha koise. Tai koise,

english_text: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”
nagamese_text: “Bhai khan, aru baba khan, moi etiya nijor laga safai te apnikhan usorte kotha kobole ase, etu ke huni bhi.”

english_text: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai Yehudi bhasa te koise, taikhan arubi ekdom chup thaki jaise. Titia tai aru koise,

english_text: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.
nagamese_text: “Moi Yehudi ase Cilicia laga Tarsus sheher te jonom luwa, etu sheher pora Gamaliel laga theng te bohi kene amikhan laga baba khan laga niyom thik pora sikhi loise, aru Isor phale jor dikena aji apnikhan jineka kori ase tineka kori ahisele.

english_text: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,
nagamese_text: Aru mota, maiki, hobi, etu dhorom Rasta te juwa khan ke bondhi ghor te dikene morai bhi di thakise,

english_text: as also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.
nagamese_text: etu kotha cholawta, bura khan aru sabha bhi sakhi dibo pare, moi taikhan pora ami laga bhai khan Damascus te thaka khan logote chithi likhi diya utu bhi loise, karone moi jai kene ta te kunba thakile dhori kene Jerusalem te ani taikhan ke sajai dibo bhabise.

english_text: “As I made my journey and came close to Damascus, about noon suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.
nagamese_text: Etu homoi moi Damascus punchibole usor hoi asele, titia din nisena homoi asele, aru sorgo pora achanak ekta dangor puhor ahi moi usorte thaki jaise.

english_text: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
nagamese_text: Aru moi matite giri jaise, aru ekta awaj moike kowa hunise, ‘Saul, Saul, kele tumi Moike digdar kori ase?

english_text: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’
nagamese_text: Karone moi hudise, ‘Probhu Apuni kun ase?’ Aru Tai moike koise, ‘Moi Nazareth Jisu ase, junke tumi dukh digdar di ase.’

english_text: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.
nagamese_text: Aru jun manu moi logot ahise, taikhan bhi puhor to dikhise aru bhoi korise, kintu taikhan moike kotha kowa laga awaj to huna nai.

english_text: I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’
nagamese_text: Titia moi koise, ‘Moi ki koribo lage Probhu?’ Aru Probhu moike koise, ‘Uthi kene Damascus te jabi, aru ta te tumi ki-ki koribo lage etu sob tumike koi dibo.’

english_text: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
nagamese_text: Aru utu puhor bisi huwa karone moi eku dikhibo para nai, titia moi laga sathi khan laga hath dhurikena he moi Damascus te ahise.

english_text: “One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,
nagamese_text: Titia Ananias koi kene ekjon asele, tai niyom mani thaka ekjon asele, aru ta te thaka Yehudi khan bisi sonman kori thaka manu ase.

english_text: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.
nagamese_text: Tai ami laga usorte ahikena koise, ‘Bhai Saul, apuni laga suku dikhi bhi.’ Aru etu homoi te moi dikhibole parise aru taike dikhise.

english_text: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
nagamese_text: Titia tai koise, ami laga baba khan laga Isor he tumike basi loise, tumi he tai itcha ke janibole aru Dharmikta Jonke sabo paribole aru tai nijor mukh pora kowa awaj ke huni bole.

english_text: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
nagamese_text: Kelemane tumi ki dikhise aru ki hunise etu sob manu ke koi dibole tai sakhi bonai dise.

english_text: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
nagamese_text: Tinehoile apuni etiya bhi kele bohi ase? Uthi kene baptizma loi lobi, aru prathana kori kene tai naam pora tumi laga paap dhui dibi.’

english_text: “When I had returned to Jerusalem and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance
nagamese_text: Titia moi aru Jerusalem te ahi kene mondoli te prathana kori asele, titia moi Atma te bhorta hoi kene darshan dikhise.

english_text: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’
nagamese_text: Aru moi Probhu ke dikhise, Tai moike koise, ‘Joldi Jerusalem chari kene jabi, kelemane taikhan Ami laga kotha tumi gawahi diya ke namanibo.’

english_text: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.
nagamese_text: Karone moi koise, ‘Probhu, moi pora biswasi khan mondoli te dhurikena bondhi ghor te diya aru mari thaka taikhan jani ase.

english_text: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Apuni nimite mori juwa Stephen ke khun giraikena morai di thakise, ta te moi bhi thakise, aru jun manu khan pora taike morai dise utu khan laga kapra ke moi rukhi thakise.’

english_text: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’”
nagamese_text: Titia Tai moike koise, ‘Jabi, kelemane moi tumike yate pora dur Porjati khan logot pathai dibo.’

english_text: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan etu kotha kowa tak taike huni thakise. Etu pichete taikhan awaj uthaikene hala kori koise, “Eneka manu ke prithibi pora hatai dibi, kelemane tai jinda thaki bole thik nohoi.”

english_text: As they cried out, threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan hala kori kene taikhan laga kapra khan ulai phelaise, aru upor hawa te dhul urai thakise,

english_text: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.
nagamese_text: titia mukhyo henedhikari pora Paul ke bondh kora jagate loi jabole hukum dise, aru manu khan kele taike iman ghusa kori ase etu janibole taike chabuk pora mari kene bhal pora hudibole koise.

english_text: When they had tied him up with straps, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan jitia taike chabuk mari bole taiyar korise, Paul pora tai usorte khara thaka henapoti ke koise, “Rome manu ke eku golti nathaki kene bhi chabuk mari bole niyom te ase?”

english_text: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”
nagamese_text: Jitia henapoti etu kotha hunise tai mukhyo henedhikari logote jai kene koise, “Apuni eneka kele kori ase? Tai Rome laga nagrik ase.”

english_text: The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
nagamese_text: Titia henedhikari tai logot te ahikena koise, “Moike kobi, tumi Rome laga nagrik ase?” Paul koise “Hoi”.

english_text: The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.” Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”
nagamese_text: Etu huni kene mukhyo henedhikari pora koise, “Moi to Rome laga nagrik hobole bisi toka poisa pora kinise.” Kintu Paul koise, “Moi to jonom pora he Rome laga nagrik ase.”

english_text: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.
nagamese_text: Titia jun taike mari bole thakise, taikhan loge- loge tai usor pora joldi hati jaise. Aru kitia mukhyo henedhikari bhi Paul to Rome laga nagrik ase koi kene janise, tai bhi bhoi khaise kele koile tai pora Paul ke dhori kene bandh kora karone.

english_text: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
nagamese_text: Dusra din Yehudi khan pora ki nimite Paul ke doshi korise, etu janibole mukhyo henedhikari pora Paul ke khuli dise, aru mukhyo purohit khan aru sabhakhan ke joma kori bole hukum dise, aru Paul ke loi kene taikhan age te khara kori dise.

english_text: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul sabha laga adhikari khan phale dhyan pora saikene koise, “Bhai khan, moi aji tak ekjon bhal nagrik nisena thakise, ami sapha mon pora Isor usorte bhal pora ahise.”

english_text: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
nagamese_text: Titia moha purohit Ananias pora jun khan Paul usorte khara ase taikhan pora Paul laga mukh te marikena bondh kori dibole hukum dise.

english_text: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul taike koise, “Isor pora apuni ke mari dibole ase, chuna pora boga kori rakha dewar khan. Isor apuni ke saja dibo, apuni niyom pora amike bisar kori bole bohi ase, aru kele niyom bhirodh te moike mari bole hukum di ase?”

english_text: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
nagamese_text: Kintu jun khan tai usorte khara asele taikhan koise, “Kile apuni Isor laga moha purohit ke ninda kori ase?”

english_text: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul koise, “Bhai khan, tai moha purohit ase koi kene moi jana nai. Kilekoile likha ase, Tumi pora tumi laga cholawta laga biya kotha nakobo.”

english_text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Paul dikhise sabha laga ekta bhag Sadducee khan aru dusra bhag Pharisee khan ase, tai sabha te jor pora koise, “Bhai khan, moi Pharisee ase aru Pharisee khan laga chokra ase, aji moike bisar kora to morija-a khan jee uthibo laga asha laga kotha kowa nimite he ase.”

english_text: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai etu koi dise, Pharisee aru Sadducee khan laga majote kotha namila hoise, aru sabha to dui bhag hoi jaise.

english_text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
nagamese_text: Kelemane Sadducee khan punoruthan, sorgodoth aru atma khan te biswas nakore: kintu Pharisee khan to etu sob bhi hosa ase koi kene mani thake.

english_text: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”
nagamese_text: Titia bisi jor pora hala hoi jaise aru Pharisee khan jaga pora uthi kene apatti kori koise, “Amikhan etu manu laga eku dosh pa-a nai. Kintu jodi ekta atma pora, nohoile bhi, ekjon sorgodoth pora taike kotha koi kene ase koile?”

english_text: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan bisi jhagara hoi jaise, aru henedhikari bhabise taikhan Paul ke tukra kori dibo, aru etu laga bhoi pora tai sipahi khan ke pathaise, aru joborjosti sabha pora taike bondh kora jagate loi jabole hukum dise.

english_text: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”
nagamese_text: Kintu utu rati te tai usorte Probhu ahi kene khara hoi kene koise, “Mon dangor hobi, kelemane tumi Jerusalem te Ami laga gawahi dise, tineka tumi Rome te bhi Ami laga gawahi dibo lagibo.”

english_text: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
nagamese_text: Jitia din ulaise, kunba Yehudi khan mili kene, jitia tak Paul ke loi kene morai nadibo, titia tak eku bhi nakhabo koi kene kosom korise.

english_text: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
nagamese_text: Jun khan kotha milai thakise eitu khan chalis-jon pora bhi bisi thakise.

english_text: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan mukhyo purohit khan aru bura khan logote jai kene koise, “Amikhan jitia tak Paul ke morai nadibo titia tak eku bhi nakhabo koi kene kosom khaise.

english_text: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
nagamese_text: Karone apnikhan aru sabhakhan mili kene mukhyo henedhikari logot khobor pathai dibi aru Paul ke bhal pora kotha hudibi kobi, aru eneka koi kene tai pora Paul apnikhan logot anibo. Aru amikhan to tai yate napuncha age te taike morai dibole taiyar ase.”

english_text: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Paul didi laga chokra pora taikhan Paul ke mari bole rukhi thaka janise, tai Paul ke bondh kora jagate ahikena taike etu kotha koi dise.

english_text: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul ekjon henapoti ke mati anikena koise, “Etu chokra ke mukhyo henadhikari logote loijabi, tai kiba kobole ase.”

english_text: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
nagamese_text: Karone tai taike loi kene mukhyo henedhikari logot jaise aru koise, “Bondhi ghor te thaka Paul pora moike matise aru moike etu lora apuni logote loi ani dibi koi kene anurodh korise. Tai apuni logote kiba kobole ase koise.”

english_text: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”
nagamese_text: Titia mukhyo henedhikari pora tai hath dhurikena kinar te alag loijai kene hudise, “Tumi moike ki kobole ase?”

english_text: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
nagamese_text: Aru tai koise, “Yehudi khan mili kene Paul laga kotha ke aru bhal pora hudibole kali sabha te taike loi anibole bhabona pora apuni logot anurodh kori bole ase.

english_text: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan laga kotha namanibi, kelemane taikhan chalis-jon pora bhi bisi manu taike morai nadiya tak ekubi kha luwa nakoribo koi kene kosom khai kene ase, aru taikhan apuni pora hukum pabole etiya bhi rukhi thaki ase.”

english_text: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
nagamese_text: Titia mukhyo henedhikari pora lora ke koise, “Etu kotha tumi moike kowa khan kunke bhi nokobi.”

english_text: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”
nagamese_text: Aru tai henapoti duijon ke mati ani kene koise, “Aji rati nou-baji te duisoh sipahi aru sat-ta ghora chola sipahi aru duisoh jathi-dhora sena khan loi kene Caesarea te jabole taiyar kori dibi.

english_text: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
nagamese_text: Aru Paul ke jabole nimite ghora taiyar koribi aru taike bachai kene Governor Felix logot loijabi.

english_text: He wrote a letter like this:
nagamese_text: Tai eneka chithi bhi likhi dise:

english_text: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
nagamese_text: “Claudius Lysias pora Rajyopal Felix ke salam jonai ase.

english_text: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
nagamese_text: Etu manu to Yehudi khan pora taike dhori kene morai dibole thaka te moi jani loise, tai Rome laga nagrik ase, moi joldi sipahi loijai kene taike bachai loise.

english_text: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan kele taike golti lagai ase, etu janibole mon hoi kene moi taike sabha te loi jaise.

english_text: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
nagamese_text: Aru moi jani paise taikhan nijor niyom kotha laga kotha namila pora taike golti kora he ase, aru taike morai dibole aru bandhi bole eneka eku bhi golti pa-a nai.

english_text: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Yehudi khan taike morai dibole kotha milai thakise, etu kotha moike jonai dise, titia moi taike joldi apuni logote pathai dise, aru tai golti diya khan ke bhi taikhan laga kotha apuni laga usorte kobole koi dise.”

english_text: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
nagamese_text: Titia sipahi khan taikhan ke kowa nisena rati te Paul ke Antipatris te loijai dise.

english_text: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
nagamese_text: Dusra dinte sipahi bisi khan wapas jai jaise, kintu ghora chola sipahi khan ke Paul logot jabole dise.

english_text: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
nagamese_text: Jitia sipahi khan Caesarea te ponchise, taikhan pora Governor ke chithi dise aru Paul ke bhi tai usorte khara kori dise.

english_text: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
nagamese_text: Aru Governor pora chithi porhi kene hudise tai kun desh laga ase. Aru jitia tai jani loise tai Cilicia desh pora ase,

english_text: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
nagamese_text: tai koise, “Jitia tumi laga golti diya khan ahibo, titia moi tumi laga kotha hunibo.” Aru taike Herod bisar kora jagah te rakhi dibi koi kene hukum dise.

english_text: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.
nagamese_text: Pans-din pichete mukhyo purohit Ananias aru kunba bura khan aru ekjon ukil jun laga naam Tertullus asele, taikhan arubi ahikena Governor ke Paul bhirodh te kotha koise.

english_text: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul ke Governor age te anise, Tertullus taike golti dikene eneka koise, “Apuni karone amikhan bisi shanti thaki ase, aru etu desh te apuni laga gyaan pora bodli korise;

english_text: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
nagamese_text: Amikhan laga sob jagah te aru hodai etu karone khushi pora apuni ke dhanyavad kori thake.

english_text: But that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi, apuni laga homoi aru bhi nolobole, ami apuni logot te anurodh ase, morom kori amikhan laga ekta kotha huni bhi.

english_text: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
nagamese_text: Kelemane etu manu to mara-mari kore aru duniya te thaka Yehudi khan laga sob jagah te bhirodh aru gondugol kori thaka Nazareth manu ekjon cholawta ase, amikhan jani paise.

english_text: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

english_text: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”
nagamese_text: Taike golti diya khan ke apuni usorte ahi kobole koise, kintu apuni nijor hudile jani jabo amikhan taike ki karone golti di ase.”

english_text: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.
nagamese_text: Aru Yehudi khan bhi mili kene taike etu sob kotha to hosa ase koi dise.

english_text: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,
nagamese_text: Titia Governor Paul ke kotha kobole nimite koise, titia Paul koise, “Ami bujhi ase apuni bisi saal pora etu jati khan laga bisar kori ahi thakise, etu karone moi khushi pora ami laga sob kotha apuni ke kobole ase.

english_text: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Kelemane apuni nijor jani jabo moi jitia pora aradhana kori bole Jerusalem te ahise, baroh-din pora bisi huwa nai.

english_text: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan moike mondoli aru mondoli aru sheher te kun logot te bhi kotha namila, nohoile gondugol lagi thaka pa-a nai.

english_text: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan ki kotha loi moike bodnam lagai ase, etu kun bhi sakhi dibo na paribo.

english_text: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
nagamese_text: Kintu moi apuni ke hosa kotha koi ase, taikhan juntu Rasta ke ekta dol mati ase, eneka laga rasta pora Isor ke sewa kori ahise. Ki niyom te ase aru ki bhabobadi khan pora likhise, etu sob te moi bhal pora mani kene ahise.

english_text: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
nagamese_text: Aru ami Isor ke mon dangor laga etu asha ase, juntu etu manu khan nijor bhi rukhi ase, juntu to ase mori kene jinda hobole thaka, dharmik aru adharmik khan sob bhi.

english_text: In this I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.
nagamese_text: Etu karone moi Isor phale bhi aru manu phale bhi sapha bhabona bhal thakibo karone kosis kori thakise.

english_text: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;

english_text: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.
nagamese_text: Taikhan ami etu kori thaka dikhise, mondoli pora sapha kori loi kene, bhir nohoile gondugol bhi thaka nai.

english_text: They ought to have been here before you and to make accusation if they had anything against me.
nagamese_text: Aru kunba Yehudi khan Asia pora ahise, taikhan ami laga bhirodh te thakile, taikhan apuni usorte ahi kene kobo lage.

english_text: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

english_text: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”

english_text: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”

english_text: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.
nagamese_text: Aru tai henapoti ke koi kene Paul ke bondhi ghor te rakhise, hoilebi taike bhi bandi narakhikena khula chari dibole koise, aru tai sathi khan tai logote ahibole bhi mana na koribi koise.

english_text: After some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
nagamese_text: Aru olop din pichete Felix tai laga Yehudi maiki Drusilla logote wapas ahise, jun Yehudini asele, aru tai Paul ke mati bole pathaise aru tai Paul dwara hunise Jisu Khrista ke biswas laga kotha.

english_text: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul pora taike dhormikta aru nijorke rukhabo para aru aha dinte bisar hobole thaka kotha khan thik pora koi dise, Felix bisi bhoi koi kene koise, “Etu bar to jai jabi. Jitia moi homoi pabo titia tumike aru matibo.”

english_text: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often and talked with him.

english_text: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

english_text: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

english_text: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

english_text: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

english_text: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”
nagamese_text: Titia tai nijor kotha koise, “Moi Yehudi khan niyom laga bhirodh, nohoile girja ke bhirodh, nohoile Caesar laga bhirodh te eku bhi golti kora nohoi.”

english_text: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by me there concerning these things?”
nagamese_text: Kintu Festus Yehudi khan ke khushi koribo itcha pora Paul ke koise, “Tumi Jerusalem te jai kene ami laga bisar jaga usorte etu kotha loi bisar korile tumi itcha hobo?”

english_text: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
nagamese_text: Titia Paul koise, “Moi etiya bhi Caesar bisar jaga usorte khara ase, ami laga bisar yate hobo lage, apuni bhi jani ase, moi Yehudi khan logot eku golti kora nohoi.

english_text: For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
nagamese_text: Jodi moi golti ase, aru etu nimite moike morai dibole layak ase koile moi morile bhi apatti nai. Kintu ki kotha loi kene moike doshi di ase, jodi ekta bhi hosa nohoi koile, kunbi moike taikhan hathte dibo na paribo, moi Caesar logot anurodh koribo.”

english_text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

english_text: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.

english_text: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

english_text: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;

nagamese_text: Karone dusra din Agrippa aru Bernica duijon dhum-dham pora bhal kapra lagai kene aru sheher laga daruga khan aru dusra cholawta logote sabha te ahise. Aru jitia Festus hukum dise, titia Paul ke loi anise.

english_text: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
nagamese_text: Festus koise, “Raja Agrippa aru jun yate ahi bohi ase, apnikhan bhi etu manu ke dikhi ase, etu manu nimite yate thaka Yehudi khan sob aru Jerusalem te thaka sob moi logote binti korise tai jinda thaki bole nalage koise.

english_text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor, I determined to send him,

english_text: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination I may have something to write.

english_text: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

english_text: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;

english_text: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

english_text: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

english_text: Why is it judged incredible with you if God does raise the dead?

english_text: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,

english_text: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
nagamese_text: Kintu Paul koise, “O mohan Festus, moi pagla nohoi, kintu hosa aru buddhi laga kotha koi ase.

english_text: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
nagamese_text: Raja bhi etu sob jani ase, moi eku bhoi nakori kene koi ase, aru etu kotha tai najana eneka ekta bhi kowa nai koi kene moi bhabi ase; etu ghatna to manu khan nathaka te kora nohoi.

english_text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
nagamese_text: Raja Agrippa, apuni bhabobadi khan ke biswas kore? Hoi, moi jane, apuni biswas kori ase.”

english_text: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
nagamese_text: Titia Agrippa Paul ke koise, “Olop homoi te, tumi aram pora moike Khristan bonai dibole ase?”

english_text: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
nagamese_text: Paul koise, “Isor logote moi anurodh kori ase, olop nohoile bisi homoi pichete hoilebi, aji apuni logote bohi ami laga kotha huni thaka sob bhi moi nisena hobole dibi, hoilebi jineka moike rusi pora bandhikena ase etu nisena nohoi.”

english_text: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai etu kotha koise, titia Raja aru Governor aru Bernice, aru taikhan logote bohi thaka sob khara hoi jaise;

english_text: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
nagamese_text: aru taikhan alag jai kene nijor te kotha korise, aru koise, “Etu manu mori bole aru bandibole eneka eku biya kaam kora nohoi.”

english_text: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
nagamese_text: Titia Agrippa pora Festus ke koise, “Jodi etu manu Caesar logot anurodh nakorile, taike chari dile bhi hobole asele.”

english_text: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia amikhan Italy te jabole faisla kori loise, taikhan Paul aru dusra bondh kora manu khan ke Julius koi kene Augustus Regiment laga henapoti ekjon laga hathte di dise.

english_text: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
nagamese_text: Titia amikhan Adramyttium pora ekta jahaaj Asia samundar phale jabole thaka te uthijaise. Aru amikhan safar korise. Thessalonica pora Macedonia laga ekjon Aristarchus koi kene bhi amikhan logote asele.

english_text: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra dinte amikhan Sidon sheher te ahise, aru Julius pora Paul ke bisi morom korise aru tai sathi logote berabo dise, aru tai ki lage sob taike di thakise.

english_text: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan ta te pora jabole ulaise hoilebi hawa bisi jor pora mara karone jahaaj to Cyprus phale loi kene jaise.

english_text: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan Cilicia aru Pamphylia samundar paar kori Lycia laga sheher Myra te ahi jaise.

english_text: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
nagamese_text: Ta te henapoti he Alexandria laga ekta jahaaj Italy te jabole thaka paikene amikhan ke ta te uthai dise.

english_text: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
nagamese_text: Amikhan bisi din aste-aste jai thakise, aru bisi digdar pora Cnidus ponchise, kintu hawa bisi mara pora amikhan age jabole para nai, etu pora jahaaj ke loi kene Crete phale loi jaise, juntu Salmone usorte ase.

english_text: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
nagamese_text: Amikhan bisi digdar pora safar korise aru Lysea sheher usorte Bhal Jaga eneka te ponchise.

english_text: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them
nagamese_text: Etiya bisi homoi jaise, panite bera bole digdar hoise, aru etiya to Yehudi khan laga upwas din bhi paar hoise, karone Paul taikhan ke hoshiar kori bole,

english_text: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
nagamese_text: koise, “Hey manu khan, amikhan etiya yate pora jaise koile digdar aru bisi nuksan bhi hobo pare, khali saman aru jahaaj he nohoi, kintu manu jibon bhi jabo pare.”

english_text: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi henapoti pora Paul laga kotha namani kene jahaaj laga malik khan laga kotha he manise.

english_text: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.
nagamese_text: Aru utu jaga to thanda dinte ta te thaki bole thik nohua karone bisi manu parile Phoenix te he thakile bhal hobo bhabise. Phoenix to Crete usorte ekta jaga ase, dakshin-paschim aru uttor-paschim phale bhi jabo para jagah ase.

english_text: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
nagamese_text: Titia dakshin pora halka-halka hawa ahise, jahaaj chola khan bhabise taikhan ki lage etu sob taikhan logot ase. Etu pora taikhan Crete phale jabole jahaaj khuli dise.

english_text: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
nagamese_text: Kintu bisi deri nohoi kene dangor hawa pani laga tufan ta te pora ahi taikhan ke lagise.

english_text: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
nagamese_text: Jitia tufan pora jahaaj ke dhorise, taikhan aru age jabo napari kene hawa pora jahaaj ke kote loi jabole ase, loijabo dise.

english_text: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
nagamese_text: Titia Cauda naam laga ekta majuli te bisi digdar pora punchise aru chutu naw ke dhori rakhibo parise.

english_text: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan chutu naw ke uthai anise aru niche pora bandi loise. Syrtis laga balu matite lagi bole bhoi pora jahaaj kapra khan khuli dise, aru jahaaj ke hawa pora loijabo dise.

english_text: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
nagamese_text: Kintu dusra din tak amikhan ke tufan pora bisi digdar di thakise, etu karone taikhan jahaaj pora saman khan samundar te phelai dise.

english_text: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
nagamese_text: Aru tin din pichete amikhan nijor hath pora jahaaj laga saman uthaikene samundar te phelai dise.

english_text: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia bisi din tak suryo aru tara khan ula nai aru tufan bhi bisi mari thakise, titia amikhan bachibole asha sob chari dise.

english_text: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.
nagamese_text: Titia bisi din pora kha-luwa nakora karone, Paul khara kori kene taikhan ke koise, “Sabi, apnikhan ami laga kotha mani kene Crete pora najaile bhal hobole asele, tinehoile amikhan eneka digdar aru nuksan nohobo asele.

english_text: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
nagamese_text: Kintu etiya moi apnikhan ke mon dangor rakhibole koi ase, kelemane khali jahaaj ke he nohoile, kunke bhi digdar nohobo.

english_text: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi jun laga ase, aru junke sewa kore, tai sorgodoth aji rati moi logote ahise.

english_text: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
nagamese_text: Aru koise, ‘Paul, tumi bhoi na koribi. Tumi Caesar age te khara hobo lagibo, aru sabi Isor tumike morom kori kene tumi logote juwa manu khan sob etiya bhi tumi logote he ase.’

english_text: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
nagamese_text: Karone manu khan mon dangor hobi! Kelemane moi Isor ke biswas kore, jineka Tai koise tineka hobo.

english_text: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
nagamese_text: Hoilebi amikhan ekta majuli te loijai kene rakhibo pare.”

english_text: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
nagamese_text: Titia choudah rati hoise, aru amikhan Adriatic Samundar majote loijai kene thaki jaise, aru adha rati te jahaaj chola khan bhabise taikhan to kunba mati usorte ahi punchise.

english_text: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan pani laga galta ke naapi sai sele bisi lamba galta thakise, ekta hath to choi feet ase, aru olop jai kene aru sai sele, pondro hath paise.

english_text: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
nagamese_text: Titia pathor te lagibo bhoi pora taikhan piche phale pora loha longor charta phelai dise, aru phojur hobole prathana kori thakise.

english_text: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
nagamese_text: Aru jahaaj chola manu khan jahaaj charikena polabole bhabise, taikhan jahaaj pora longor phelai diya nisena bahana pora chutu naw ke niche samundar te girai dise.

english_text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
nagamese_text: Titia Paul pora henapoti aru sipahi khan ke koise, “Jodi eitu khan jahaaj te nathakile apnikhan kitia bhi bachibole na paribo.”

english_text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
nagamese_text: Titia sipahi khan jai kene chutu naw laga rusi khan kati girai dise.

english_text: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia phojur hobole hoise, Paul sob manu ke kiba khabole koise. Tai koise, “Aji choudah din hoise apnikhan eku nakhai kene bhukha thaki ase.

english_text: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
nagamese_text: Karone moi apnikhan ke koi ase, kiba khai lobi, kelemane eneka korile bachibo paribo, tumi laga matha pora ekta chuli bhi na giribo.”

english_text: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia tai utu koi dise, tai roti loi kene Isor ke dhanyavad dise, aru taikhan khai loise.

english_text: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan bhi sob mon dangor hoi kene kha luwa kori loise.

english_text: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan jahaaj te thaka khan sob 276 jon asele.

english_text: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
nagamese_text: Karone jitia taikhan kha luwa kora hoise, taikhan jahaaj ke halka kori bole gehu uthaikene samundar te phelai dise.

english_text: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
nagamese_text: Jitia din hoise, taikhan kuntu jagate ase janibole para nai, kintu ekta mati jagah dikhise, aru jahaaj ke ta te loijai kene rakhibole bhabise.

english_text: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan longor khan ke samundar te chari dise, aru jahaaj cholai thaka khuri bandi thaka ke khuli dise, aru jahaaj laga kapra khan age phale thaka ke uthaikene hawa pora kinar te loija bole dise,

english_text: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
nagamese_text: Kintu jahaaj to jai kene samundar laga duita pani laga takot pora dhuri loise, aru jahaaj matite lagi kene thaki jaise, aru piche phale pani pora mari kene bhangai dise.

english_text: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
nagamese_text: Aru koidi manu khan pani khilikena polai jabo bhoi pora sipahi khan taikhan ke morai dibole bhabise.

english_text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
nagamese_text: Kintu henapoti pora Paul ke bachai dibo mon asele, etu karone taikhan ke rukhai dise, aru jun pani khilibo jane, jap mari kene poila sukha matite jai jabole hukum dise.

english_text: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
nagamese_text: Aru baki khan takhta pora aru kunba jahaaj bhanga tukra pora jabole hukum dise, aru sob bachi kene sukha matite punchise.

english_text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
nagamese_text: Titia amikhan bachi kene ulai ahise, etu majuli laga naam Malta ase eneka jani loise.

english_text: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.
nagamese_text: Aru ta te laga manu khan bhi amikhan ke bisi morom korise, aru pani gira karone bisi thanda thakise, taikhan jui jolai amikhan ke jui thapibo dise.

english_text: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Paul khuri mutha uthaikene jui te haali se, ta te ekta saph gorom paikene khuri pora ulaise, aru tai hathte bandhi loise.

english_text: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”
nagamese_text: Titia ta te laga manu khan saph tai hathte bandi thaka dikhise aru taikhan majote kotha korise, “Ki hoilebi etu manu morai diya manu ase, tai samundar pora to bachi kene ahise, hoilebi niyom pora taike jinda thakibo nadibo.”

english_text: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.
nagamese_text: Kintu tai hath hilai kene saph ke jui te phelai dise, aru tai eku huwa nai.

english_text: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
nagamese_text: Kintu taikhan bhabise tai gaw phuli jabo, nohoile giri kene mori jabo. Kintu bisi deri tak sai thaki bole taike eku huwa nai, titia, taikhan laga bhabona alag hoise, aru tai ekta Isor ase bhabona korise.

english_text: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.
nagamese_text: Etu jagah usorte Publius koi kene etu majuli laga prodhan cholawta asele, aru etu jaga laga mati bisi laga tai malik thakise, aru tai amikhan ke tai ghor te loijai kene tin-din bhal pora rakhi sewa korise.

english_text: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.
nagamese_text: Aru eneka hoise Publius laga baba bukhar aru pet-jai thakisele, Paul tai ghor te jai kene Isor ke prathana kori dise, aru tai uporte hath rakhi taike bhal kori dise.

english_text: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.
nagamese_text: Jitia eneka hoise, etu dikhi kene utu jaga laga manu khan jun bemar ase sob loi ani bhal hoi kene jaise.

english_text: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan amikhan ke bisi sonman dise, aru jitia amikhan ta te pora jabole hoise, amikhan ki-ki lage sob ani jahaaj te rakhidise.

english_text: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”
nagamese_text: Tin mohina pichete, amikhan Alexandria laga ekta jahaaj te uthi kene jaise, jun thanda dinte ahi ta te thakise, etu jahaaj te “Jurwa Bhagwan” laga nuksa lagikena thaka asele.

english_text: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan ahi Syracus sheher te ponchise, aru ta te tin din thakise.

english_text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
nagamese_text: Ta te pora amikhan Rhegium te ghuri ahise, aru ek din pichete dakshin phale pora hawa ahise, aru dusra din Puteoli te punchise.

english_text: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.
nagamese_text: Ta te amikhan biswasi bhai khan paise aru taikhan kowa karone taikhan logote saat din thaki jaise. Eneka pora amikhan Rome phale jaise.

english_text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia ta te biswasi bhai khan Appius Bajar aru Tinta Taverns kowa te amikhan ke lok kori bole ahise. Jitia Paul taikhan ke dikhise, tai Isor ke dhanyavad dise, aru tai mon bhi bisi mon dangor hoise.

english_text: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
nagamese_text: Jitia amikhan Rome te ahi punchise, Paul ke saithaka ekta sipahi logote alag te thaki bole agya dise.

english_text: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
nagamese_text: Tin din pichete tai Yehudi laga cholawta khan ke matise. Aru jitia taikhan ahi joma hoise, tai koise, “Bhai khan, ami pora moi laga manu bhirodh te nohoile khandan khan laga niyom bhirodh te eku bhi kora nohoi, hoilebi moike Jerusalem pora bondhi bonai kene Rome manu laga hathte di dise.

english_text: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.
nagamese_text: Taikhan huda-hudi kori kene moike chari bole hoisele, kelemane moi pora mori bole laga eku bodnam panai.

english_text: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia Yehudi khan etu bhirodh te koise, moike Caesar logote anurodh koribo lagise, hoilebi moi nijor jati manu ke bodnam dibole kora nohoi.

english_text: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
nagamese_text: Karone moi apnikhan ke lok kori kene kotha kori bole mati anise, manu khan moike rusi pora bandi rakha to Israel manu laga asha karone ase.”

english_text: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan taike koise, “Amikhan Judea pora apuni laga naam te eku chithi bhi pa-a nai, aru bhai khan pora kunbi ahi kene apuni laga eku biya kotha kowa nai.

english_text: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”
nagamese_text: Kintu apuni laga bhabona ki ase, utu hunibo mon kori ase, kelemane sob jagah etu kotha mana khan bhirodh ase, amikhan jane.”

english_text: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan ek din tai logote ahi lok koribo koi kene jai jaise, aru bisi manu tai logote ahi joma hoise, titia tai phojur pora saam tak Isor rajyo laga kotha bhal pora bujhi bo karone Moses laga niyom aru bhabobadi khan laga kitab te likha khan to bhal pora samjhai dise.

english_text: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
nagamese_text: Titia kunba tai laga kotha ke biswas kori loise, kintu kunba to biswas kora nai.

english_text: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan majote kotha namila hoise, aru taikhan Paul pora etu kowa pichete jai jaise, “Pobitro Atma he bhabobadi Isaiah pora ami laga baba khan ke thik koise.

english_text: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.
nagamese_text: Tai koise, ‘Jai kene etu manu khan ke koi dibi, “Tumikhan huna to huni thakibo, kintu eku bhi nabujhi bo; Aru tumikhan sa-a to sai thakibo kintu eku bhi najanibo.

english_text: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, then I would heal them.’
nagamese_text: Kelemane eitu khan laga mon tan hoise Taikhan laga kaan bhi nahune, Aru taikhan suku bhi bondh kori loise. Eneka nohobo lage taikhan suku pora dikhi loi, Aru kaan pora huni loi, Aru mon pora bujhi loi kene ghuri ahile, Moi taikhan ke bhal kori dibo.’”

english_text: “Be it known therefore to you that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”
nagamese_text: Etu karone tumikhan jani lobi, Isor etu poritran laga kotha Porjati khan logote di dise, aru taikhan etu huni lobo.”

english_text: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Paul etu kotha koi dise, Yehudi khan apaste kotha namila hoise, aru jai jaise.

english_text: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house and received all who were coming to him,
nagamese_text: Titia, Paul bhara ghor loi kene dui-saal ta te thakise, aru jun taike lok kori bole ahe, khushi pora taikhan ke grohon kori thakise.

english_text: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
nagamese_text: Aru tai bhoi nakori kene Isor rajyo laga kotha prochar kori aru Probhu Jisu Khrista laga kotha ke sikhai thakise, aru kun bhi taike rukhabole kosis kora nai.

english_text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,
nagamese_text: Paul, Jisu Khrista laga ekjon noukar, Tai laga basi luwa manu hobole nimite mati luwa aru Tai laga susamachar koi dibole alag rakhi luwa,

english_text: which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures,
nagamese_text: jun to Tai age din pora bhabobadi khan logot Tai laga kosom to pobitro kotha khan te di dise,

english_text: concerning his Son, who was born of the offspring of David according to the flesh,
nagamese_text: Tai laga Putro dibo nimite kosom diya to, aru kun gaw mangso hisab te David raja laga khandan pora ahise.

english_text: who was declared to be the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai mora pora jee uthi kene Pobitrota laga Atma dwara Tai Isor laga Putro ase eneka hokti pora jonai dise, etu Jisu Khrista amikhan laga Probhu.

english_text: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations for his name’s sake;
nagamese_text: Khrista dwara amikhan anugrah aru apostle hobole paise, aru etu biswas pora kotha mani kene sob desh khan te, Tai laga naam nimite.

english_text: among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ;
nagamese_text: Etu desh khan majote, apnikhan ke bhi Jisu Khrista laga hobole mati kene ase.

english_text: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
nagamese_text: Etu chithi to Rome te thaka sob jonke, Isor pora morom kora khan, jun khan ke pobitro hobole nimite likhise. Apuni khan logot anugrah hobi aru amikhan Baba Isor aru Probhu Jisu Khrista pora anondo hobi.

english_text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
nagamese_text: Shuru te, moi apnikhan nimite Jisu Khrista dwara Isor ke dhanyavad di ase kelemane apuni khan laga biswas to duniya laga sob jagate prochar kori ase.

english_text: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers,
nagamese_text: Kelemane Isor moi laga gawahi ase, kunke moi sewa kore moi laga atma pora, Tai Putro laga susamachar nimite, aru kineka moi narokhi kene apuni laga kotha koi ase.

english_text: requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.
nagamese_text: Moi laga prathana te apuni khan ke yaad kori kene Isor laga itcha hoile ki hoilebi apnikhan usorte ahibo karone moi hodai prathana kori ase.

english_text: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;
nagamese_text: Kelemane apnikhan ke dikhi bole bisi itcha ase titia apnikhan ke atma te takot hobo nimite atma laga bordan bhag kori dibo.

english_text: that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.
nagamese_text: Titia amikhan eke logote nijor biswas pora ekjon-ekjon laga atma uthai di thakibo.

english_text: Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far), that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.
nagamese_text: Aru etiya, bhai khan ke etu najani kene thakibo dibole mon nai, moi apnikhan logote ahibo nimite bisi bar taiyar korise, (kintu etiya tak kiba ekta pora moike hodai rukhai thakise), jineka Porjati khan pora ami bhal bijon kati bole paise, thik etu nisena ami apnikhan majot te bhi bhal bijon katibo dibole itcha ase.

english_text: I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
nagamese_text: Moi Yunani jati aru dusra desh manu, gyaan thaka aru murkho manu khan sob logote dhar bukhi kene ase.

english_text: So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, Rome te thaka apnikhan sob logote susamachar prochar kori bole moi bisi itcha ase.

english_text: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi susamachar nimite sorom nakore, kun he etu ke biswas kore taikhan sob nimite etu poritran pabole laga Isor laga hokti ase, shuru te Yehudi khan karone, etu pichete Yunani khan nimite.

english_text: For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”
nagamese_text: Kelemane susamachar te Isor laga dharmikta to biswas pora biswas uporte dikhai di ase, Shastro te eneka likhi kene thaka nisena, “Hosabi, dharmik manu khan biswas pora jinda thakibo.”

english_text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
nagamese_text: Kelemane sorgo pora Isor laga khong adharmik manu khan sob uporte ahi thaka dikhai dise.

english_text: because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them.
nagamese_text: Etu eneka ase kelemane Isor laga ki janikena ase, etu taikhan suku pora dikhibo pari ase. Kelemane Isor nijor pora taikhan ke dikhai dise.

english_text: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.
nagamese_text: Kelemane suku pora dikhibo napara Tai laga gunn, Tai laga anonto hokti aru sobhab, pura shristi bona din pora sob dikhai dise aru ki bonaise etu pora bujhai dise. Etu karone manu khan pora etiya najane eneka kobo napare.

english_text: Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.
nagamese_text: Etu eneka hoise kelemane, Isor ke janile bhi, taikhan pora Isor ke kineka mohima koribo lage etu kora nai, nohoile dhanyavad diya nai, kelemane taikhan karone etu bhabona to eku kaam thaka nai aru taikhan laga murkho mon to andhera hoi kene thakise.

english_text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
nagamese_text: Gyaani ase eneka bhabi kene taikhan murkho hoise.

english_text: and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.
nagamese_text: Aru kitia bhi namora Isor laga mohima ke mori jabole manu laga protima logote bodli kori loise; chiriya khan, theng pora ja janwar khan aru pet pora ja janwar khan laga murti bonai loise.

english_text: Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves;
nagamese_text: Etu karone Isor taikhan nijor laga letera aru sapha nathaka mon laga itcha te jabole dise, aru taikhan laga gaw to taikhan majote moila kori thaki bole nimite.

english_text: who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Isor laga hosa kotha to misa logote bodli kori dise, aru juntu Isor pora bonaise, etu ke sewa korise, aru sob sristi Bona-Jonke nohoi, jun laga mohima hodai nimite ase. Amen.

english_text: For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, Isor pora taikhan ke mangso itcha laga biya kaam te taikhan ke chari dise, kele koile taikhan laga maiki khan bhi niyom te ki ase etu nohoikena ki nohobo lage etu he itcha korise.

english_text: Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena, mota khan bhi taikhan laga maiki khan logot ki niyom koribo lage etu nohoikena, dusra mota khan logote niyom te nathaka letera kaam kori ase, aru taikhan nijor etu letera kaam kora laga saja paise.

english_text: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;
nagamese_text: Kelemane taikhan to Isor taikhan logote ase koi kene mana nai, etu pora Isor he taikhan ke biya bhabona kora manu khan laga hathte di dise, kun to kaam khan thik nohoi eitu khan kori bole nimite.

english_text: being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers,
nagamese_text: Taikhan sob adharmikta pora bhorta hoi kene ase, biya kaam kora manu, lalchi kora manu, aru dusra ke dukh kori bole diya manu. Taikhan suku jola pora bhorta hoi kene ase, morai diya, khong uthi kene kotha namila, manu ke thogai diye, aru biya bhabona kori thake. Taikhan manu laga biya kotha koi thake,

english_text: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
nagamese_text: manu laga bhirodh te misa kotha koi, Isor ke ghin kore, manu ke hisab nakore, nijorke he bhal bhabe, phutani kore, biya kaam kori bole nimite rasta bisari thake; aru taikhan baba ama laga kotha namane.

english_text: without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful;
nagamese_text: Taikhan eku chinta bhabona nai, biswas nathaka manu, mon biya manu aru morom nathaka manu khan ase.

english_text: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Isor laga dharmik kaam khan jane, kun etu biya kaam khan koribo taikhan moribo. Kintu taikhan khali eitu khan kora nohoi, hoilebi kun manu biya kaam kori ase taikhan laga mon bhi eneka kaam khan kori bole mon dangor kori diye.

english_text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things.
nagamese_text: Etu karone apuni khan logote bahana kori bole eku nai, O manu, kun dusra ke bisar kore, jitia apuni dusra ke bisar kore, titia apuni nijor logote thaka golti ke bhi bodnam kori ase. Kelemane apuni kunkhan bisar kore, thik utu khan nisena he kore.

english_text: We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things.
nagamese_text: Kintu Isor utu khan ke bisar kore jun khan eneka kaam khan kore aru amikhan jani ase Tai laga bisar to hosa ase.

english_text: Do you think this, O man who judges those who practice such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgment of God?
nagamese_text: Kintu bhabi sabi, apuni khan jun dusra ke bisar kore, utu golti khan nimite juntu apuni khan bhi kore. Tinehoile apnikhan Isor laga bisar pora bachibole paribo naki?

english_text: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
