nagamese_text: Etu nimite, ahibole din laga digdar nimite etu bhal ase, ekjon manu kineka ase eneka he thaki bole.

english_text: Are you bound to a wife? Don’t seek to be freed. Are you free from a wife? Don’t seek a wife.
nagamese_text: Apuni ekjon maiki logot bandi kene ase? Khuli bole nabisaribi. Apuni ekjon maiki pora khuli kene ase? Ekjon maiki nabisaribi.

english_text: But if you marry, you have not sinned. If a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have oppression in the flesh, and I want to spare you.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi apuni shadi korise koile, apuni paap kora nohoi; aru ekta kumari pora shadi korise koile, tai paap kora nai. Eneka hoile bhi eitu khan mangso te digdar pabo: aru ami apuni khan etu digdar pora bacha bole itcha kori ase.

english_text: But I say this, brothers: the time is short. From now on, both those who have wives may be as though they had none;
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi etu ami koi ase, bhai khan, homoi komti hoise: eneka thakibi, jineka jun khan maiki ase taikhan bhi maiki nathaka nisena;

english_text: and those who weep, as though they didn’t weep; and those who rejoice, as though they didn’t rejoice; and those who buy, as though they didn’t possess;
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan jun khan kandi ase, jineka taikhan kanda nai; aru taikhan jun khan khushi pai ase, jineka taikhan khushi pa-a nai; aru taikhan jun khan kini ase, jineka taikhan laga eku nai;

english_text: and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.
nagamese_text: aru taikhan jun khan etu prithibi ke cholai ase, taikhan etu ke nachola nisena. Kilekoile etu prithibi thaka to jai-jai ase.

english_text: But I desire to have you to be free from cares. He who is unmarried is concerned for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi, apnikhan chinta pora ajad thakibi. Tai jun shadi kora nai utu khan nimite bhabi ase juntu Probhu laga ase, kineka pora tai Probhu ke khushi kori bole paribo.

english_text: but he who is married is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi tai jun shadi kori kene ase tai kineka pora tai laga maiki ke khushi koribo etu nimite bhabi thake, aru tai laga mon aru bhabona dui bhag hoijai. Ekjon shadi nakora nohoile kumari mahila

english_text: There is also a difference between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares about the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she who is married cares about the things of the world—how she may please her husband.
nagamese_text: to khali Probhu laga kaam nimite bhabi thake, etu nimite tai gaw aru atma duita te bhi pobitro thake. Hoile bhi tai jun shadi kori kene ase prithibi laga jinis nimite bhabi ase, kineka pora tai tai laga mota ke khushi koribo.

english_text: This I say for your own benefit, not that I may ensnare you, but for that which is appropriate, and that you may attend to the Lord without distraction.
nagamese_text: Aru etu ami apnikhan laga nijor labh nimite koi ase, apnikhan uporte ekta phang rakha nohoi, hoile bhi juntu sabole sundur ase etu hoi thakibo nimite, aru ta te apnikhan mon ulta nohoikena Probhu phine mon dibole paribo.

english_text: But if any man thinks that he is behaving inappropriately toward his virgin, if she is past the flower of her age, and if need so requires, let him do what he desires. He doesn’t sin. Let them marry.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi jodi kunba mota bhabi ase tai shadi kori bole thaka kumari mahila logote thik niyom pora thakibo napare,- jodi kumari mahila to shadi kori bole umor bisi hoi ase koile- tai laga itcha nisena kori bole dibi. Tai paap kora nohoi: taikhan ke shadi kori bole dibi.

english_text: But he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no urgency, but has power over his own will, and has determined in his own heart to keep his own virgin, does well.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi tai jun mon bhitor te thik khara ase, aru taike dorkar nai, aru tai nijor bhabona te takot ase, aru tai monte mani loise tai shadi nakori kene thakibo, tai to ekdom thik kori ase.

english_text: So then both he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who doesn’t give her in marriage does better.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite tai jun shadi kori ase, bhal kori ase; hoilebi tai jun shadi nakore, tai bisi bhal kori ase.

english_text: A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if the husband is dead, she is free to be married to whomever she desires, only in the Lord.
nagamese_text: Ekjon maiki tai laga mota jinda thaka tak tai logote niyom pora bandi kene ase; hoilebi tai laga mota morise koile, tai junke khushi ase eitu ke shadi kori bole azadi ase; hoile bhi khali Probhu te.

english_text: But she is happier if she stays as she is, in my judgment, and I think that I also have God’s Spirit.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi tai eneka thakise koile he khushi thakibo, ami laga hisab te. Aru ami etu bhi bhabi ase ami logote Isor laga Atma ase.

english_text: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
nagamese_text: Etiya, murti khan ke kha luwa laga bolidan diya kotha juntu apnikhan hudise, etu laga likhibo: Amikhan jani ase amikhan sob logote gyaan ase. Kintu gyaan to manu ke phutani kori diye, hoile bhi morom to manu khan ke bonai diye.

english_text: But if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he doesn’t yet know as he ought to know.
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba ekjon kiba jani ase koi kene bhabe, tai asol te janibole thaka to eku bhi jana nai.

english_text: But anyone who loves God is known by him.
nagamese_text: Kintu jun Isor ke morom kore, etu manu ke Isor pora jani ase.

english_text: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God but one.
nagamese_text: Tinehoile, murti ke bolidan diya laga kha luwa kora: Amikhan jani ase etu prithibi te murti to eku nai aru amikhan jani ase khali ekjon Isor he ase.

english_text: For though there are things that are called “gods”, whether in the heavens or on earth—as there are many “gods” and many “lords”—
nagamese_text: Kilekoile isor khan bisi thakile bhi, sorgote nohoile prithibi te, jineka bisi “isor khan” aru “probhukhan” ase,

english_text: yet to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we live through him.
nagamese_text: hoile bhi amikhan nimite to ekjon Baba Isor he ase, sob to Tai pora he ahise aru Tai nimite amikhan jinda ase, aru ekjon Probhu Jisu Khrista, jun karone he sob jinis ase, aru jun karone amikhan jinda ase.

english_text: However, that knowledge isn’t in all men. But some, with consciousness of an idol until now, eat as of a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
nagamese_text: Kineka hoile bhi, etu gyaan to sob jon bhitor te nohoi. Hoile bhi, kunba to poila te murti khan ke bisi mani kene thakise, etu nimite taikhan murti ke bolidan diya laga kha luwa nisena bhabikena khai diye; etu nimite taikhan laga bhabona komjur aru letera hoi kene ase.

english_text: But food will not commend us to God. For neither, if we don’t eat are we the worse, nor if we eat are we the better.
nagamese_text: Kintu kha luwa pora amikhan ke Isor age te dikhai nadibo. Amikhan nakhaile biya hoi najai, nohoile bhi khai le bhal ase eneka hoi najai.

english_text: But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
nagamese_text: Kintu hoshiar hoi kene thakibi apuni laga etu ajadi nimite dusra manu khan karone komjur kori diya porikha hobole nadibi.

english_text: For if a man sees you who have knowledge sitting in an idol’s temple, won’t his conscience, if he is weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols?
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jodi kunba pora etu gyaan thaka manu ke murti ke diya laga kha luwa khai thaka dikhise koile, utu dimag komjur thaka manu to murti ke bolidan diya kha luwa khabole sikhi lobo nohoi?

english_text: And through your knowledge, he who is weak perishes, the brother for whose sake Christ died.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite ekjon jun komjur ase, utu bhai nimite jun Khrista jibon di dise, apuni laga kaam dikhi kene tai nosto hoi jaise.

english_text: Thus, sinning against the brothers, and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, jitia apnikhan bhai khan laga age te paap kaam kori kene taikhan laga komjur bhabona ke ghao kori diye, apnikhan to Khrista age te paap hoise.

english_text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will eat no meat forever more, that I don’t cause my brother to stumble.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, jodi kha luwa nimite bhai khan porikha te giri jai, tinehoile ami mangso bhi nakhabo, titia moi pora ami nimite ami laga bhai khan ke porikha te giribole nadibo.

english_text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Haven’t I seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Aren’t you my work in the Lord?
nagamese_text: Moi ajad nohoi naki? Moi apostle nohoi naki? Moi amikhan laga Probhu Jisu ke dikhai nai naki? Apnikhan ami logote Probhu nimite kaam kora manu khan nohoi naki?

english_text: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
nagamese_text: Jodi ami dusra khan nimite ekjon apostle nohoi koile bhi, apnikhan nimite to ase. Kilekoile ami Probhu laga apostle kaam kora to apnikhan he ami laga gawahi ase.

english_text: My defense to those who examine me is this:
nagamese_text: Etu he ami laga raksha ase jun khan para amike sai thake:

english_text: Have we no right to eat and to drink?
nagamese_text: Kha luwa kori bole amikhan adhikar nai naki?

english_text: Have we no right to take along a wife who is a believer, even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
nagamese_text: Amikhan ekjon biswasi maiki ke shadi kori bole amikhan laga adhikar nai naki, aru dusra apostle khan nisena, aru Probhu te bhai thaka khan, aru Cephas nisena?

english_text: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?
nagamese_text: Nohoile, khali Barnabas aru moi he kaam kori bole adhikar nathaka duijon ase?

english_text: What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock, and doesn’t drink from the flock’s milk?
nagamese_text: Kun sipahi kaam kori kene nijorke tangkha diye? Kun bagan kora manu bagan kori kene nijor bagan laga guti khabole napare? Nohoile kun ekjon roikhya manu nijor laga mer khan ke saikene taikhan laga dudh nakhai?

english_text: Do I speak these things according to the ways of men? Or doesn’t the law also say the same thing?
nagamese_text: Eitu khan kowa to manu laga adhikar hisab te kowa nohoi naki? Nohoile niyom te bhi eneka ase nohoi?

english_text: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain.” Is it for the oxen that God cares,
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Moses laga niyom te eneka likhi kene ase, “Goru laga mukh te rusi pora bandhi kene bondh kori nadibi jitia tak tai dhaan uporte theng chipai kene ghuri thake.” Isor to goru khan nimite eku chinta ase, na chinta kore?

english_text: or does he say it assuredly for our sake? Yes, it was written for our sake, because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes in hope should partake of his hope.
nagamese_text: Na, khali amikhan nimite he likhi kene ase? Kile mane etu amikhan nimite likhi kene ase, kun kheti khunde aru kun dhaan guti ke alag kore, tai duijon bhi hajira pabo lage.

english_text: If we sowed to you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?
nagamese_text: Jodi amikhan atma laga bijon khan apnikhan majote phelai, tinehoile apnikhan amikhan ke duniya laga jinis khan bhi dibole napare naki?

english_text: If others partake of this right over you, don’t we yet more? Nevertheless we didn’t use this right, but we bear all things, that we may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.
nagamese_text: Jodi dusra khan apuni uporte kiba pabole adhikar ase koile, apnikhan bhi taikhan uporte pabole adhikar ase nohoi? Kintu amikhan etu adhikar to lobole para nai. Ulta Khrista laga susamachar kaam digdar nohobole nimite amikhan dhorjo korise.

english_text: Don’t you know that those who serve around sacred things eat from the things of the temple, and those who wait on the altar have their portion with the altar?
nagamese_text: Apnikhan najane, jun mondoli nimite kaam kore, tai to mondoli laga kaam khan he khai; aru jun bedi te kha luwa khan sai, tai to bedi laga kha luwa he khai?

english_text: Even so the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.
nagamese_text: Thik etu nisena, Probhu pora hukum dise jun Khrista laga susamachar koi diya kaam kore tai laga hajira to susamachar pora he pabo.

english_text: But I have used none of these things, and I don’t write these things that it may be done so in my case; for I would rather die, than that anyone should make my boasting void.
nagamese_text: Kintu moi etu adhikar khan eku bhi luwa nai. Kilekoile ami etu likha to kiba pabole nimite likha nohoi, kele koile etu likhi kene phutani kora pora to ami nimite morija to he bhal hobo.

english_text: For if I preach the Good News, I have nothing to boast about, for necessity is laid on me; but woe is to me if I don’t preach the Good News.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jitia moi susamachar prochar kore, etu te ami eku phutani dikha bole motlob nai, kelemane etu to ami laga jimedari he ase. Aru ami uporte dukh hobole dibi jodi ami susamachar to prochar nakore!

english_text: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward. But if not of my own will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jodi ami khushi pora prochar korile, moi nimite inam ase. Kintu jodi moi khushi nai joborjosti pora, titia hoile moi uporte sabole jimedari di dise.

english_text: What then is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I may present the Good News of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.
nagamese_text: Tinehoile ami laga inam to ki ase? Ami jitia susamachar prochar kore ami eku bhi daam noloi, eneka hoile he ami susamachar laga naam pora khushi-khushi kori bole sesta nakoribo.

english_text: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ami to sob pora ajad hoi kene thakile bhi, ami nijorke dusra khan laga nokor bonai dise, eneka hoile ami aru bhi bisi pabo.

english_text: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;
nagamese_text: Yehudi khan nimite ami Yehudi hoi jaise, eneka hoile Yehudi khan ke jiti lobo. Aru ami nijor bhi niyom bhitor te thaka nai, kintu jun khan niyom bhitor te ase, taikhan uporte jitibo nimite ami nijorke niyom bhitor te thaka ekjon kori loise.

english_text: to those who are without law, as without law (not being without law toward God, but under law toward Christ), that I might win those who are without law.
nagamese_text: Aru jun khan niyom bahar te ase, ami nijorke niyom bahar te thaka ekjon hoi jaise eneka hoile niyom bahar te thaka khan ke jiti lobo (asol te ami Isor laga niyom bahar te nohoi, kintu Khrista laga niyom bhitor te ase).

english_text: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
nagamese_text: Komjur khan nimite ami bhi komjur hoi jaise, eneka hoile komjur khan ke jiti lobo. Moi sob khan nimite sob hoi jaise, eneka hoile ami kineka hoile bhi kunba khan ke bacha bole paribo.

english_text: Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.
nagamese_text: Ami eitu khan sob to susamachar nimite he kori ase, eneka hoile ami bhi etu laga ekta bhag hobo.

english_text: Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, so that you may win.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan najane, polabole laga khila te sob khilari khan polai, kintu khali ekjon he inam loi? Etu nimite eneka pora polabi jineka pora apuni jitibo.

english_text: Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
nagamese_text: Jun khan etu khila te bhag loi, taikhan to sob jinis te nijorke rukhabo para laga taiyari kure. Taikhan etu kura to harai jabole mukut pabole nimite kore, kintu amikhan to ketia bhi naharabole mukut pabo nimite kore.

english_text: I therefore run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,
nagamese_text: Etu karone moi polai, ekjon eku motlob nathaki kene nohoi; moi lorai kore, ekjon hawa te mari thaka nisena nohoi.

english_text: but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.
nagamese_text: Kintu ami nijor gaw ke dhuri loi aru moi laga noukar bonai loi, eneka hoile jitia ami dusra khan ke prochar kora pichete, ami nijorke hari bole nadibo.

english_text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ami apnikhan ke eku najani kene thakibo dibole mon nai, bhai khan, amikhan laga baba khan jitia badal pora loijai thakise, taikhan samundar paar kori bole parise.

english_text: and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
nagamese_text: Taikhan sob Moses logote badal aru samundar pora baptizma loise,

english_text: and all ate the same spiritual food;
nagamese_text: aru taikhan sob eke atma laga kha luwa korise.

english_text: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank of a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
nagamese_text: Taikhan sob eke atmik laga pani khaise, kele koile taikhan atma laga pathor jun taikhan piche ahise etu pora he khaise, aru etu pathor to Khrista ase.

english_text: However with most of them, God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
nagamese_text: Kintu Isor to taikhan kunba uporte te khushi thaka nai, aru etu nimite taikhan ke balu laga pahar te morai dise.

english_text: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.
nagamese_text: Etiya eitu khan sob to amikhan nimite ekta saikene bujhi bole kotha ase, eneka hoile amikhan biya jinis khan te itcha nahobo, jineka taikhan itcha kori sele.

english_text: Don’t be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”
nagamese_text: Murti puja kora manu khan nahobi, jineka taikhan majote kunba thakisele; Shastro te eneka likhi kene ase, “Manu khan bohi kene kha luwa kori thakise, aru khili bole uthi loise.”

english_text: Let’s not commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and in one day twenty-three thousand fell.
nagamese_text: Bebichar kaam khan na koribi, jineka taikhan bisi manu bebichar korise, aru etu nimite teis hajar manu utu dinte mori jaise.

english_text: Let’s not test Christ, as some of them tested, and perished by the serpents.
nagamese_text: Khrista ke kitia bhi porikha na koribi, jineka bisi manu Taike kora nisena, aru etu nimite taikhan ke saph pora khotom kori dise.

english_text: Don’t grumble, as some of them also grumbled, and perished by the destroyer.
nagamese_text: Khong uthi kene sikayat na koribi, jineka bisi manu korise, aru etu nimite taikhan ke khotom kori diya jon pora khotom kori dise.

english_text: Now all these things happened to them by way of example, and they were written for our admonition, on whom the ends of the ages have come.
nagamese_text: Etiya eitu khan sob to amikhan nimite ekta saikene bujhi bole laga kotha ase. Kilekoile etu Shastro te likha to amikhan hoshiar hobo nimite ase, jun khan uporte yug khotom huwa din ahi jaise.

english_text: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.
nagamese_text: Etu karone jun manu khan khara ase bhabe, taikhan na giribole nimite hoshiar koribi.

english_text: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
nagamese_text: Eku porikha bhi apuni ke girai dibole para nai, khali mamuli porikha khan te he girise, jun te sob manu khan giri thake. Kintu, Isor ke biswas thakibi. Tai kitia bhi bukhi bole napara porikha apuni ke nadibo, kintu jitia apuni porikha pabo, Tai apuni ke etu porikha pora bacha bole nimite rasta bhi dibo, titia apuni dhorjo kori bole paribo.

english_text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, moi laga morom thaka khan, murti puja khan pora dur thakibi.

english_text: I speak as to wise men. Judge what I say.
nagamese_text: Moi buja manu khan ke koi ase. Moi ki koi ase etu pora apnikhan nijorke bisar koribi.

english_text: The cup of blessing which we bless, isn’t it a sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, isn’t it a sharing of the body of Christ?
nagamese_text: Amikhan jun asirbad laga kup pora asis kore, etu to Khrista laga khun te bhag loi ase nohoi? Aru juntu roti amikhan bhangai kene bhag kori ase, etu to Khrista laga gaw ase nohoi?

english_text: Because there is one loaf of bread, we, who are many, are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf of bread.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ta te khali ekta roti ase, etu nimite amikhan bisi jon hoilebi, sob ekta gaw he ase, kele koile amikhan sob to ekta roti pora he bhag kore.

english_text: Consider Israel according to the flesh. Don’t those who eat the sacrifices participate in the altar?
nagamese_text: Israel laga manu khan ke sabi. Jitia taikhan bolidan diya janwar khan ke khai, taikhan etu bedi te bhag kori kene khai nohoi?

english_text: What am I saying then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
nagamese_text: Tinehoile ami ki koi ase? Kha luwa murti khan ke bolidan kora to ki ase? Nohoile ekta murti to kiba ekta ase naki?

english_text: But I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I don’t desire that you would have fellowship with demons.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi, ami laga motlob to etu ase, jitia Porjati khan pora bolidan diye, taikhan etu Isor ke nohoi kene bhoot khan ke bolidan diye! Kintu moi apnikhan ke bhoot khan laga bhag hobole dibo mon nai!

english_text: You can’t both drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You can’t both partake of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan Isor laga kup pora bhi aru bhoot khan laga kup pora bhi khabole na paribo. Apnikhan Probhu laga kha luwa jagate bhi aru saitan laga kha luwa jagate bhi bhag lobole na paribo.

english_text: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
nagamese_text: Na amikhan Probhu ke mon julabole dikhai ase naki? Amikhan Probhu pora bhi hokti thaka nohoi, na ase?

english_text: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are profitable. “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things build up.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan koi, “Sob to kori bole niyom ase.” Kintu sob to labh nohoi. “Sob to kori bole niyom ase,” kintu sob to manu khan ke thik bonai nadiye.

english_text: Let no one seek his own, but each one his neighbor’s good.
nagamese_text: Kun bhi nijor laga bhal nimite bisaribo nalage, dusra khan laga bhal he nohoile.

english_text: Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,
nagamese_text: Apnikhan juntu bajar te kine eitu khan sob to khabole pare, nijor laga bhabona ke nahudi kene.

english_text: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.”
nagamese_text: Kilekoile “prithibi aru tai bhitor te sob to Probhu laga ase.”

english_text: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba biswas nakora manu apuni ke bhat khabole mate, aru apuni jabole mon hoi, tai apnike ki khabole diye eitu khan sob apuni laga bhabona ke nahudi kene khai lobi.

english_text: But if anyone says to you, “This was offered to idols,” don’t eat it for the sake of the one who told you, and for the sake of conscience. For “the earth is the Lord’s, with all its fullness.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi kunba apuni ke koi, “Etu boli kora laga ase,” titia etu to nakhabi, kele koile manu khan laga bhabona hisab te etu thik nai kun pora apuni ke khobor dise, aru nijor bhabona nimite bhi-

english_text: Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?
nagamese_text: Etiya ami laga motlob to, apnikhan nijor laga bhabona ke nohoi, kintu dusra laga bhabona ke koi ase. Kilekoile ami laga ajadi to kele dusra khan laga bhabona pora bisar hobole dibo?

english_text: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I denounced for something I give thanks for?
nagamese_text: Jodi ami kha luwa laga bhag te sonman pora loi, tinehoile kele amike apman kori ase juntu ami Isor ke dhanyavad dikene khaise?

english_text: Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, kha luwa ki hoile bhi, apuni ki kore, sob to Isor laga mohima nimite koribi.

english_text: Give no occasion for stumbling, whether to Jews, to Greeks, or to the assembly of God;
nagamese_text: Yehudi aru Porjati khan ke, aru Isor laga girja ke biya na koribi,

english_text: even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be saved.
nagamese_text: jineka moi bhi manu khan ke sob te khushi kori dibole kosis kore. Ami nijor labh hobole nimite nibisare, kintu dusra khan nimite bisare, eneka kori kene taikhan bhi bachi jabo nimite.

english_text: Be imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
nagamese_text: Moi jineka Khrista laga niyom cholai, eneka nisena tumikhan bhi moi laga niyom khan koribi.

english_text: Now I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in all things, and hold firm the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.
nagamese_text: Etiya moi apnikhan ke prosansa kori ase kele koile apnikhan moi nimite sob to yaad kore, aru apuni laga jati laga niyom khan takot pora dhure, jineka moi apnikhan laga hathte punchai dise.

english_text: But I would have you know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
nagamese_text: Etiya moi apnikhan ke bujhai dibole mon thaka to Khrista to mota manu khan laga matha ase, aru mota khan to maiki khan laga matha ase, aru Isor to Khrista laga matha ase.

english_text: Every man praying or prophesying, having his head covered, dishonors his head.
nagamese_text: Sob manu jun prathana aru bhabobani kore, etu homoi te tai laga matha te kiba jinis rakhise koile, tai laga matha ke opman kori ase.

english_text: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered dishonors her head. For it is one and the same thing as if she were shaved.
nagamese_text: Kintu kun mahila prathana aru bhabobani kore aru tai laga matha dhakikena nakore, tai laga matha ke opman kore. Kilekoile etu to eke kotha nisena ase jineka ekjon mahila tai laga matha te thaka chuli sob kati loi.

english_text: For if a woman is not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her be covered.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jodi ekjon mahila tai laga matha ke nadhake, tinehoile taikhan laga chuli bhi kati bole dibi. Kintu jodi mahila khan taikhan laga chuli kati bole nahoile bhi matha takulu kori bole opman lage koile, taikhan ke taikhan laga matha dhakibole kobi.

english_text: For a man indeed ought not to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ekjon mota pora matha dhaka to thik nohoi, kelemane tai to Isor laga noksa aru mohima nisena taike bonaise. Kintu ekjon maiki to tai laga mota laga mohima ase.

english_text: For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
nagamese_text: Kilekoile mota manu to maiki pora nohoi. Ulta, maiki he mota manu pora ase.

english_text: for man wasn’t created for the woman, but woman for the man.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile mota manu to maiki khan nimite bona nohoi, kintu maiki ke mota manu nimite bonaise.

english_text: For this cause the woman ought to have authority over her own head, because of the angels.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite maiki khan to taikhan laga matha dhaki kene rakhibo lage, eneka hoile manu khan janibo tai mota laga adhikar te ase koi kene, aru tai eitu khan kora to sorgodoth khan nimite ase.

english_text: Nevertheless, neither is the woman independent of the man, nor the man independent of the woman, in the Lord.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi, Probhu logote to, maiki to mota pora ajad nohoi, aru mota bhi maiki pora ajad nohoi.

english_text: For as woman came from man, so a man also comes through a woman; but all things are from God.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile maiki to mota manu pora ase, aru mota bhi maiki pora he ase: kintu sob jinis to Isor pora he ase.

english_text: Judge for yourselves. Is it appropriate that a woman pray to God unveiled?
nagamese_text: Nijor pora bisar kori sabi: ekjon mahila tai laga matha nadhaki kene Isor ke prathana kora to thik ase naki?

english_text: Doesn’t even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
nagamese_text: Etu prithibi laga niyom nijor pora he apnikhan ke nasikhai, jodi ekjon mota chuli lamba kore, etu to tai nimite sorom ase nohoi?

english_text: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, for her hair is given to her for a covering.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi ekjon maiki chuli lamba rakhe, etu tai laga mohima ase nohoi? Kilekoile taike lamba chuli diya to taike dhakibole nimite dise.

english_text: But if any man seems to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither do God’s assemblies.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi kunba manu etu kotha khan pora mon khushi nai, amikhan logote bhi aru Isor laga girja khan te bhi aru etu pora alag dusra niyom nai.

english_text: But in giving you this command I don’t praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.
nagamese_text: Kintu etiya moi kobole thaka adesh khan, moi apnikhan ke prosansa kora nohoi, apnikhan eke logote aha to, bhal hobole nohoi, kintu bisi biya nimite.

english_text: For first of all, when you come together in the assembly, I hear that divisions exist among you, and I partly believe it.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile sob pora age te, moi etu huni bole paise jitia apnikhan girja te eke logote joma hoi, apnikhan majote mon namili kene alag thake, aru etu kotha ke biswas kori bole tan nai.

english_text: For there also must be factions among you, that those who are approved may be revealed among you.
nagamese_text: Kelemane kunba biswasi khan nijor dimag cholai kene kun he asol biswasi ase koi kene sabole, alag dol khan shuru kori bole bhabe.

english_text: When therefore you assemble yourselves together, it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat.
nagamese_text: Kelemane jitia apnikhan ekta jagate eke logote ahe, etu to Probhu laga Bhoj kha luwa kori bole nahe.

english_text: For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jitia kha luwa kora somoi hobo, sob manu nijor laga kha luwa to poila khai loi; kunba to khabole napaikena bhuka thake, aru kunba to bisi khai kene nisa hoi kene thake.

english_text: What, don’t you have houses to eat and to drink in? Or do you despise God’s assembly and put them to shame who don’t have enough? What shall I tell you? Shall I praise you? In this I don’t praise you.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile apnikhan kha luwa kori bole nimite nijor ghor nai naki? Na apnikhan Isor laga girja ke ghin kore aru gorib manu khan ke sorom khilai?

english_text: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile moike Probhu pora ki dise etu moi apnikhan ke di ase, Probhu Jisu he, Taike thogai diya rati te, roti loise,

english_text: When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”
nagamese_text: aru Tai dhanyavad dise, aru Tai bhangai kene koise, “Etu Moi laga khun ase, juntu tumikhan nimite ase. Moike yaad kori kene etu koribi.”

english_text: In the same way he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”
nagamese_text: Thik etu nisena, Tai bhi kha luwa kora pichete kup to loise, eneka koi kene, “Etu kup to Ami laga khun te ekta notun laga vachan ase. Apnikhan kiman bar etu pibo, Moike yaad kori kene etu koribi.”

english_text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile hodai jitia apnikhan etu roti pora khabi aru etu kup pora pibo, apnikhan Probhu mora laga khobor to prochar kori thakibo jitia tak Tai wapas nahhe.

english_text: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord’s cup in a way unworthy of the Lord will be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, jun hoilebi, thik pora nabuji kene Probhu laga roti khai nohoile kup pora pi loi, tai to Probhu laga gaw aru Tai laga khun age te te golti hobo.

english_text: But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread and drink of the cup.
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon manu tai nijorke poila sai lobole dibi, aru etu nisena taike roti khabole aru kup pora pibole dibi.

english_text: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy way eats and drinks judgment to himself if he doesn’t discern the Lord’s body.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun manu tai nijor gaw ke bhal pora nasai kene khai aru pi loi, tai to nijorke bisar kora laga khai loi aru pi loi.

english_text: For this cause many among you are weak and sickly, and not a few sleep.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite apnikhan majote bisi manu komjur aru bemar ase, aru bisi manu ghumai kene ase.

english_text: For if we discerned ourselves, we wouldn’t be judged.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia amikhan nijorke sai, amikhan ke bisar nahobo.

english_text: But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia amikhan ke Probhu pora bisar kore, etu amikhan ke sidha kori bole nimite ase, eneka hoile amikhan ke prithibi logote bodnam nohobo.

english_text: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, moi laga bhai khan, jitia apnikhan eke logote Probhu laga Bhojan khabole ahe, ekjon-ekjon nimite rukhi bhi.

english_text: But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest your coming together be for judgment. The rest I will set in order whenever I come.
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba ekjon bhuk lagi thakile, taike ghor te khabole dibi, eneka hoile tumi duijon Isor laga bisar te eke logote nahibo. Aru apnikhan pora dusra kiba likha khan to, moi aha pichete apnikhan ke dikhai dibo.

english_text: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.
nagamese_text: Etiya, bhai khan moi atma laga bordan laga kotha koi dibo, apnikhan pora etu najane eneka hobo dibo mon nai.

english_text: You know that when you were heathen, you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan jani ase jitia apnikhan biswas nathaka asele, apnikhan nijorke ulta rasta te loi jaise aru jibon nathaka murti khan ke puja kori thakise.

english_text: Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.
nagamese_text: Etu karone moi apnikhan ke janai di ase, kun bhi Isor laga Atma pora eneka kobole na paribo, “Jisu ke shrap hobi,” aru kun bhi Pobitro Atma nathaki kene eneka kobole na paribo, “Jisu he Probhu ase.”

english_text: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
nagamese_text: Etiya, etu te bisi kisim laga bordan khan ase, kintu Isor laga Atma to eke ase.

english_text: There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
nagamese_text: Aru etu te alag-alag sewkai khan ase, kintu ekjon he Probhu ase.

english_text: There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.
nagamese_text: Aru etu te alag-alag kisim laga kaam khan ase, kintu ekjon he Isor ase, jun pora kaam khan sob logote kori ase.

english_text: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.
nagamese_text: Etiya ekjon-ekjon logote Atma dikene ase, ekjon-ekjon ke modot koribo paribo nimite.

english_text: For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Atma pora kunba ke buddhi laga kotha dise, aru etu eke Atma pora kunba ke gyaan laga kotha dise,

english_text: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit,
nagamese_text: eke Atma pora kunba ke biswas dise, aru etu eke Atma pora bhal kori diya bordan dise,

english_text: and to another workings of miracles, and to another prophecy, and to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of languages, and to another the interpretation of languages.
nagamese_text: aru kunba ke bhal kaam kora laga hokti dise, kunba ke bhabobani, kunba ke bhal biya atma bujhi bole para, kunba ke alag kisim laga bhasha, aru kunba ke alag kisim laga bhasha ke bujhai dibo para laga bordan dise.

english_text: But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon aru eke Atma pora etu sob kaam khan kori ase, aru Tai laga itcha hisab te ekjon-ekjon ke bhag kori kene diye.

english_text: For as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile manu laga khali ekta gaw he ase hoilebi alag-alag kaam hisab te bhag ase, kintu jiman bhag hoilebi gaw to ekta he ase; thik etu nisena Khrista bhi ekjon he ase.

english_text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile ekjon Atma pora he amikhan sobke baptizma dikene ekta gaw bonai dise, Yehudi hoile bhi Porjati hoile bhi, bandi kene thaka nohoile bhi ajad thakile bhi, amikhan sobke ekjon Atma he khabole dise.

english_text: For the body is not one member, but many.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile gaw to khali ekta bhag he nohoi, kintu bisi ase.

english_text: If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.
nagamese_text: Jodi theng pora koi, “Ami to hath nohoi, etu nimite ami to gaw laga bhag nohoi,” eneka koile bhi tai etu gaw laga ekta bhag he ase.

english_text: If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi kaan pora eneka koi, “kelemane moi to suku nohoi, etu nimite moi etu gaw laga bhag nohoi,” eneka koile bhi tai etu gaw laga ekta bhag he ase.

english_text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?
nagamese_text: Jodi pura gaw to suku ase koi, tinehoile kote pora huni bole paribo? Jodi pura gaw to kaan ase koi, tinehoile kote pora gundha bole paribo?

english_text: But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.
nagamese_text: Kintu Isor pora Tai laga itcha hisab te alag-alag bhag ke ekjon-ekjon laga gaw te rakhidise.

english_text: If they were all one member, where would the body be?
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi taikhan sob eke bhag ase koi, tinehoile etu gaw to kote hobo?

english_text: But now they are many members, but one body.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite ta te bisi bhag ase, hoile bhi ekta gaw he ase.

english_text: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
nagamese_text: Suku pora hath ke eneka kobole na paribo, “Ami apuni ke nalage.” Nohoile bhi aru, matha pora theng ke koi, “Ami apuni ke nalage.”

english_text: No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi asol kotha to, gaw laga bhag khan jun to bisi komjur dikhe, taikhan he asol kaam laga bhag ase,

english_text: Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty,
nagamese_text: aru juntu gaw laga bhag ke amikhan kaam nai koi kene bhabe, etu bhag ke amikhan bisi bhal pora sai, aru juntu bhag ke dikha bole napare etu bhag ke amikhan bisi bhal pora sai,

english_text: while our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,
nagamese_text: Hoile bhi amikhan laga dikha bole sundur bhag ke bisi bhal pora nasai le bhi hobo. Kintu Isor pora sob bhag ke ekta gaw te eke logote milai dise, eneka hoile sob bhag ke eke sonman hobo,

english_text: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
nagamese_text: etu nimite gaw majote kun bhi alag-alag bhag nahobo, kintu utu bhag to ekjon-ekjon ke eke mon pora sabo.

english_text: When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
nagamese_text: Eneka hoile, jitia ekta bhag dukh pabo, sob bhag bhi dukh hoi jabo; aru jitia ekta bhag ke sonman pabo, sob bhag bhi etu logote khushi koribo.

english_text: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.
nagamese_text: Etiya apnikhan sob Khrista laga gaw ase, aru ekjon-ekjon Tai laga bhag khan ase.

english_text: God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.
nagamese_text: Aru hosa pora bhi Isor pora kunba ke girja te sabole rakhise, poila jaga to Tai laga basi luwa chela khan hobo, dusra to bhabobadi khan, tisra to hikhok khan, etu pichete asurit kaam kora khan, pichete bhal kori diya laga bordan, modot kora khan, bhal pora cholai kene ja, aru alag kisim laga bhasha kowa khan.

english_text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
nagamese_text: Sob to apostle khan ase naki? Sob to bhabobadi khan ase naki? Sob to hikhok khan ase naki? Sob to asurit kaam kora manu ase naki?

english_text: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?
nagamese_text: Sob logote changai kori diya bordan ase naki? Sob to alag bhasha kobole pare naki? Sob to alag bhasha khan ke bujhai dibole pare naki?

english_text: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
nagamese_text: Kintu sob pora dangor bordan ke mon dikene lobole itcha koribi. Aru etiya, ami apnikhan ke sob pora bhal rasta dikhai dibo.

english_text: If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
nagamese_text: Jodi moi manu aru sorgo duth khan laga bhasha pora koi, kintu moi logote morom nai koile, titia hoile ami to ekta hala kori thaka tina nisena ase nohoile bhi ekta awaj di thaka thali nisena ase.

english_text: If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi moi logote bhabobani laga bordan aru bujhi bole napara kotha aru sob bujhi jaa gyaan khan ase koile, aru jodi moi logote pahar ke hata bole para laga biswas ase, kintu jodi ami logote morom to nai, tinehoile ami to eku bhi nohoi.

english_text: If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi ami laga dhun sompoti khan sob bhag kori diye, aru jodi moi laga gaw ke boli nimite daan di diye, kintu ami logote morom nai koile, moi eku bhi labh nohobo.

english_text: Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
nagamese_text: Morom to rukhibole pare aru norom ase; morom to suku najule; morom to phutani nadikhai, etu khong nohoi.

english_text: doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
nagamese_text: Etu khechera nakore, etu nijor nimite nabisare, etu joldi ghusa nauthe, etu golti khan ke monte narakhe.

english_text: doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
nagamese_text: Etu adharmik kaam khan te khushi nakore, hoilebi hosa te khushi kore.

english_text: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
nagamese_text: Etu sobke dhorjo kori bole pare, sob te biswas rakhe, sob asha rakhe, dukh digdar te dhorjo kori bole pare.

english_text: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will be done away with. Where there are various languages, they will cease. Where there is knowledge, it will be done away with.
nagamese_text: Morom kitia bhi khotom nohoi. Kintu bhabobani khan laga bordan khan bhi sob khotom hoi jabo: alag kisim laga bhasha kori bole para laga bordan, aru gyaan laga bordan khan sob khotom hoi jabo.

english_text: For we know in part and we prophesy in part;
nagamese_text: Kilekoile amikhan etu bhabobani aru gyaan ke pura najane aru adha kaam he kore.

english_text: but when that which is complete has come, then that which is partial will be done away with.
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia pura thik thaka to ahibo, titia juntu khan pura nohoi, eitu khan sob khotom hoi jabo.

english_text: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child. Now that I have become a man, I have put away childish things.
nagamese_text: Jitia moi bacha thakisele, moi bacha nisena kotha korise, moi bacha nisena bhabona korise, moi bacha nisena kaam kori thakise. Jitia moi dangor manu hoise, moi bacha nisena laga kaam khan sob chari dise.

english_text: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile etiya amikhan ayna te bhal pora sabole napare, kintu pichete usor pora ekjon-ekjon laga chehera sabole paribo. Etiya moi olop bhag he jane, kintu pichete moi pura jani jabo, jineka Isor pora amike pura janikena ase.

english_text: But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu tinta to thaki jabo: biswas, asha aru morom. Kintu eitu khan majote sob pora dangor to morom ase.

english_text: Follow after love and earnestly desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
nagamese_text: Morom laga piche koribi aru atma laga bordan karone mon julibi, kintu asol bordan apnikhan bhal pora janibo laga to bhabobani ase.

english_text: For he who speaks in another language speaks not to men, but to God, for no one understands, but in the Spirit he speaks mysteries.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jun ekjon bhasha alag pora kotha koi ase tai to manu ke kotha kora nohoi kintu Isor ke kori ase; kelemane kun nabuje, kintu tai lukaikene thaka kotha khan atma te koi ase.

english_text: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, exhortation, and consolation.
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon kun bhabobani kore, taikhan manu khan ke utsah kore, aru taikhan manu khan laga mon aram aru dangor kori diye.

english_text: He who speaks in another language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the assembly.
nagamese_text: Jun alag bhasha laga kotha khan koi, taikhan to nijor laga biswas ke dangor kore, kintu jun bhabobani kore taikhan to girja laga biswas ke dangor kore.

english_text: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but even more that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.
nagamese_text: Etiya moi laga itcha to apnikhan sob bhi alag bhasha te kotha koribo lage, kintu etu pora bhi bhabobani kora to he bisi itcha ase. Kilekoile jun bhabobani kore, taikhan to alag bhasha kora khan pora bhi dangor ase (notun bhasha laga motlob koi diya to girja te biswasi thaka khan ke uthabole nimite te ase).

english_text: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking with other languages, what would I profit you unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?
nagamese_text: Kintu bhai khan, jodi moi apnikhan ke alag bhasha pora kotha kori kene ahe, apnikhan laga ki labh hobo, jitia tak moi etu bhasha laga asol motlob, nohoile bhi tai laga gyaan, nohoile bhi bhabobani, nohoile bhi sikhai dibole thaka kotha to apnikhan ke koi nadiye koile?

english_text: Even lifeless things that make a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they didn’t give a distinction in the sounds, how would it be known what is piped or harped?
nagamese_text: Etu hosa ase utu jibon nathaka bajana khan juntu awaj khan ulai basuri hoilebi taar laga bajana hoilebi, jodi taikhan alag-alag awaj khan nadiye koile, kineka pora eitu khan ke janibo, basuri pora ki bajai ase aru taar laga bajana pora ki bajai ase?

english_text: For if the trumpet gave an uncertain sound, who would prepare himself for war?
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jodi bhigul bajana pora najana alag awaj diye koile, kun pora etu huni kene lorai karone taiyari koribo?

english_text: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.
nagamese_text: Apuni khan bhi thik eneka nisena he ase. Jitia tak apnikhan bujhi bole bhasha nakoi, tinehoile kineka pora apnikhan laga kotha janibo? Kilekoile apnikhan to hawa ke kotha kora nisena hobo.

english_text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning.
nagamese_text: Etu prithibi te bisi kisim bhasha ase kowa to hosa ase, aru ekta bhasha bhi motlob nathaka to nai.

english_text: If then I don’t know the meaning of the language, I would be to him who speaks a foreigner, and he who speaks would be a foreigner to me.
nagamese_text: Jodi moi etu bhasha laga motlob ki ase najane koile, moi utu kotha kora manu nimite bahar desh laga manu nisena lagibo, aru ekjon jun amike kotha kori ase tai bhi ami nimite dusra desh laga manu nisena lagibo.

english_text: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek that you may abound to the building up of the assembly.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite apnikhan jun atma laga bordan bisi lobole itcha kori thaki ase, taikhan utu bordan lobi juntu girja khan laga biswas ke bisi dangor kori dibo.

english_text: Therefore let him who speaks in another language pray that he may interpret.
nagamese_text: Eneka hoile jun ekjon alag bhasha pora kotha kore, tai etu bhasha buja bo paribole nimite prathana koribo lage.

english_text: For if I pray in another language, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
nagamese_text: Jodi moi alag bhasha pora prathana kore, moi laga atma bhi prathana kore, kintu ami laga bhabona to eku bhi nakore.

english_text: What should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, ami ki koribo lagibo? Moi nijor laga atma logote prathana koribo, kintu moi nijor laga bhabona logote bhi prathana koribo. Moi nijor laga atma logote gana koribo, aru moi nijor laga bhabona logote bhi gana koribo.

english_text: Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say the “Amen” at your giving of thanks, seeing he doesn’t know what you say?
nagamese_text: Nohoile, jodi apuni atma pora Isor ke dhanyavad kore, kintu ekjon nabuja manu to kineka apuni laga dhanyavad ke “Amen” kobo, kele koile apuni ki koi ase tai eku bhi nabuje?

english_text: For you most certainly give thanks well, but the other person is not built up.
nagamese_text: Apuni to pura mon pora dhanyavad di thakibo pare, kintu dusra manu to eku labh hobo napare.

english_text: I thank my God, I speak with other languages more than you all.
nagamese_text: Ami Isor ke dhanyavad diye kele koile moi apnikhan pora bhi bisi alag bhasha te kotha kore.

english_text: However, in the assembly I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in another language.
nagamese_text: Kintu girja te dos hajar alag bhasha laga kotha kora pora to juntu pansta kotha ami laga bhabona pora dusra khan ke buja bole pare, etu he kobo.

english_text: Brothers, don’t be children in thoughts, yet in malice be babies, but in thoughts be mature.
nagamese_text: Bhai khan, apnikhan laga bhabona te bacha nisena nahobi. Etu pora to, biya kaam te bacha nisena hobi, hoile bhi bhabona te dangor manu nisena thakibi.

english_text: In the law it is written, “By men of strange languages and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people. They won’t even listen to me that way, says the Lord.”
nagamese_text: Niom laga kitab te eneka likhi kene ase, “Alag bhasha kora manu khan aru alag kotha kowa manu khan ke loi kene, Moi etu manu khan ke kotha koribo, Kintu eneka korile bhi taikhan moike nahunibo, Probhu he koise.”

english_text: Therefore other languages are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to the unbelieving; but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to those who believe.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite, alag bhasha kora khan to ekta chihna ase, biswasi khan karone nohoi, kintu abiswasi khan nimite; hoilebi bhabobani kora khan to abiswasi khan nimite nohoi, kintu biswasi khan nimite ase.

english_text: If therefore the whole assembly is assembled together and all speak with other languages, and unlearned or unbelieving people come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?
nagamese_text: Jodi, etu karone, pura biswasi khan eke logote ekta jagate joma hoi aru taikhan sob alag bhasha te kotha kori bole shuru hoijai, kintu kunba abiswasi aru bordan nathaka manu khan ahe, taikhan ke dikhi kene apnikhan pagala hoise nakobo naki?

english_text: But if all prophesy, and someone unbelieving or unlearned comes in, he is reproved by all, and he is judged by all.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi apnikhan sob bhabobani kori thakise, kintu kunba bordan nathaka nohoile bhi abiswasi apnikhan logote ahe, taikhan laga paapkhan sob apnikhan pora koi dibo aru apnikhan laga kotha pora taikhan ke bisar koribo,

english_text: And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed. So he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.
nagamese_text: monte lukai kene thaka janai dibo aru tai athukari kene Isor ke aradhana koribo, janai dibo, “Isor hosa bhi apnikhan laga majot te ase.”

english_text: What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has another language, or has an interpretation. Let all things be done to build each other up.
nagamese_text: Moi laga bhai khan apuni khan ki koribo lage? Jitia apuni khan eke logote joma kore ekjon gana kore, ekjon sikhai, ekjon Isor laga kotha koi, ekjon alag bhasha koi nahoile alag bhasha laga motlob bujhai diye. Eitu khan sob to girja age jabo nimite ase.

english_text: If any man speaks in another language, let there be two, or at the most three, and in turn; and let one interpret.
nagamese_text: Jitia ekjon alag bhasa pora kotha koi, bisi hoilebi duijon nahoile tinjon he kobole lage, aru ekjon to etu laga motlob kobo lage.

english_text: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi jitia motlob koi dibole manu nathakile, etu manu ke girja te chup kori dibi. Aru tai nijorke Isor logote kotha kori bole dibi.

english_text: Let two or three of the prophets speak, and let the others discern.
nagamese_text: Duijon nahoile tinjon bhabobadi ke kobole dibi, aru etu ki koise dusra ke faisla kori bole dibi.

english_text: But if a revelation is made to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi ekta kotha Isor pora dusra bohi thaka ekjon ke diye, tinehoile age ula ke chup hobole dibi.

english_text: For you all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be exhorted.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile apnikhan sob ekta piche ekta kori kene bhabobani koribo pare, titia sob bujhi bole paribo aru utsah pabo.

english_text: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
nagamese_text: Hosa pora bhi bhabobadi khan laga atma to bhabobadi khan nijor laga nichete kaam kore.

english_text: for God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Isor to ulta-polti laga Isor nohoi, kintu shanti laga ase. Sob pobitro manu khan laga girja te,

english_text: Let the wives be quiet in the assemblies, for it has not been permitted for them to be talking except in submission, as the law also says,
nagamese_text: mahila khan ke girja bhitor te chup thaki bole dibi. Kilekoile taikhan ke kotha kori bole agya nai, kintu taikhan adhikar thaka manu nichete thakibo lage, Moses laga niyom te koise.

english_text: if they desire to learn anything. “Let them ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a wife to be talking in the assembly.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi taikhan sikhi bole itcha hoile, taikhan laga nijor mota ke ghor te hudibole dibi, kele koile ekjon mahila pora girja ghor te kotha kora to sorom laga kotha ase.

english_text: What!? Was it from you that the word of God went out? Or did it come to you alone?
nagamese_text: Na Isor laga kotha to apnikhan pora he ulaise? Na khali apnikhan he etu paise?

english_text: If any man thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognize the things which I write to you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba manu nijorke bhabobadi hobole nohoile bhi bordan paikena ase koi kene bhabe, tinehoile moi apnikhan ke itu chithi te likhi ase etu sob to Isor laga hukum ase koi kene bujhi bo lage.

english_text: But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi kunba manu murkho nisena thake, taike murkho he thaki bole dibi.

english_text: Therefore, brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy, and don’t forbid speaking with other languages.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite, bhai khan, bhabobani korate pura mon dibi, aru kunke bhi alag bhasha kobole narukhabi.

english_text: Let all things be done decently and in order.
nagamese_text: Kintu sob kaam to bhal aru thik niyom pora koribo lage.

english_text: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,
nagamese_text: Bhai khan, etiya moi susamachar apnikhan ke koi diya to yaad rakhibole di ase, juntu apnikhan bhi pai loise, aru jun to te apnikhan khara ase,

english_text: by which also you are saved, if you hold firmly the word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
nagamese_text: juntu pora apnikhan poritran pai loi ase, hoile bhi apnikhan ami prochar kora kotha to thik pora dhori kene thakile, jodi apnikhan biswas kori luwa to eku bhi labh nathaka nahoile.

english_text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
nagamese_text: Kilekoile moi ki paise etu apnikhan ke di dise - Shastro te likha nisena Khrista amikhan laga paap nimite morise,

english_text: that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
nagamese_text: aru Taike mati bhitor te dabai dise, aru Tai tisra dinte jinda hoise, Isor kotha hisab te,

english_text: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
nagamese_text: aru Tai Cephas ke dikhai dise, aru etu pichete Tai laga baroh ta chela khan ke.

english_text: Then he appeared to over five hundred brothers at once, most of whom remain until now, but some have also fallen asleep.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Tai ekbar te pans-soh upor bhai khan logot Tai dikhai dise. Kunba to etiya bhi jinda ase, kintu kunba to mori jaise.

english_text: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
nagamese_text: Etu pichete Tai James ke dikhai dise, etu pichete Tai laga sob apostle khan ke.

english_text: and last of all, as to the child born at the wrong time, he appeared to me also.
nagamese_text: Aru sobse anth te, Tai moike dikhai dise, jineka ekjon bacha homoi napunchi kene jonom huwa nisena.

english_text: For I am the least of the apostles, who is not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Isor laga apostle majote moi he sob pora chutu ase, moi eneka koi ase kele koile moi Isor laga girja khan ke dukh digdar di thakise, etu karone moi Tai laga apostle hobole yogya nohoi.

english_text: But by the grace of God I am what I am. His grace which was given to me was not futile, but I worked more than all of them; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
nagamese_text: Kintu aji moi ki ase sob Isor laga anugrah pora he ase, aru juntu anugrah moi logote thakise etu ene khali pora nohoi. Hoilebi, dusra khan pora bhi moi he bisi kaam korise, kintu asol te moi laga hokti pora kaam kora nohoi, hoilebi Isor laga anugraha ami logote thaka nimite.

english_text: Whether then it is I or they, so we preach, and so you believed.
nagamese_text: Etu karone, ami hoilebi taikhan hoilebi, amikhan sob ekta khobor he prochar kori ase aru etu nimite apnikhan biswas korise.

english_text: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
nagamese_text: Etiya jodi Khrista ke amikhan Tai mora pora punoruthan hoise koi kene prochar kore, tinehoile kunba apnikhan majote kele mora manu khan punoruthan nohoi koi kene dusra ke koi ase?

english_text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.
nagamese_text: Kintu jodi ta te mora manu khan mori kene punoruthan nohoi, tinehoile Khrista bhi mora pora punoruthan huwa nai;

english_text: If Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith also is in vain.
nagamese_text: aru jodi Khrista ke punoruthan kori diya nai, tinehoile amikhan laga prochar to sob misa misi ase, aru apnikhan laga biswas to misa misi ase.

english_text: Yes, we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified about God that he raised up Christ, whom he didn’t raise up if it is true that the dead are not raised.
nagamese_text: Arubi, amikhan to Isor laga misa gawahi prochar kori ase koi kene pabo, kelemane amikhan Isor laga gawahi kowa to Tai he Jisu ke punoruthan kori dise, aru jodi kunke bhi mora pora punoruthan kori diya nai, tinehoile Isor pora Khrista ke bhi punoruthan kori diya nai.

english_text: For if the dead aren’t raised, neither has Christ been raised.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jodi mora khan punoruthan huwa nai, tinehoile Khrista bhi punoruthan huwa nai;

english_text: If Christ has not been raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins.
nagamese_text: aru jodi Khrista punoruthan huwa nai, tinehoile apnikhan laga biswas to misa misi ase; aru apnikhan etiya paap te ase.

english_text: Then they also who are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
nagamese_text: Aru jun khan Khrista nimite morise, taikhan sob harai jaise.

english_text: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.
nagamese_text: Jodi etu prithibi te amikhan laga jibon to Khrista laga asha te jinda thake, tinehoile etu prithibi te sob pora mon dukh manu khan to amikhan he hobo.

english_text: But now Christ has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruit of those who are asleep.
nagamese_text: Kintu asol te Khrista ke mora pora punoruthan uthai dise, aru morija khan bhitor te Tai he prothom phol ase.

english_text: For since death came by man, the resurrection of the dead also came by man.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile mora to manu pora anise, aru mora pora jee utha bhi dusra manu pora ahise.

english_text: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile jineka Adam te sob morija-a nisena, Khrista te sob aru jinda hoi jabo.

english_text: But each in his own order: Christ the first fruits, then those who are Christ’s at his coming.
nagamese_text: Kintu sob to thik hisab te hobo: Khrista, prothom phol, etu pichete jitia Khrista wapas ahibo, kun Khrista laga ase, taikhan khan uthibo.

english_text: Then the end comes, when he will deliver up the Kingdom to God the Father, when he will have abolished all rule and all authority and power.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete hekh homoi to ahibo, jitia Khrista etu prithibi laga sob cholawta, adhikari, aru sob takot khan ke khotom kori dibo. Etu pichete Tai pora Baba Isor ke rajyo to di dibo.

english_text: For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile Khrista he raj koribo jitia tak Isor pora Tai laga dushman khan ke Khrista laga theng nichete narakhe.

english_text: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.
nagamese_text: Mora to he sob pora hekh dushman hobo junke Isor pora khotom koribo.

english_text: For, “He put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when he says, “All things are put in subjection”, it is evident that he is excepted who subjected all things to him.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile, “Isor pora sob jinis ke Tai laga theng nichete rakhise.” Kintu jitia eneka koi ase “Tai sob jinis ke rakhise,” etu bhal pora bujhi ase Isor to sob jinis ke Tai laga nichete rakha to Tai nijorke milai kene kowa nohoi.

english_text: When all things have been subjected to him, then the Son will also himself be subjected to him who subjected all things to him, that God may be all in all.
nagamese_text: Etiya, jitia sob to Tai laga nichete ase, tinehoile Khrista nijor bhi Isor laga nichete ase jun pora sobke nichete rakhi kene ase, eneka hoile Isor he sob uporte raj koribo.

english_text: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?
nagamese_text: Nohoile, dusra khan ki koribo jun khan mora nimite baptizma loi ase koi kene? Jodi mora khan kitia bhi punoruthan nohoi, tinehoile taikhan kele mora nimite baptizma loi ase?

english_text: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?
nagamese_text: Aru amikhan nimite kineka? Amikhan kele amikhan nijorke sob somoite khatra te rakhe?

english_text: I affirm, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
nagamese_text: Ami hodai din mori ase! Moi hosa pora koi ase, bhai khan, amikhan laga Probhu Jisu Khrista te apnikhan ke moi khushi pora phutani kore.

english_text: If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
nagamese_text: Moi Ephesus sheher te jongli janwar logote lorai korise, manu khan laga khushi hisab nimite, kintu moi nimite ki labh hoise? Jodi mora khan ke punoruthan kora nai koile, “Ahibi amikhan kha-luwa koribo, kele koile amikhan kali moribo.”

english_text: Don’t be deceived! “Evil companionships corrupt good morals.”
nagamese_text: Dhoka nakhabi: “Biya sathi khan pora bhal adot ke biya kori diye.”

english_text: Wake up righteously and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
nagamese_text: Nisa hoi kene nathakibi! Dharmik jibon te thakibi! Paap kaam kori nathakibi. Kilekoile apnikhan kunba Isor ke bhal pora najane- moi eitu khan kowa to apnikhan ke sorom khila bole nimite koi ase.

english_text: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba pora hudibo, “Mora khan kineka punoruthan hoi, aru taikhan ki kisim laga gaw te ahibo?”

english_text: You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
nagamese_text: Apnikhan bisi murkho khan ase! Jitia apuni kiba bijon matite rupai, etu bijon age mori jabo lage etu pichete tai jinda hoi kene uthibo.

english_text: That which you sow, you don’t sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, maybe of wheat, or of some other kind.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi apuni kiba bijon rupai, ki ulabole ase etu nohoi, kintu ki rupai se khali etu bijon he ase- dhaan guti nohoile kiba ekta bijon hobo pare.

english_text: But God gives it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.
nagamese_text: Kintu Isor laga itcha hisab te etu bijon ke gaw dibo, aru ekta-ekta bijon ke bhi nijor laga gaw dibo.

english_text: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds.
nagamese_text: Sob mangso to eke nohoi. Kintu, sob manu laga mangso to eke ase, aru sob janwar laga mangso eke ase, aru sob chiriya laga bhi eke ase, aru sob maas laga bhi eke ase.

english_text: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial differs from that of the terrestrial.
nagamese_text: Ta te sorgo laga gaw khan ase aru prithibi laga gaw khan bhi ase. Kintu sorgo laga gaw to ekta gaw ase, aru prithibi laga gaw to alag ase.

english_text: There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
nagamese_text: Ta te suryo laga ekta gaw ase, aru chand laga alag ekta gaw ase, aru tara khan laga alag ekta gaw ase. Aru sob tara to taikhan nijor hisab te sundur ase.

english_text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown perishable; it is raised imperishable.
nagamese_text: Etu nisena mora khan pora punoruthan huwa bhi eneka ase. Ji gaw to matite rupai dise etu to puchi jabo, aru anonto jibon te uthijabo.

english_text: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
nagamese_text: Etu ke eku sonman nathaki kene rupai dise; kintu mohima hoi kene uthe. Etu ke komjur pora rupai se; kintu hokti hoi kene uthe.

english_text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is also a spiritual body.
nagamese_text: Etu ke mangso laga gaw hoi kene rupai dise; kintu atma laga gaw hoi kene uthe. Jodi ta te mangso laga gaw thake, tinehoile atma laga gaw bhi thake.

english_text: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
nagamese_text: Isor laga kotha te likhi kene ase, “Poila manu, Adam, ekta jinda jibon hoise.” Kintu hekh Adam to jibon diya atma hoise.

english_text: However, that which is spiritual isn’t first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual.
nagamese_text: Kintu atma he poila aha nohoi, mangso he poila ahise, aru etu pichete he atma.

english_text: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.
nagamese_text: Prithibi laga prothom manu ke bona to mati pora bonaise. Kintu dusra manu to sorgo pora ase.

english_text: As is the one made of dust, such are those who are also made of dust; and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
nagamese_text: Jineka ekjon prithibi laga thakise, thik eneka dusra khan bhi prithibi laga ase; aru jineka sorgo laga thakise, etu nisena dusra khan bhi sorgo laga ase.

english_text: As we have borne the image of those made of dust, let’s also bear the image of the heavenly.
nagamese_text: Aru jineka amikhan sabole prithibi laga protima bukha nisena hoise, etu nisena amikhan sorgo laga protima bukha nisena bhi hobo.

english_text: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
nagamese_text: Etiya ami koi ase, bhai khan, mangso aru khun pora Isor laga rajyote uttoradhikari napabo. Nohoile bhi harai juwa pora harai najuwa ke uttoradhikar nohobo.

english_text: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
nagamese_text: Sabi! Ami apuni khan ke ekta lukai kene thaka kotha koi dibo: Amikhan sob naghuma bo, kintu amikhan sob bodli hoi jabo-

english_text: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
nagamese_text: Ekbar te he, suku bondh kori kene khula pora bhi joldi, hekh somoi laga bhigul hala korate. Etu bhigul laga awaj ulabo, aru mora khan kitia bhi namori bole nimite jinda hoi kene uthibo, aru amikhan sob bodli hoi jabo.

english_text: For this perishable body must become imperishable, and this mortal must put on immortality.
nagamese_text: Kilekoile harai jabole laga gaw to kitia bhi harai najabole laga gaw lagai pindhi lobo lage, aru etu mora laga gaw to namora laga gaw hobo lage.

english_text: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
nagamese_text: Kintu jitia harai juwa gaw pora kitia bhi harai naja gaw ke pindhi loi, aru jitia mora gaw pora kitia bhi namora gaw ke pindhi loi, titia Shastro te ki likhi kene ase etu ahijabo, “Mrityu ke harai dise aru pura jiti jaise.”

english_text: “Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?”
nagamese_text: “Hey mrityu, tumi laga jit to kote ase? Mrityu, tumi laga dunkh kot te ase?”

english_text: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi mrityu laga dunkh to paap ase, aru paap laga shakti to niyom ase.

english_text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi Isor ke dhanyavad ase, jun amikhan ke jiti bole diye Probhu Jisu Khrista pora.

english_text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite ami morom kora bhai khan thik pora biswas ke dhori kene thakibi, nahili kene, hodai mon dikene Probhu laga kaam kori thakibi, etu jani kene thakibi ki apuni Probhu karone kaam kora to misa misi nahobo.

english_text: Now concerning the collection for the saints: as I commanded the assemblies of Galatia, you do likewise.
nagamese_text: Etiya Isor laga manu khan nimite daan joma korise, ami Galatia jaga laga girjakhan te kowa nisena, apuni khan bhi eneka he koribi.

english_text: On the first day of every week, let each one of you save as he may prosper, that no collections are made when I come.
nagamese_text: Hodai hafta laga prothom dinte, apuni khan alag joma kori lobi, apuni khan laga kamai pora joma kori kene rakhibi, kelemane jitia moi ahibo, apuni khan titia joma kori nathakibo.

english_text: When I arrive, I will send whoever you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete jitia moi punchibo, jun hoilebi, apnikhan pora basikena moi logot patha manu khan ke apnikhan laga daan logote chithi likhi kene Jerusalem te pathai dibo.

english_text: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.
nagamese_text: Aru jodi moi bhi jabo parise koile, taikhan moi logote jabo.

english_text: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
nagamese_text: Hoilebi moi apuni khan logote ahibo Macedonia jagate ja pichete. Kilekoile ami Macedonia majot pora jai ase.

english_text: But with you it may be that I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that you may send me on my journey wherever I go.
nagamese_text: Ami apuni khan logote thakibo parise koile thanda din tak thakibo, etu hoile ami dusra kun jaga khan te jabole ase etu nimite apnikhan amike modot kori bole paribo.

english_text: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits.
nagamese_text: Kelemane moi apuni khan ke khali paar hoi kene dikha he nohoikena, ami asha kore, Probhu laga itcha hoile apuni khan logote olop somoi karone thaki bole.

english_text: But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
nagamese_text: Kintu moi Ephesus te thakibo Pentecost napuncha tak.

english_text: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.
nagamese_text: Kelemane ekta dangor dorja ami karone khula ase, aru ta te dushman khan bhi bisi ase.

english_text: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
nagamese_text: Etiya jodi Timothy ahile, sabi tai apuni khan ke bhoi nakore, kelemane tai Probhu laga kaam kore, moi nisena.

english_text: Therefore let no one despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brothers.
nagamese_text: Kunbi taike chutu nabhabi bhi, hoilebi tai kot te jabole ase, shanti pora taike modot kori dibi, eneka pora tai moi logot ahibo, kele koile ami bhabona kori ase, ami laga bhai khan logote tai bhi ahibo koi kene.

english_text: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his desire to come now; but he will come when he has an opportunity.
nagamese_text: Etiya amikhan laga bhai Apollos laga kotha to, moi taike apnikhan logote jabole nimite bisi mon dangor kori disele. Kintu apnikhan logote etiya ahibole nimite tai laga itcha nai. Hoile bhi tai jitia bhal somoi pabo titia ahibo.

english_text: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
nagamese_text: Hoshiar pora thakibi; biswas te thik pora thakibi; mon dangor thakibi; takot thakibi.

english_text: Let all that you do be done in love.
nagamese_text: Ji kaam korile bhi morom pora koribi.

english_text: Now I beg you, brothers—you know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to serve the saints—
nagamese_text: Apuni khan jani ase, bhai khan, Stephanas laga ghor manu khan, taikhan to Achaia jaga laga poila bijon khan ase, aru taikhan to pobitro manu khan laga kaam koribo nimite nijorke di dise. Moi apuni khan ke koi ase,

english_text: that you also be in subjection to such, and to everyone who helps in the work and labors.
nagamese_text: taikhan nisena cholawta manu khan aru dusra jun khan mon dikene tai logote mili kene sewa kori ase eitu khan laga pichete jabi,

english_text: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus; for that which was lacking on your part, they supplied.
nagamese_text: Moi khushi ase Stephanas aru Fortunatus, aru Achaicus aha nimite, kelemane taikhan apuni khan ki napuncha thakise etu punchai dise.

english_text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge those who are like that.
