english_text: and he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father—to him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
nagamese_text: Khrista pora amikhan ke ekta rajyo bonai dise, Isor aru Baba laga ekjon purohit Tai laga mohima aru takot hodai nimite hobole dibi. Amen.

english_text: Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen.
nagamese_text: Sabi, Khrista badal logote ahi ase; Sob suku pora taike dikhibo, Jun manu Taike marise taikhan bhi etu dikhibo. Prithibi te jiman jat ase eitu khan sob pora Tai nimite mon dukh hoi kene kandibo. Hoi, Amen.

english_text: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.”
nagamese_text: “Moi Alpha aru Omega ase,” Probhu Isor koi ase, “Jun etiya ase, aru thakise, aru kun ahibole ase, sob pora Mohan.”

english_text: I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression, Kingdom, and perseverance in Christ Jesus, was on the isle that is called Patmos because of God’s Word and the testimony of Jesus Christ.
nagamese_text: Moi, John- apnikhan laga bhai aru ekjon jun Tai laga rajyo nimite eke logote mili kene dukh korise, aru nomro kori kene Jisu nimite sob kaam korise- Moi Patmos laga ekta majuli majote thakise, Isor laga kotha aru Jisu laga gawahi nimite.

english_text: I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, like a trumpet
nagamese_text: Probhu laga din te, moi atma te thakise aru moi laga piche pora ekta bhigul nisena jor awaj hunise.

english_text: saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”
nagamese_text: Aru koise, “Tumi ki dikhi ase etu kitab te likhibi, aru sat-ta girja khan te pathai dibi- Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, aru Laodicea khan ke.”

english_text: I turned to see the voice that spoke with me. Having turned, I saw seven golden lamp stands.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete moi piche phale ghuri kene kun pora moike kotha kori ase etu saise, aru jitia moi ghuri kene saise ta te sat-ta suna pora bona deevat dikhise.

english_text: And among the lamp stands was one like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching down to his feet, and with a golden sash around his chest.
nagamese_text: Aru etu deevat laga majote ekjon manu laga bacha nisena thakise, tai lagai kene thaka kapra tai laga theng niche tak thakise aru suna laga ekta kapra chati te lagai kene thakise.

english_text: His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow. His eyes were like a flame of fire.
nagamese_text: Tai laga matha aru chuli to wool nisena boga thakise aru borop nisena boga thakise aru tai laga suku to juli thaka jui nisena thakise.

english_text: His feet were like burnished brass, as if it had been refined in a furnace. His voice was like the voice of many waters.
nagamese_text: Tai laga theng khan to bhal pora sapha kori kene thaka pitol nisena thakise, jui pora sapha kori diya pitol nisena, aru tai laga awaj to nodi te pani jai thaka laga awaj nisena thakise.

english_text: He had seven stars in his right hand. Out of his mouth proceeded a sharp two-edged sword. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.
nagamese_text: Tai laga dyna hathte sat-ta tara thakise aru tai laga mukh pora dui phale bhi dhar thaka talwar ulaise. Tai laga chehera to suryo nisena ujala di thakise.

english_text: When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last,
nagamese_text: Jitia moi taike dikhise, moi Tai laga theng nichete ekjon mora manu giri juwa nisena giri jaise. Tai laga dyna hath pora moi uporte rakhise, aru koise, “Tumi bhoi nokoribi. Moi he shuru aru Moi he hekh ase,

english_text: and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever. Amen. I have the keys of Death and of Hades.
nagamese_text: Aru etiya Moi jinda ase. Moi mori jaisele, kintu sabi, Moi hodai aru hodai nimite jinda ase! Aru Moi logote mora laga aru etu prithibi nichete thaka Hades laga chabi ase.

english_text: Write therefore the things which you have seen, and the things which are, and the things which will happen hereafter.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite tumike ki dikhai ase etu sob likhi lobi aru etiya ki ahise aru pichete ki hobole ase etu sob likhibi.

english_text: The mystery of the seven stars which you saw in my right hand, and the seven golden lamp stands is this: The seven stars are the angels of the seven assemblies. The seven lamp stands are seven assemblies.
nagamese_text: Etu sat-ta tara aru sat-ta suna laga deevat laga lukai kene thaka motlob to etu ase: jun to tumi Moi laga dyna hathte dikhise, etu sat-ta tara to sat-ta girja laga sorgodoth khan ase aru etu sat-ta deevat khan to sat-ta girjakhan ase.”

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Ephesus write: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, he who walks among the seven golden lamp stands says these things:
nagamese_text: “Ephesus laga girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Ekjon kun laga dyna hathte sat-ta tara dhori ase aru kun etu sat-ta suna laga deevat khan uporte berai ase, Tai eneka koi ase:

english_text: “I know your works, and your toil and perseverance, and that you can’t tolerate evil men, and have tested those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and found them false.
nagamese_text: “Moi jani ase tumikhan laga kaam aru dukh kori thaka to aru tumikhan dhorjo kori kene dukh uthai thaka to, aru manu pora biya kaam kori thaka tumikhan bhal napai. Tumikhan bhal pora jani loise kun manu taikhan to apostle khan ase koi kene tumi usorte ahe, kintu taikhan nohoi, aru taikhan misa koi ase koi kene tumi jani loi.

english_text: You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary.
nagamese_text: Moi jane tumikhan dhorjo kori kene sob dukh khan uthai thakise, aru tumi Moi laga naam nimite bisi dukh paise, hoile bhi tumikhan alsi huwa nai.

english_text: But I have this against you, that you left your first love.
nagamese_text: Kintu moi tumike bhirodh kori ase kelemane tumikhan laga prothom morom to pahori kene chari jaise.

english_text: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu yaad koribi kuntu jaga pora tumi girise. Mon ghura bhi aru ki kaam prothom te kori thakise etu koribi. Kintu eneka nohoi koile, Moi ahibo aru tumikhan laga jaga pora etu deevat to hatai dibo- jodi tumi mon naghurai.

english_text: But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu tumikhan logote ase: Tumi Nicolas laga dol khan pora kora kaam khan ghin kore, Moi bhi etu ghin kore.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God.
nagamese_text: Jun manu logote kan ase, Atma pora girja khan ke ki koi ase etu huni bhi. Kun manu sob to pari kene jiti loi, taike Moi jibon laga ghas pora khabole nimite dibo, juntu Isor laga Paradise te ase.”’”

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Smyrna write: “The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things:
nagamese_text: “Smyrna girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Etu ekjon kun prothom aru hekh ase, jun mori jaisele aru kun mora pora jinda hoi jaise, eneka koi ase:

english_text: “I know your works, oppression, and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.
nagamese_text: “Moi jani ase tumikhan dukh paikene thaka to -kintu tumikhan dhuni ase- aru moi jane kun manu misa koi kene taikhan Yehudi ase koi, kintu taikhan nohoi. Kintu taikhan Saitan laga mondoli ase.

english_text: Don’t be afraid of the things which you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested; and you will have oppression for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
nagamese_text: Bhoi nokoribi dukh pabole thaka nimite. Sabi! Saitan pora tumikhan kunba ke bondhi ghor te phelai dibole ase tumikhan laga mon to sabole nimite, aru tumikhan dos din tak dukh pabo. Nomora tak biswasi hoi thakibi, aru titia moi tumikhan ke jibon laga mukut dibo.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. He who overcomes won’t be harmed by the second death.
nagamese_text: Kun manu logote kan ase, huni lobi Atma pora girja khan ke koi ase. Kun manu sob to paikene jiti loi tai aru duibar dukh paikene namoribo.’””

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Pergamum write: “He who has the sharp two-edged sword says these things:
nagamese_text: “Pergamum girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Ekjon kun logote dui phale dhar thaka talwar ase, Tai eneka koi ase.

english_text: “I know your works and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold firmly to my name, and didn’t deny my faith in the days of Antipas my witness, my faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
nagamese_text: “Moi jane tumikhan kote thaki ase, jun jagate Saitan laga singhason ase ta te. Hoile bhi tumikhan moi laga naam to loi thake aru tumikhan moi uporte biswas thaka bhi inkar kora nai. Tumikhan eneka he thakise, Moi laga gawahi aru ekjon biswasi Antipas laga homoi te bhi, jun tumikhan majot te morai dise, jun jagate Saitan thake.

english_text: But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality.
nagamese_text: Kintu moi tumikhan laga bhirodh te ase: Tumikhan majote Balaam laga sikhai diya kotha etiya bhi kunba dhori kene ase, kun pora Balak ke Israel laga bacha khan usorte dukh digdar anibole nimite dise, taikhan ke murti puja kori kene diya laga khan khilai kene biya kaam kori bole dibo nimite.

english_text: So also you likewise have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite, etu nisena he tumikhan majote bhi Nicolas laga dol khan pora sikhai diya to eneka dhori kene ase.

english_text: Repent therefore, or else I am coming to you quickly and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth.
nagamese_text: Mon ghura bhi, etu nimite! Kintu jodi tumikhan eneka nakore, titia Moi tumikhan usorte joldi ahibo aru Moi laga mukh te talwar thaka loi kene tumikhan logote lorai koribo.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written which no one knows but he who receives it.
nagamese_text: Kun manu logote kan ase, huni bhi ki Atma pora girja khan ke koi ase. Kun manu sob kori kene jiti loi, Moi lukai kene rakhi thaka manna taikhan ke dibo, aru Moi taikhan ke ekta boga pathor dibo aru ta te ekta notun naam pathor te likhi kene thakibo, etu naam kun pora bhi najanibo khali kunke etu pathor dibo tai pora he janibo.”’”

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Thyatira write: “The Son of God, who has his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet are like burnished brass, says these things:
nagamese_text: “Thyatira girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Isor laga Putro, kun laga suku jui juli thaka nisena ase, aru Tai laga theng sapha kori kene thaka pitol nisena ase, Tai eneka koi ase:

english_text: “I know your works, your love, faith, service, patient endurance, and that your last works are more than the first.
nagamese_text: “Moi tumikhan laga kaam jani ase, tumikhan laga morom, tumikhan laga biswas, tumikhan laga sewkai, aru nomro pora sob dukh loi kene thaka. Tumikhan poila kori thaka kaam to aji-kali kori thaka kaam he dangor ase.

english_text: But I have this against you, that you tolerate your woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and seduces my servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi tumikhan logote etu bhirodh kori ase: Tumikhan mon biya paile bhi Jezebel ke eku kowa nai, kun tai nijorke ekjon bhabobadi koi. Tai pora sikhai diya kotha khan Moi laga noukar khan ke bebichar kaam kori bole dibo nimite chalak kore aru murti ke puja kori kene khana kha luwa khan anikena taikhan ke khabole diye.

english_text: I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her sexual immorality.
nagamese_text: Moi taike mon ghura bole nimite homoi dise, kintu tai biya kaam charikena mon ghura bole nimite itcha thaka nai.

english_text: Behold, I will throw her and those who commit adultery with her into a bed of great oppression, unless they repent of her works.
nagamese_text: Sabi! Moi taike bemar laga bemar laga bisna te phelai dibo, aru kun manu tai logote mili kene biya kaam kore, taikhan ke bhi dangor dukh dibo, jodi taikhan laga paap aru biya pora mon na ghuraile.

english_text: I will kill her children with Death, and all the assemblies will know that I am he who searches the minds and hearts. I will give to each one of you according to your deeds.
nagamese_text: Moi tai laga bacha khan ke maribo aru morai dibo, aru sob girja khan janibo Moi he ekjon ase kun sob manu laga bhabona aru mon bisare. Aru Moi tumikhan laga kaam hisab te tumikhan ke dibo.

english_text: But to you I say, to the rest who are in Thyatira—as many as don’t have this teaching, who don’t know what some call ‘the deep things of Satan’—to you I say, I am not putting any other burden on you.
nagamese_text: Kintu jiman manu Thyatira te ase aru jun manu khan etu kotha khan namani kene thake, aru kiman manu Saitan laga bhitor kotha aru kaam khan najane- Tumikhan ke moi koi ase, ‘Moi tumikhan uporte aru dusra bhar nadhalibo.’

english_text: Nevertheless, hold that which you have firmly until I come.
nagamese_text: Kintu Moi naha tak bhal kori kene sob kotha khan mani kene thakibi.

english_text: He who overcomes, and he who keeps my works to the end, to him I will give authority over the nations.
nagamese_text: Kun manu hekh tak sob kaam te jiti kene, aru kun manu Moi laga kaam khotom nohua tak kore, taike Moi desh khan uporte adhikar dibo.

english_text: He will rule them with a rod of iron, shattering them like clay pots, as I also have received of my Father;
nagamese_text: ‘Tai loha laga lathi pora taikhan uporte raj koribo, Mati pora bonai diya kolsi nisena, tai etu sob tukra kori kene bhangai dibo.’

english_text: and I will give him the morning star.
nagamese_text: Jineka Moi laga Baba pora Moi paise, Moi bhi taike phojur laga tara dibo.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
nagamese_text: Kun manu logote kan ase, huni bhi Pobitro Atma pora girja khan ke ki koi ase.’””

english_text: “And to the angel of the assembly in Sardis write: “He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars says these things: “I know your works, that you have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead.
nagamese_text: “Sardis girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Ekjon kun Isor laga sat-ta atma khan dhori kene ase aru sat-ta tara dhori kene ase, Tai eneka koi ase: “Moi tumikhan laga kaam jane. Tumikhan jinda ase koi kene bhal naam pora thaki ase, kintu tumikhan mora ase.

english_text: Wake up and strengthen the things that remain, which you were about to throw away, for I have found no works of yours perfected before my God.
nagamese_text: Uthibi aru ki to bachi kene ase etu ke takot kori lobi, kun to mori bole he ase, kelemane Moi laga Isor laga suku usorte tumikhan laga kaam pura kori kene thaka dikha nai.

english_text: Remember therefore how you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If therefore you won’t watch, I will come as a thief, and you won’t know what hour I will come upon you.
nagamese_text: Yaad koribi, etu karone, tumikhan ki paise aru hunise. Mani thakibi, aru mon ghura bhi. Kintu tumikhan ghumai thaka pora nauthile, Moi chor nisena achanak pora ahibo, aru tumikhan najanibo Moi kuntu homoi te tumikhan laga bhirodh te ahibo.

english_text: Nevertheless you have a few names in Sardis that didn’t defile their garments. They will walk with me in white, for they are worthy.
nagamese_text: Kintu kunba manu Sardis te ase taikhan laga kapra letera kora nai, aru taikhan Moi logote berabo, boga kapra lagabo, kelemane taikhan etu pabole nimite yogya ase.

english_text: He who overcomes will be arrayed in white garments, and I will in no way blot his name out of the book of life, and I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
nagamese_text: Kun manu taikhan nisena sob kotha to mani kene jiti loi, taikhan bhi boga kapra lagai dibo, aru tai laga naam to kitia bhi Jibon laga Kitab pora nahatabo, aru tai laga naam Moi Baba usorte shikar koribo, aru Tai laga pobitro sorgodoth majote kobo.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
nagamese_text: Kun manu logote kan ase, huni bhi Atma pora girja khan ke ki koi ase.’””

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Philadelphia write: “He who is holy, he who is true, he who has the key of David, he who opens and no one can shut, and who shuts and no one opens, says these things:
nagamese_text: “Philadelphia girja laga sorgodoth ke likhibi: ‘Pobitro ekjon, hosa ekjon David, laga chabi dhori kene thaka ekjon, Tai pora khuli le aru kun pora bhi bondh nakore, Aru jitia tai bondh kori diye kun pora bhi aru nakhule, Tai he eneka koi ase:

english_text: “I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut), that you have a little power, and kept my word, and didn’t deny my name.
nagamese_text: “Moi tumikhan laga kaam jani ase. Sabi, Moi tumikhan usorte eneka ekta dorja khuli kene rakhidi ase juntu kun pora bhi bondh koribo na paribo. Kelemane tumikhan logote takot komti ase, hoile bhi tumikhan Moi laga kotha mani kene thakise aru Moi laga naam kobole chara nai.

english_text: Behold, I make some of the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but lie—behold, I will make them to come and worship before your feet, and to know that I have loved you.
nagamese_text: Sabi! Moi Saitan laga mondoli uporte bisar koribo, taikhan kun Yehudi khan ase koi. Hoile bhi taikhan nohoi, kintu, taikhan misa kowa manu khan ase- Sabi, Moi taikhan ke tumikhan laga theng nichete ahi kene pranam kori bole dibo, titia taikhan janibo Moi tumikhan ke kiman morom korise.

english_text: Because you kept my command to endure, I also will keep you from the hour of testing which is to come on the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan Moi laga kotha nomro hoi kene mani thaka nimite, Moi bhi tumikhan ke porikha kora laga homoi pora bachai kene rakhibo, kuntu pura duniya nimite ahibole ase, kun manu prithibi te thaki ase taikhan ke porikha kori bole nimite.

english_text: I am coming quickly! Hold firmly that which you have, so that no one takes your crown.
nagamese_text: Moi joldi ahi ase. Tumikhan logote ki ase etu dhori kene rakhibi, kun pora bhi jit laga mukut tumi logot pora chinikene loi najabole.

english_text: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will go out from there no more. I will write on him the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name.
nagamese_text: Kun manu sob mani kene jiti loi, Moi taike Isor laga ghor te ekta bhal khamba bonai kene rakhibo. Aru etu jaga pora tai kitia bhi bahar te ulaikene najabo, aru tai uporte Moi Isor laga naam likhi dibo, Moi laga Isor laga desh naam to likhi dibo -Notun Jerusalem, kuntu sorgo pora nichete ahe, Moi laga Isor pora- aru Moi laga notun naam.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.
nagamese_text: Kun logote kan ase, huni bhi Atma pora girja khan ke ki koi ase.’””

english_text: “To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea write: “The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of God’s creation, says these things:
nagamese_text: “Laodicea girja laga sorgodoth nimite likhibi: ‘Amen, jun bharosa koribo para aru hosa ekjon gawahi ase, Isor laga sristi shuru kora Jon koi ase:

english_text: “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot.
nagamese_text: “Moi tumikhan laga kaam jani ase, aru tumikhan gorom bhi nohoi aru thanda bhi nohoi. Moi itcha kore, tumikhan duita bhitor te ekta hoi kene thakile he bhal ase!

english_text: So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will vomit you out of my mouth.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan olop he gorom ase- gorom bhi nohoi aru thanda bhi nohoi- etu nimite Moi laga mukh pora tumikhan ke ulti kori kene thuk phela nisina phelai dibo.

english_text: Because you say, ‘I am rich, and have gotten riches, and have need of nothing,’ and don’t know that you are the wretched one, miserable, poor, blind, and naked;
nagamese_text: Kelemane tumikhan koise, ‘Moi dhuni ase moi logote bisi dhun sampoti ase, aru moike eku dorkar nai.’ Kintu tumikhan nijor najane ki halat te tumikhan thaki ase, tumikhan sobse dukh te thaka manu ase, bechara, gorib, andha aru lengta ase.

english_text: I counsel you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich; and white garments, that you may clothe yourself, and that the shame of your nakedness may not be revealed; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, that you may see.
nagamese_text: Tumikhan ke Moi logot pora jui pora sapha kori kene bonai rakha suna kini bole nimite koise, aru etu pora tumikhan dhuni hobole nimite, aru ekdom bhal sapha boga kapra nijor lagai kene tumikhan laga sorom to manu ke nadikha bole nimite koisele, aru suku sapha kori kene dikhi bole nimite bhal molom lobole korisile.

english_text: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
nagamese_text: Moi morom kora manu khan ke bhal rasta te anibole nimite sikhai diye. Etu karone, hosa pora mon ghura bhi.

english_text: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
nagamese_text: Sabi, Moi dorja usorte khara kori kene khat-khatai ase. Jodi kunba Moi laga awaj to huni kene dorja to khule, Moi tai logote ahibo, aru tai logote khabo, aru tai bhi Moi logote kha luwa koribo.

english_text: He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.
nagamese_text: Kun manu sob to mani kene jiti loi, Moi laga singhason usorte bohi bole nimite adhikar dibo, Moi Baba laga singhason te bohi bole nimite Moi bhi sob to mani kene jiti loise.

english_text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.”
nagamese_text: Kun manu logote kan ase, huni bhi Pobitro Atma pora girja khan ke ki koi ase.’””

english_text: After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven; and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, “Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.”
nagamese_text: Etu sob huwa pichete moi saise, aru sabi- sorgote ekta dorja khula thakise! Juntu prothom awaj moi hunise moi logote bhigul nisena kotha koi thakise, etu pora koise, “Yate uporte ahibi, aru Moi tumike etu pichete ki hobole ase etu sob to dikhai dibo.”

english_text: Immediately I was in the Spirit. Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne
nagamese_text: Etu homoi te Isor laga Atma moi logote thakise aru sabi- ekta singhason sorgote rakhidise! Aru kunba ekjon etu singhason te bohi thakise.

english_text: that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius. There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at.
nagamese_text: Etu ekjon kun ta te bohi thakise Tai ekta ujala diya jasper aru carnelian pathor nisena dikhi thakise. Tai laga singhason usorte dhanush thakise kun to sabole alag-alag rong thaka emerald pathor pora bonai kene rakha nisena dikhise.

english_text: Around the throne were twenty-four thrones. On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting, dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads.
nagamese_text: Aru etu singhason usorte aru bhi choubees singhason thakise, aru etu singhason te choubees bura manu khan boga kapra lagai kene bohi thakise, aru taikhan laga matha te suna laga mukut lagai kene thakise.

english_text: Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders. There were seven lamps of fire burning before his throne, which are the seven Spirits of God.
nagamese_text: Aru etu singhason pora bhijili laga ujala ulai thakise, awaj dikene, aru bhijili nisena dangor awaj ulai thakise. Sat-ta jui laga diya taikhan laga singhason usorte joli thakise, eitu khan Isor laga sat-ta atma khan thakise.

english_text: Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind.
nagamese_text: Aru etu singhason age te shisa laga samundar nisena thakise, crystal pathor nisena. Aru etu singhason majot aru usorte charta jinda janwar thakise, age pichete suku pora bhorta hoi kene thaka dikhise.

english_text: The first creature was like a lion, the second creature like a calf, the third creature had a face like a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle.
nagamese_text: Poila jinda thaka janwar to bagh nisena thakise, dusra jinda thaka janwar chutu guru laga bacha nisena thakise, tisra jinda janwar manu laga chehera nisena thakise aru charta ula jinda thaka janwar to uri thaka chil chiriya nisena thakise.

english_text: The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within. They have no rest day and night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!”
nagamese_text: Sob charta janwar laga choita pankha thakise, tai laga upor aru bhitor te bhi suku pora bhorta thakise. Rati aru din taikhan eneka koi thake, “Pobitro, pobitro, pobitro Probhu Isor Mohan ase, Tai thakise, ase, aru ahibole Jon ase.”

english_text: When the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever,
nagamese_text: Jitia jinda thaka janwar khan pora sonman, adar, aru dhanyavad diye jun singhason te bohi ase, Isor kun hodai nimite jinda ase

english_text: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne, saying,
nagamese_text: titia choubees bura manu khan Ekjon kun singhason te bohi ase, Tai age te athukarikena Taike aradhana kore kun hodai aru hodai nimite jinda ase. Taikhan laga mukut ulaikene Tai laga singhason age te rakhi kene koi thake,

english_text: “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed and were created!”
nagamese_text: “Sob mohima Apuni laga ase, moi khan laga Probhu aru Isor, Sob adar, aru mohima aru takot, Apuni sob to bonai dise, Aru Apuni laga itcha pora sob to hoise aru bonai dise.”

english_text: I saw, in the right hand of him who sat on the throne, a book written inside and outside, sealed shut with seven seals.
nagamese_text: Titia moi dikhise singhason te bohi kene thaka Isor laga dyna hathte kitab ase, juntu te age aru pichete bhi likhi kene thakise, aru sat-ta chihna pora mari kene thakise.

english_text: I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the book, and to break its seals?”
nagamese_text: Aru moi dikhise ekjon mohan sorgodoth dangor awaj pora koi thakise, “Kun etu kitab laga chihna to bhangi bole nimite yogya ase?”

english_text: No one in heaven above, or on the earth, or under the earth, was able to open the book or to look in it.
nagamese_text: Kintu kunbi sorgo aru prithibi aru prithibi laga nichete etu kitab khuli kene puribole para nai.

english_text: Then I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to look in it.
nagamese_text: Titia moi bisi mon dukh kori kene kandise kelemane etu khuli kene puri bo nimite kun manu bhi thaka nai.

english_text: One of the elders said to me, “Don’t weep. Behold, the Lion who is of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome: he who opens the book and its seven seals.”
nagamese_text: Kintu ekjon bura manu moike koise, “Tumi nakandibi. Sabi! Judah jat laga Bagh, David laga Jor, Tai he etu sob to jiti loise. Tai he etu kitab to khuli bole pare aru ta te lagai kene thaka sat-ta chihna Tai he khuli bole pare.”

english_text: I saw in the middle of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the middle of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth.
nagamese_text: Titia moi ekta Mer laga bacha ke dikhise, jun singhason laga majot khara hoi kene thakise aru charta janwar khan majot khara thakise aru bura manu khan majote khara thakise, Taike morai diya nisena dikhise. Tai laga sat-ta seing aru sat-ta suku thakise, juntu Isor laga sat-ta atma khan thakise, kunkhan ke prithibi laga sob jagate pathai dise.

english_text: Then he came, and he took it out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne.
nagamese_text: Tai jai kene singhason te bohi thaka ekjon laga dyna hath pora etu kitab loise.

english_text: Now when he had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each one having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
nagamese_text: Jitia Tai etu kitab loise, charta jinda thaka janwar aru choubees bura manu Mer laga bacha usorte athukari jaise. Taikhan logote nijor laga veena aru suna laga bati te joli kene mitha sugandh thaka pora bhorta hoi kene thaka dikhise, eitu khan to pobitro manu khan laga prathana khan thakise.

english_text: They sang a new song, saying, “You are worthy to take the book and to open its seals, for you were killed, and bought us for God with your blood out of every tribe, language, people, and nation,
nagamese_text: Taikhan notun gana korise, “Apuni etu kitab to lobole nimite yogya ase, Aru ta te chihna mari kene thaka khuli bole nimite takot ase. Kelemane apuni ke morai disele aru apuni laga khun pora Isor manu khan ke kini loise. Aru sob jati, bhasa, manu aru desh pora.

english_text: and made us kings and priests to our God; and we will reign on the earth.”
nagamese_text: Apuni taikhan ke ekta rajyo aru Apuni ke shewa kori bole nimite purohit bonai dise, Aru taikhan duniya te raj koribo.”

english_text: I looked, and I heard something like a voice of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. The number of them was ten thousands of ten thousands, and thousands of thousands,
nagamese_text: Titia moi saise aru bisi sorgodoth laga awaj hunise taikhan etu singhason usorte thakise aru jinda thaka janwar aru bura manu khan, sob mili kene dos hajar aru hajar-hajar thakise.

english_text: saying with a loud voice, “Worthy is the Lamb who has been killed to receive the power, wealth, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and blessing!”
nagamese_text: Taikhan dangor awaj pora koise, “Etu Mer laga Bacha yogya ase kun manu pora morai dise takot aru sob dhun pabole nimite aru gyaan, takot, adar aru sonman pabole nimite.”

english_text: I heard every created thing which is in heaven, on the earth, under the earth, on the sea, and everything in them, saying, “To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing, the honor, the glory, and the dominion, forever and ever! Amen!”
nagamese_text: Titia moi hunise sob bonai diya saman jun to sorgo aru prithibi te thakise, aru prithibi laga bhitor te thakise, aru samundar te aru kiman saman ta te thakise, taikhan koi thakise, “Tai ekjon kun singhason te bohi ase aru etu Mer bacha ke adar aru prosansa aru raj kori bole takot, hodai aru hodai nimite thakibi.”

english_text: The four living creatures said, “Amen!” Then the elders fell down and worshiped.
nagamese_text: Aru charta jinda thaka janwar para koise, “Amen!” Aru titia cholawta khan athukari kene Taike aradhana korise.

english_text: I saw that the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder, “Come and see!”
nagamese_text: Titia moi saise jitia Mer pora etu sat-ta chihna khuli se, aru moi hunise ekjon charta janwar majot pora dangor bhijili laga awaj nisena pora koise, “Ahibi!”

english_text: Then a white horse appeared, and he who sat on it had a bow. A crown was given to him, and he came out conquering, and to conquer.
nagamese_text: Titia moi saise aru ta te ekta boga ghora thakise! Aru etu uporte bohi thaka ekjon pora dhanush nisena dhori thakise, aru Taike ekta mukut dikene thakise. Tai ekta jiti luwa manu nisena jiti bole jaise.

english_text: When he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come!”
nagamese_text: Jitia Mer pora dusra chihna to khuli se, moi hunise dusra jinda thaka janwar pora koise, “Ahibi!”

english_text: Another came out, a red horse. To him who sat on it was given power to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another. There was given to him a great sword.
nagamese_text: Titia aru ekta ghora ulaikene ahise- jui nisena lal juli thaka ekta. Aru etu uporte bohi thaka ke prithibi pora shanti uthai loi jabole nimite takot dise, etu pora manu khan ekjon-ekjon ke morai dibole nimite. Etu ghora chola ke dangor ekta dangor talwar dise.

english_text: When he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, “Come and see!” And behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a balance in his hand.
nagamese_text: Jitia etu Mer pora tisra chihna to khuli se, Moi janwar pora kowa hunise, “Ahibi!” Moi saise aru ta te ekta kala ghora dikhise! Aru etu ghora uporte bohi thaka ekjon tai laga hathte palah nisena dhori thakise.

english_text: I heard a voice in the middle of the four living creatures saying, “A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenix of barley for a denarius! Don’t damage the oil and the wine!”
nagamese_text: Titia moi hunise etu charta janwar khan majote pora kowa hunise, “Gehu dhan ek bhag te ekta denarius daam ase, aru barley dhan tin bhag to ekta denarius daam ase, kintu draikha ros aru tel ke nuksan na koribi.”

english_text: When he opened the fourth seal, I heard the fourth living creature saying, “Come and see!”
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Mer pora charta chihna to khuli se, Moi charta jinda thaka janwar pora koi thaka hunise, “Ahibi!”

english_text: And behold, a pale horse, and the name of he who sat on it was Death. Hades followed with him. Authority over one fourth of the earth, to kill with the sword, with famine, with death, and by the wild animals of the earth was given to him.
nagamese_text: Titia moi saise, aru ta te komjur ghora ekta thakise! Aru etu uporte bohi thaka laga naam to Mora thakise, aru Hades tai laga pichete jai thakise. Prithibi laga char bhag laga ek bhag to taike adhikar dise, talwar pora morai dibole nimite, aru akaal pora, aru bemar pora, aru jongol te thaka janwar khan pora morai dibole nimite.

english_text: When he opened the fifth seal, I saw underneath the altar the souls of those who had been killed for the Word of God, and for the testimony of the Lamb which they had.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Mer pora pasta ula chihna to khuli se moi dikhise kiman manu Isor laga kotha aru kaam kora nimite morai dise taikhan laga atma etu puja kora bedi nichete thakise.

english_text: They cried with a loud voice, saying, “How long, Master, the holy and true, until you judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?”
nagamese_text: Taikhan awaj dangor pora hala kori kandi kene, koise, “Kiman deri hobo, sob uporte Raj kora ekjon, Pobitro aru hosa thaka, jitia prithibi te thaka khan uporte bisar koribo, aru kitia moi khan laga khun ula laga taikhan ke saja dibo?”

english_text: A long white robe was given to each of them. They were told that they should rest yet for a while, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who would also be killed even as they were, should complete their course.
nagamese_text: Titia taikhan sobke boga kapra dise, aru taikhan ke aru olop deri rukhibole koise jitia tak nokor aru bhai khan ke morai diya laga ginti napunche, jineka taikhan ke bhi morai disele.

english_text: I saw when he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake. The sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became as blood.
nagamese_text: Jitia Mer pora choutha ula chihna to khuli se, Moi dikhise aru titia dangor mati hili se. Suryo to chuli pora bonai diya bosta nisena kala hoi jaise, aru chand to khun nisena lal hoi jaise.

english_text: The stars of the sky fell to the earth, like a fig tree dropping its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind.
nagamese_text: Aru sorgote thaka tara khan prithibi te giri jaise, dimoru ghas te napaki kene thaka phol jitia dangor hawa pani marile giri jai, etu nisena tara khan giri jaise.

english_text: The sky was removed like a scroll when it is rolled up. Every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
nagamese_text: Aru akas to ekta kitab ke lipi luwa nisena lipi jaise aru harai jaise. Sob pahar aru samundar usorte thaka mati khan alag-alag hoi jaise.

english_text: The kings of the earth, the princes, the commanding officers, the rich, the strong, and every slave and free person, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains.
nagamese_text: Titia duniya laga raja aru dangor manu khan, aru sahab khan, dhuni manu khan, aru takot pora thaka khan, aru sob manu, noukar aru ajad pora thaka khan, taikhan nijorke pahar nichete aru pahar laga pathor nichete lukaise.

english_text: They told the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,
nagamese_text: Taikhan hala kori kene etu pahar aru pathor khan ke koise, “Moi khan uporte giri bhi! Lukai dibi tai laga chehera usor pora etu ekjon kun singhason te bohi ase aru Mer laga khong pora.

english_text: for the great day of his wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
nagamese_text: Kelemane Isor aru Mer laga dangor khong to ahi jaise, aru kun manu etu usorte khara kori bole pare?”

english_text: After this, I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete moi charta sorgodoth khan ke prithibi laga charta kinar te khara kori thaka dikhise, duniya laga hawa ke jor pora dhori thakise, eneka pora pura duniya, aru samundar, aru ghas khan ke hawa namaribole nimite.

english_text: I saw another angel ascend from the sunrise, having the seal of the living God. He cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea,
nagamese_text: Titia moi aru ekta sorgodoth ke purab pora ahi thaka dikhise, tai logote jinda Isor laga chihna thakise. Tai dangor awaj pora jun charta sorgodoth khan ke prithibi aru samundar te dukh dibole nimite adesh dise, taikhan

english_text: saying, “Don’t harm the earth, the sea, or the trees, until we have sealed the bondservants of our God on their foreheads!”
nagamese_text: ke koise, “Prithibi ke dukh nadibi, aru samundar ke bhi, aru ghas khan ke bhi jitia tak moi khan Isor laga noukar khan ke matha te chihna mari nadiye.”

english_text: I heard the number of those who were sealed, one hundred forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the children of Israel:
nagamese_text: Titia moi hunise kun manu khan ke etu chihna dise: 144,000, kiman Israel laga bacha khan laga ase etu chihna dise:

english_text: of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed, of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,
nagamese_text: Baroh hajar Judah laga jat khan ke chihna dise, Baroh hajar Reuben laga jat khan ke, Gad laga Baroh hajar jat khan ke chihna dise,

english_text: of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, of the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand, of the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand,
nagamese_text: Asher laga baroh hajar jat khan ke chihna dise, Baroh hajar Naphtali jat khan ke, Baroh hajar manasseh laga jat khan ke,

english_text: of the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand, of the tribe of Levi twelve thousand, of the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand,
nagamese_text: Simeon laga Baroh hajar jat khan ke chihna dise, Baroh hajar Levi laga jat khan ke, Baroh hajar Issachar laga jat khan ke chihna dise,

english_text: of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, of the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, and of the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.
nagamese_text: Baroh hajar Zebulun laga jat khan ke dise, Joseph laga baroh hajar jat khan ke chihna dise, Aru baroh hajar Benjamin laga jatikhan ke chihna mari dise.

english_text: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.
nagamese_text: Eitu khan sob huwa pichete moi saise, aru ta te bisi manu thakise kun bhi ginti kori bole napara thakise- sob desh, jati, manu, aru alag kotha kowa manu thakise- singhason aru Mer usorte khara kori thakise. Taikhan boga kapra pindhi kene thakise aru palm ghas laga pata hathte loi kene thakise,

english_text: They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan dangor awaj pora mati kene koise, “Anonto jibon moi khan Isor laga ase, etu ekjon kun singhason te bohi ase, aru Mer ke bhi!”

english_text: All the angels were standing around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces before his throne, and worshiped God,
nagamese_text: Aru sob sorgodoth singhason usorte khara kori thakise, aru bura manu khan usorte charta janwar khan thakise, aru jhukikena taikhan laga matha singhason usorte rakhikena Isor ke aradhana kori thakise,

english_text: saying, “Amen! Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might, be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”
nagamese_text: aru koise, “Amen! Adar aru mohima aru gyaan aru dhanyavad aru prosansa aru hokti aru takot hodai aru hodai nimite moi khan laga Isor ke hobo dibi! Amen!”

english_text: One of the elders answered, saying to me, “These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they, and where did they come from?”
nagamese_text: Titia ekjon cholawta moike hudise, aru koise, “Eitu khan kun ase, kun boga kapra lagai kene ase, aru taikhan kot pora ahise?”

english_text: I told him, “My lord, you know.” He said to me, “These are those who came out of the great suffering. They washed their robes and made them white in the Lamb’s blood.
nagamese_text: Titia moi taike jowab dise, “Moi laga Probhu, Apuni jane.” Titia tai moike koise, “Eitu khan sobse dangor dukh pora ulaikene aha khan ase. Taikhan laga kapra dhulai loise aru Mer laga khun pora boga kori loise.

english_text: Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple. He who sits on the throne will spread his tabernacle over them.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite, taikhan Isor laga singhason usorte khara kori ase Aru Tai laga ghor te din aru rati taike mohima di ase. Tai laga tambu khuli kene taikhan uporte lagai dibo.

english_text: They will never be hungry or thirsty any more. The sun won’t beat on them, nor any heat;
nagamese_text: Taikhan aru kitia bhi bhuka nathakibo, aru kitia bhi pyaas nalagibo, Aru suryo laga gorom taikhan uporte kitia bhi nalagibo.

english_text: for the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them and leads them to springs of life-giving waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
nagamese_text: Etu Mer kun singhason laga majote bohi ase taikhan ke cholai kene loijabo Aru taikhan ke jinda pani usorte thaki bole dibo, Aru Isor he taikhan laga sob suku pani mussai dibo.”

english_text: When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia Mer pora sat-ta chihna to khuli se, purah sorgote adha ghonta tak ekdom chup thakise.

english_text: I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
nagamese_text: Titia moi sat-ta sorgodoth khan kun Isor usorte khara hoi thaka dikhise, aru taikhan ke sat-ta bhigul dise.

english_text: Another angel came and stood over the altar, having a golden censer. Much incense was given to him, that he should add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar which was before the throne.
nagamese_text: Dusra ekjon sorgodoth ahise, tai suna laga bati bhal gundh pora bhorta kori kene thaka dhori thakise, aru bedi usorte khara hoi kene thakise. Bisi mitha sugandh taike dise kelemane tai pora he etu daan koribo, sob pobitro manu khan laga prathana loi kene, utu suna laga bedi te juntu singhason usorte ase.

english_text: The smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God out of the angel’s hand.
nagamese_text: Etu mitha sugandh laga dhuwa, pobitro manu khan laga prathana logote, sorgodoth laga hath pora uthi kene Isor usorte jaise.

english_text: The angel took the censer, and he filled it with the fire of the altar, then threw it on the earth. Thunders, sounds, lightnings, and an earthquake followed.
nagamese_text: Titia sorgodoth etu mitha sugandh laga bati loi kene puja kora laga bedi laga jui pora bhorta kori loise. Tai prithibi te etu phelai dise, aru titia bhijili nisena dangor awaj ulaise, ujala hoise aru mati khan hili se.

english_text: The seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.
nagamese_text: Titia sat-ta sorgodoth khan kunke sat-ta bhigul dise, taikhan awaj kori bole nimite taiyar korise.

english_text: The first sounded, and there followed hail and fire, mixed with blood, and they were thrown to the earth. One third of the earth was burned up, and one third of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
nagamese_text: Prothom sorgodoth pora tai laga bhigul bojaise, aru titia pathor aru khun logote jui milai kene ulaise. Titia etu ke prithibi te phelai dise, aru prithibi laga tin bhag juli jaise, aru tin bhag laga ghas khan juli jaise, aru jiman bhi hara ghas thakise, eitu khan sob juli jaise.

english_text: The second angel sounded, and something like a great burning mountain was thrown into the sea. One third of the sea became blood,
nagamese_text: Titia dusra sorgodoth pora tai laga bhigul bojaise, aru kiba ekta dangor pahar jui pora juli thaka nisena samundar te phelai dise. Aru tin bhag laga samundar khun hoi jaise,

english_text: and one third of the living creatures which were in the sea died. One third of the ships were destroyed.
nagamese_text: aru tin bhag samundar te jinda thaka janwar khan sob mori jaise, aru tin bhag jahaaj khan sob khotom hoi jaise.

english_text: The third angel sounded, and a great star fell from the sky, burning like a torch, and it fell on one third of the rivers, and on the springs of water.
nagamese_text: Titia tisra sorgodoth pora tai laga bhigul bojaise, aru dangor ekta tara akas pora girise, ujala kori kene ase, aru etu tin bhag laga nodi te girise aru sapha panite giri jaise.

english_text: The name of the star is “Wormwood.” One third of the waters became wormwood. Many people died from the waters, because they were made bitter.
nagamese_text: Etu tara laga naam to Wormwood thakise. Aru etu laga tin bhag pani pura tita hoi jaise, aru bisi manu etu pani khai kene mori jaise.

english_text: The fourth angel sounded, and one third of the sun was struck, and one third of the moon, and one third of the stars, so that one third of them would be darkened; and the day wouldn’t shine for one third of it, and the night in the same way.
nagamese_text: Titia choutha sorgodoth tai laga bhigul bojaise, aru suryo laga tin bhag te lagi jaise, aru chand laga tin bhag eneka hoise aru tara khan laga tin bhag bhi eneka hoi jaise, etu pora tin bhag pura andhera hoi jaise. Din laga tin bhag te ujala nathaka hoise, aru etu nisena rati bhi eneka hoi jaise.

english_text: I saw, and I heard an eagle, flying in mid heaven, saying with a loud voice, “Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the other blasts of the trumpets of the three angels, who are yet to sound!”
nagamese_text: Titia moi saise, aru moi chil chiriya laga awaj hunise tai matha uporte uri kene dangor awaj pora mati kene koi thakise, “Hai, hai, hai ase jun manu prithibi te thaki ase, kelemane aru bhi tinta sorgodoth khan laga bhigul bajabole ase.”

english_text: The fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star from the sky which had fallen to the earth. The key to the pit of the abyss was given to him.
nagamese_text: Titia pansta ula sorgodoth tai laga bhigul bojaise aru moi dikhise sorgo pora ekta tara prithibi te giri jaise. Etu tara ke khotom nathaka mati niche laga chabi di dise.

english_text: He opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke went up out of the pit, like the smoke from a burning furnace. The sun and the air were darkened because of the smoke from the pit.
nagamese_text: Jitia tai khotom nathaka mati niche laga dorja khuli se, ta te laga dhuwa upor phale dangor jui nisena uthijaise. Suyro aru hawa etu laga dhuwa pora andhar hoi jaise.

english_text: Then out of the smoke came locusts on the earth, and power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power.
nagamese_text: Titia etu dhuwa pora phoring pukakhan prithibi te ahise, aru taikhan ke bhichoo nisena prithibi te takot dise.

english_text: They were told that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree, but only those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan prithibi laga ghas aru nohoile hara thaka ghas nohoile hara thaka ghas khan ke nuksan nakoribole, kintu kun manu taikhan laga matha te chihna laga nai taikhan ke he nuksan kori bole koise.

english_text: They were given power, not to kill them, but to torment them for five months. Their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan ke manu ke morai dibole nimite kowa nai, kintu khali taikhan ke panch mohina tak dukh dibole koise. Aru taikhan laga dukh to hoile jitia ekta bhichoo pora kamure aru bikhai eneka he taikhan dukh pabo.

english_text: In those days people will seek death, and will in no way find it. They will desire to die, and death will flee from them.
nagamese_text: Aru etu laga din khan te manu khan mori bole mon jabo, kintu mori bole na paribo. Taikhan mori jabole nimite itcha koribo, kintu mora taikhan pora polai jabo.

english_text: The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war. On their heads were something like golden crowns, and their faces were like people’s faces.
nagamese_text: Aru etu phoring pukakhan lorai te jabole ghora khan ke taiyar kora nisena ase. Aru taikhan laga matha te suna laga mukut lagai kene thaka nisena dikhise, aru taikhan laga chehera manu laga chehera nisena thakise.

english_text: They had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like those of lions.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan laga chuli mahila khan laga chuli nisena ase, aru taikhan laga dath to bagh laga dath nisena he thakise.

english_text: They had breastplates like breastplates of iron. The sound of their wings was like the sound of many chariots and horses rushing to war.
nagamese_text: Taikhan laga chati te laga thali khan loha laga thali nisena dikhise, aru taikhan laga pankha laga awaj lorai te polaikene jai thaka ghora khan nisena thakise.

english_text: They have tails like those of scorpions, with stingers. In their tails they have power to harm men for five months.
nagamese_text: Aru taikhan laga puchur te bhichoo pora dunkh mari bole thaka nisena taikhan laga puchur te bhi thakise, aru taikhan laga puchur te manu khan ke panch mohina tak dukh dibole nimite takot thakise.

english_text: They have over them as king the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is “Abaddon”, but in Greek, he has the name “Apollyon”.
nagamese_text: Taikhan uporte raj kora laga raja to khotom nathaka mati niche laga duth ase. Tai laga naam Ibrani bhasa te Abaddon ase, aru Yunani te tai laga naam Apollyon thakise.

english_text: The first woe is past. Behold, there are still two woes coming after this.
nagamese_text: Poila dukh to paar korise. Sabi! Etu pichete aru bhi duita dukh ahibole baki ase.

english_text: The sixth angel sounded. I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar which is before God,
nagamese_text: Titia choita ula sorgodoth tai laga bhigul bojaise, aru moi ekta awaj janwar laga seing pora ahi thaka hunise kun to Isor age te rakhi thaka suna pora bona bedi pora ulaise.

english_text: saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, “Free the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates!”
nagamese_text: Titia etu awaj pora choita sorgodoth ke koise kun logote bhigul thakise, “Etu charta sorgodoth kunkhan Euphrates Nodi te bandhi kene ase, taikhan ke chari dibi.”

english_text: The four angels were freed who had been prepared for that hour and day and month and year, so that they might kill one third of mankind.
nagamese_text: Karone etu charta sorgodoth, kunkhan ke etu homoi, etu din, etu mohina, aru etu saal, nimite taiyar kori thakise, taikhan ke chari dise. Aru taikhan tin bhag manu jati khan ke morai dibole nimite chari dise.

english_text: The number of the armies of the horsemen was two hundred million. I heard the number of them.
nagamese_text: Ghora pichete thaka sipahi khan sob milai kene 200,000,000 thakise. Moi taikhan laga ginti hunise.

english_text: Thus I saw the horses in the vision and those who sat on them, having breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and sulfur yellow; and the horses’ heads resembled lions’ heads. Out of their mouths proceed fire, smoke, and sulfur.
nagamese_text: Etiya moi ghora laga sapna dikhise aru taikhan uporte te bohi kene thaka khan ke bhi dikhise, chati te thaka thali to lal rong, nila rong, aru jui nisena haldi rong thakise. Ghora khan laga matha sabole bagh laga matha nisena thakise, aru taikhan laga mukh pora jui aru dhuwa ulai thakise.

english_text: By these three plagues, one third of mankind was killed: by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur, which proceeded out of their mouths.
nagamese_text: Tin bhag manu khan etu laga tinta dukh pora mori jaise: Jui pora, dhuwa pora aru taikhan laga mukh pora jui ula pora.

english_text: For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails. For their tails are like serpents, and have heads; and with them they harm.
nagamese_text: Kelemane etu ghora laga takot to tai laga mukh te aru puchur te thakise- taikhan laga puchur to hoile saph pora matha thaka nisena, aru etu pora taikhan manu ke jokhom dise.

english_text: The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues, didn’t repent of the works of their hands, that they wouldn’t worship demons, and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of brass, and of stone, and of wood, which can’t see, hear, or walk.
nagamese_text: Kun manu etu sob dukh pora nomori kene bachi jaise, taikhan pora ki paap kaam korise, etu pora mon ghura nai aru suna, chandi, pitol, pathor aru khuri pora bona murti ke puja nakoribole rukhanai- eitu khan pora eku dikhi bole napare, aru huni bole bhi napare, aru taikhan bera bole napare.

english_text: They didn’t repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts.
nagamese_text: Aru, taikhan manu ke morai diya pora mon ghura nai, aru jadu kora pora bhi ghura nai, biya letera kaam, aru chor kori kene aha pora bhi taikhan mon ghura nai.

english_text: I saw a mighty angel coming down out of the sky, clothed with a cloud. A rainbow was on his head. His face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire.
nagamese_text: Arubi moi dusra maha sorgodoth ke sorgo pora ahi thaka dikhise. Tai badal pora bondh kori kene thakise, aru tai laga matha uporte dhanush thakise. Tai laga chehera suryo nisena aru Tai laga theng khan jui juli thaka khamba nisena thakise.

english_text: He had in his hand a little open book. He set his right foot on the sea, and his left on the land.
nagamese_text: Tai ekta huru kitab dhori thakise, aru etu tai laga hathte khuli se. Tai laga dyna theng samundar te rakhise aru tai laga baya theng matite rakhise.

english_text: He cried with a loud voice, as a lion roars. When he cried, the seven thunders uttered their voices.
nagamese_text: Titia Tai bagh pora hala kora nisena dangor awaj pora hala korise. Jitia tai hala korise, sat-ta bhijili nijor laga awaj te kotha kobole shuru hoise.

english_text: When the seven thunders sounded, I was about to write; but I heard a voice from the sky saying, “Seal up the things which the seven thunders said, and don’t write them.”
nagamese_text: Jitia sat-ta bhijili kotha koise, aru moi likhi bole thakise, kintu moi sorgo pora ekta awaj hunise aru koise, “Sat-ta bhijili pora ki koise etu lukai kene rakhibi. Etu kitab te nilikhibi.”

english_text: The angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to the sky
nagamese_text: Aru moi kuntu sorgodoth samundar aru prithibi te khara hoi thaka dikhise tai laga dyna hath to sorgo phale uthaise.

english_text: and swore by him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it, the earth and the things that are in it, and the sea and the things that are in it, that there will no longer be delay,
nagamese_text: Aru Tai kun hodai aru hodai nimite jinda ase Tai laga naam kosom khaise, aru kun he etu sob aru ta te thaka sob saman bonaise, etu prithibi aru sob saman khan, aru samundar te ki ase, “Aru etiya olop bhi deri nahobo.

english_text: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound, then the mystery of God is finished, as he declared to his servants the prophets.
nagamese_text: Kintu sat-ta sorgodoth laga awaj dinte, jitia Tai laga bhigul bajabo taiyar hobo, titia Isor laga asurit kaam to purah hoi jabo, kineka Tai laga noukar bhabobadi khan ke etu bhal kotha koi disele.”

english_text: The voice which I heard from heaven, again speaking with me, said, “Go, take the book which is open in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land.”
nagamese_text: Titia kun to awaj moike sorgo pora kotha korise aru moike koise: “Jabi, sorgodoth kun samundar aru matite khara kori ase Tai laga hath pora etu kitab to lo bhi.”

english_text: I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little book. He said to me, “Take it and eat it. It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.”
nagamese_text: Titia moi sorgodoth logote jai kene moike etu kitab to dibole nimite koise. Tai moike koise, “Lo bhi aru khai lobi. Etu pora tumi laga peth to tita koribo, kintu tumi laga mukh mou pani nisena mitha kori dibo.”

english_text: I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth. When I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
nagamese_text: Titia moi sorgodoth laga hath pora etu kitab to loi kene khai loise. Aru moi laga mukh to mou pani nisena mitha hoi jaise, kintu moi jitia etu khaise, moi laga peth tita hoi jaise.

english_text: They told me, “You must prophesy again over many peoples, nations, languages, and kings.”
nagamese_text: Titia kunba pora moike koise, “Tumi aru bisi manu ke etu bhabobani kobi, desh khan ke, alag bhasa kowa manu khan ke, aru raja khan ke.”

english_text: A reed like a rod was given to me. Someone said, “Rise and measure God’s temple, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
nagamese_text: Etu pichete, ekta patla lathi nisena moike naap kori bole nimite dise. Moike koise, “Uthibi aru Isor laga mondoli aru bedi laga naap lobi, aru kun manu ta te aradhana kore taikhan laga bhi naap lobi.

english_text: Leave out the court which is outside of the temple, and don’t measure it, for it has been given to the nations. They will tread the holy city under foot for forty-two months.
nagamese_text: Kintu mondoli laga bahar jaga to naap nolobi, etu to Porjati manu khan ke di dise. Taikhan etu pobitro sheher Jerusalem ke tin saal adha tak theng pora chipa bo.

english_text: I will give power to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy one thousand two hundred sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.”
nagamese_text: Aru Moi laga duita gawahi khan ke adhikar dibo, aru taikhan 1,260 din tak bhabobani kobo, bosta laga kapra lagai kene.”

english_text: These are the two olive trees and the two lamp stands, standing before the Lord of the earth.
nagamese_text: Etu duita oliv ghas aru duita saaki jola laga khuri ase juntu prithibi laga Probhu usorte khara ase.

english_text: If anyone desires to harm them, fire proceeds out of their mouth and devours their enemies. If anyone desires to harm them, he must be killed in this way.
nagamese_text: Kunba manu etu ke nuksan kori bole kosis korile, taikhan laga mukh para jui ulaikene dushman khan ke khotom kori dibo.

english_text: These have the power to shut up the sky, that it may not rain during the days of their prophecy. They have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they desire.
nagamese_text: Taikhan logote akas to bondh kori bole adhikar ase kelemane jitia taikhan bhabobani kobo etu homoi te pani nagiribo. Taikhan logote pani ke khun bonai dibole takot ase aru etu prithibi te alag kisim laga dukh aru bemar pora bhorta kori bole nimite taikhan logote adhikar ase.

english_text: When they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war with them, and overcome them, and kill them.
nagamese_text: Jitia taikhan laga gawahi kora to khotom hobo, etu khotom nakora mati nichete thaka janwar taikhan uporte lorai koribo. Taikhan ke morai dikene sob jiti lobo.

english_text: Their dead bodies will be in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.
nagamese_text: Taikhan laga mora gaw to dangor sheher laga rasta te giri thakibo -kuntu ke Sodom aru Egypt koi- jun jagate taikhan laga Probhu ke Cross te mari disele.

english_text: From among the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations, people will look at their dead bodies for three and a half days, and will not allow their dead bodies to be laid in a tomb.
nagamese_text: Aru tin din adha tak sob jati, desh aru alag kotha kowa manu khan taikhan laga mora gaw to sabo aru taikhan laga gaw to kobor te hali bole nimite nadibo.

english_text: Those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, and they will be glad. They will give gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth.
nagamese_text: Aru kiman manu etu prithibi te ase, taikhan etu dikhi kene khushi koribo. Taikhan ekjon-ekjon ke uphar dikene duita bhabobadi khan kun duniya te thakise etu naam pora khushi koribo.

english_text: After the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood on their feet. Great fear fell on those who saw them.
nagamese_text: Kintu tin din adha pichete Isor laga saas to taikhan uporte di dibo, aru taikhan laga theng te khara hobo aru kun manu etu dikhibo taikhan bisi bhoi koribo.

english_text: I heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, “Come up here!” They went up into heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.
nagamese_text: Titia sorgo pora dangor awaj pora taikhan ke koi thaka hunibo, “Yate uporte ahibi!” Titia taikhan badal pora sorgote jai jabo, aru taikhan laga dushman khan sai thakibo.

english_text: In that day there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. Seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
nagamese_text: Thik etu homoi te, mati dangor pora hili bo, aru sheher laga dos bhag khotom hoi jabo. Sat-ta hajar manu etu homoi te moribo, aru kun manu bachi jai taikhan bhoi lagibo aru etu dikhi kene Isor ke mohima dibo.

english_text: The second woe is past. Behold, the third woe comes quickly.
nagamese_text: Aru dusra hai kotha bhi paar hoise. Sabi! Tisra hai kotha to joldi ahi ase.

english_text: The seventh angel sounded, and great voices in heaven followed, saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ. He will reign forever and ever!”
nagamese_text: Titia sat-ta sorgodoth pora tai laga bhigul bajaise, aru sorgote dangor awaj khan pora koise, “Etu duniya laga rajyo to Probhu aru Khrista laga rajyo hoise, Aru Tai hodai nimite raj koribo.”

english_text: The twenty-four elders, who sit on their thrones before God’s throne, fell on their faces and worshiped God,
nagamese_text: Titia choubees bura manu khan, kun Isor laga usorte singhason te bohi ase taikhan laga matha niche kori kene Isor ke aradhana koribo.

english_text: saying: “We give you thanks, Lord God, the Almighty, the one who is and who was, because you have taken your great power and reigned.
nagamese_text: Taikhan koise, “Moi khan Apuni ke dhanyavad di ase, Mohan Probhu Isor, kun thakise, aru hodai ase, Apuni dangor takot to loi loise aru raj korise.

english_text: The nations were angry, and your wrath came, as did the time for the dead to be judged, and to give your bondservants the prophets, their reward, as well as to the saints and those who fear your name, to the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth.”
nagamese_text: Etu desh khan khong uthise, Kintu Apuni laga khong to ahise, Aru mora manu khan ke bisar kori bole nimite, Aru Apuni laga noukar khan ke inam dibole nimite, Bhabobadi aru pobitro manu khan ke inam dibole nimite, Aru kun manu apuni laga naam te bhoi kori kene thake, Chutu aru dangor, Aru kun manu etu prithibi to khotom kore taikhan ke khotom kori dibole nimite.”

english_text: God’s temple that is in heaven was opened, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant was seen in his temple. Lightnings, sounds, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail followed.
nagamese_text: Titia sorgote thaka mondoli to khuli jaise aru Probhu laga vachan laga ark to tai laga mondoli majote dikhise. Etu homoi te dangor bhijili ujala ahise, jor pora hala kori kene, aru mati hili se aru dangor pathor khan girise.

english_text: A great sign was seen in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
nagamese_text: Titia ekta dangor chihna sorgote ulaise: ekjon mahila suryo pora kapra lagai kene, aru chand tai laga theng nichete, aru baroh ta tara laga mukut tai laga matha te pindhise.

english_text: She was with child. She cried out in pain, laboring to give birth.
nagamese_text: Tai bacha bhuki thakise, aru bacha jonom hobole laga bikha pora kandi thakise, aru bacha ulabole nimite dukh pai thakise.

english_text: Another sign was seen in heaven. Behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven crowns.
nagamese_text: Titia aru dusra ekta chihna sorgote ulaise: Sabi, ekta dangor ajgar janwar tai laga dosta matha aru dosta seing, aru sat-ta mukut tai laga matha te ase.

english_text: His tail drew one third of the stars of the sky, and threw them to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child.
nagamese_text: Aru tai laga puchur pora tin bhag tara sorgote jhari kene hatai dise aru prithibi phale phelai dise. Aru etu ajgar janwar bacha pabole thaka mahila usorte khara korise, jitia tai bacha pabo, etu ajgar janwar pora bacha ke khai dibole.

english_text: She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron. Her child was caught up to God and to his throne.
nagamese_text: Titia utu mahila pora ekta mota bacha jonom dise, aru tai etu desh ke loha laga lathi pora raj chola bole thakise. Tai laga bacha ke Isor aru singhason usorte chingi kene loi jaise,

english_text: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that there they may nourish her one thousand two hundred sixty days.
nagamese_text: aru etu mahila jongol te polai jaise, tai nimite Isor pora ekta jaga taiyar kori kene rakhidise, taike 1,260 din tak bhal kori kene sai dibole.

english_text: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war.
nagamese_text: Etiya sorgote dangor lorai hoise. Michael aru tai laga sorgodoth khan etu ajgar janwar logote lorai korise; aru etu ajgar janwar bhi tai laga duth khan ke loi kene lorai korise.

english_text: They didn’t prevail. No place was found for them any more in heaven.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu ajgar janwar aru tai laga duth khan takot thaka nathaka hoi jaise aru taikhan nimite akash te thaki bole jaga bhi nathaka hoise.

english_text: The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.
nagamese_text: Etu karone dangor ajgar janwar ke nichete phelai dise- purana ekta saph, taike bhoot atma aru Saitan koi, tai pura duniya ke thogai diye- taike prithibi te phelai dise, aru tai laga duth khan bhi tai logote phelai dise.

english_text: I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come; for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.
nagamese_text: Titia moi sorgo pora dangor awaj te koi thaka hunise, “Etiya amikhan laga poritran aru takot Aru Isor laga rajyo to ahise, Aru Tai laga Khrista laga adhikar ase. Moi laga bhai khan ke dukh diya ekjon ke nichete phelai dise, Kun pora Isor usorte din aru rati taikhan ke dukh dise.

english_text: They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.
nagamese_text: Taikhan Mer bacha laga khun aru gawahi pora sob to jiti loise, Kelemane mori bole thaka homoi te bhi taikhan nijor laga jibon to morom kora nai.

english_text: Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time.”
nagamese_text: Etu nimite sorgo khan khushi koribi, aru Kiman manu ta te thaki ase! Kintu prithibi aru samundar khan dukh hobo, Kelemane saitan to tumikhan majote ase! Tai bisi khong pora bhorta hoi ase, Tai jani ase tai logote olop homoi he bachi kene ase!

english_text: When the dragon saw that he was thrown down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child.
nagamese_text: Aru jitia taike prithibi nichete phelai dise koi kene ajgar janwar to janise, tai jai kene etu mota bacha jonom diya mahila ke digdar dise.

english_text: Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, so that she might be nourished for a time, times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.
nagamese_text: Kintu etu mahila ke chil chiriya laga pankha nisena duita dise, tai etu loi kene jongol phale tai laga jagate polai jabo nimite, etu jagate taike tin saal aru adha tak nimite bhal kori kene sai dibo, homoi, aru olop homoi nimite- etu saph laga chehera age pora dur te thaki bole.

english_text: The serpent spewed water out of his mouth after the woman like a river, that he might cause her to be carried away by the stream.
nagamese_text: Etu nimite saph pora tai laga mukh pora nodi nisena pani etu mahila laga pichete jabo dise, etu pora ban-pani aha nisena mahila ke loi jabole nimite.

english_text: The earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon spewed out of his mouth.
nagamese_text: Kintu prithibi pora mahila ke modot korise aru prithibi pora mukh khuli kene sob pani to khai loise.

english_text: The dragon grew angry with the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony.
nagamese_text: Titia ajgar pora mahila uporte bisi khong uthise aru tai laga khandan khan uporte lorai kori bole nimite jaise, kun manu Isor laga kotha mani thakise aru Jisu laga gawahi dhori kene thakise, taikhan ke khotom kori bole nimite lorai korise.

english_text: Then I stood on the sand of the sea. I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, blasphemous names.
nagamese_text: Titia moi ekta janwar samundar pora ulaikene aha dikhise. Etu janwar laga dosta seing aru sat-ta matha thakise. Aru matha khan ke dosta mukut thakise, aru ekta-ekta matha uporte Isor ke bodnam kora naam khan thakise.

english_text: The beast which I saw was like a leopard, and his feet were like those of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority.
nagamese_text: Aru etiya kuntu janwar moi dikhise etu sabole ekta chetak nisena thakise. Tai laga theng to bhalu laga theng nisena, aru tai laga mukh ekta bagh janwar laga mukh nisena thakise. Ajgar janwar pora taike takot dise aru tai laga singhason dise, aru sob manu ke raj kori bole laga adhikar dise.

english_text: One of his heads looked like it had been wounded fatally. His fatal wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled at the beast.
nagamese_text: Ekta janwar laga matha to morai diya nisena dikhise, kintu tai laga bahar jokhom khan bhal hoi jaise. Pura prithibi to asurit hoi kene tai laga piche jaise.

english_text: They worshiped the dragon because he gave his authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?”
nagamese_text: Taikhan etu ajgar janwar ke puja korise, kelemane tai pora tai laga adhikar etu janwar ke dise. Aru taikhan etu janwar ke bhi puja korise aru koi thakise, “Etu janwar nisena aru kun ase?” Aru “Kun he tai logote lorai kori bole paribo?”

english_text: A mouth speaking great things and blasphemy was given to him. Authority to make war for forty-two months was given to him.
nagamese_text: Etu janwar ke phutani laga kotha khan aru Isor ke bodnam diya kotha khan kobole nimite mukh dise, aru tin saal adha tak etu sob kaam khan kori bole nimite adhikar dise.

english_text: He opened his mouth for blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, his dwelling, and those who dwell in heaven.
nagamese_text: Titia etu janwar Isor laga biya kotha koise, Tai laga naam ke hinsa korise, aru Tai kun jagate thake etu laga biya kobole, aru jiman manu sorgote thake, taikhan sob laga biya kobole tai laga mukh khuli se.

english_text: It was given to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them. Authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation was given to him.
nagamese_text: Aru etu janwar ke biswasi aru pobitro manu khan uporte lorai kori bole nimite aru taikhan uporte jiti lobole nimite takot dise. Aru sob jati, desh, bhasa aru manu khan uporte adhikar dise.

english_text: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been killed.
nagamese_text: Aru jiman manu prithibi te thake, taikhan sob etu ke puja koribo, aru kunkhan laga naam kitab te likha nai taikhan bhi, duniya bona laga suru pora, Jibon laga Kitab te, juntu Mer bacha laga ase, kunke morai disele.

english_text: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
nagamese_text: Jodi kunba manu kan ase koile, tai huni lobi.

english_text: If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.
nagamese_text: Kunba manu ke bandhi kene loi jabole ase koile, Taike eneka he loijabo. Jodi kunba manu ke talwar pora mora bole ase koile, Etu talwar pora he tai moribo. Etu he nomro, dukh kosto koribo para aru pobitro khan laga biswas ase.

english_text: I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. He had two horns like a lamb and it spoke like a dragon.
nagamese_text: Titia moi aru bhi ekta janwar prithibi pora ulaikene ahi thaka dikhise, aru tai to ajgar janwar nisena kotha koi.

english_text: He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.
nagamese_text: Tai laga usorte poila ulaikena aha janwar laga kiman adhikar ase sob to dikhai dise, aru etu prithibi aru ta te thaka kiman manu ase sobke etu poila janwar ke puja kori bole nimite dise- etu ekjon kun laga bahar laga jokhom to bhal hoi jaisele.

english_text: He performs great signs, even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth in the sight of people.
nagamese_text: Tai bisi dangor asurit kaam khan korise, aru tai manu usorte sorgo pora jui prithibi te bhi ahibole dise aru manu khan ke dikhai dise.

english_text: He deceives my own people who dwell on the earth because of the signs he was granted to do in front of the beast, saying to those who dwell on the earth that they should make an image to the beast who had the sword wound and lived.
nagamese_text: Aru juntu sob chihna khan janwar laga usorte kori bole nimite adhikar dise, jiman manu prithibi te ase taikhan ke thogai dise. Aru taikhan ke janwar laga murti bona bole nimite koise kun logote talwar laga jokhom ase, kintu jinda ase.

english_text: It was given to him to give breath to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause as many as wouldn’t worship the image of the beast to be killed.
nagamese_text: Aru etu janwar laga murti ke saas dibole nimite monjuri dise, kelemane etu janwar laga murti to kotha kobole paribo, aru kun manu etu murti ke puja nokorile taike morai dibo.

english_text: He causes all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, and the free and the slave, to be given marks on their right hands or on their foreheads;
nagamese_text: Taikhan joborjosti korise, chutu aru dangor, dhuni aru gorib, noukar aru aram pora thaka manu, taikhan laga matha age te nohoile dyna hathte chihna mari bole nimite.

english_text: and that no one would be able to buy or to sell unless he has that mark, which is the name of the beast or the number of his name.
nagamese_text: Aru etu karone, kun manu bhi etu chihna nathakile eku bhi bikiri aru kini bole na paribo jitia tak taikhan logote etu laga chihna nathakibo- etu janwar laga naam, nohoile tai naam laga ginti.

english_text: Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. His number is six hundred sixty-six.
nagamese_text: Yate gyaan ase: kun manu bujhi bole pare, tai etu janwar laga ginti to ongkho kori lobi. Kelemane etu ekjon manu laga ginti ase, aru tai laga ongkho to hoile 666 ase.
